stories.summaryEn: Sigurðr comes to the court of King Gjúki, where Queen Grímhildr gives him a drink of forgetfulness; he forgets Brynhildr, marries the princess Guðrún and swears brotherhood with her brothers Gunnarr and Högni. Grímhildr then sends Gunnarr to woo Brynhildr, who will wed only the man who rides through her wall of fire. In Gunnarr's shape Sigurðr rides the flames and spends three nights with her, the naked Gram between them, taking back Andvaranautr. Years later the two queens quarrel at the river and Guðrún shows the ring; the truth comes out. Brynhildr, in grief and fury, demands Sigurðr's death; he is murdered in his bed, and Brynhildr follows him, burned on his pyre.
stories.summaryZh: 西古尔德来到居基王的宫廷，王后格里姆希尔德给他喝下遗忘之酒，他忘记了布伦希尔德，娶了公主古德伦，与她的兄弟贡纳尔、霍格尼结为兄弟。格里姆希尔德又让贡纳尔去向布伦希尔德求婚，可是只有能骑马穿过火墙的人才能娶她。西古尔德变成贡纳尔的模样穿过火焰，与布伦希尔德同住三夜，中间放着出鞘的格拉姆，又取走了安德瓦拉诺特。多年后，两位王后在河边争吵，古德伦亮出那枚戒指，真相大白。布伦希尔德悲愤欲绝，要求贡纳尔杀死西古尔德。西古尔德被谋杀在床上，布伦希尔德也随他而去，与他一起被火化。
stories.titleZh: 沃尔松格萨迦 · 第三部 西古尔德与布伦希尔德

claims.statement: Brynhildr interprets Guðrún's dreams of a golden hawk and a golden hart, foretelling that she will marry Sigurðr through her mother's guile, lose him through Brynhildr, then marry Atli and lose her brothers.
At Gjúki's court Queen Grímhildr gives Sigurðr a magic drink that makes him forget Brynhildr; he marries Guðrún and swears blood-brotherhood with Gunnarr and Högni under a strip of turf.
When Gunnarr's horse shies from the fire round Brynhildr's hall and Grani will not move under him, he and Sigurðr exchange shapes by the craft Grímhildr taught them.

In Gunnarr's shape Sigurðr rides Grani through Brynhildr's fire, claims her by her vow, lies three nights with the naked Gram between them, and takes from her the ring Andvaranautr, giving her another.
At the end of Gunnarr and Brynhildr's wedding feast Sigurðr remembers all his oaths to Brynhildr, but, married to Guðrún and bound to his sworn brother, he keeps silent.

When Brynhildr claims precedence while washing their hair in the Rhine, Guðrún reveals that Sigurðr, not Gunnarr, rode through the fire and shows her the ring Andvaranautr, and Brynhildr goes home pale and silent.
Brynhildr lies silent for days, then reproaches Gunnarr for winning her by deceit, condemns Grímhildr's drink of forgetfulness and curses the house of Gjúki as oath-breakers.

Sigurðr tells Brynhildr he forgot her through the drink and offers to leave Guðrún for her, but she refuses to have two husbands in one hall, and his grief bursts the rings of his mail-coat as he leaves.
Pressed by Brynhildr's false charge, Gunnarr, bound with Högni by oaths of brotherhood, has their brother Guttormr, fed on wolf and serpent flesh, kill Sigurðr in his bed on the third morning.
Mortally wounded, Sigurðr hurls Gram after Guttormr and cuts him in two, declares to Guðrún that he never wronged Gunnarr or betrayed their oath, and dies, while Brynhildr laughs at Guðrún's wailing.
Guðrún sits dry-eyed by Sigurðr's body until her sister lays his bloodied head in her lap, and then she weeps and laments that he stood among Gjúki's sons like a tall leek above the grass.
Having foretold the fall of Gjúki's house, Brynhildr stabs herself and asks to be burned on Sigurðr's pyre with a naked sword between them as in their three nights, and they are burned together.

events.summaryEn: South of the Rhine ruled King Gjúki, with three sons, Gunnarr, Högni and the youngest, Guttormr, and a daughter, Guðrún, the fairest of maidens; his queen Grímhildr was skilled in magic and hard of heart.
events.summaryZh: 在莱茵河以南，有一个名叫居基的国王，他有三个儿子：贡纳尔、霍格尼和年纪最小的古托姆，还有一个女儿古德伦，她是那里最美丽的少女。

events.summaryEn: Soon Sigurðr came to Gjúki's court riding Grani with Fáfnir's gold.
events.summaryZh: 不久，西古尔德骑着格拉尼，带着法夫纳的黄金，来到了居基王的宫廷。

events.summaryEn: Grímhildr told Gunnarr he should take a wife, and the best match was Brynhildr.
events.summaryZh: 格里姆希尔德又对儿子贡纳尔说：你应该娶一个妻子，最合适的就是布伦希尔德。

events.summaryEn: In Gunnarr's shape Sigurðr mounted Grani with Gram in hand and golden spurs on his heels, and Grani leapt at the fire as soon as he felt the spurs; the earth shook and the flames rose to heaven, but Grani went through as if the fire died down before them.
events.summaryZh: 西古尔德以贡纳尔的样子骑上了格拉尼，手握格拉姆，金色的马刺踢向马腹。

events.summaryEn: Brynhildr went to her father and told Heimir that a king called Gunnarr had ridden her fire and she must marry him — though she had told him that Sigurðr, to whom she had sworn at Hlymdalir, was the only man who could do it.
events.summaryZh: 布伦希尔德回到父亲那里，对赫米尔说：一个名叫贡纳尔的国王穿过了我的火墙，我只好嫁给他。

events.summaryEn: One day Brynhildr and Guðrún went to the Rhine to wash their hair, and Brynhildr waded further out.
events.summaryZh: 有一天，布伦希尔德和古德伦一起到莱茵河里洗头。

events.summaryEn: Brynhildr lay in her bed for days without eating, drinking or speaking, and paid no heed to Gunnarr, Högni or Guðrún.
events.summaryZh: 布伦希尔德躺在床上，一连几天不吃不喝，也不说话。

events.summaryEn: Sigurðr went in and bade Brynhildr wake, for the sun shone over the hall and she had slept long enough.
events.summaryZh: 西古尔德走进布伦希尔德的房间，对她说：醒醒吧，布伦希尔德，太阳照着整个宫殿，你睡得够久了，不要再悲伤了。

events.summaryEn: Brynhildr told Gunnarr that if he wished her to live, he must kill Sigurðr and his son, or she would leave him — claiming falsely that Sigurðr had betrayed him in those three nights beyond the fire.
events.summaryZh: 布伦希尔德对贡纳尔说：你若想要我活下去，就必须杀死西古尔德和他的儿子，否则我就离开你，回到我的亲人那里去。

events.summaryEn: Run through, Sigurðr woke, seized Gram beside the bed and hurled it after the fleeing Guttormr; it struck him in the back and cut him in two at the waist, so that his head and arms fell inside the chamber and his legs outside the door.
events.summaryZh: 西古尔德被剑刺穿，醒了过来。

events.summaryEn: Guðrún sat by Sigurðr's body, motionless and dry-eyed, and they feared she would die of grief.
events.summaryZh: 古德伦坐在西古尔德的尸体旁，一动不动，一滴眼泪也流不出来，人们都害怕她会因悲伤而死去。

events.summaryEn: Brynhildr told Gunnarr she had dreamed that all would pay for the deed, and foretold the fate of Gjúki's house: Guðrún would marry her brother Atli, Gunnarr and Högni would die at Atli's hands, and Guðrún would avenge them.
events.summaryZh: 布伦希尔德对贡纳尔说：我做了一个梦，梦见所有的人都会为这件事付出代价。

versions.labelEn: Völsunga saga, chapters 25–32 (Morris and Magnússon translation, long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第25–32章（莫里斯与马格努松译本，长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 古德伦的梦、遗忘之酒与结拜、火墙前的贡纳尔、交换容貌、火中的三夜、河边的争吵、布伦希尔德的悲痛、最后的谈话、誓言与谋杀、西古尔德之死、古德伦的哀哭、布伦希尔德的结局
versions.rightsNote: 莫里斯与马格努松的英译本属公共领域；本站发布按章节顺序的独立讲述。

sections.bodyEn: South of the Rhine ruled King Gjúki, with three sons, Gunnarr, Högni and the youngest, Guttormr, and a daughter, Guðrún, the fairest of maidens; his queen Grímhildr was skilled in magic and hard of heart. Guðrún dreamed she had a fair hawk with golden feathers, dearer to her than all her treasures, and it soon died; her maids urged her to ask Brynhildr, who was wisest in dreams. She went with them to Brynhildr, sat in a golden seat, told that dream and another, of a great golden hart, fairest of all, which she longed for but which Brynhildr shot before her eyes. Brynhildr read them plainly: Sigurðr would come to her father's court and marry her, but her mother would make him forget Brynhildr by guile; they would not be together long; Brynhildr would bring about his death, and Guðrún would then marry Atli, king of the Huns, lose her brothers, and kill Atli. Guðrún, grieved and afraid, said she wished she had not learned it, and went home.
sections.bodyZh: 在莱茵河以南，有一个名叫居基的国王，他有三个儿子：贡纳尔、霍格尼和年纪最小的古托姆，还有一个女儿古德伦，她是那里最美丽的少女。王后格里姆希尔德是一个懂得魔法、心肠很硬的女人。有一天，古德伦做了一个梦，梦见自己有一只美丽的猎鹰，羽毛是金色的，她觉得这只鹰比她所有的珍宝都珍贵，可是不久它就死了。她闷闷不乐，侍女们劝她去问问布伦希尔德，因为布伦希尔德最懂得解梦。古德伦带着侍女们来到布伦希尔德的住处，坐在金色的座位上，讲起了自己的梦，又说了另一个梦：她梦见一头金色的大鹿，比所有的鹿都美，她想得到它，可是布伦希尔德在她的面前把鹿射死了。布伦希尔德听了，直截了当地说出了梦的意思：西古尔德会来到你父亲的宫中，你会嫁给他，可是你的母亲会用诡计让他忘记我，你们不会长久，你将失去他。我会害死他，然后你会嫁给匈人的国王阿特利，失去你的兄弟们，然后杀死阿特利。古德伦听了，悲伤而惊恐，说：我真不愿知道这些事。说完就回家去了。

sections.bodyEn: Soon Sigurðr came to Gjúki's court riding Grani with Fáfnir's gold. No one had seen a knight so tall, fair and splendidly arrayed, and he stayed there long, honoured by the king and his sons, yet he thought of Brynhildr and often spoke of her. Queen Grímhildr, seeing his nobility and wealth, wished him married to her daughter. At a feast she gave him a horn of mead she had brewed with magic, saying that Gjúki would be his father, she his mother and her sons his brothers. He drank, and at once forgot Brynhildr entirely. He married Guðrún, with a feast lasting many days, and he, Gunnarr and Högni swore brotherhood in the old way, letting their blood run together under a strip of turf. Sigurðr gave Guðrún some of Fáfnir's heart to eat, and she became grimmer and wiser; they had a son named Sigmundr.
sections.bodyZh: 不久，西古尔德骑着格拉尼，带着法夫纳的黄金，来到了居基王的宫廷。人们从没见过这样高大英俊、装束华丽的骑士，国王和王子们热情地款待了他，他在那里住了很久。他每天都想着布伦希尔德，常常说起她。王后格里姆希尔德看出了西古尔德的高贵和他拥有的巨大财富，心想如果能让他娶了自己的女儿，对她的家族将是多么大的好处。她调制了一种魔法的酒，在一次宴会上亲手递给西古尔德，说：我们都很喜欢你，居基王愿意做你的父亲，我愿意做你的母亲，我的儿子们愿意做你的兄弟。西古尔德喝下了这杯酒。酒一下肚，他就把布伦希尔德忘得干干净净，一点也想不起来了。不久，他娶了古德伦为妻，婚礼持续了许多天。西古尔德又和贡纳尔、霍格尼按照古老的习俗，让鲜血流在一起，在一块草皮下面立誓结为兄弟，发誓像亲兄弟一样彼此忠诚。西古尔德给了古德伦一块法夫纳的心，她吃了以后变得更加冷酷，也更加聪明。他们生了一个儿子，取名西格蒙德。

sections.bodyEn: Grímhildr told Gunnarr he should take a wife, and the best match was Brynhildr. Gunnarr was willing, and Sigurðr agreed to ride with him. Her father, King Buðli, said Brynhildr would choose for herself, for she had vowed to marry only the man who rode through the fire burning round her hall; Heimir said the same. They came to her hall and saw the flames blazing up to the sky. Gunnarr rode at the fire, but his horse shied back and would not go on. Sigurðr lent him Grani, but Grani would not move under him, for he would bear no one but Sigurðr. Then they used the craft Grímhildr had taught them: Sigurðr and Gunnarr exchanged shapes, Sigurðr taking Gunnarr's likeness and Gunnarr Sigurðr's.
sections.bodyZh: 格里姆希尔德又对儿子贡纳尔说：你应该娶一个妻子，最合适的就是布伦希尔德。她是一位尊贵的女子，你若娶了她，我们的家族就更加强大了。贡纳尔愿意去求婚，西古尔德也答应陪他一起去。他们先去见布伦希尔德的父亲布德利国王，国王说：我女儿自己决定嫁给谁，她发誓只嫁给能骑马穿过她厅堂四周燃烧的火墙的人。他们又去找赫米尔，赫米尔也说，这要由布伦希尔德自己来定。他们来到布伦希尔德住的地方，只见她的厅堂四周燃着熊熊的火焰，火光直冲天空。贡纳尔骑着他的马冲向火墙，可是马一靠近火焰就惊恐地退了回来，怎么也不肯往前走。西古尔德说：你骑我的格拉尼试试吧。贡纳尔骑上格拉尼，可是格拉尼一动也不动，因为它只听西古尔德的。贡纳尔没有办法了。这时，他们想起了格里姆希尔德教给他们的魔法：西古尔德和贡纳尔交换容貌。于是西古尔德变成了贡纳尔的样子，贡纳尔变成了西古尔德的样子。

sections.bodyEn: In Gunnarr's shape Sigurðr mounted Grani with Gram in hand and golden spurs on his heels, and Grani leapt at the fire as soon as he felt the spurs; the earth shook and the flames rose to heaven, but Grani went through as if the fire died down before them. In the hall Brynhildr sat on a high seat like a swan on the waves, with helm and sword. Asked who he was, he said he was Gunnarr, son of Gjúki, come through the fire as her vow required. She did not know what to answer, thinking of her vow and of Sigurðr, but the vow could not be broken, and she consented. Sigurðr stayed three nights and they lay in one bed, but he laid the naked sword Gram between them; when she asked why, he said it was fated that he should wed his bride so or die. When he left he took from her the ring Andvaranautr — the very ring he had given her — and gave her another from Fáfnir's hoard. He rode back through the fire to his comrade, and they took their own shapes again.
sections.bodyZh: 西古尔德以贡纳尔的样子骑上了格拉尼，手握格拉姆，金色的马刺踢向马腹。格拉尼一感觉到马刺，就向火墙冲去。大地震动，火焰冲天，可是格拉尼毫不畏惧地穿过了火海，仿佛火焰在他们面前自动熄灭了一样。西古尔德走进厅堂，布伦希尔德坐在高座上，像一只坐在水面上的天鹅，头戴头盔，手握宝剑。她问他是谁，他说：我是居基的儿子贡纳尔，你发过誓，谁能穿过火墙，你就嫁给谁，现在我来了。布伦希尔德一时不知如何回答，她想起了自己的誓言，又想起了西古尔德，可是誓言不能违背，她只好同意嫁给他。西古尔德在那里住了三夜，他们同睡在一张床上，可是西古尔德把出鞘的格拉姆放在两人中间。布伦希尔德问他为什么这样做，他说：命运要求我这样迎娶我的新娘，否则我就会死去。临别时，他从布伦希尔德的手上取下了那枚安德瓦拉诺特戒指——那正是当年他亲手送给她的——又从法夫纳的财宝中取出另一枚戒指给她。然后他骑马穿过火墙，回到同伴那里，两人换回了自己的容貌。

sections.bodyEn: Brynhildr went to her father and told Heimir that a king called Gunnarr had ridden her fire and she must marry him — though she had told him that Sigurðr, to whom she had sworn at Hlymdalir, was the only man who could do it. Doubt filled her heart. The wedding of Gunnarr and Brynhildr was held at Gjúki's court with a feast of many days; and when the feast ended, Sigurðr remembered all his oaths to Brynhildr, for the drink's magic had passed. But he was married to Guðrún and she to his sworn brother, and he said nothing and bore it in silence. So they lived long at the same court, giving no sign when they met; yet Brynhildr always wondered why it was not Sigurðr who had come through the fire, and Sigurðr kept the truth hidden, for telling it would shame his sworn brother. Beneath the calm, the tragedy drew nearer every day.
sections.bodyZh: 布伦希尔德回到父亲那里，对赫米尔说：一个名叫贡纳尔的国王穿过了我的火墙，我只好嫁给他。可是我曾对你说过，在赫利姆谷许下誓言的是西古尔德，只有他才能做到这件事。她心中充满了疑惑。不久，盛大的婚礼在居基王的宫中举行，贡纳尔娶了布伦希尔德。宴会持续了很多天。就在婚宴结束的时候，西古尔德忽然想起了他对布伦希尔德许下的所有誓言，那杯遗忘之酒的魔力消失了。可是他已经娶了古德伦，布伦希尔德也已经成了他结拜兄弟的妻子。他什么也没有说，默默地忍受着这一切。萨迦说，从那以后，西古尔德和布伦希尔德在同一个宫廷里生活了很长时间，两人见面时都不露声色，可是布伦希尔德的心中一直有一个疑问：为什么穿过火墙的不是西古尔德？西古尔德心里藏着真相，不能说出来，因为那会让他的结拜兄弟蒙羞。表面的平静之下，悲剧正在一天天逼近。

sections.bodyEn: One day Brynhildr and Guðrún went to the Rhine to wash their hair, and Brynhildr waded further out. When Guðrún asked why, Brynhildr said she would not be on a level with her in this: her father was mightier, and her husband had done great deeds and ridden through the burning fire, while Guðrún's was a thrall of King Hjálprekr. Guðrún, angered, said she had better be silent: her husband had slain Fáfnir and Reginn and won the gold, and it was he, not Gunnarr, who rode through the fire and lay three nights beside her with the sword between them. When Brynhildr would not believe it, Guðrún held out her hand and asked if she knew this ring — and it was Andvaranautr. Brynhildr went pale as death, said nothing, and went home, and from that day, says the saga, she lay in her bed and would not speak. The queens' quarrel laid bare the long-hidden secret, and Andvari's curse began to work on the ring's owners.
sections.bodyZh: 有一天，布伦希尔德和古德伦一起到莱茵河里洗头。布伦希尔德往河里走得更远，古德伦问她为什么。布伦希尔德说：在这件事上，我为什么要和你平起平坐？我的父亲比你的父亲更有权势，我的丈夫做了许多大事，骑马穿过了燃烧的火墙，而你的丈夫只不过是希亚尔普雷克国王的一个奴仆。古德伦大怒，说：你还是闭嘴为好，我的丈夫杀死了法夫纳和雷金，得到了那些黄金，而穿过火墙的正是他，不是贡纳尔。在你身边睡了三夜、把宝剑放在你们中间的，就是西古尔德。布伦希尔德不相信。古德伦伸出手来，说：你看看我手上的这枚戒指，你认得它吗？布伦希尔德一看，那正是安德瓦拉诺特。她的脸一下子变得像死人一样惨白，一句话也没有说，转身回家去了。萨迦说，从这一天起，她再也不说话，整天躺在床上。两个王后之间的这一场争吵，把隐藏了多年的秘密全部揭开了，安德瓦利的诅咒终于开始在这枚戒指的主人们身上应验。

sections.bodyEn: Brynhildr lay in her bed for days without eating, drinking or speaking, and paid no heed to Gunnarr, Högni or Guðrún. When Gunnarr asked what ailed her, she reproached him bitterly: he had deceived her; it was Sigurðr, not he, who rode through the fire; she had vowed to marry the bravest man, and that was Sigurðr, yet by guile they had wedded her to Gunnarr; his mother Grímhildr was the worst of women, who had given Sigurðr the drink of forgetfulness; she would rather die than see them. She cursed the house of Gjúki as oath-breakers who would be repaid. Gunnarr had no answer. Her grief and wrath grew until the household dreaded her sighs; even Sigurðr's heart was heavy, knowing no good could come of it. Gunnarr asked Sigurðr to speak with her, hoping he alone could calm her.
sections.bodyZh: 布伦希尔德躺在床上，一连几天不吃不喝，也不说话。贡纳尔、霍格尼和古德伦先后来看她，她都不理睬。贡纳尔来问她到底怎么了，她才开口，痛苦地责备他：你骗了我。那个穿过火墙的人不是你，是西古尔德。当年我发誓只嫁给最勇敢的人，那就是西古尔德，可是你们用诡计让我嫁给了你。你的母亲格里姆希尔德是最坏的女人，是她给西古尔德下了遗忘的药。我宁愿去死，也不愿再看见你们。她诅咒居基王的家族，说他们背弃了誓言，必将遭到报应。贡纳尔无言以对。她的悲伤和愤怒越来越深，宫里的人听见她的叹息声，都觉得可怕。萨迦说，布伦希尔德的愤怒像火一样燃烧，任何人都不敢靠近她，就连西古尔德自己，也感到心中沉重，他知道这件事不会有好的结局。贡纳尔去找西古尔德，请他去和布伦希尔德谈一谈，也许只有他能平息她的怒火。

sections.bodyEn: Sigurðr went in and bade Brynhildr wake, for the sun shone over the hall and she had slept long enough. She asked how he dared come to her, who had betrayed her worst of all. He had not deceived her, he said; the drink of forgetfulness had made him forget her, and when he remembered it was too late; he loved her as he loved himself. He would rather she were his wife; his heart toward her had never changed, and to end her grief he would leave Guðrún and marry her. She answered that she would not have two husbands in one hall, and would rather die than betray Gunnarr; she had sworn to wed the man who rode the fire and would keep that oath though it cost her life. Sigurðr was long silent, and when he went out his grief was so great, says the saga, that the rings of his mail-coat burst asunder. Two who had sworn to each other were brought by a drink, a deceit and a ring to a place from which there was no return.
sections.bodyZh: 西古尔德走进布伦希尔德的房间，对她说：醒醒吧，布伦希尔德，太阳照着整个宫殿，你睡得够久了，不要再悲伤了。布伦希尔德说：你怎么敢来见我？你比任何人都更狠心地背叛了我。西古尔德说：我并没有骗你，那杯遗忘之酒让我忘记了你，等我想起来的时候，一切都已经晚了。可是我很快就认出了你，我对你的爱，和我对自己的爱一样深。他说：我宁愿你嫁给了我，现在我对你的心从来没有变过。如果能让你不再痛苦，我愿意抛弃古德伦，娶你为妻。布伦希尔德回答：我不愿意要两个丈夫在同一个大厅里，我宁愿死也不会背叛贡纳尔。我曾经发过誓，要嫁给那个穿过火墙的人，我也会遵守这个誓言，哪怕它让我失去性命。西古尔德沉默了很久，走出房间时，他的悲伤是那么巨大，萨迦说，他胸前的锁子甲的环子都被撑断了。两个曾经互相许下誓言的人，因为一杯酒、一个诡计和一枚戒指，走到了无法回头的地步。

sections.bodyEn: Brynhildr told Gunnarr that if he wished her to live, he must kill Sigurðr and his son, or she would leave him — claiming falsely that Sigurðr had betrayed him in those three nights beyond the fire. Gunnarr, sorely troubled, took counsel with Högni, who said they were bound by their oaths of brotherhood and could not kill him with their own hands. Then let Guttormr do it, said Gunnarr, for he was young and had sworn no oath. They fed Guttormr the flesh of wolf and serpent and other things to make him fierce, and promised him gold and lands. Twice at dawn Guttormr went into Sigurðr's chamber and found him awake, looking at him with keen eyes, and dared not strike; the third morning Sigurðr was asleep, and Guttormr drew his sword and thrust it through him so that the point stood in the bedding beneath.
sections.bodyZh: 布伦希尔德对贡纳尔说：你若想要我活下去，就必须杀死西古尔德和他的儿子，否则我就离开你，回到我的亲人那里去。她说，西古尔德在火中的那三夜背叛了贡纳尔——这不是真的，可是她要用这句话逼贡纳尔下手。贡纳尔十分苦恼，他和霍格尼商量。霍格尼说：我们和西古尔德发过结拜兄弟的誓言，不能违背誓言亲手杀他。贡纳尔说：那就让古托姆去做吧，他年纪小，没有参加我们的誓言。他们用狼肉和蛇肉做成食物，又加上了别的东西，给古托姆吃了，让他变得凶狠暴躁，又答应给他大量的黄金和土地，怂恿他去杀死西古尔德。第一天清晨，古托姆走进西古尔德的卧室，西古尔德醒着，用锐利的目光看着他，古托姆不敢下手，退了出去。第二天清晨也是这样。第三天清晨，西古尔德睡着了，古托姆拔出剑，一剑刺穿了他的身体，剑尖一直刺进了床下的木板。

sections.bodyEn: Run through, Sigurðr woke, seized Gram beside the bed and hurled it after the fleeing Guttormr; it struck him in the back and cut him in two at the waist, so that his head and arms fell inside the chamber and his legs outside the door. Guðrún, asleep in Sigurðr's arms, woke in his blood and cried out in grief. Sigurðr told her not to weep: her brothers were alive, and their son was too young to guard himself against his enemies; Brynhildr had brought this about, who loved him above all men; and he swore he had never wronged Gunnarr, but had kept their oaths and never been his wife's lover. Had he known of it, he could have stood against them. Then he died. Guðrún heaved a great sigh, and her wailing rang through the hall so that the geese in the yard cried out. Brynhildr, hearing it, laughed. When Gunnarr asked whether she rejoiced at the dreadful deed, she said she had dreamed it all: they had broken their oaths and killed a far better man, and their own end would be evil.
sections.bodyZh: 西古尔德被剑刺穿，醒了过来。他抓起放在床边的格拉姆，向正在逃跑的古托姆扔了过去。宝剑击中了古托姆的后背，把他从腰部劈成了两段，上半身倒在房间里面，下半身和双脚倒在门外。古德伦正睡在西古尔德的怀里，她在血泊中醒来，看见丈夫浑身是血，悲痛地哭喊起来。西古尔德对她说：不要哭，我的亲人们都还活着。我们的儿子还太小，不懂得防备敌人。这件事是布伦希尔德一手造成的，她爱我胜过爱任何人。可是我可以作证，我从来没有对贡纳尔做过任何不义的事，我一直遵守着我们的誓言，从来没有做过他妻子的情人。如果我早知道这一切，提前防备，我就能和这些人对抗。说完这些话，西古尔德死去了。古德伦发出一声长长的叹息，她的哭声传遍了整个宫殿，院子里的鹅也惊叫起来。布伦希尔德在自己的房间里听见了古德伦的哭声，竟然大笑起来。贡纳尔问她为什么笑，难道她是在为这件可怕的事高兴吗？布伦希尔德说：我梦见过这一切，你们背弃了誓言，杀死了比你们好得多的人，你们的结局也不会好。

sections.bodyEn: Guðrún sat by Sigurðr's body, motionless and dry-eyed, and they feared she would die of grief. Noble women came and each told the greatest sorrow of her life — one had lost husband and children, another her brothers and her freedom — to make her weep, but she could not. At last her sister drew the covering from Sigurðr and laid his head in Guðrún's lap, bidding her look on her beloved and kiss him as if he lived. She saw his fair hair clotted with blood, his keen eyes dimmed, his breast pierced by the sword, and she fell on him weeping until her tears ran like rain, and the geese in the yard cried with her. Over his body, says the saga, she said her Sigurðr among the sons of Gjúki had been like a tall leek above the grass, like a bright gem on a golden band, and now she was as small in the hall as a leaf in the wind.
sections.bodyZh: 古德伦坐在西古尔德的尸体旁，一动不动，一滴眼泪也流不出来，人们都害怕她会因悲伤而死去。贵族的妇人们来到她身边，一个个讲述自己一生中遭遇过的最大的不幸，想让她明白，世上的人都有痛苦，好让她哭出来。一个妇人说，她失去了丈夫和孩子；另一个说，她的兄弟们都被杀死了，自己也成了俘虏。可是古德伦仍然没有哭。最后，她的姐姐揭开了盖在西古尔德身上的布，把他的头放在古德伦的膝上，对她说：看看你所爱的人吧，亲吻他，就像他还活着时那样。古德伦看了一眼，看见他美丽的头发上沾满了鲜血，他锐利的眼睛已经失去了光彩，他的胸膛被剑刺穿了。她终于伏在他身上，放声大哭，泪水像雨水一样流了下来，院子里的鹅也和她一起叫了起来。萨迦说，古德伦对着西古尔德的尸体，说她的西古尔德在居基的儿子们中间，就像高高的韭葱长在青草之上，像一颗明亮的宝石镶在金带上，现在她失去了他，在王宫里就像风中的一片树叶那样渺小。

sections.bodyEn: Brynhildr told Gunnarr she had dreamed that all would pay for the deed, and foretold the fate of Gjúki's house: Guðrún would marry her brother Atli, Gunnarr and Högni would die at Atli's hands, and Guðrún would avenge them. Then she gave her gold to her maids, put on a golden byrnie and stabbed herself with a sword. As she lay dying, she asked Gunnarr to build one broad pyre for Sigurðr and herself, to lay her by his side as in the three nights they shared, with a naked sword between them, and to lay on it Sigurðr's men, two hawks, hounds and her maids, so that they would go together into the other world and the door of Hel would not fall on his heels. Gunnarr did as she asked, and Sigurðr and Brynhildr were burned together; men said no one like Sigurðr would ever be born again. The saga goes on to tell of Guðrún and Atli and how the gold sank at last into the Rhine — but that is another story.
sections.bodyZh: 布伦希尔德对贡纳尔说：我做了一个梦，梦见所有的人都会为这件事付出代价。她预言了居基家族的未来：古德伦将嫁给她的哥哥阿特利，贡纳尔和霍格尼将死在阿特利的手里，古德伦又将为兄弟们报仇。说完，她把自己的金子分给侍女们，穿上金色的铠甲，用剑刺进了自己的身体。贡纳尔赶来时，她已经奄奄一息了。她对贡纳尔说出了最后的请求：请为西古尔德和我建一座宽大的火葬堆，让我躺在他的身边，就像我们曾经同床的那三夜一样，在我们中间放一把出鞘的宝剑；把西古尔德的随从、两只猎鹰、几条狗，还有我的侍女们都放在火葬堆上，让我们一同到另一个世界去，这样，地狱的门就不会砸在他的脚后跟上。贡纳尔照她的话做了。西古尔德和布伦希尔德一起被火化了，火焰熊熊燃起，人们都说，世上再也不会出现像西古尔德这样的人了。萨迦接下来还讲了古德伦与阿特利的故事，以及那批黄金如何最后沉入莱茵河，那将是另一个故事了。

stories.canonicalTitle: The Cattle Raid of Cooley, Part 1: Cú Chulainn at the fords
stories.editorialNote: 依据邓恩 1914 年英译莱因斯特书本《夺牛长征记》前半，按情节顺序讲述；书中许多单打独斗的对手只择要讲述。原文对战斗和身体有不少直白描写，本篇保留情节，不渲染细节。

series.labelEn: Part 1: Cú Chulainn at the fords
series.labelZh: 上部 · 库丘林守浅滩

stories.summaryEn: Medb and Ailill, queen and king of Connacht, compare their possessions in bed and find them equal except for a white-horned bull. To win the matching Brown Bull of Cúailnge, Medb musters the four provinces of Ireland against Ulster. The Ulstermen lie under a curse of weakness, and the seventeen-year-old Cú Chulainn guards the border alone. On the march the exiled Ulsterman Fergus tells of Cú Chulainn's boyhood: beating a hundred and fifty boys at five, earning his name by killing the smith Culann's hound, taking arms on a day of prophecy. At the fords Cú Chulainn fights champion after champion, refuses the goddess Morrígan, is healed by his father Lugh, and when the boy-troop of Ulster dies for him, falls on the host in his battle-frenzy in a great slaughter.
stories.summaryZh: 康诺特的女王梅芙和国王艾利尔在枕边比较财产，一切都相等，只差一头白角公牛。为了得到能与之相比的库利褐色公牛，梅芙集结了爱尔兰四省的大军进攻阿尔斯特。阿尔斯特的男人们正受着诅咒，陷入衰弱，只有十七岁的库丘林独自守卫边界。流亡的阿尔斯特人弗格斯在行军途中讲述了库丘林少年时的事迹：五岁打败一百五十个男孩，杀死铁匠库兰的猛犬而得名，在预言的那一天拿起武器。库丘林在浅滩上一天接一天地与对手决斗，拒绝了女神莫莉甘，又得到父亲鲁格的医治；当阿尔斯特的少年队为他战死时，他在狂暴的变身中向大军发起了大屠杀。
stories.titleZh: 夺牛长征记 · 上部 库丘林守浅滩

claims.statement: In the pillow-talk at Cruachan, Medb and Ailill count their possessions and find them equal except for the White-horned Bull Finnbennach, born in Medb's herd but gone over to Ailill's, which Medb cannot match.

Medb sends Mac Roth to borrow the Brown Bull of Cúailnge from Dáire mac Fiachna, who agrees until a drunken messenger boasts it would have been taken by force, whereupon Dáire refuses and Medb resolves to take it.
Before the host sets out from Cruachan, the prophetess Fedelm tells Medb 'I see it crimson, I see it red' and sings of a young warrior who will destroy her army alone.

While the Ulstermen lie under Macha's curse of debility and Cú Chulainn alone guards the border, Fergus leads Medb's host astray to give Ulster time, and persuades Medb to scatter the outstanding Gailióin through the host instead of killing them.

Cú Chulainn halts Medb's host with an ogam-inscribed withe twisted with one hand, one foot and one eye, and with a four-pronged fork driven one-handed into a ford bearing the heads of four scouts, which only Fergus can pull out.
Fergus tells Medb and Ailill how the boy Sétanta, not yet five, came alone to Emain Macha, warded off the hundred and fifty boys of the boy-troop and was taken in by King Conchobar.

As a boy Sétanta kills the smith Culann's ferocious hound with his ball and a standing stone, offers to guard Culann's house himself until a whelp is grown, and is named Cú Chulainn, 'the hound of Culann', by the druid Cathbad.

Hearing Cathbad say that whoever takes arms that day will be famous but short-lived, the boy Cú Chulainn takes Conchobar's own arms and chariot, kills the three sons of Nechta Scéne, and is cooled from his battle-fury in three vats of water.

Cú Chulainn agrees with Medb to fight one champion a day at the ford while the host advances only during the combat, drowns Fráech and kills many others, and gives way before Fergus on his promise to yield in return one day.

Refused by Cú Chulainn when she offers her love as a king's daughter, the Morrígan attacks him as eel, wolf and heifer during his fight with Lóch and is wounded thrice, then is healed by his blessings as she gives him milk as an old woman.
At Lerga, Lug mac Ethnenn comes from the síd unseen through the host, tells the wounded Cú Chulainn that he is his father, and heals him with herbs of the síd while he sleeps three days and nights.
While Cú Chulainn sleeps under Lugh's care, the boy-troop of Emain led by Conchobar's son Follomain attacks Medb's host three times and is slain to the last boy.

To avenge the boy-troop, Cú Chulainn in his ríastrad, the monstrous battle-distortion, drives his scythed chariot round the host of the four provinces in the Great Slaughter on the plain of Muirthemne.

events.summaryEn: In the royal palace of Cruachan in Connacht, Queen Medb and King Ailill lay in bed, and Ailill said it was true what they say, that a good man's wife is well off — she was better off now than before she married him.
events.summaryZh: 在康诺特的克鲁亨王宫里，女王梅芙和国王艾利尔躺在床上，艾利尔说：俗话说得好，嫁给了好男人的女人是好女人。

events.summaryEn: Medb asked her messenger Mac Roth whether there was a bull in Ireland to match the White-horned.
events.summaryZh: 梅芙叫来了信使马克·罗斯，问他是否知道爱尔兰哪里有一头能和白角公牛相比的公牛。

events.summaryEn: Medb mustered the men of Connacht, Leinster and Munster, and the Ulster exiles in Connacht led by Fergus mac Róich, once king of Ulster, who had left his homeland because of King Conchobar's treachery.
events.summaryZh: 梅芙召集了康诺特、伦斯特、芒斯特的大军，还有流亡在康诺特的阿尔斯特人，他们由弗格斯·马克·罗伊率领——弗格斯曾是阿尔斯特的国王，因为国王康胡巴尔背信弃义而离开了故乡。

events.summaryEn: The host set out.
events.summaryZh: 大军出发了。

events.summaryEn: Finding the host at the border, Cú Chulainn cut an oak sapling and, using only one hand, one foot and one eye, twisted it into a ring, cut an ogam inscription on it and set it round a standing stone as a warning: none must pass unless one of them made a ring the same way.
events.summaryZh: 库丘林在边界上发现了大军，他从一棵橡树上砍下一根树枝，只用一只手、一只脚、一只眼睛，把它弯成一个环，在上面刻上了欧甘文字，套在了一块立石上，作为警告：谁也不能越过这里，除非有人能用同样的方法——用一只手、一只脚、一只眼睛——做出一个同样的环。
events.titleEn: The withe and the forked branch

events.summaryEn: Ailill asked who this Ulsterman was.
events.summaryZh: 艾利尔问：这个阿尔斯特人是谁？

events.summaryEn: Cormac Cond Longas then told another tale.
events.summaryZh: 康诺特的科马克·孔德·隆加斯接着讲了另一件事。

events.summaryEn: Fiachu mac Fir Febe told a third tale.
events.summaryZh: 接着，菲亚胡·马克·菲尔费巴讲了第三件事。

events.summaryEn: Medb and Ailill now knew what enemy they faced.
events.summaryZh: 听完这些故事，梅芙和艾利尔明白了，他们面对的是一个可怕的敌人。

events.summaryEn: One day a young woman of great beauty in a many-coloured mantle came to Cú Chulainn, saying she was the daughter of King Búan and had come with her treasures and cattle because she loved him for his deeds.
events.summaryZh: 一天，一位美丽的年轻女子来到库丘林面前，她穿着各种颜色的衣服，容貌非常秀美。

events.summaryEn: After day after day of combat Cú Chulainn was covered with wounds and worn out.
events.summaryZh: 日复一日的战斗之后，库丘林遍体鳞伤，疲惫不堪。

events.summaryEn: While Cú Chulainn slept, the boy-troop of Emain — a hundred and fifty boys not yet under the curse of debility — heard that he guarded the border alone and came to help him, led by Follomain, son of King Conchobar, armed with their hurleys.
events.summaryZh: 就在库丘林沉睡的时候，艾温·马哈的少年队——一百五十个还没有受到衰弱诅咒的男孩——听说了库丘林独自守卫边界的事，决定前来帮助他。

events.summaryEn: Cú Chulainn resolved to avenge the boys.
events.summaryZh: 库丘林决心为少年们报仇。

versions.labelEn: Táin Bó Cúalnge, first half (Dunn 1914 translation, long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 《夺牛长征记》前半（邓恩 1914 年译本，长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 枕边的比较、白角公牛与褐色公牛、四省集结与女先知、阿尔斯特人的衰弱、橡枝环与叉枝、男孩的事迹、库兰的猎犬、拿起武器的那一天、浅滩上的决斗、莫莉甘、鲁格的医治、少年队之死、大屠杀
versions.rightsNote: 邓恩 1914 年英译属公共领域；本站发布按情节顺序的独立讲述。

sections.bodyEn: In the royal palace of Cruachan in Connacht, Queen Medb and King Ailill lay in bed, and Ailill said it was true what they say, that a good man's wife is well off — she was better off now than before she married him. Medb answered that she had been rich before: her father was High King of Ireland and she the most generous and noblest of his six daughters; she had married Ailill because he was without meanness, jealousy or fear, and her dowry was greater than his wealth. Neither would yield, so their possessions were brought out and counted: cups and vessels of gold and silver, finger-rings and bracelets, garments of purple, blue, black, green and yellow, flocks of sheep, horses, swine, and at last the herds of cattle. Everything was equal but one thing: in Ailill's herd was the great White-horned Bull, Finnbennach, born among Medb's cows but unwilling to be owned by a woman, which had gone over to Ailill's herd. Medb had no bull to match it, and her spirits fell as if she owned nothing at all.
sections.bodyZh: 在康诺特的克鲁亨王宫里，女王梅芙和国王艾利尔躺在床上，艾利尔说：俗话说得好，嫁给了好男人的女人是好女人。梅芙问他为什么这样说，艾利尔说：因为你嫁给我以后，比从前富裕多了。梅芙说：我在嫁给你之前就已经很富有了，我的父亲是爱尔兰的至高王，我是他六个女儿中最慷慨、最尊贵的一个。我嫁给你，是因为你没有吝啬、没有嫉妒、也没有畏惧；我带来的嫁妆比你的财产还多。两人争论不下，就叫人把他们的财产都拿出来比较：酒杯和金银器、指环和手镯、紫色、蓝色、黑色、绿色、黄色的衣服，羊群、马群、猪群，最后是牛群。每一样都一一点数，结果全都一样多，只有一样不同：艾利尔的牛群里有一头了不起的白角公牛芬本纳赫。它本来是在梅芙的牛群里出生的，可是它不愿意被一个女人拥有，就跑到了艾利尔的牛群里。梅芙的财产里没有一头能和它相比的公牛，她的心情一下子变得非常沮丧，好像她什么也没有了一样。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·枕边的比较。

sections.bodyEn: Medb asked her messenger Mac Roth whether there was a bull in Ireland to match the White-horned. He knew of a better and greater one, he said: the Brown Bull of Cúailnge, in the house of Dáire mac Fiachna in Ulster. Medb sent him to ask the loan of it for a year, promising fifty heifers in return and, if Dáire came himself, land on the plain equal to his own, a chariot worth twenty-one bondmaids, and her own friendship. Dáire was so delighted that he burst the seams of the flock-bed under him, and agreed. But at the feast that night one of the drunken messengers said it was as well Dáire had given the bull freely, for otherwise Medb and Ailill would have taken it by force. Dáire's steward told his master, who swore the bull would not leave unless taken by force. The messengers returned empty-handed, and Medb said there was no need to smooth the matter over: since it would not be given, it would be taken.
sections.bodyZh: 梅芙叫来了信使马克·罗斯，问他是否知道爱尔兰哪里有一头能和白角公牛相比的公牛。马克·罗斯说：我知道一头比它更好、更大的公牛，在阿尔斯特的库利地方，在达雷·马克·菲亚赫纳的家里，它叫库利的褐色公牛。梅芙说：你去找达雷，请他把这头牛借给我一年，一年以后我会把牛还给他，外加五十头小母牛作为租金；如果他自己愿意带着牛来，我会在平原上赐给他一块同样大小的土地，一辆价值二十一个女奴的马车，还有我自己的亲近和友谊。马克·罗斯带着九个信使来到达雷家里，达雷听了非常高兴，竟高兴得把身下的床垫都坐破了，立刻答应借牛。信使们受到了盛情款待，可是他们喝醉了酒，有一个信使在宴会上说：幸亏他自愿把牛借给我们，否则就算他不愿意，梅芙和艾利尔也会用武力把它抢走。达雷的管家听见了，告诉了主人。达雷大怒，发誓说：除非他们用武力来抢，否则这头牛绝不会离开这里。第二天，信使们空手回到了克鲁亨。梅芙说：用不着把好话弄平了，他们不愿意好好给，那就用武力去抢。

sections.bodyEn: Medb mustered the men of Connacht, Leinster and Munster, and the Ulster exiles in Connacht led by Fergus mac Róich, once king of Ulster, who had left his homeland because of King Conchobar's treachery. Before they set out from Cruachan, Medb met in her chariot a young woman sitting on the shaft of a chariot weaving a fringe with a gold weaver's staff, with three pupils in each eye. She was Fedelm, prophetess of Connacht, returned from learning the art in Alba. 'How do you see our host?' asked Medb. 'I see it crimson, I see it red.' That could not be, said Medb, for the Ulstermen were in their debility and none could bear arms. 'I see it crimson, I see it red,' Fedelm said again and again, and sang of a young warrior, not tall, whose body would be terribly transformed in battle, who alone would destroy their host, strewing the plain with their dead, so that many women would weep for their husbands. That warrior was Cú Chulainn.
sections.bodyZh: 梅芙召集了康诺特、伦斯特、芒斯特的大军，还有流亡在康诺特的阿尔斯特人，他们由弗格斯·马克·罗伊率领——弗格斯曾是阿尔斯特的国王，因为国王康胡巴尔背信弃义而离开了故乡。大军在克鲁亨集结，准备出发。出发前，梅芙乘着马车，遇见了一位年轻的女子，她坐在马车的车辕上，用一根金色的织针织着一条带子，她的每只眼睛里都有三个瞳孔。梅芙问她是谁，她说：我是康诺特的女先知费德尔姆，从阿尔巴学习预言回来。梅芙说：那你看看，我们的大军将会怎样？费德尔姆说：我看见它是深红色的，我看见它是血红色的。梅芙说：不可能，阿尔斯特人正在受苦，他们的男人都在衰弱之中，没有一个人能拿起武器。你再看看。费德尔姆又说：我看见它是深红色的，我看见它是血红色的。她连说了几遍，然后唱了一首诗，描述了一个年轻的勇士：他身材不高，可是在战场上他的身体会发生可怕的变化，他将独自摧毁你们的大军，你们的尸体会堆满平原，许多女人会为她们的丈夫哭泣。这个勇士，就是库丘林。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·女先知费德尔姆。

sections.bodyEn: The host set out. The men of Ulster were then under a strange weakness: whenever danger came, the grown men of Ulster fell into pains like a woman in childbirth and lay helpless for days, unable to bear arms — a curse laid on them long before by Macha, a woman whom the Ulstermen had wronged, as a separate tale tells; the Táin itself only states the debility. Only Cú Chulainn was free of it in all Ulster, and his father Sualtam; so the seventeen-year-old youth guarded the border alone in his chariot. Fergus guided the host but still loved his homeland, and led them astray, south and then north, to give the Ulstermen time to recover; when Medb reproached him, he said it was to avoid Cú Chulainn. On the march Medb saw that the three thousand Gailióin of Leinster outshone everyone, first to camp, to cook, to eat and to sleep; fearing they would take the glory, she wished to kill them, but at Fergus's urging she scattered them through the host so they could not band together.
sections.bodyZh: 大军出发了。这时阿尔斯特人正遭受着一种奇怪的衰弱：每当危难来临，阿尔斯特的成年男人就会像临产的妇女一样，在剧痛中倒下，一连几天不能动弹，无法拿起武器。另一篇故事《阿尔斯特人的衰弱》讲到，这是很久以前一个被阿尔斯特人逼迫的妇人马查留下的诅咒，《夺牛长征记》本身只说明了这种衰弱的存在。在全阿尔斯特，只有库丘林不受这种衰弱的影响，他的父亲苏阿尔塔姆也不受影响。于是，这个十七岁的少年独自一人，赶着马车，守卫在阿尔斯特的边界上。弗格斯为大军带路，可是他心里仍然爱着自己的故乡，他故意领着大军绕道，向南走，又向北走，好让阿尔斯特人有时间从衰弱中恢复过来。梅芙察觉了，责备他，弗格斯却说：我这样走是有原因的，为了躲开库丘林。行军途中，梅芙发现，来自伦斯特的盖勒奥因部队比其他人都要出色，他们扎营最快，做饭最快，吃饭睡觉都比别人早。梅芙担心他们会夺走全军的功劳，甚至想杀死他们。最后，在弗格斯的劝说下，她把这支三千人的队伍分散到了全军各处，让他们不能聚在一起。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·行军与阿尔斯特人的衰弱。

sections.bodyEn: Finding the host at the border, Cú Chulainn cut an oak sapling and, using only one hand, one foot and one eye, twisted it into a ring, cut an ogam inscription on it and set it round a standing stone as a warning: none must pass unless one of them made a ring the same way. Fergus read it and said that if they ignored it, Cú Chulainn would kill one of them before morning, so the host camped and went round. Next day, at a ford, Cú Chulainn cut a four-pronged fork with one stroke and with one hand drove it from his chariot deep into the riverbed; when four of Medb's scouts came, he cut off their heads and set one on each prong. Fergus declared that the fork had been thrust in with one hand from a chariot, and none might cross the ford until someone drew it out the same way. No one could, until Fergus himself, after breaking fourteen chariots, pulled it out with one hand.
sections.bodyZh: 库丘林在边界上发现了大军，他从一棵橡树上砍下一根树枝，只用一只手、一只脚、一只眼睛，把它弯成一个环，在上面刻上了欧甘文字，套在了一块立石上，作为警告：谁也不能越过这里，除非有人能用同样的方法——用一只手、一只脚、一只眼睛——做出一个同样的环。大军来到立石前，弗格斯读出了上面的文字，说：如果我们不遵守这个规矩，不管那个人在不在家里，他都会在天亮之前杀死我们中的一个人。于是大军停下来过夜，绕道而行。第二天，库丘林在一个浅滩上，用剑一下子砍下了一根有四个分叉的树枝，然后只用一只手，从马车上把树枝深深地插进了河床里。梅芙的四个先遣队员赶来，库丘林砍下了他们的头，把四颗头分别插在四个树杈上。大军来到浅滩，看见了这可怕的景象。弗格斯说：这根树枝是一只手从马车上插进去的，谁也不能越过这个浅滩，除非有人也用一只手从马车上把它拔出来。大军中没有人做得到，最后弗格斯亲自去拔，他弄坏了十四辆马车，才终于用一只手把树枝拔了出来。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·橡枝环与叉枝。
sections.headingEn: The withe and the forked branch

sections.bodyEn: Ailill asked who this Ulsterman was. 'My foster-son,' said Fergus, 'son of Conchobar's sister Deichtine: Cú Chulainn.' And he told of his boyhood. Called Sétanta, he lived in his mother's house on the plain of Muirthemne and heard of the boy-troop of Emain Macha, a hundred and fifty noble boys at play. His mother said he was too young — not yet five — and needed an Ulster champion to escort him; he would not wait, but set out with toy shield, toy javelin, hurley and ball, driving the ball ahead, throwing the hurley after it and the javelin after the hurley, and catching each before it fell. At Emain he ran onto the field without first asking the boys' protection, an insult by their rules. The hundred and fifty boys threw at him a hundred and fifty javelins, balls and hurleys, and he warded them all off; then for the first time his body was terribly distorted, and he rushed at them and laid fifty low. King Conchobar, playing chess nearby, caught him, learned the cause, and took him in under the boys' protection.
sections.bodyZh: 艾利尔问：这个阿尔斯特人是谁？弗格斯说：他是我的养子，是康胡巴尔的妹妹德赫特蕾的儿子，他的名字叫库丘林。接着，弗格斯讲起了库丘林少年时代的事迹。他说：那时他还叫塞坦塔，住在穆尔赫姆尼平原上他母亲的家里，听人们讲起阿尔斯特王宫艾温·马哈的少年队，一百五十个贵族家的男孩在那里一起游戏。他向母亲请求去那里，母亲说他太小了，还不到五岁，而且需要有阿尔斯特的勇士护送。他不肯等，带着他的玩具盾牌、玩具标枪、曲棍和球，独自上路了，一路上把球打出去，又把曲棍扔出去追上球，再把标枪扔出去追上曲棍，在它们落地前一一接住。他来到艾温·马哈，没有先请求少年们的保护，就冲进了他们的游戏场。按照规矩，这是对少年队的侮辱。一百五十个男孩向他扔来一百五十支标枪、一百五十个球、一百五十根曲棍，他全都挡住了。然后他的身体第一次发生了可怕的变化，他冲向他们，打倒了五十个男孩。康胡巴尔国王正在一旁下棋，他拉住了这个男孩，问清了缘由，从此接纳他，把他交给少年们保护。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·男孩的事迹·少年队。

sections.bodyEn: Cormac Cond Longas then told another tale. The smith Culann invited King Conchobar to a feast; passing the playing-field, the king invited Sétanta, who said he would finish his game and follow. At Culann's house, asked whether anyone else was coming, the king forgot the boy and said no, and Culann loosed his fierce hound, which needed three chains with three men on each to hold it. When the boy came, the hound sprang at him; he struck his ball down its throat, seized it by the hind legs and dashed it against a standing stone. The king's company rushed out expecting him dead and found him unharmed. Culann mourned his hound, guardian of his goods and herds; the boy promised to rear a whelp of the same breed and to be Culann's hound himself until it was grown. The druid Cathbad said he should be called Cú Chulainn, 'the hound of Culann'. He said he preferred his own name, Sétanta; but from then on he was called Cú Chulainn.
sections.bodyZh: 康诺特的科马克·孔德·隆加斯接着讲了另一件事。铁匠库兰邀请国王康胡巴尔去赴宴，国王路过游戏场，看见塞坦塔一个人打败了全部少年，就邀请他一起去。男孩说：我要把游戏玩完，然后再跟上来。国王到了库兰的家里，库兰问：还有人要来吗？国王忘了男孩的事，说：没有了。于是库兰放出了他的猛犬看守家门。这条猎犬凶猛无比，需要三条锁链、每条三个人才能拉住。男孩来到门前，猛犬张开大嘴扑向他。男孩扔掉了玩具，用球一击，把球打进了猎犬的喉咙，又抓住它的后腿，把它摔在一块立石上，摔得粉碎。国王和众人冲出来，以为男孩已经死了，却看见他好好地站着。库兰看着自己的猎犬，悲伤地说：你来我这里我很欢迎，可是你杀死了我的猎犬，它守护着我的家产和牲畜。男孩说：别难过，我会为你找一只同样血统的小狗，把它养大；在它长大之前，我自己做你的猎犬，守护你的家。德鲁伊卡斯巴德说：那你以后就叫库丘林吧，意思是“库兰的猎犬”。男孩说：我更喜欢我自己的名字塞坦塔。可是从此以后，人们都叫他库丘林了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·男孩的事迹·库兰的猎犬。

sections.bodyEn: Fiachu mac Fir Febe told a third tale. One day the druid Cathbad, teaching his pupils north-east of Emain, was asked what the day was good for, and said that the youth who took arms that day would have a name in Ireland for ever, but a short life. Cú Chulainn heard and went to Conchobar for weapons; he shattered set after set until the king gave him his own, and shook chariot after chariot to pieces until he was given the king's. He drove to the border against the three sons of Nechta Scéne, who had killed many Ulstermen, slew them and took their heads; on the way back he brought down wild swans alive with his sling and ran down a wild stag, tying them all to his chariot. He came back to Emain still in his battle-fury, and the people, fearing for the household, sent the women out to meet him; he turned his face away in shame, and they seized him and plunged him into three vats of cold water. The first burst its staves, the second boiled with great bubbles, and the third grew only warm, and his fury was calmed.
sections.bodyZh: 接着，菲亚胡·马克·菲尔费巴讲了第三件事。有一天，德鲁伊卡斯巴德在艾温·马哈的东北方教他的学生们，一个学生问：今天这个日子有什么吉凶？卡斯巴德说：今天拿起武器的少年，他的名字将在爱尔兰永远流传，他的事迹将被人们传颂，可是他的生命会很短暂。库丘林听见了，立刻去找康胡巴尔，要求得到武器。国王给了他武器，他一挥就把它们打碎了，一副接一副，最后国王把自己的武器给了他，那副武器才经受住了他的力量。他又要马车，把一辆接一辆的马车都摇散了，只有国王自己的马车承受得住。他驾着马车来到阿尔斯特的边界，去找涅赫塔·斯凯内的三个儿子，他们杀死了许多阿尔斯特人。库丘林杀死了这三兄弟，砍下了他们的头。回来的路上，他用投石器打下了几只活的野天鹅，又追上了一头野鹿，把它们都拴在马车上。他回到艾温·马哈时，战斗的狂暴还没有消退，人们害怕他会伤害王宫里的人，于是王宫里的女人们出来迎接他，他羞得把脸转了过去。人们趁机抓住他，把他浸进三个装着冷水的大桶里：第一个桶里的水沸腾起来，把桶都炸裂了；第二个桶里的水冒起了巨大的气泡；第三个桶里的水才变得温热。这时，他的狂暴终于平息了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·男孩的事迹·拿起武器。

sections.bodyEn: Medb and Ailill now knew what enemy they faced. Each night Cú Chulainn killed many of the host with his sling, and even killed the pet marten and pet bird on Medb's shoulders. Medb sent to parley, and he set terms: each day one champion should come to fight him at the ford; while the combat lasted the host might advance, but when the champion fell it must halt and camp until the next day. Medb thought it better to lose one man a day than a hundred a night. So champion after champion came. Handsome Fráech came first and fought him in the water; Cú Chulainn held him under until he drowned rather than yield, and when his people carried him off, women of the síd came keening and bore him into the fairy mound. Etarcomol, Nadcrantail and many others fell in turn. Fergus himself was sent; by their agreement Cú Chulainn gave way before him, and Fergus promised that one day he would give way before Cú Chulainn.
sections.bodyZh: 听完这些故事，梅芙和艾利尔明白了，他们面对的是一个可怕的敌人。库丘林每天夜里用投石器杀死大军中的许多人，连梅芙肩上的宠物貂和宠物鸟都被他用石子打死了。梅芙派人去和他谈判，库丘林提出了一个条件：每天派一个勇士到浅滩上和他单打独斗；在决斗进行的时候，大军可以向前行进，一旦那个勇士被杀死，大军就必须停下来扎营，直到第二天。梅芙觉得这个条件对自己有利：每天只损失一个人，总比每夜损失一百人好。于是，勇士们一个接一个地来到浅滩。年轻英俊的弗雷赫第一个来，他在水里和库丘林搏斗，库丘林把他按进水里，弗雷赫不肯认输，就这样淹死了，他的族人们把他抬走，仙丘里的女子们出来哀哭，把他带进了仙丘。接着来的是艾泰科莫尔、纳德克兰塔尔，以及许多别的勇士，都死在了库丘林的手下。弗格斯也被派去和他决斗，库丘林按照约定在弗格斯面前退了一步，弗格斯也承诺，将来有一天会在他面前退让一次。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·浅滩上的决斗。

sections.bodyEn: One day a young woman of great beauty in a many-coloured mantle came to Cú Chulainn, saying she was the daughter of King Búan and had come with her treasures and cattle because she loved him for his deeds. It was no time for a woman, he said; he was hungry and weary, fighting a host. Then she would help him, she said; he had not come for a woman's help, he answered. Then, she said, when he fought his enemies she would come against him: as an eel to coil round his feet, a grey she-wolf to drive the cattle on him, a hornless red heifer at the head of fifty heifers. He said he would break her ribs, her eye and her leg. She was the Morrígan, goddess of war. When he fought the champion Lóch, she came as eel, wolf and heifer, and he wounded her each time as he had said, and killed Lóch with the Gáe Bulga. Later, as an old woman milking a cow with three teats, she gave the parched hero milk, and with each draught he blessed her, and her three wounds were healed.
sections.bodyZh: 一天，一位美丽的年轻女子来到库丘林面前，她穿着各种颜色的衣服，容貌非常秀美。库丘林问她是谁，她说：我是国王布安的女儿，我听说了你的事迹，爱上了你，我带着我的财宝和牛群来找你。库丘林说：现在不是和女人亲近的好时候，我在这里饥饿疲惫，正在与大军苦战。女子说：那我会在你的战斗中帮助你。库丘林说：我来这里不是为了女人的帮助。女子说：既然如此，当你和敌人搏斗的时候，我就来和你作对。我会变成一条鳗鱼，缠住你的脚；变成一头灰色的母狼，把牛群赶向你；变成一头没有角的红色小母牛，带着五十头小母牛冲向你。库丘林说：我会打断你的肋骨，打瞎你的眼睛，打断你的腿。这个女子就是战争女神莫莉甘。后来，在库丘林与勇士罗赫决斗的时候，莫莉甘果然先后变成了鳗鱼、母狼和小母牛来攻击他，库丘林按照他说过的话，一一打伤了她。罗赫也被他用迦耶·博尔加杀死了。之后，莫莉甘变成一个老妇人，在路边挤一头有三个乳头的母牛的奶。库丘林又渴又累，向她要奶喝，每喝一口，就祝福她一次，她的三处伤也就痊愈了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·莫莉甘与罗赫之战。

sections.bodyEn: After day after day of combat Cú Chulainn was covered with wounds and worn out. At Lerga, seeing the host's fires flicker at dusk, he shook his weapons and raised his battle-cry in wrath and grief, and many in the camp died of terror. His charioteer Láeg saw a tall, handsome man coming from the north straight through the camp, unnoticed by anyone, in a green mantle with shield and spear. He told Cú Chulainn: 'I am your father from the síd, Lug mac Ethnenn. Sleep for three days and nights, and I will hold off the host.' Cú Chulainn lay down and slept deeply, while Lugh laid herbs of the síd on his wounds, and they healed one by one as he slept; for those three days and nights Lugh guarded the ford. This was the god of every skill who in the Second Battle of Mag Tuired slew Balor, come now as a father to guard his mortal son.
sections.bodyZh: 日复一日的战斗之后，库丘林遍体鳞伤，疲惫不堪。在莱尔加，他看见大军的营火在暮色中闪烁，心中充满了愤怒和悲哀，他挥舞着武器，发出了战斗的呐喊，营地里的许多人在惊恐中死去。他的车夫莱格看见一个高大英俊的人从北方走来，穿过大军的营地，没有一个人注意到他。他披着绿色的斗篷，手里拿着盾牌和长矛。那人走到库丘林面前，说：我是你的父亲，来自仙丘的鲁格·马克·埃特涅恩。你睡吧，睡三天三夜，我会替你抵挡大军。库丘林躺下，沉沉地睡去了。鲁格用仙丘里的草药敷在他的伤口上，为他治疗，在他睡着的时候，他的伤口一个接一个地愈合了。这三天三夜里，鲁格替他守卫着浅滩，大军无法前进。鲁格就是爱尔兰神话中那位无所不能的神，在《第二次马格图雷德之战》中曾杀死独眼巨人巴洛尔，现在他以父亲的身份，来守护他凡人的儿子。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·鲁格在莱尔加。

sections.bodyEn: While Cú Chulainn slept, the boy-troop of Emain — a hundred and fifty boys not yet under the curse of debility — heard that he guarded the border alone and came to help him, led by Follomain, son of King Conchobar, armed with their hurleys. They charged the host three times and each time killed three times their number, but they were only boys and too few, and they all fell; Follomain swore he would not return to Emain without Ailill's golden diadem, and he too was slain. On the third day Cú Chulainn woke, stretched and felt as strong as if he were going to an assembly, a feast or a great festival. He asked how long he had slept — three days and nights, said Lugh — and what had happened; told that the boy-troop had come and been slain, he grieved: 'Pity that I was not in my strength; had I been, the boys would not have fallen.'
sections.bodyZh: 就在库丘林沉睡的时候，艾温·马哈的少年队——一百五十个还没有受到衰弱诅咒的男孩——听说了库丘林独自守卫边界的事，决定前来帮助他。他们由国王康胡巴尔的儿子福洛曼率领，手持他们的游戏用的曲棍，向梅芙的大军发起了进攻。他们向大军冲了三次，每次都杀死了三倍于自己人数的敌人，可是他们毕竟只是孩子，人数太少，最后全部战死了，只有福洛曼一个人还在战斗。福洛曼发誓，除非带着艾利尔的金冠，否则绝不回到艾温·马哈。他也被杀死了。库丘林在第三天醒来，伸了伸身子，觉得精力充沛，像要去参加集会、宴会或者盛大的节日一样。他问父亲鲁格：我睡了多久？鲁格说：三天三夜。库丘林又问发生了什么事，鲁格告诉了他：少年队来了，与大军交战，全部战死了。库丘林听了，悲痛万分，说：真可惜，我当时没有力气，如果我有力气，少年们就不会死了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·少年队之死。

sections.bodyEn: Cú Chulainn resolved to avenge the boys. He had Láeg harness the scythed chariot, bristling with hooks, spikes and blades, and then his body underwent the terrible distortion called the ríastrad. He trembled like a reed in a flood; every muscle and joint twisted; his feet and knees turned backward and his heels and calves to the front; one eye sank deep into his head and the other bulged out on his cheek; his mouth stretched to his ears so that his throat could be seen; his hair stood up like a hawthorn thicket with a drop of blood on each point; from the crown of his head rose a jet of dark blood thick as a ship's mast, and the hero's light shone from his brow. In the scythed chariot he drove round and round the host of the four provinces, the iron wheels cutting deep ruts and the blades mowing down men in swathes; those who fell were beyond counting — the Great Slaughter on the plain of Muirthemne. Next day he showed himself in his own fair form and fine clothes, and the women of Medb's host climbed on the men's shoulders to see him.
sections.bodyZh: 库丘林决心为少年们报仇。他让车夫莱格备好那辆装着镰刀的战车，车上满是铁钩、尖刺和利刃，然后他的身体发生了可怕的变形——书中把它叫作“扭曲”。他的全身像风暴中的芦苇一样颤抖，每一块肌肉、每一个关节都在扭动，他的脚和膝盖转到了后面，脚跟和小腿转到了前面；一只眼睛深深地陷进头里，另一只眼睛凸出在脸颊上；他的嘴巴张大到耳根，能看见他的喉咙；他的头发像山楂树的荆棘一样根根竖起，每根头发的尖上都有一滴血；从他的头顶上升起一道像船桅一样粗的黑血柱，又像一团黑雾笼罩着他，他的额头上闪耀着英雄的光芒。他驾着镰刀战车，冲进了四省大军之中，绕着大军转了一圈又一圈，战车的铁轮在地上压出了深深的车辙，镰刀和利刃把敌人成片地砍倒。书中说，那天死在他手下的人多得数不清，这就是“穆尔赫姆尼平原大屠杀”。第二天，库丘林恢复了原来的样子，穿上了华丽的衣服，在妇女和诗人面前展示他的英俊，梅芙大军中的女人们都爬到男人们的肩上去看他。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·穆尔赫姆尼平原大屠杀。

stories.canonicalTitle: The Cattle Raid of Cooley, Part 2: Fer Diad and the battle of the bulls
stories.editorialNote: 依据邓恩 1914 年英译莱因斯特书本《夺牛长征记》后半，按情节顺序讲述；梅芙撤退时的身体细节和大战中众多勇士的名录只作概述。

series.labelEn: Part 2: Fer Diad and the bulls
series.labelZh: 下部 · 费迪亚德与公牛之战

stories.summaryEn: With her daughter, her treasures and the threat of poets' satire, Medb forces Cú Chulainn's foster-brother Fer Diad to fight him. The two friends who learned arms together under Scáthach fight four days at the ford, sending each other herbs and food each night; on the fourth day Cú Chulainn kills Fer Diad with the dreadful Gáe Bulga and weeps over him. His father Sualtam's cry at Emain Macha rouses the Ulstermen from their debility. In the great battle at Gárech, Fergus keeps his promise and yields to Cú Chulainn, the host of the four provinces breaks, and Cú Chulainn spares Medb's life. But the Brown Bull has been driven to Connacht; through a whole night it fights the White-horned across Ireland, tears it to pieces, returns home, and dies when its heart breaks.
stories.summaryZh: 梅芙用女儿、财宝和诗人的讽刺逼迫库丘林的结拜兄弟费迪亚德出战。两个曾在斯卡塔赫门下一同学艺的朋友在浅滩上苦战四天，白天拼杀，夜里互赠草药和食物；第四天，库丘林用可怕的迦耶·博尔加杀死了费迪亚德，抱着他的尸体痛哭。库丘林的父亲苏阿尔塔姆到艾温·马哈呼喊求援，阿尔斯特人终于从衰弱中醒来。在加雷赫的大战中，弗格斯遵守诺言在库丘林面前退让，四省大军溃散，库丘林饶了梅芙的性命。可是褐色公牛已经被带到了康诺特，它与白角公牛在一整夜里跑遍了爱尔兰，把对手撕成碎片，最后回到故乡，心碎而死。
stories.titleZh: 夺牛长征记 · 下部 费迪亚德与公牛之战

claims.statement: Medb forces Fer Diad, Cú Chulainn's foster-brother and fellow pupil of Scáthach, to fight him by threatening him with poets' satire and promising her daughter Finnabair, land and freedom from tribute.

On the first day at the ford Fer Diad and Cú Chulainn fight with casting-weapons from morning to evening, then embrace, and that night share healing herbs and food, their horses in one paddock and their charioteers at one fire.

On the second day Cú Chulainn and Fer Diad fight with heavy spears from their chariots and still exchange courtesies at night; on the third, with heavy swords, after which they part without embracing.
On the fourth day at the ford, as Fer Diad's sword pierces him, Cú Chulainn calls for the Gáe Bulga, casts it from between his toes through Fer Diad's iron and stone, and Fer Diad dies in his arms.
Cú Chulainn carries the dead Fer Diad across the ford to the northern bank, faints beside him, and laments that all fighting before had been play and pleasure until he met Fer Diad.

When Sualtam, beheaded by the rim of his own shield as his horse wheels, still cries from the shield that Ulster's men are slain, women carried off and cattle driven, Conchobar swears to restore them all and the Ulstermen rise from their debility.
As the risen Ulstermen march on the plain of Gárech, Mac Roth describes each approaching company to Medb and Ailill, and the exiled Fergus names their leaders.

In the battle of Gárech Fergus strikes Conchobar's shield with Caladbolg until a warrior (in some versions Cormac Cond Longas) persuades him to turn his wrath on the hills, and he strikes the tops from three hills, the three Maela of Meath.

Hearing Caladbolg strike Conchobar's shield, Cú Chulainn bursts his bonds and calls on Fergus to keep his promise; Fergus retreats three steps, and his exiles and the men of Leinster and Munster leave the field.
With the host routed and the Brown Bull sent ahead to Connacht, Cú Chulainn finds Medb on her retreat, spares her because he will not kill a woman, and guards her until the host crosses Áth Luain.

Brought to Connacht, the Brown Bull of Cúailnge fights the White-horned Bull Finnbennach through a whole night across Ireland, trampling the judge Bricriu, and is seen at dawn with Finnbennach's remains on its horns.

Scattering Finnbennach's remains across Ireland, giving names to places such as Áth Luain, the Brown Bull returns to Cúailnge and dies on Druim Tairb when its heart breaks, and peace is made for seven years.

events.summaryEn: As champion after champion fell, Medb and Ailill agreed that only Fer Diad could overcome Cú Chulainn: his foster-brother, who had learned arms with him under the woman-warrior Scáthach in Alba, equal to him in every feat except the Gáe Bulga, which only Cú Chulainn had learned; and Fer Diad had a skin of horn that no weapon could pierce.
events.summaryZh: 勇士们一个接一个死在浅滩上，梅芙和艾利尔商量：派谁去才能打败库丘林？

events.summaryEn: At dawn Fer Diad waited on the north side of the ford and Cú Chulainn came to the south.
events.summaryZh: 第二天清晨，费迪亚德来到浅滩，在浅滩北岸等候，库丘林从南岸来了。

events.summaryEn: On the second day Cú Chulainn chose broad heavy spears, fighting from their chariots so that they might come to a decision sooner, and from morning to evening they pierced each other until birds could have flown in and out of their wounds.
events.summaryZh: 第二天，轮到库丘林选择兵器，他说：今天我们用宽刃的重矛吧，坐在战车上作战，离得更近一些，好让我们早点分出胜负。

events.summaryEn: On the fourth morning Fer Diad, knowing this day would decide everything, put on his strongest armour and bound a great flat stone over his belly against the Gáe Bulga.
events.summaryZh: 第四天清晨，费迪亚德知道这一天将决定一切，他穿上了最坚固的战甲，在腹部绑上一块大石头，以防备那可怕的迦耶·博尔加。

events.summaryEn: Cú Chulainn lifted Fer Diad and carried him with his arms and armour across the ford to the north side; then he fainted beside him.
events.summaryZh: 库丘林抱起费迪亚德，带着他的武器和铠甲，把他抬过浅滩，放在北岸。

events.summaryEn: Cú Chulainn's father Sualtam came to his wounded son, who sent him to Emain Macha to rouse the Ulstermen: their men were being slain, their women carried off, their cattle driven away.
events.summaryZh: 库丘林的父亲苏阿尔塔姆听说儿子伤重，赶来看他。

events.summaryEn: Conchobar sent messengers to summon the champions of Ulster, and from north and south, east and west the Ulstermen rose from their weakness, took up arms and gathered to the king at Slemain, then marched to the plain of Gárech where Medb's host lay.
events.summaryZh: 康胡巴尔派出使者，召集阿尔斯特各地的勇士们。

events.summaryEn: The battle of Gárech and Irgárech began.
events.summaryZh: 加雷赫和伊尔加雷赫的大战开始了。

events.summaryEn: Cú Chulainn heard the groan and asked who dared strike the shield of his foster-father Conchobar; it was Fergus, he was told.
events.summaryZh: 库丘林听见了盾牌的呻吟声，问：是谁敢砍我的养父康胡巴尔的盾牌？

events.summaryEn: By evening Medb's host was routed, a remnant guarding her retreat westward.
events.summaryZh: 到了傍晚，梅芙的大军已经溃不成军，只剩下一些残兵护送着她向西撤退。

events.summaryEn: Driven into Connacht, the Brown Bull saw the fair strange land and bellowed three times.
events.summaryZh: 褐色公牛被赶到了康诺特，它看见了一片陌生的、美丽的土地，发出了三声震耳欲聋的吼叫。

events.summaryEn: The Brown Bull ran east with the White-horned's remains, scattering its limbs across Ireland: at the ford of Athlone it dropped the loins, so the place was called Áth Luain, 'ford of the loins', and at Trim the liver, and other parts elsewhere, each place taking its name from them.
events.summaryZh: 褐色公牛带着白角公牛的残骸一路向东奔跑，把对手的肢体一块块抛撒在爱尔兰各地。
events.titleEn: The death of the Brown Bull

versions.labelEn: Táin Bó Cúalnge, second half (Dunn 1914 translation, long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 《夺牛长征记》后半（邓恩 1914 年译本，长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 梅芙说服费迪亚德、第一天的投枪、第二天的长矛、第三天的重剑、第四天的浅滩与迦耶·博尔加、库丘林的哀歌、苏阿尔塔姆的呼喊、阿尔斯特人觉醒、加雷赫之战与弗格斯的三座山丘、弗格斯退兵、梅芙被饶、两头公牛的决斗、褐色公牛之死
versions.rightsNote: 邓恩 1914 年英译属公共领域；本站发布按情节顺序的独立讲述。

sections.bodyEn: As champion after champion fell, Medb and Ailill agreed that only Fer Diad could overcome Cú Chulainn: his foster-brother, who had learned arms with him under the woman-warrior Scáthach in Alba, equal to him in every feat except the Gáe Bulga, which only Cú Chulainn had learned; and Fer Diad had a skin of horn that no weapon could pierce. He refused to fight his brother, so Medb sent druids, satirists and spell-makers to threaten him with satire that would raise three blisters on his face — shame, blemish and disgrace — so that he would lose his honour before he died. For his honour's sake he came. Medb feasted him, and when he was drunk promised him a chariot worth four times seven bondmaids, equipment for twelve men, land on the plain, freedom from tribute for him and his descendants, her daughter Finnabair as wife, and her own friendship. He demanded six sureties for these, and she gave them, and next day he agreed to fight. Fergus heard and went to warn Cú Chulainn.
sections.bodyZh: 勇士们一个接一个死在浅滩上，梅芙和艾利尔商量：派谁去才能打败库丘林？他们一致认为，只有费迪亚德能做到。费迪亚德是库丘林的结拜兄弟，两人曾一起在阿尔巴的女武士斯卡塔赫门下学习武艺，他们的本领几乎一样，只是库丘林学会了迦耶·博尔加的用法，费迪亚德没有学；而费迪亚德有一身像角一样坚硬的皮肤，任何刀剑都刺不穿。可是费迪亚德不肯和自己的兄弟作战，拒绝了梅芙的使者。梅芙就派去了德鲁伊、讽刺诗人和咒术师，威胁他说，如果他不来，他们就要用讽刺诗羞辱他，让他的脸上长满三个水泡：耻辱、污点和羞愧，让他在死前就失去名誉。费迪亚德为了自己的名誉，只好来了。梅芙热情地款待他，等他喝醉了，许诺给他：一辆价值四个七个女奴的马车，十二个人的武装，从平原上分给他一块土地，免除他和他子孙的一切赋税，还把她的女儿芬达维尔嫁给他，外加她自己的友谊。费迪亚德要求六位担保人立誓保证这些承诺，梅芙一一满足了。第二天，他答应出战。弗格斯听说了，赶去警告库丘林。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·说服费迪亚德。

sections.bodyEn: At dawn Fer Diad waited on the north side of the ford and Cú Chulainn came to the south. Fer Diad taunted him that at Scáthach's he had been only his servant, readying his weapons and his bed; Cú Chulainn answered that he had been young then, but now there was no warrior he could not overcome, and reproached Fer Diad for coming against his foster-brother, with whom he had shared training, dangers and a bed, for a woman's sake. At last they fought. Cú Chulainn gave Fer Diad the choice of weapons, and he chose casting-weapons: shields with rims, eight darts, eight ivory-hilted swords and eight spears, which flew between them like bees on a fine day from morning till noon, every one striking a shield and none wounding; from noon to evening they cast polished javelins, and both were wounded. At nightfall they went to each other, embraced and kissed three times. That night their horses grazed in one paddock and their charioteers warmed themselves at one fire; Cú Chulainn sent Fer Diad half of every healing herb the Ulster physicians brought him, and Fer Diad sent Cú Chulainn half of the food and drink Medb sent.
sections.bodyZh: 第二天清晨，费迪亚德来到浅滩，在浅滩北岸等候，库丘林从南岸来了。两人隔着河水对望，费迪亚德说：你怎么敢来和我决斗？当年我们在斯卡塔赫那里，你不过是我的侍从，给我准备武器和床铺。库丘林说：那时我年纪小，确实是你的侍从，可是今天，世上没有一个勇士是我打不过的。我们曾经一同学艺，一同出生入死，同睡一张床，是心心相印的兄弟，你不该为了一个女人来和我作对。两人争论了很久，终于决定开战。库丘林让费迪亚德先选武器，费迪亚德说：我们先用投掷的兵器吧。他们拿起了八面有边的盾牌、八支标枪、八把象牙柄的短剑和八支短矛，像蜜蜂在晴天里飞来飞去一样，把兵器向对方投去，从清晨一直投到中午，没有一件兵器没有击中对方的盾牌，可是谁也没有伤到谁。中午，他们又换上了磨光的轻矛，一直投到黄昏，两人都受了伤，流了血。天黑了，他们停战，走到对方身边，互相拥抱，亲吻了三次。那一夜，他们的马在同一片草地上吃草，他们的车夫在同一堆火边取暖。库丘林把阿尔斯特的医生用的草药分一半送给费迪亚德，费迪亚德把梅芙送来的美食和酒分一半送给库丘林。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·费迪亚德之战·第一天。

sections.bodyEn: On the second day Cú Chulainn chose broad heavy spears, fighting from their chariots so that they might come to a decision sooner, and from morning to evening they pierced each other until birds could have flown in and out of their wounds. At nightfall they embraced and kissed three times as before, their horses grazed together and their charioteers shared a fire, and they exchanged herbs and food. On the third morning Fer Diad's face was gloomy and changed; Cú Chulainn told him he looked like a man come to his death, and Fer Diad said Medb had dragged him into the fight and one of them must fall that day. He chose heavy, hard-smiting swords, and from morning till evening they hewed great pieces of flesh from each other's shoulders and thighs. That night they parted without embracing; their horses did not graze together nor their charioteers share a fire. Both knew the next day would be the last.
sections.bodyZh: 第二天，轮到库丘林选择兵器，他说：今天我们用宽刃的重矛吧，坐在战车上作战，离得更近一些，好让我们早点分出胜负。他们驾着战车，从清晨战到黄昏，用重矛互相刺击，两人的身上都布满了伤口，鸟儿可以从他们的伤口里飞进飞出。天黑后，他们又像前一天一样，互相拥抱，亲吻了三次，把马放在一起吃草，把车夫留在同一堆火边，库丘林又把草药送给费迪亚德，费迪亚德又把食物和酒送给库丘林。第三天清晨，库丘林看见费迪亚德走来，觉得他的脸色阴沉，和往日不同。库丘林说：你今天脸色这么难看，费迪亚德，你是来送死的。费迪亚德说：我被梅芙拖进了这场决斗，我知道，我们两人之中，今天必有一个要倒下。这一天，费迪亚德选择了沉重的、能劈开一切的大剑，两人从清晨砍杀到黄昏，从肩膀到大腿砍下了一块块的血肉。天黑后，他们分开了，可是这一夜，两人没有再拥抱，他们的马不再在一起吃草，他们的车夫也不再在同一堆火边取暖。两个朋友心里都明白，明天将是最后一天。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·费迪亚德之战·第二、三天。

sections.bodyEn: On the fourth morning Fer Diad, knowing this day would decide everything, put on his strongest armour and bound a great flat stone over his belly against the Gáe Bulga. Cú Chulainn asked what weapons they would use; 'Your choice,' said Fer Diad, and Cú Chulainn chose the feat of the ford, at which Fer Diad's heart sank, for Cú Chulainn had never been beaten at a ford. Fighting in the water, Cú Chulainn leapt again and again onto the rim of Fer Diad's shield to strike at his head, and each time Fer Diad shook him off into the ford. Then Cú Chulainn's distortion came on him and he swelled like a giant, while Fer Diad's sword pierced his breast and his blood reddened the stream. 'The Gáe Bulga!' he called to Láeg, who sent it down the stream; Cú Chulainn caught it between his toes and cast it at Fer Diad. It went through the iron and the stone, and inside him its thirty barbs opened and filled his body. Fer Diad fell, saying it was unfairly done and his death was Cú Chulainn's doing, and died in his arms.
sections.bodyZh: 第四天清晨，费迪亚德知道这一天将决定一切，他穿上了最坚固的战甲，在腹部绑上一块大石头，以防备那可怕的迦耶·博尔加。库丘林说：今天我们用什么兵器？费迪亚德说：由你来选。库丘林说：那就用“浅滩的技艺”吧。费迪亚德听了，心中一沉，他知道库丘林在浅滩上从未被打败过。两人在浅滩中激战，库丘林几次跳上费迪亚德的盾牌边缘，想从上面刺他的头，都被费迪亚德用盾牌震落到水里。库丘林的身体开始发生可怕的变形，他像一个巨人一样高大起来，费迪亚德的剑刺进了他的胸膛，鲜血染红了河水。这时，库丘林向他的车夫莱格喊道：把迦耶·博尔加给我！莱格把那支矛顺着河水推了过去，库丘林用脚趾夹住，向费迪亚德掷去。那支矛刺穿了费迪亚德的铁甲和石头，进入他的身体后，矛头上的三十个倒钩张开，充满了他的全身。费迪亚德倒了下去，说：你用得不公平，我的死是你造成的。他倒在库丘林的怀里，死去了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·费迪亚德之战·第四天。

sections.bodyEn: Cú Chulainn lifted Fer Diad and carried him with his arms and armour across the ford to the north side; then he fainted beside him. Láeg roused him: the host of Connacht was coming, and this was no time to lie down. Why should he rise, said Cú Chulainn, when he had killed this man with his own hand? Looking on Fer Diad's face, he sang his lament: all was play and pleasure until he met Fer Diad; they had learned together at Scáthach's side and sworn never to be enemies; every fight before had been a game, and now Fer Diad had fallen and his heart was like a broken stone. Again and again he called his name, recalling their days in Alba. At last he had Láeg cut the Gáe Bulga out of the body, for he could not be without his weapon, and looking on his brother's blood he said he would remember him to the day of doom. From then he was so badly wounded that for days he could not stand.
sections.bodyZh: 库丘林抱起费迪亚德，带着他的武器和铠甲，把他抬过浅滩，放在北岸。然后，库丘林倒在他的身边，昏了过去。莱格喊醒他，说：快起来，库丘林，康诺特的大军要来了，现在不是躺着的时候。库丘林说：我为什么要起来？我亲手杀死了他。他看着费迪亚德的脸，唱起了哀歌：那是游戏，那是欢乐，直到我遇见了费迪亚德；我们一起学艺，一起在斯卡塔赫的身边，我们发誓永远不互相为敌。他说：在我遇见费迪亚德之前，所有的战斗都只是游戏，如今他倒下了，我的心也像一块破碎的石头。他回忆起两人在阿尔巴的日子，回忆起斯卡塔赫的教导，回忆起他们并肩作战的往事，一遍又一遍地呼唤着他的名字。最后，他对莱格说：剖开费迪亚德的身体，把迦耶·博尔加取出来吧，我不能没有我的武器。莱格取出了那支矛，库丘林看着满身鲜血的兄弟，说：直到最后的审判之日，我也会记着你。从这一刻起，库丘林自己也伤重得无法站立，有好些天，他只能躺在那里养伤。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·哀悼费迪亚德。

sections.bodyEn: Cú Chulainn's father Sualtam came to his wounded son, who sent him to Emain Macha to rouse the Ulstermen: their men were being slain, their women carried off, their cattle driven away. Sualtam rode Cú Chulainn's Grey of Macha to Emain and cried it aloud, but the Ulstermen lay in their debility and none answered, for by Ulster's custom no one might speak before the king, and the king not before the druids. After his third cry the druid Cathbad asked who was killing and plundering; Sualtam repeated it, was ignored, and turned his horse in anger to leave. As the horse wheeled, the sharp rim of his own shield cut off his head, which fell into the shield; the horse carried the body back into the palace, and the head in the shield still cried the same words. 'That cry is too loud,' said King Conchobar: 'the sky is above us, the earth beneath us, the sea around us; unless the sky falls with its stars, or the sea overwhelms the earth, I will bring every cow back to its byre and every woman to her home.' The Ulstermen rose from their debility.
sections.bodyZh: 库丘林的父亲苏阿尔塔姆听说儿子伤重，赶来看他。库丘林对父亲说：你到艾温·马哈去，告诉阿尔斯特人起来作战，我已经无力再守护他们了，他们的牛群被抢走了，他们的妇女被掳走了。苏阿尔塔姆骑上库丘林的灰马，飞驰到艾温·马哈，高声呼喊：阿尔斯特的男人们被杀了，女人们被掳走了，牛群被赶走了！可是阿尔斯特人还在衰弱中，没有人回答他。按照阿尔斯特的规矩，在国王开口之前，谁也不能说话，而国王只能在德鲁伊们开口之后说话。他喊了三次，德鲁伊卡斯巴德终于说：是谁在这里杀人、抢劫、掳掠？苏阿尔塔姆又重复了一遍，没有人理睬他，他愤怒地掉转马头要离开。马猛地一转身，苏阿尔塔姆自己的盾牌的锋利边缘竟割断了他的脖子，他的头落进了盾牌里。灰马驮着他的尸体又回到了王宫，盾牌里的头仍在喊着同样的话：阿尔斯特的男人们被杀了，女人们被掳走了，牛群被赶走了！国王康胡巴尔说：这喊声太响了，天还在上面，大地还在下面，大海还在四周，除非天塌下来，海水淹没大地，我一定会把每一头牛送回它的牛棚，把每一个女人送回她的家。阿尔斯特人终于从衰弱中醒来了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·苏阿尔塔姆的呼喊。

sections.bodyEn: Conchobar sent messengers to summon the champions of Ulster, and from north and south, east and west the Ulstermen rose from their weakness, took up arms and gathered to the king at Slemain, then marched to the plain of Gárech where Medb's host lay. Medb's messenger Mac Roth went to look and saw them come: troop after troop descending the hills; a mist on the plain lit by sparks like stars, which were the warriors' eyes; thunder, which was the chariot wheels; a great wind, which was the breath of heroes. He described each company — purple cloaks with golden brooches, golden hair, shields rimmed with silver — and the exiled Fergus beside Medb named each leader: this is King Conchobar himself, this his son, this such a hero, each a mighty warrior. Medb and Ailill grew more and more uneasy. 'Today,' said Fergus, 'the Ulstermen will show you what they are.'
sections.bodyZh: 康胡巴尔派出使者，召集阿尔斯特各地的勇士们。从北到南，从东到西，阿尔斯特人纷纷从衰弱中站起来，拿起武器，向国王身边集结。他们在斯兰内会合，然后向梅芙大军所在的加雷赫平原进发。梅芙的信使马克·罗斯被派去察看敌情，他站在高处，看见了阿尔斯特人的大军：一队又一队勇士从山丘上走下来，平原上升起了浓雾，雾中闪着光亮，像天上的星星，那是勇士们的眼睛；雷声隆隆，那是战车的车轮；还有一阵狂风，那是勇士们的呼吸。马克·罗斯一队一队地描述来者的模样：有的勇士披着紫色的斗篷，佩着金色的胸针，有的头发金黄，有的盾牌上镶着白银。流亡的弗格斯站在梅芙身边，听马克·罗斯描述一队，就说出那一队的首领是谁：这是康胡巴尔国王本人，这是他的儿子，这是某某英雄，他们个个都是勇猛无比的战士。梅芙和艾利尔听着，心中越来越不安。弗格斯说：今天，阿尔斯特人会让你们明白，他们是什么样的人。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·阿尔斯特集结。

sections.bodyEn: The battle of Gárech and Irgárech began. Three times Medb's host broke through the Ulster lines into their rear. Fergus, wielding his sword Caladbolg, which when raised was like a rainbow, hewed through the Ulstermen seeking King Conchobar, and when he found him struck his shield so that it groaned aloud, and all the shields of Ulster groaned with it. Then a warrior seized his arm — the versions differ on who, some naming Conchobar's son Cormac Cond Longas — saying: let him not strike his king nor destroy his people, but turn his wrath elsewhere — strike the hills. Fergus turned and with Caladbolg struck off the tops of three hills, which stand to this day as the three Maela of Meath, the three bald hills. And at that moment Cú Chulainn, lying wounded, heard the groan of Conchobar's shield under Caladbolg's stroke.
sections.bodyZh: 加雷赫和伊尔加雷赫的大战开始了。两军相遇，喊杀声震天。梅芙的大军三次冲破阿尔斯特人的阵线，每一次都杀到了阿尔斯特人的后方。弗格斯手握他的宝剑卡拉德博尔格——这把剑举起来像一道彩虹——在阿尔斯特人中间左右砍杀，他要找到国王康胡巴尔。弗格斯找到了康胡巴尔，用卡拉德博尔格砍向他的盾牌，盾牌发出了巨大的呻吟声。全阿尔斯特人的盾牌都跟着呻吟起来。这时，有一位勇士赶来抓住了弗格斯的手臂——各个本子里此人的名字说法不一，有的说是康胡巴尔的儿子科马克·孔德·隆加斯——对他说：不要砍你的国王，不要毁灭你的族人，你的愤怒应该发泄在别处。把你的剑转向山丘吧，砍向那些山顶，这样你就不会杀死你的同胞。弗格斯听从了他的劝告，转过身去，举起卡拉德博尔格，向三座山丘砍去，削平了三座山头。直到今天，米斯平原上还有三座被削平山顶的小山，人们称它们为“米斯的三座秃丘”。就在这时，躺在床上养伤的库丘林听见了卡拉德博尔格砍击康胡巴尔盾牌的呻吟声。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·加雷赫之战。

sections.bodyEn: Cú Chulainn heard the groan and asked who dared strike the shield of his foster-father Conchobar; it was Fergus, he was told. He was so badly wounded that the Ulstermen had bound him to his bed with hoops and stakes lest his wounds open; but he burst every bond, the hoops and stakes flew off and his wounds broke open. He sprang into his chariot, found Fergus and told him to turn back or suffer for it. Who spoke so proudly? asked Fergus. His foster-son Cú Chulainn, who had his promise to give way before him one day — and this was the day. 'I promised it,' said Fergus, and turned and went back three great steps. As he withdrew, the Ulster exiles under him withdrew too, and the men of Leinster and Munster, seeing Fergus go, left the field, so that only Medb and Ailill with the men of Connacht and their sons remained. At midday Cú Chulainn came into the battle.
sections.bodyZh: 库丘林听见了盾牌的呻吟声，问：是谁敢砍我的养父康胡巴尔的盾牌？人们告诉他，那是弗格斯。库丘林伤得很重，阿尔斯特人用铁箍和木桩把他固定在床上，免得他的伤口裂开。可是他一听到这个声音，就猛地挣脱了所有的束缚，那些铁箍和柱子都被崩飞了，他的伤口也全部裂开，鲜血涌了出来。他跳上战车，冲向战场，找到了弗格斯，对他说：转过身来，弗格斯，否则你会后悔的。弗格斯问：是谁这么傲慢地对我说话？库丘林说：是你的养子库丘林，你答应过我，有一天会在我面前退让，现在就是那一天。弗格斯说：我确实答应过。他转过身去，向后退了三大步。他一退，他所率领的阿尔斯特流亡者也跟着撤退了；伦斯特人和芒斯特人看见弗格斯撤退，也跟着撤离了战场，只剩下梅芙和艾利尔率领的康诺特人，还有他们的子孙们。正午时分，库丘林冲进了战场。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·弗格斯退让。

sections.bodyEn: By evening Medb's host was routed, a remnant guarding her retreat westward. She had sent the Brown Bull ahead by a short way to Connacht with a company of men — she had the bull at least. On the way back Medb had to stop and step aside, and there Cú Chulainn came upon her. She asked his protection and his mercy. He said it would be no more than her due if he killed her from behind; but he did not, for he would not kill a woman. He let her go and guarded her retreat until the host of Connacht had crossed the ford at Áth Luain into their own land. Looking on the routed army, Fergus said to Medb that it was a shameful day for them all, but it was usual for a herd led by a mare to stray and be destroyed — meaning the disaster came from her leadership. Behind the retreating host, Cú Chulainn struck the tops from three hills with his sword in answer to Fergus's three hills.
sections.bodyZh: 到了傍晚，梅芙的大军已经溃不成军，只剩下一些残兵护送着她向西撤退。梅芙把褐色公牛交给了一队人，让他们抄近路赶回康诺特，无论如何，她终于得到了那头牛。在撤退的路上，梅芙不得不停下来，躲到一旁，正在这时，库丘林找到了她。梅芙对他说：我请求你的保护，饶了我吧。库丘林说：如果我在你背后杀死你，那也是你应得的。可是他没有下手，因为他不杀女人。他让梅芙离开，保护着她撤退，直到康诺特的大军全部越过了阿特隆的浅滩，回到了自己的国土上。弗格斯看着溃败的大军，对梅芙说：今天我们这些人遭遇的事，真是一场羞辱。可是一群由母马领头的马队，走错了路、被毁掉了，这本来就是常有的事。他的意思是，这场灾难都是因为梅芙的领导。库丘林在撤退的大军后面，用他的剑砍断了三座山丘的山顶，作为对弗格斯的那三座山丘的回应。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·梅芙被饶。

sections.bodyEn: Driven into Connacht, the Brown Bull saw the fair strange land and bellowed three times. Ailill's White-horned Bull, Finnbennach, heard — no bull dared bellow so in its pastures — and came toward Cruachan with its head raised. All gathered to watch the fight, choosing as judge Bricriu, who was recovering from his wounds, since he favoured neither. The bulls met, pawing the earth and flinging it over their backs, their eyes like balls of fire, their nostrils blowing like smiths' bellows, their horns clashing like thunder. They trampled Bricriu to death beneath their hooves. Night fell and only their bellowing and clashing could be heard; through that night they fought across all Ireland, their hooves marking the ground wherever they went. In the morning the Brown Bull was seen passing west of Cruachan with the remains of the White-horned on its horns.
sections.bodyZh: 褐色公牛被赶到了康诺特，它看见了一片陌生的、美丽的土地，发出了三声震耳欲聋的吼叫。艾利尔牛群里的白角公牛芬本纳赫听见了，没有一头公牛敢在它的地盘上这样吼叫，它昂起头，向克鲁亨跑来。所有的人都聚集在一起，要看两头公牛决斗。人们推举了刚刚结束战斗、还在养伤的布里克留来做裁判，因为他对两头牛都没有偏心。两头公牛相遇了，它们用脚刨地，把泥土抛过头顶，眼睛像燃烧的火球，鼻孔喷着气，像铁匠的风箱，两头牛的角撞在一起，发出雷鸣般的巨响。它们打斗着，把站在旁边的裁判布里克留踩在脚下，踩死了。夜幕降临，人们只能听见它们的吼叫和撞击声。在这一整夜里，两头公牛打遍了整个爱尔兰，它们所到之处，大地被踩出了深深的痕迹。第二天早晨，人们看见褐色公牛向西经过了克鲁亨，它的角上挑着白角公牛的残骸。
sections.evidenceNote: 《夺牛长征记》（邓恩译本）·公牛之战。

sections.bodyEn: The Brown Bull ran east with the White-horned's remains, scattering its limbs across Ireland: at the ford of Athlone it dropped the loins, so the place was called Áth Luain, 'ford of the loins', and at Trim the liver, and other parts elsewhere, each place taking its name from them. It came home to Cúailnge and raged among the people there, killing many, until on a ridge its heart broke in its breast and it fell dead; the ridge was called Druim Tairb, 'the ridge of the bull'. So the war fought for a bull ended, with both bulls dead and countless warriors fallen at fords and on plains. Ailill and Medb made peace with Ulster and with Cú Chulainn, and for seven years there was no war between Ulster and Connacht; Finnabair stayed with Cú Chulainn, the men of Connacht returned home, and the Ulstermen went back to Emain Macha in glory. At the end of the tale the scribe wrote a blessing on all who would faithfully remember it and add nothing to it.
sections.bodyZh: 褐色公牛带着白角公牛的残骸一路向东奔跑，把对手的肢体一块块抛撒在爱尔兰各地。它在阿特隆的浅滩上抛下了白角公牛的腰，从此那里被叫作“阿特·卢安”，意思是“腰的浅滩”；它在特雷姆抛下了肝脏，在别处又抛下了其他的部分，每一个地方都因此得到了名字。褐色公牛回到了家乡库利，它狂怒地冲向那里的人群，杀死了许多人。最后，它来到了一座山脊上，它的心终于在胸中碎裂了，它倒在地上死去了。那座山脊从此被叫作“德鲁姆·塔尔布”，意思是“公牛的山脊”。这场为了一头牛而发动的战争，就这样结束了：两头公牛都死了，无数的勇士倒在了浅滩上和平原上。艾利尔和梅芙与阿尔斯特人、与库丘林讲和，此后七年间，阿尔斯特和康诺特之间没有再发生战争。芬达维尔留在了库丘林那里，康诺特人回到了自己的土地上，阿尔斯特人也带着荣誉回到了艾温·马哈。故事在这里结束，抄写者在书的末尾写道：愿所有忠实地记住这个故事、不再添加别的东西的人得到祝福。
sections.headingEn: The death of the Brown Bull

stories.canonicalTitle: The Four Branches of the Mabinogi, Part 1: Pwyll
stories.editorialNote: 依据格斯特夫人英译《马比诺吉昂》第一支，按情节顺序讲述。这些故事在十四世纪的《里德赫奇白书》和《赫杰斯特红书》中保存下来，写成年代约在十一至十二世纪，学者对其中多少保存了更古老的神话意见不一。

series.titleEn: The Four Branches of the Mabinogi (series)

stories.summaryEn: Out hunting, Pwyll, prince of Dyfed, offends Arawn, king of the Otherworld Annwn, and in amends exchanges shapes and kingdoms with him for a year, killing Arawn's rival Hafgan with a single blow at the ford and keeping chaste with Arawn's queen, so that he is called Head of Annwn. On the mound of Arberth he meets Rhiannon on her white horse, who chooses him over her betrothed; he almost loses her through a rash promise and wins her back by trapping his rival in a magic bag. Their son vanishes on the night of his birth, the waiting-women accuse Rhiannon of devouring him, and she is condemned to carry visitors at the gate for seven years — until Teyrnon, who found a child by his stable, brings the golden-haired boy home, and he is named Pryderi.
stories.summaryZh: 达费德王子皮威尔在打猎时冒犯了彼世安农的国王阿拉文，为了赔罪，他与阿拉文交换容貌和王国一年，替他在浅滩上一击杀死了宿敌哈夫甘，一年里对阿拉文的王后秋毫无犯，从此被称为“安农之主”。他在阿伯斯的土丘上遇见了骑白马的里安农，她抛弃了原来的婚约选择了他；皮威尔一句轻率的许诺差点失去她，又用一只魔法口袋把情敌骗了进去。他们的儿子在出生的夜里失踪了，侍女们诬陷里安农吃掉了孩子，里安农被罚在宫门边驮客七年；直到邻国的领主泰尔农发现了他在马厩边捡到的孩子，金发的男孩才回到母亲身边，被取名为普雷德里。
stories.titleZh: 马比诺吉昂四支 · 第一支 皮威尔

claims.statement: Hunting at Glyn Cuch, Pwyll drives off a pack of shining white red-eared hounds from their stag and is rebuked by their master, Arawn, king of Annwn, who asks him to rid him of his rival Hafgan in amends.
In Arawn's shape Pwyll rules Annwn for a year in all its splendour, and every night turns his back to Arawn's queen and keeps faith with Arawn.
At the ford Pwyll, in Arawn's shape, mortally wounds Hafgan with one blow and refuses to strike a second, so that Hafgan dies and his nobles submit, uniting Annwn under Arawn.
Returning to Annwn, Arawn learns from his queen that Pwyll never touched her in the whole year, and he and Pwyll become firm friends, Pwyll being called Head of Annwn.

Sitting on Gorsedd Arberth to see a wonder, Pwyll sees a lady on a white horse whom no rider can overtake though she rides slowly, until on the third day he calls on her to stop for the sake of the one she loves best.

Rhiannon, daughter of Hefeydd the Old, chooses Pwyll over her betrothed, but at their wedding feast Pwyll rashly grants a boon to Gwawl son of Clud, who claims the bride, and Rhiannon devises a plan with a little bag.

Disguised as a beggar, Pwyll asks Gwawl to fill Rhiannon's magic bag with food, traps Gwawl in it when he treads the food down, and releases him in the first game of Badger in the Bag on condition he renounce Rhiannon.
When Rhiannon's newborn son vanishes in the night, her six sleeping attendants smear her with a staghound pup's blood and accuse her of devouring the child.
Falsely accused, Rhiannon accepts the penance of sitting seven years by the horse-block at Arberth's gate, telling her tale to strangers and offering to carry them on her back into the court.
Watching his mare on May Eve, Teyrnon cuts off a monstrous claw that seizes her foal through the window and finds an infant boy in satin at his door, whom he and his wife rear as Gwri Golden-hair.
Seeing that the swiftly growing Gwri is the image of Pwyll and hearing of Rhiannon's penance, Teyrnon and his wife resolve to return the boy to Arberth.

When Teyrnon brings the boy to Arberth and he is recognised as Pwyll's image, Rhiannon says she is delivered of her anxiety (pryder), and the boy is named Pryderi; he later rules Dyfed and marries Cigfa.

events.summaryEn: Pwyll, prince of Dyfed, lord of seven cantrefs, was at Arberth when he wished to hunt and went to Glyn Cuch.
events.summaryZh: 达费德的王子皮威尔统治着七个坎特雷夫的土地。

events.summaryEn: Arawn said he would give Pwyll his own shape so that he could reign in Annwn for a year, and no one, not even Arawn's wife, would know him; Arawn would take Pwyll's shape and rule Dyfed.
events.summaryZh: 阿拉文说：我会把你变成我的样子，让你代替我在安农做一年的国王，我的王国里没有一个人会认出你，连我的妻子也不会；而我会变成你的样子，替你统治达费德。

events.summaryEn: On the appointed day Pwyll went to the ford with the nobles of Annwn, and Hafgan came with his host.
events.summaryZh: 约定的那一天到了，皮威尔带着安农的贵族们来到浅滩，哈夫甘也带着他的人马来了。

events.summaryEn: At the year's end Pwyll met Arawn at Glyn Cuch and each took his own shape again.
events.summaryZh: 一年期满，皮威尔来到格林·库赫，与阿拉文相见，两人各自恢复了原来的模样。

events.summaryEn: One day after a feast at Arberth, Pwyll went up the mound above the court called Gorsedd Arberth, of which it was said that any noble who sat on it would either receive wounds or see a wonder.
events.summaryZh: 有一天，皮威尔在阿伯斯的王宫里举行宴会，宴罢之后，他走上了宫殿上方一座名叫戈尔塞斯·阿伯斯的土丘。
events.titleEn: The lady on the white horse

events.summaryEn: She lifted her veil and he thought he had never seen a fairer face.
events.summaryZh: 女子揭开面纱，皮威尔觉得自己从没见过这样美丽的面容。

events.summaryEn: A year later Gwawl came to his feast.
events.summaryZh: 一年后，格瓦尔来赴他的婚宴。

events.summaryEn: Pwyll and Rhiannon ruled Dyfed happily, but after two years they had no child, and in the third year the nobles urged Pwyll to take another wife who could bear him an heir.
events.summaryZh: 皮威尔和里安农幸福地统治着达费德，可是过了两年，他们还没有孩子。

events.summaryEn: The nobles demanded that Pwyll put her away.
events.summaryZh: 消息传开了，贵族们要求皮威尔休掉里安农，皮威尔说：他们要我休妻，理由是她不能生育；可是她已经生了孩子，我不会休掉她。

events.summaryEn: Teyrnon Twrf Liant, lord of Gwent Is Coed, had the fairest mare in his land; every May Eve she foaled, and no one knew what became of the foal.
events.summaryZh: 格温特·伊斯·科伊德的领主泰尔农·特威尔夫·里安特有一匹母马，是他国土上最美的马。

events.summaryEn: The boy grew wondrously: at one year he walked like a child of three, at two he was as big as a child of six, and before he was four he was bargaining with the grooms to let him lead the horses to water.
events.summaryZh: 这个孩子长得飞快，一岁时就像三岁的孩子一样会走路，两岁时像六岁的孩子一样强壮，不到四岁，就要和马夫们讨价还价，要他们让他把马牵到河边去饮水。
events.titleEn: The boy who looked like Pwyll

events.summaryEn: Teyrnon came to Arberth with the boy and two knights and found Rhiannon by the horse-block.
events.summaryZh: 泰尔农带着男孩和两个骑士来到阿伯斯，看见里安农坐在宫门边的上马石旁。
