sections.bodyEn: Math son of Mathonwy was king of Gwynedd, and he could not live unless his feet were in the lap of a maiden, except when war prevented it. His footholder was Goewin, the fairest maiden of her time. His nephew Gilfaethwy fell sick with love for her. His brother Gwydion saw it, but they could not plot at court, for Math could hear any whisper the wind caught. So Gwydion devised a war between Gwynedd and the south to draw Math away. He had heard that Pryderi of Dyfed had beasts never before seen in the island — swine, sent to him from Annwn by Arawn its king. With Gilfaethwy and ten companions in the guise of bards he came to Pryderi's court, and that night, being the best storyteller in the world, he held the whole court spellbound. When he asked for the swine, Pryderi said he was bound by covenant with his people not to sell or give them until they had bred double their number. Gwydion by magic made twelve stallions, twelve hounds and twelve golden shields out of fungus and exchanged them for the swine; next day they turned back into fungus.
sections.bodyZh: 马索努伊的儿子马斯是格温内斯的国王。他有一个奇特的命运：除非国家处于战争之中，他必须时刻把双脚放在一位少女的膝上，否则他就会死去。那时为他持足的少女名叫戈尔文，是那个时代最美的少女。马斯的外甥吉尔维修伊爱上了戈尔文，日夜思念，渐渐消瘦。他的哥哥格威迪恩看出了弟弟的心事，可是马斯有一种能力：人们之间说的任何悄悄话，只要被风吹到，他都能听见，所以他们不能在宫里商量。格威迪恩想出了一个计策：挑起格温内斯和南方之间的战争，让马斯离开宫殿。他听说达费德的普雷德里有一种从来没有在这个岛上出现过的动物——猪，那是安农的国王阿拉文从彼世送给普雷德里的礼物。格威迪恩带着弟弟和十个同伴，扮成诗人来到普雷德里的宫中，格威迪恩是世上最会讲故事的人，那天晚上，他讲的故事让整个宫廷都听得入了迷。然后他请求普雷德里把猪给他，普雷德里说：我与我的人民有约，在这些猪繁殖到原来的两倍之前，不卖也不送。格威迪恩用魔法把菌菇变成了十二匹骏马、十二条猎犬和十二面金盾牌，用它们换走了猪。可是第二天，那些马、狗和盾牌就变回了菌菇。
sections.evidenceNote: 《马比诺吉昂》第四支·普雷德里的猪。
sections.headingZh: 持足少女与普雷德里的猪

sections.bodyEn: Discovering the deceit, Pryderi marched north with the men of the south, and war broke out; Math mustered Gwynedd against him. On the night the king left his court for the war, Gwydion and Gilfaethwy went back, drove out the maidens, and Gilfaethwy violated Goewin against her will in Math's own bed; next day they returned to the host. As the war went on with great loss, Pryderi proposed that since it was Gwydion's doing alone, the two should settle it in single combat and spare their people. Math agreed. They met at Maen Tyriawg, and through strength and magic Gwydion killed Pryderi, who was buried at Maen Tyriawg above Melenryd, where his grave is still. So died the prince found by Teyrnon and restored to his mother Rhiannon, in a war begun by a trick, and the men of the south went home in grief.
sections.bodyZh: 普雷德里发现自己被骗了，带着南方的大军向北追来，战争爆发了。马斯召集了格温内斯的军队出征迎敌。就在国王离开宫殿去打仗的那一夜，格威迪恩和吉尔维修伊回到了宫里，把宫中的少女们都赶了出去，吉尔维修伊违背戈尔文的意愿，强占了她。第二天，两兄弟回到了战场。战争持续着，双方死伤惨重，普雷德里提出：这场战争是因为格威迪恩一个人的诡计而起的，让他和我单独决斗，免得两边的人再这样白白送死。马斯同意了。普雷德里和格威迪恩在一个叫马恩·提里奥格的地方相遇，开始了决斗。普雷德里是一个勇敢的战士，可是格威迪恩有力量，也有魔法，他用魔法和力量杀死了普雷德里。普雷德里被葬在梅南特格的马恩·提里奥格，他的坟墓至今还在那里。这位从小被泰尔农捡回、让母亲里安农受尽苦难才回到身边、在第三支里被魔法困住的王子，就这样死在了一场由诡计挑起的战争中。南方的人们哀悼着回到了故乡。
sections.evidenceNote: 《马比诺吉昂》第四支·普雷德里之死。

sections.bodyEn: When Math returned and would put his feet in Goewin's lap, she told him to seek another maiden, for she was one no longer, and told him what had been done. He would have justice for her and for himself, he said, and to spare her shame he took her as his wife and gave her authority over his realm. Gwydion and Gilfaethwy kept away until they had to come before him. For the shame they had brought him and the death of Pryderi, Math struck Gilfaethwy with his wand and made him a hind, and Gwydion a stag, to live as beasts for a year; at the year's end they returned with a fawn, which Math made into a boy and had baptised. Then he made them a wild boar and sow, and they came back with a young one; then wolves, and they returned with a cub — each made a boy. After three years he restored their human shape, saying they had suffered punishment and shame enough.
sections.bodyZh: 马斯回到宫中，要把双脚放在戈尔文的膝上。戈尔文说：大人，另找一个少女吧，我已经不再是少女了。她把发生的一切告诉了国王。马斯说：我会为你主持公道，也会为我自己讨回公道。为了不让她蒙受耻辱，马斯娶了戈尔文为妻，把整个王国的统治权交到她的手中。格威迪恩和吉尔维修伊不敢回宫，在外面躲藏，最后不得不来见国王。马斯说：你们给我带来了耻辱，杀死了普雷德里，我要惩罚你们。他用魔杖碰了碰吉尔维修伊，把他变成了一头母鹿，又把格威迪恩变成了一头公鹿，命令他们像野兽一样在林中生活一年，一年后再回来。一年后，两头鹿带着一只小鹿回来了，马斯把小鹿变成了一个男孩，给他施了洗礼。然后，他又把两兄弟变成了一对野猪，一年后他们带回来一头小猪，马斯也把它变成了男孩。第三年，他把他们变成了一对狼，一年后，他们又带回来一只小狼，也变成了男孩。三年期满，马斯恢复了他们的人形，说：你们已经为你们的罪行受到了足够的惩罚，也蒙受了足够的耻辱。
sections.evidenceNote: 《马比诺吉昂》第四支·兄弟受罚。

sections.bodyEn: Math needed a new footholder, and Gwydion proposed his sister Arianrhod daughter of Dôn. Asked whether she was a maiden, she said she knew not otherwise. Math bent his magic wand and laid it on the ground and bade her step over it, that he might know. As she stepped over, she dropped a fine yellow-haired boy, who cried aloud; and as she made for the door, something small dropped from her, which Gwydion snatched up before anyone could see it, wrapped in a sheet of satin and hid in a small chest at the foot of his bed. Math had the yellow-haired boy baptised, and at once the child made for the sea, plunged in and took on the nature of the sea, swimming as well as the best fish; he was called Dylan Eil Ton, Dylan son of the Wave, and no wave ever broke beneath him. He was later killed by a blow from his uncle Gofannon, one of the Three Unhappy Blows.
sections.bodyZh: 马斯需要一位新的持足少女，格威迪恩推荐了他的妹妹、多恩的女儿阿丽安萝德。阿丽安萝德来到宫中，马斯问她：你是少女吗？她说：据我所知，我是。马斯拿出他的魔杖，弯成一个弧形放在地上，说：从这根魔杖上跨过去，如果你是少女，我就会知道。阿丽安萝德从魔杖上跨了过去，就在她跨步的时候，她生下了一个金发的强壮男孩。男孩一落地就大声哭叫，阿丽安萝德转身往门口走去，在走向门口的路上，又有一个小东西从她身上掉了下来。还没有人看清那是什么，格威迪恩就抢先把它抱起来，用一块锦缎裹好，藏进了自己床脚边的一个小箱子里。马斯给那个金发男孩施了洗礼，男孩一受洗，就跑向大海，跳进了海里，立刻就有了大海的天性，像最好的鱼一样游泳，从此被叫作“浪之子迪兰”，海浪从来不会在他身下破碎。后来，他被他的舅舅格万农用一支长矛杀死了，那是三次不幸的一击之一。
sections.evidenceNote: 《马比诺吉昂》第四支·魔杖的考验。

sections.bodyEn: One morning Gwydion heard a cry from the chest, opened it and found a little boy stretching out his arms. He had him nursed in the town; the boy grew fast — at one year as big as a child of two, at two able to walk to court alone, at four as big as a child of eight — and loved Gwydion above all. One day Gwydion took him to Caer Arianrhod. Told the boy was her son, Arianrhod was angry that Gwydion kept her shame before her, and asked his name; he had none yet. 'Then I lay this destiny on him: he shall never have a name until he gets one from me.' Gwydion and the boy came by sea to Caer Arianrhod in a ship made by magic, disguised as shoemakers, and made fine shoes, and Arianrhod came aboard to be measured. A wren alighted on the deck, and the boy struck it with a stone between the sinew and the bone of its leg. 'It is with a skilful hand that the fair one has hit it,' she laughed. 'You have named him,' said Gwydion: 'Lleu Llaw Gyffes, the fair one of the skilful hand.' Then ship and shoes turned back to seaweed and sedge.
sections.bodyZh: 有一天早晨，格威迪恩在床上听见箱子里传出哭声，他打开箱子，看见一个小男孩伸出双臂。他把孩子交给城里的一个妇人哺育。这孩子长得飞快，一岁时像两岁的孩子，两岁时就能自己走到宫里来，格威迪恩亲自照顾他，孩子也最爱格威迪恩。四岁时，他已经像八岁的孩子一样大了。一天，格威迪恩带着孩子去卡耳·阿丽安萝德见他的母亲。阿丽安萝德问：这个孩子是谁？格威迪恩说：是你的儿子。阿丽安萝德大怒，责备他把自己的耻辱一直留在身边，问孩子叫什么名字。格威迪恩说：他还没有名字。阿丽安萝德说：那我给他下一个命运：除非我亲自给他取名，否则他永远不会有名字。格威迪恩想出了一个计策。他和孩子扮成鞋匠，乘一条魔法变出的船来到卡耳·阿丽安萝德的海边，做起了漂亮的鞋子。阿丽安萝德亲自来到船上量脚。这时，一只鹪鹩落在船的甲板上，男孩拿起投石器一投，正好击中了鹪鹩的腿，打在筋骨之间。阿丽安萝德笑着说：这个金发的孩子真有一双巧手！格威迪恩说：你已经给他取了名字，他就叫勒伊·劳·吉菲斯——巧手的金发人。船和鞋子都变回了莎草和海藻。
sections.evidenceNote: 《马比诺吉昂》第四支·勒伊得名。
sections.headingEn: The fair one with the skilful hand

sections.bodyEn: Arianrhod, tricked, laid a second destiny: he should never bear arms until she armed him herself. Lleu grew and could ride, but was downcast without arms. One morning he and Gwydion came to Caer Arianrhod as two bards from Glamorgan and were made welcome, and Gwydion told tales that night. At dawn Gwydion worked his magic: trumpets and shouting resounded round the castle, and a fleet beyond counting appeared on the sea as if to attack. Arianrhod ran to them in alarm; Gwydion told her to shut the gates and defend herself and to give them arms to help. She brought two suits, gave one to Gwydion and armed the young bard herself. 'You may take off his arms; we need them no more,' said Gwydion. 'And the fleet?' 'There is no fleet; it was an illusion I made so that you should arm your son yourself. He has his arms now — and not by your goodwill.'
sections.bodyZh: 阿丽安萝德知道自己上当了，又下了第二个命运：除非我亲手给他武器，否则他永远不能拥有武器。勒伊渐渐长大，能骑马了，可是他没有武器，郁郁不乐。格威迪恩说：不要难过，我会让你得到武器。一天早晨，他们扮成两个从格拉摩根来的诗人，来到卡耳·阿丽安萝德，受到了殷勤的款待。晚上，格威迪恩讲故事，大家都听得很高兴。第二天天刚亮，格威迪恩施展魔法，让城堡四周响起了号角声和呐喊声，海面上出现了一支看不见尽头的舰队，似乎正要攻打城堡。阿丽安萝德惊慌失措地跑来，问他们该怎么办。格威迪恩说：把大门关紧，尽力防守吧，给我们武器，我们也会帮你守城。阿丽安萝德拿来了两副武器，一副交给格威迪恩，另一副由她亲手给那个年轻的诗人穿戴上，为他束好铠甲。格威迪恩说：好了，你可以脱下他的武器了，我们用不着它们了。阿丽安萝德说：外面的舰队怎么办？格威迪恩说：根本没有舰队，那是我为了让你亲手给你的儿子武器而变出来的幻象。他现在已经得到了武器，而且不是靠你的好意。
sections.evidenceNote: 《马比诺吉昂》第四支·获得武器。

sections.bodyEn: Furious, Arianrhod laid a third destiny: he should never have a wife of the race that was now on the earth. 'You are a wicked woman,' said Gwydion, 'but he shall have a wife nonetheless.' He went to Math, who said: 'We will seek, I and you, by our magic and enchantment, to make a wife for him out of flowers.' They took the blossoms of the oak, the broom and the meadowsweet and from them conjured the fairest and most graceful maiden ever seen, baptised her and named her Blodeuedd, 'flowers'. She and Lleu were married, and Math gave Lleu the cantref of Dinoding, where he made his court at Mur Castell and ruled to the content of all. They seemed a perfect pair — a hero raised in a chest who won his name and arms by craft, and a woman made of flowers. But a heart made of flowers did not necessarily know faithfulness.
sections.bodyZh: 阿丽安萝德愤怒至极，下了第三个命运：他永远不能娶这世上任何一个种族的女子为妻。格威迪恩说：你真是一个恶毒的女人，可是他还是会有一个妻子。格威迪恩来到马斯那里，向国王诉说了这件事。马斯说：我们用我们两人的魔法和幻术，从花朵里为他造一个妻子吧。他们采来了橡树的花、金雀花和绣线菊的花，用这些花朵变出了一个少女，她是世上最美丽、最优雅的女子。他们为她施了洗礼，给她取名为布罗黛维德，意思是“花朵”。勒伊和布罗黛维德举行了婚礼，婚宴之后，两人同床共枕。马斯又把丁诺丁坎特雷夫的土地赐给了勒伊，让他在那里建立自己的宫廷，勒伊就在穆尔·卡斯泰尔安了家。他统治着那片土地，人们都满意他的统治，对他心悦诚服。这对夫妻看起来是如此美满：一个是在箱子里长大、靠着计策得到名字和武器的英雄，一个是由鲜花变成的美丽女子。可是用花朵造成的心，并不一定懂得忠诚。

sections.bodyEn: One day while Lleu was visiting Math, Blodeuedd, walking in the court at Mur Castell, heard a horn and saw a weary stag pass with hounds and huntsmen after it: Gronw Pebr, lord of Penllyn, was hunting. They killed the stag and were flaying it and feeding the hounds until nightfall. It would be discourteous, said Blodeuedd, to let the lord go at that hour, and she invited him to stay. When they saw each other, both were filled with love, and that night they did not hide it from each other but lay together. She asked him to stay the next day and the next, and they took counsel how they might be together always. The only way, said Gronw, was to kill Lleu, but he was not easily killed; she would find out from him, she said, pretending concern for his safety, how he might die. Gronw left, and that evening Lleu came home.
sections.bodyZh: 一天，勒伊去拜访马斯，布罗黛维德独自留在穆尔·卡斯泰尔。她在宫中散步，听见一阵号角声，看见一头疲惫的雄鹿跑过，后面追着猎犬和猎人。那是彭林的领主格罗努·佩布尔在打猎。他们杀死了雄鹿，一直剥皮、喂狗到了天黑。布罗黛维德说：如果我们让这位领主在这个时候离开，他会说我们无礼。她派人去请格罗努到宫中过夜。格罗努来了，布罗黛维德看着他，心中充满了爱意；格罗努看着她，也和她一样。那一夜，他们没有隐瞒彼此的爱，同床共枕。第二天，布罗黛维德请他不要走，他又留了一天；第三天也是如此。他们商量着怎样才能永远在一起。格罗努说：只有一个办法，就是杀死勒伊。可是勒伊不是一个容易杀死的人。布罗黛维德说：我会想办法从他那里打听出来，他怎样才会死去，我会假装是因为关心他。格罗努离开了，当天晚上，勒伊回到了家里。
sections.evidenceNote: 《马比诺吉昂》第四支·格罗努·佩布尔。

sections.bodyEn: That night Blodeuedd was silent, and when Lleu asked why, she said she feared he would die before her. Unless God willed it, he said, he would not easily be slain. Then for God's sake and hers, she said, let him tell her how, so that she might guard against it. He could not be slain within a house nor without, he said, nor on horseback nor on foot; only by a spear a year in the making, worked on only during Mass on Sundays; and only on a riverbank, under a thatched roof over a bath, with one foot on the edge of the bath and the other on the back of a he-goat. She told Gronw, who spent a year making the spear. Then she asked Lleu to show her how he would stand; as he set one foot on the bath's edge and the other on the goat's back, Gronw rose from behind a hill and cast the poisoned spear, which struck him. Lleu gave a fearful scream, rose in the form of an eagle and flew away, and was seen no more.
sections.bodyZh: 那天晚上，布罗黛维德一言不发，勒伊问她为什么不高兴。她说：我在想一件你绝不会为我想的事：我担心你会比我先死。勒伊说：除非上帝要我死，否则我不会那么容易被杀死。她说：那么，为了上帝和我的缘故，告诉我你怎样才会被杀死吧，我会比你更小心地提防。勒伊说：我不能在屋里被杀，也不能在屋外被杀；不能在马背上被杀，也不能在步行时被杀。要杀死我，必须用一支花一年时间打造的长矛，而且只能在每个星期天人们做弥撒的时候打造。还必须在河岸边，用茅草搭一个屋顶，屋顶下放一个浴盆，让我在浴盆里洗澡，我的一只脚踩在浴盆的边上，另一只脚踩在一头公山羊的背上，只有在那时被击中，我才会死。布罗黛维德把这一切告诉了格罗努。格罗努花了一年时间，每个星期天打造那支长矛。一年后，布罗黛维德请勒伊演示给她看，让他站成那个姿势。就在勒伊一只脚踩在浴盆边、一只脚踩在公山羊背上的时候，躲在山坡后的格罗努掷出了毒矛，矛刺进了他的身体。勒伊发出一声可怕的尖叫，化作一只鹰飞上了天空，再也不见了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《马比诺吉昂》第四支·勒伊的秘密。
sections.headingEn: Neither in a house nor out of doors

sections.bodyEn: Gronw took Lleu's court and lands. When Math and Gwydion heard, they grieved greatly, and Gwydion swore not to rest until he found Lleu. He searched Gwynedd and Powys and lodged with a peasant in Arfon, whose swineherd said that a sow of his ran out each morning as soon as the sty was opened and no one knew where she went until evening. Next morning Gwydion followed her up a brook to an oak tree, where she stopped to feed — on putrid flesh and maggots. Looking up, he saw an eagle at the top of the tree, and whenever it shook itself, rotting flesh and maggots fell, which the sow ate. Gwydion knew the eagle was Lleu and sang an englyn to it: an oak grows between two lakes, dark is the sky and the glen; if I speak truly, these are the limbs of Lleu. The eagle came down to the middle of the tree; he sang a second, and it came to the lowest branch; a third, and it alighted on his knee. He struck it with his wand, and Lleu took his own form — nothing but skin and bone, the most pitiful sight ever seen.
sections.bodyZh: 格罗努占据了勒伊的宫殿和土地。消息传到马斯和格威迪恩那里，两人悲痛万分。格威迪恩发誓，不找到勒伊的下落，他绝不休息。他走遍了格温内斯和波伊斯，来到阿尔丰的一个农户家里借宿。农户家的猪倌说，他有一头母猪，每天早晨猪圈门一开，它就跑出去，谁也不知道它去了哪里，晚上才回来。格威迪恩第二天一早跟着母猪，一直跟到一条小溪的上游，母猪在一棵橡树下停了下来，吃着什么东西。格威迪恩走近一看，母猪吃的是腐烂的肉和蛆。他抬头望去，看见橡树的顶上栖着一只鹰，每当鹰抖动身体，就有腐肉和蛆从它身上掉下来，母猪就在树下吃。格威迪恩知道，那只鹰就是勒伊。他对着鹰唱起了一首诗：在两个湖之间长着一棵橡树，天空和山谷之间一片阴暗，如果我说的是真话，这就是勒伊的肢体。鹰慢慢地从树顶落到了半空。他又唱了第二首，鹰又落到了更低的树枝上。他唱了第三首，鹰落到了格威迪恩的膝上。格威迪恩用魔杖一碰，勒伊恢复了人形，可是他瘦得只剩下皮包骨头，谁也没见过这样可怜的人。
sections.evidenceNote: 《马比诺吉昂》第四支·橡树上的鹰。

sections.bodyEn: Lleu was brought to Caer Dathyl, and all the best physicians of Gwynedd tended him until by the year's end he was whole again. Now, he told Math, he would have redress from the one who had wronged him. Math mustered Gwynedd, and Gwydion went ahead to Mur Castell after Blodeuedd. She fled with her maidens over the mountain, and as they went they looked back in fear, and fell one by one into a lake and were drowned, all but Blodeuedd; the lake was called Llyn y Morwynion, the Lake of the Maidens. Gwydion overtook her and said he would not kill her but do worse: turn her into a bird. Because of the shame she had brought on Lleu, she would never dare show her face by day, she would fear all other birds, and every bird would attack and mob her wherever it found her; and she would not lose her name, but be called Blodeuwedd always. So she became an owl, and to this day, the tale says, the owl is called blodeuwedd, and all birds are its enemies.
sections.bodyZh: 勒伊被带到卡耳·达瑟尔，格温内斯所有最好的医生都来为他治疗，到了年底，他终于恢复了健康。他对马斯说：现在是我向那个害我的人报仇的时候了。马斯召集了格温内斯的军队，和勒伊、格威迪恩一起向穆尔·卡斯泰尔进发。格威迪恩走在最前面，直奔宫殿去找布罗黛维德。布罗黛维德听说他们来了，带着她的侍女们逃出宫殿，翻过山去，逃向一座山上的宫殿。她们一边跑一边回头张望，害怕得不敢往前看，结果一个接一个地掉进了湖里淹死了，只剩下布罗黛维德一个人，那个湖从此被叫作“少女湖”。格威迪恩追上了布罗黛维德，说：我不会杀死你，我要做一件比杀死你更糟的事：我要把你变成一只鸟。因为你给勒伊带来了耻辱，你永远不敢在白天露面，你会害怕所有其他的鸟，所有的鸟都会攻击你、驱赶你，无论在哪里遇见你。你的名字也不会消失，你将永远被叫作布罗黛维德。就这样，布罗黛维德被变成了一只猫头鹰。萨迦说，直到今天，人们在威尔士语里仍然把猫头鹰叫作布罗黛维德，而所有的鸟都与猫头鹰为敌。

sections.bodyEn: Gronw Pebr fled to Penllyn and sent to ask whether Lleu would take land or gold and silver in compensation. 'I will not, by my confession to Heaven,' said Lleu. 'The least I will accept is that he go to the place where I was when he struck me, and I stand where he stood, and cast a spear at him.' Gronw asked his men which of them would take the blow for him; none would, and for that they are called one of the Three Disloyal War-bands. So Gronw went himself to the bank of the Cynfael, and each stood where the other had stood. Gronw asked, since it was a woman's wiles that drove him to it, to set between them a stone he saw by the river, and Lleu would not refuse him. Lleu cast the spear; it pierced the stone and Gronw too, breaking his back, and he died. The stone pierced by the spear stands on the bank of the Cynfael and is called Llech Gronw. Lleu took possession of his lands again and ruled them well, and the tale says he afterwards became lord over Gwynedd. So ends this Branch of the Mabinogi.
sections.bodyZh: 格罗努·佩布尔逃回了他的领地彭林，派使者去问勒伊，愿不愿意接受土地、金银作为赔偿。勒伊说：我向天发誓，我不接受。我要的最少的赔偿是：他要到我被他的长矛刺中的那个地方去，站在我当时站的位置，让我站在他当时站的位置，向他投出一支长矛。格罗努问他的手下们：你们谁愿意替我挨这一矛？没有一个人愿意，因此他们后来被称为“三个不忠的战团”之一。格罗努只好自己去。两人来到阿夫农·辛瓦尔的河岸边，格罗努站在勒伊当年站的地方，勒伊站在格罗努当年站的地方。格罗努说：勒伊，我当年做那件事，是因为一个女人的诡计，请你允许我在我们之间放一块我在河边看见的石头，挡在我和你的矛之间。勒伊说：我不会拒绝你的请求。格罗努把一块石板挡在身前。勒伊掷出了长矛，长矛穿透了那块石头，也穿透了格罗努的身体，把他的脊背刺断了。格罗努·佩布尔就这样死去了。那块被长矛刺穿的石头至今还在阿夫农·辛瓦尔的岸边，被叫作“格罗努之石”。勒伊重新得到了他的土地，统治得非常好，据故事说，他后来做了格温内斯的君主。第四支，也是马比诺吉昂的最后一支，就这样结束了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《马比诺吉昂》第四支·格罗努之石。

stories.canonicalTitle: Kojiki, Part 3: Ōkuninushi, from the hare of Inaba to the yielding of the land
stories.editorialNote: 依据张伯伦 1882 年英译《古事记》第二十至三十二节（sacred-texts 页码 kj027–kj039），按节顺序讲述；第二十六节与第二十九节的神谱只择要提及。大国主今天仍在出云大社等神社受到祭祀，本篇只讲述《古事记》文本，不代表神社的信仰与祭仪。
stories.summaryEn: Ōkuninushi is a descendant of Susanoo. Carrying the bag for his eighty brothers as they go to woo the princess of Inaba, he heals a skinned white hare, which foretells that the princess will choose him. His jealous brothers kill him twice, and twice he is restored by deities his mother calls down from heaven. He flees to the Nether-Distant-Land, where Susanoo's daughter Suseri-bime helps him survive the snake room, the centipede-and-wasp room and the burning moor; at last he escapes carrying her on his back with Susanoo's sword, bow and speaking lute, and becomes Master of the Great Land. He makes the land with the tiny Sukuna-bikona and enshrines a deity who comes over the sea on Mount Mimoro. Amaterasu wants her descendants to rule the land: the envoys Ame-no-hohi and Ame-no-Wakahiko never report back, Takemikazuchi sits cross-legged on the point of an upturned sword, Kotoshironushi agrees and Takeminakata flees, and Ōkuninushi yields the land, asking only for a great palace.
stories.summaryZh: 大国主是须佐之男的后代。他替八十位兄长背着袋子去稻羽求婚，路上治好了被剥了皮的白兔，白兔预言八上比卖会嫁给他。兄长们嫉恨他，两次把他害死，都被母亲求来的神救活。他逃到根之坚洲国，在须佐之男的女儿须势理毘卖帮助下熬过了蛇室、蜈蚣与蜂之室和火烧原野，最后背着她、带着须佐之男的生太刀、生弓矢和天诏琴逃回人间，成为“大国主”。他与小小的少名毘古那一起造国，又在御诸山供奉来自海上的神。天上的天照大神要她的子孙来统治这片土地：天菩比神和天若日子都没有回来复命，建御雷神坐在倒插的剑尖上逼问，儿子事代主答应、建御名方败逃，大国主终于让出国土，只求为他建一座高大的宫殿。
stories.titleZh: 古事记 · 第三部 大国主：从稻羽白兔到让国

claims.statement: Kojiki Section XX lists Susanoo's descendants and gives Ōkuninushi's five names: Ōkuninushi, Ōnamuji, Ashihara-shiko-wo, Yachihoko and Utsushi-kunitama.

Kojiki Section XXI says Ōnamuji, carrying his brothers' bag, healed the hare of Inaba with fresh water and sedge pollen after the Eighty Deities had made its injuries worse, and the hare foretold that Princess Yakami would choose him.
Kojiki Section XXII says the Eighty Deities killed Ōnamuji by rolling down a red-hot boulder at Mount Tema, and Kami-musubi sent Princess Cockle-Shell and Princess Clam, who restored him to life.

Kojiki Section XXII says the Eighty Deities crushed Ōnamuji in a cleft tree, his mother restored him and sent him to Oho-ya-biko in Ki, who let him escape through the fork of a tree towards Susanoo's Nether-Distant-Land.
Kojiki Section XXIII says Suseri-bime married Ōnamuji when he arrived, and when Susanoo made him sleep in the snake room she gave him a snake-scarf to wave three times, so that he came out unharmed.
Kojiki Section XXIII says that when Susanoo next put Ōnamuji in a room of centipedes and wasps, Suseri-bime again gave him a scarf against them and he came out unharmed.

Kojiki Section XXIII says that when Susanoo set fire to the moor around Ōnamuji, a mouse showed him a hollow in the ground to shelter in and brought back the whizzing arrow, and he presented the arrow to Susanoo.
Kojiki Section XXIII says that when Susanoo made Ōnamuji pick centipedes from his hair, Suseri-bime gave him muku berries and red earth to chew and spit, so that Susanoo fell asleep pleased with him.

Kojiki Section XXIII says Ōnamuji escaped with Suseri-bime and Susanoo's sword, bow and speaking lute, and Susanoo, pursuing to the Even Pass of Yomi, called on him to drive away his brothers, become Ōkuninushi and make Suseri-bime his chief wife.
Kojiki Sections XXIV–XXV say that as Yachihoko he wooed Princess Nunakawa of Koshi with songs, and that when Suseri-bime was jealous they exchanged songs and pledged each other with a wine-cup.

Kojiki Section XXVII says Sukuna-bikona came over the waves to Cape Miho in a seed-pod boat, Kami-musubi named him her child who slipped through her fingers, and he made the land with Ōkuninushi before crossing to the Eternal Land.

Kojiki Section XXVIII says that after Sukuna-bikona left, a deity came over the sea illuminating it and offered to make the land with Ōkuninushi if worshipped on the eastern mountain of Yamato, the deity of Mount Mimoro.

Kojiki Sections XXX–XXXI say Ame-no-hohi and then Ame-no-Wakahiko failed to report from the Central Land, and that when Ame-no-Wakahiko shot the pheasant Naki-me, Takagi-no-kami threw the arrow back and it killed him on his bed.

Kojiki Section XXXII says Takemikazuchi, seated on an upturned sword on a wave at Inasa, demanded the land; Kotoshironushi agreed, Takeminakata was overpowered and fled to Suwa, and Ōkuninushi yielded the land on condition that a great palace be built for him.

events.summaryEn: After telling how Susanoo built his palace in Izumo and married Kushinada-hime, the Kojiki lists his descendants: their son Yashima-jinumi, and so on down the generations to Ame-no-fuyu-kinu, who married Sashikuni-waka-hime, daughter of the great deity of Sashikuni, and fathered the hero of this part — the sixth generation from Susanoo.
events.summaryZh: 《古事记》在讲完须佐之男在出云建宫、娶栉名田比卖之后，接着列出了他的子孙：须佐之男和栉名田比卖生下八岛士奴美神，此后一代代往下传，传到天之冬衣神，天之冬衣神娶了刺国大神的女儿刺国若比卖，生下的就是这一部故事的主人公——从须佐之男往下数，正好是第六代。
events.titleEn: The five names of the Master of the Great Land

events.summaryEn: The Eighty Deities all wished to marry Princess Yakami of Inaba, and set out together, making Ōnamuji carry their bag like a servant.
events.summaryZh: 八十神都想娶稻羽的八上比卖，一起出发去求婚，让大穴牟迟背着袋子，像仆人一样跟在后面。

events.summaryEn: Princess Yakami told the Eighty Deities: 'I will not listen to you.
events.summaryZh: 八上比卖果然对八十神说：我不听你们的话，我要嫁给大穴牟迟。
events.titleEn: The red boar of Mount Tema

events.summaryEn: Seeing him alive again, the Eighty Deities set another trap.
events.summaryZh: 八十神看见他又活了，再次设下圈套。

events.summaryEn: The Nether-Distant-Land, the mother's land that Susanoo had once wept to go to, was now his dwelling.
events.summaryZh: 根之坚洲国——张伯伦译作“幽远之国”——就是当年须佐之男哭着要去的母亲之国，如今他住在这里。

events.summaryEn: The next night Susanoo put him in a room full of centipedes and wasps.
events.summaryZh: 第二天晚上，须佐之男又让他睡在一间满是蜈蚣和马蜂的屋子里。
events.titleEn: The room of centipedes and wasps

events.summaryEn: Next Susanoo shot a whizzing arrow into a great moor and sent Ōnamuji to fetch it.
events.summaryZh: 须佐之男又把一支鸣镝——箭头上装着中空的响器、射出去会呼啸作响的箭——射进一片大草原，命令大穴牟迟去把箭找回来。
events.titleEn: The burning moor and the mouse

events.summaryEn: Susanoo took him back into the house, called him into a great room eight fathoms wide, and made him pick the lice from his head.
events.summaryZh: 须佐之男把大穴牟迟带回家里，叫进一间八寻宽的大屋子，让他替自己捉头上的虱子。

events.summaryEn: While Susanoo slept, Ōnamuji tied his hair to the rafters of the room, blocked the door with a rock that would take five hundred men to move, took his wife Suseri-bime on his back, and fled carrying Susanoo's great sword of life, his bow and arrows of life, and his heavenly speaking lute.
events.summaryZh: 大穴牟迟趁须佐之男睡着，把他的头发一缕缕绑在屋子的椽子上，用一块要五百个人才拉得动的大石头堵住屋门，背起妻子须势理毘卖，带上须佐之男的生太刀、生弓矢和天诏琴，逃了出去。
events.titleEn: The sword of life, the bow and the speaking lute
events.titleZh: 生太刀、生弓矢与天诏琴

events.summaryEn: As Yachihoko, the Deity of Eight Thousand Spears, he went to distant Koshi to woo Princess Nunakawa.
events.summaryZh: 以八千矛神为名的大国主，又到遥远的越国去向沼河比卖求婚。
events.titleEn: The songs of the Deity of Eight Thousand Spears

events.summaryEn: Once, at Cape Miho in Izumo, Ōkuninushi saw a deity riding the crests of the waves in a little boat made from a seed-pod of the kagami plant, clothed in the whole stripped skin of some small creature — the character is read by some as a goose and by others as a moth.
events.summaryZh: 有一天，大国主在出云的美保岬，看见一位神乘着用萝藦豆荚做成的小船，踏着浪花漂过来，身上穿着用整张剥下来的小动物的皮做的衣服——原文的字一说是鹅，一说指飞蛾。

events.summaryEn: With Sukuna-bikona gone, Ōkuninushi said in sorrow: 'How can I make this land alone?
events.summaryZh: 少名毘古那走了，大国主忧愁地说：我一个人怎么能把这片国土造好呢？

events.summaryEn: Amaterasu declared that the Luxuriant Reed-Plains Land of Fresh Rice-Ears should be ruled by her son Ame-no-oshi-ho-mimi.
events.summaryZh: 天照大神说：丰苇原的瑞穗国应该由我的儿子天忍穗耳命来统治。

events.summaryEn: Last, the deities sent Takemikazuchi, with Ame-no-tori-fune.
events.summaryZh: 众神最后派出了建御雷神，由天鸟船神陪同。
events.titleEn: Takemikazuchi and the yielding of the land

versions.labelEn: Kojiki, Chamberlain translation, Sections XX–XXXII (long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十至三十二节（长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 大国主的五个名字、稻羽白兔、手间山的赤猪、大树的裂缝、根之国的蛇室与蜈蚣蜂室、火烧原野与老鼠、带着宝物逃走、八千矛的求婚之歌、少名毘古那、御诸山的神、天若日子与雉鸣女、建御雷与国让
versions.rightsNote: 张伯伦 1882 年译本属公共领域；本站发布按节顺序的独立讲述，神名采用现代通行读法。

sections.bodyEn: After telling how Susanoo built his palace in Izumo and married Kushinada-hime, the Kojiki lists his descendants: their son Yashima-jinumi, and so on down the generations to Ame-no-fuyu-kinu, who married Sashikuni-waka-hime, daughter of the great deity of Sashikuni, and fathered the hero of this part — the sixth generation from Susanoo. The text gives him five names: Ōkuninushi, Ōnamuji, Ashihara-shiko-wo, Yachihoko and Utsushi-kunitama. They surface one by one in the story: as a youth he is Ōnamuji; in the Nether-Distant-Land Susanoo calls him Ashihara-shiko-wo, the Ugly Male of the Reed-Plains; as a wooer he is Yachihoko, the Deity of Eight Thousand Spears; and at the Even Pass of Yomi Susanoo charges him to become Ōkuninushi and Utsushi-kunitama, ruler of the living land. He has many brothers, the Eighty Deities, and a mother, Sashikuni-waka-hime, who twice goes weeping to save him. When the story begins he is the most put-upon of the brothers.
sections.bodyZh: 《古事记》在讲完须佐之男在出云建宫、娶栉名田比卖之后，接着列出了他的子孙：须佐之男和栉名田比卖生下八岛士奴美神，此后一代代往下传，传到天之冬衣神，天之冬衣神娶了刺国大神的女儿刺国若比卖，生下的就是这一部故事的主人公——从须佐之男往下数，正好是第六代。书中说他有五个名字：大国主神、大穴牟迟神、苇原色许男神、八千矛神、宇都志国玉神。这些名字后来会在故事里一个个出现：年轻时人们叫他大穴牟迟；在根之国，须佐之男叫他苇原色许男，也就是“苇原中国的丑男子”；求婚时他叫八千矛神，也就是“拥有八千支矛的神”；最后，须佐之男在黄泉比良坂上命令他成为“大国主”和“宇都志国玉”，也就是统治人间国土的神。他还有许多兄弟，书中称为八十神。他的母亲刺国若比卖，在后面的故事里两次哭着去救他。故事开始的时候，他还只是兄弟中最受欺负的一个。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十节。
sections.headingEn: The five names of the Master of the Great Land

sections.bodyEn: The Eighty Deities all wished to marry Princess Yakami of Inaba, and set out together, making Ōnamuji carry their bag like a servant. At Cape Keta they found a hare lying stripped of its fur. They told it to bathe in the sea and lie on a high mountain in the wind; it did, and as the salt dried its skin split, and it lay weeping with pain. Ōnamuji came last and asked why it wept. The hare said: 'I lived on the island of Oki and wanted to cross. I tricked the wani of the sea, saying, let us count whose tribe is larger; line up and I will count you as I step across your backs. They lined up and I trod across, but just before landing I said, you have been deceived! The last wani seized me and stripped off all my clothing.' Ōnamuji told it to wash in the fresh water of the river-mouth and roll in the pollen of the sedges. It did, and its body was restored. This, says the text, is the White Hare of Inaba, now called the Hare Deity. The hare said: 'The Eighty Deities will not win the princess. Though you carry the bag, she will be yours.'
sections.bodyZh: 八十神都想娶稻羽的八上比卖，一起出发去求婚，让大穴牟迟背着袋子，像仆人一样跟在后面。走到气多岬，他们看见一只被剥光了皮的兔子躺在地上。八十神对兔子说：你去海里洗个澡，然后躺在高山顶上吹风。兔子照做了，海水干了以后，它的皮肤被风吹得裂开，痛得直哭。大穴牟迟最后赶到，问它为什么哭。兔子说：我本来住在淤岐岛，想渡海过来，就骗海里的和迩说，我们来比一比谁的族人多，你们排成一行，我从你们背上踩过去数一数。和迩们排好了队，我一路踩着它们的背走过来，快到岸时却说了一句：你们上当了！最后那只和迩就抓住我，剥光了我的衣服。大穴牟迟教它到河口用淡水洗身，再把蒲草的花粉铺在地上，在上面打滚。兔子照做，身体恢复如初。书中说，这就是稻羽的白兔，现在叫作兔神。兔子对他说：八十神得不到八上比卖，虽然你背着袋子，她一定会嫁给你。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十一节。

sections.bodyEn: Princess Yakami told the Eighty Deities: 'I will not listen to you. I will marry Ōnamuji.' Furious, they plotted to kill him. They took him to the foot of Mount Tema in Hahaki, roughly the west of present-day Tottori, and said: 'There is a red boar on this mountain. We will drive it down; you wait below and catch it. If you fail, we will kill you.' Then they heated in fire a great stone shaped like a boar and rolled it down. Ōnamuji caught it, was burned fast to it and died. His mother went up weeping to heaven and begged Kami-musubi for help, and Kami-musubi sent down two women, Princess Cockle-Shell and Princess Clam, named for the ark-shell and the clam. Princess Cockle-Shell scraped powder from her shell and Princess Clam brought water, and they mixed them like a mother's milk and smeared it over him. He came to life again as a handsome young man and walked about. It was the first time he died and lived again.
sections.bodyZh: 八上比卖果然对八十神说：我不听你们的话，我要嫁给大穴牟迟。八十神大怒，商量要杀死大穴牟迟。他们把他带到伯伎国手间山的山脚下——伯伎国大致在今天鸟取县的西部——对他说：山上有一头红色的野猪，我们把它赶下来，你在下面等着抓住它。要是抓不住，就杀了你。他们在山上把一块像野猪那样大的石头用火烧得通红，推下山去。大穴牟迟去抓那块石头，被烧得粘在石头上死了。他的母亲哭着上天，向神产巢日神求救。神产巢日神派了两位女神下来：蚶贝比卖和蛤贝比卖，她们的名字就是赤贝和蛤蜊。蚶贝比卖刮下贝壳上的粉末，蛤贝比卖取来水，把两样东西调和成像母亲的乳汁一样的药，涂遍他的全身。大穴牟迟又活了过来，变成了一个英俊的年轻人，到处走动。这是他第一次死而复生。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十二节。
sections.headingEn: The red boar of Mount Tema

sections.bodyEn: Seeing him alive again, the Eighty Deities set another trap. They led Ōnamuji into the mountains, felled a great tree, drove a wedge into the cleft of the trunk, made him stand in the cleft, and then pulled out the wedge and crushed him to death. Again his mother searched for him weeping, found him, split the tree, took him out and restored him — the second time he had died and lived again. She said: 'If you stay here, you will be destroyed by the Eighty Deities in the end,' and sent him to the deity Oho-ya-biko, Chamberlain's Great-House-Prince, in the land of Ki, later called Kii. But the Eighty Deities pursued him there, fitting arrows to their bows and demanding him. Oho-ya-biko let him slip away through the fork of a tree, telling him: 'Go to the Nether-Distant-Land where Susanoo dwells. That great deity will surely counsel you.' So Ōnamuji left the living world to seek his ancestor.
sections.bodyZh: 八十神看见他又活了，再次设下圈套。他们把大穴牟迟带进山里，砍倒一棵大树，在树干的裂缝里打进一个楔子，让他站进裂缝中间，然后猛地拔掉楔子，把他夹死在树干里。母亲又一次哭着到处寻找，终于找到了他，劈开大树，把他取出来救活了。这已经是他第二次死而复生。母亲对他说：你再住在这里，终究会被八十神害死的。她把他送到木国——也就是后来的纪伊国——的大屋毘古神那里躲避，张伯伦把这位神的名字译作“大屋之王子”。可是八十神一路追到了木国，拉满了弓，向大屋毘古神要人。大屋毘古神就让大穴牟迟从一棵树的树杈之间悄悄逃走，对他说：你到须佐之男所在的根之坚洲国去吧，那位大神一定会为你出主意。大穴牟迟就这样离开了人间，去寻找自己的祖先。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十二节。

sections.bodyEn: The Nether-Distant-Land, the mother's land that Susanoo had once wept to go to, was now his dwelling. When Ōnamuji came to Susanoo's palace, Susanoo's daughter Suseri-bime came out; they looked at each other and were married at once. She went in and told her father: 'A very handsome deity has come.' Susanoo went out, looked at him and said: 'This is the Ugly Male of the Reed-Plains' — shiko-wo, literally ugly male, though some read it as a fierce one. He called him in, but made him sleep in a room full of snakes. Suseri-bime secretly gave her husband a snake-scarf, a long cloth worn over the shoulders, and said: 'When the snakes are about to bite you, wave this scarf three times to drive them off.' He did as she said, the snakes grew quiet, and he slept peacefully and came out unharmed in the morning. It was the first of Susanoo's trials; three more were to follow.
sections.bodyZh: 根之坚洲国——张伯伦译作“幽远之国”——就是当年须佐之男哭着要去的母亲之国，如今他住在这里。大穴牟迟来到须佐之男的宫殿，须佐之男的女儿须势理毘卖出来迎接，两人四目相对，一见钟情，当即结为夫妻。须势理毘卖回到殿里对父亲说：来了一位非常英俊的神。须佐之男出来一看，说：这是苇原色许男啊。“色许男”字面是“丑男子”，也有人理解为强悍的男子。须佐之男把他叫进来，却让他睡在满是毒蛇的蛇室里。须势理毘卖偷偷把一条驱蛇的领巾交给丈夫——领巾是一种披在肩上的长巾——对他说：蛇要咬你的时候，你就把这条领巾挥三下，把它们赶开。大穴牟迟照她的话做了，蛇都安静下来，他安安稳稳地睡了一夜，第二天平安走了出来。这是须佐之男给他的第一次考验，此后还有三次。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十三节。

sections.bodyEn: The next night Susanoo put him in a room full of centipedes and wasps. Again Suseri-bime gave him a scarf, which the text calls the centipede-and-wasp scarf, and taught him to wave it in danger as before, and again he came out unharmed. Susanoo's trials were not over. The great deity who had once run riot in High Heaven and been driven out by the gods now tested the young man who had come for his daughter, and in his eyes the youth had proved nothing yet. In the story it is Suseri-bime's wit and love that save Ōnamuji each time: she takes her husband's side and quietly works against her father's will. Women who step in at the decisive moment are not rare in the Kojiki; Toyotama-bime and Oto-tachibana-hime will do the same later on. Trial by trial, the young man once bullied by his brothers was becoming a deity fit to rule the land.
sections.bodyZh: 第二天晚上，须佐之男又让他睡在一间满是蜈蚣和马蜂的屋子里。须势理毘卖又交给他一条领巾，书中叫作“蜈蚣与蜂之比礼”，像上一次一样教他在危急的时候挥动。大穴牟迟又平安地度过了一夜，第二天照样走了出来。须佐之男的考验并没有到此为止。这位大神当年在高天原上也曾胡作非为，被众神驱逐出天界，如今轮到他来考验来娶自己女儿的年轻人。在这位暴躁的大神眼里，这个年轻人还远远没有证明自己。而在故事里，每一次真正救了大穴牟迟的，都是须势理毘卖的智慧与爱。她站在丈夫一边，悄悄地违背父亲的意愿；在《古事记》里，这样在关键时刻出手相助的女子并不少见，后面的丰玉毘卖和弟橘比卖也是如此。一次次的考验，也让这个曾被兄长们欺负的年轻人渐渐成为能统治国土的神。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十三节。
sections.headingEn: The room of centipedes and wasps

sections.bodyEn: Next Susanoo shot a whizzing arrow into a great moor and sent Ōnamuji to fetch it. When he was deep in the moor, Susanoo set fire to it all round. Ōnamuji could find no way out, until a mouse came and said: 'Inside, hollow-hollow; outside, narrow-narrow.' Understanding, he stamped on the ground, fell into a hole, and hid there while the fire passed over him. Soon the mouse brought him the whizzing arrow in its mouth; its feathers had been eaten by the mouse's children. Suseri-bime, thinking her husband dead, came weeping with the things for a funeral, and Susanoo, thinking the same, stood on the burned moor. But Ōnamuji came out with the arrow and presented it to him. The mouse's words in the original, uchi wa hora-hora, soto wa subu-subu, sound almost like a spell. In High Heaven the gods had drawn Amaterasu from her cave with fire and laughter; here it is a small mouse in a burrow that saves Ōnamuji.
sections.bodyZh: 须佐之男又把一支鸣镝——箭头上装着中空的响器、射出去会呼啸作响的箭——射进一片大草原，命令大穴牟迟去把箭找回来。等他走进草原深处，须佐之男就从四面放火，烧起了整片原野。火从四面围上来，大穴牟迟找不到出路。这时一只老鼠出来对他说：里面空荡荡，外面窄窄窄。他明白了老鼠的意思，用脚一踩地面，就掉进了一个地洞，躲在里面，大火从头顶烧了过去。不久，老鼠又把那支鸣镝衔来交给他，箭上的羽毛已经被小老鼠们啃光了。须势理毘卖以为丈夫已经死了，哭着拿着办丧事的器具来到原野上；须佐之男也以为他死了，走出来站在烧过的原野上。大穴牟迟却拿着那支箭走了出来，把箭献给了须佐之男。老鼠的那两句话，在原文里是“内者富良富良，外者须夫须夫”，读起来就像一句咒语。在高天原上，众神曾用火与笑声把天照大神请出岩户；在这里，救下大穴牟迟的却是一只地洞里的小老鼠。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十三节。
sections.headingEn: The burning moor and the mouse

sections.bodyEn: Susanoo took him back into the house, called him into a great room eight fathoms wide, and made him pick the lice from his head. But the creatures on Susanoo's head were centipedes. Suseri-bime secretly gave her husband berries of the muku tree, small dark fruit that look like crushed insects when chewed, and some red earth. Ōnamuji chewed the berries and spat them out with the red earth, and Susanoo, thinking he was biting the centipedes to pieces and spitting them out, felt fond of him in his heart — the text's own words — and fell asleep. From the snake room to the centipedes and wasps, the burning moor and now the 'lice', each trial was more dangerous than the last, and each was quietly undone by his daughter. It was the last trial, and Ōnamuji's chance to escape. Susanoo, who once slew the eight-forked serpent in Izumo and saved Kushinada-hime, now lay asleep with his fate in the young man's hands.
sections.bodyZh: 须佐之男把大穴牟迟带回家里，叫进一间八寻宽的大屋子，让他替自己捉头上的虱子。大穴牟迟一看，须佐之男头上爬的根本不是虱子，而是一只只蜈蚣。须势理毘卖悄悄递给丈夫一把椋树的果实和一些红土。椋树的果实是黑紫色的小果子，嚼碎了就像碾碎的虫子。大穴牟迟把椋树果放进嘴里咬碎，再和着红土一起吐出来。须佐之男以为他在把蜈蚣一只只咬碎吐掉，原文说他“心里觉得这个年轻人可爱”，就放心地睡着了。从蛇室、蜈蚣与蜂之室，到火烧原野，再到头上的“虱子”，须佐之男的考验一次比一次危险，而每一次都被他的女儿悄悄化解。这是最后一次考验，也是大穴牟迟逃走的机会。须佐之男曾经在出云斩杀八岐大蛇、救下栉名田比卖，如今他睡着时，命运却交到了这个年轻人手里。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十三节。

sections.bodyEn: While Susanoo slept, Ōnamuji tied his hair to the rafters of the room, blocked the door with a rock that would take five hundred men to move, took his wife Suseri-bime on his back, and fled carrying Susanoo's great sword of life, his bow and arrows of life, and his heavenly speaking lute. The lute brushed against a tree and the earth resounded. Susanoo woke and pulled the whole house down with his hair; by the time he had untied it from the rafters they were far away. He pursued them to the Even Pass of Yomi and, gazing after them, called out: 'With the sword of life and the bow of life drive your brothers down the slopes and into the river-beds! Become Ōkuninushi, become Utsushi-kunitama, make my daughter Suseri-bime your chief wife, and at the foot of Mount Uka set your palace pillars deep in the bedrock and raise your cross-beams to the Plain of High Heaven, and dwell there, you rascal!' He did so, drove away the Eighty Deities and began to make the land. Princess Yakami came to him too, but in fear of the chief wife she left her child in the fork of a tree and went home.
sections.bodyZh: 大穴牟迟趁须佐之男睡着，把他的头发一缕缕绑在屋子的椽子上，用一块要五百个人才拉得动的大石头堵住屋门，背起妻子须势理毘卖，带上须佐之男的生太刀、生弓矢和天诏琴，逃了出去。逃跑时天诏琴碰到了树，大地都震动起来。须佐之男被惊醒，一拉头发，把整座屋子都拉倒了。等他把绑在椽子上的头发解开，两人已经逃得很远。须佐之男一直追到黄泉比良坂，远远望着他们喊道：用你拿走的生太刀和生弓矢，把你的兄弟们赶到山坡下、河滩上去！你要成为大国主神，成为宇都志国玉神，让我的女儿须势理毘卖做你的正妻，在宇迦山下把宫柱深深地立在地底的岩石上，把屋梁高高地架到高天原，住在那里吧，你这家伙！大穴牟迟照他的话赶走了八十神，开始造国。八上比卖也来到他身边，但她害怕正妻须势理毘卖，把生下的孩子夹在树杈之间就回去了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十三节。
sections.headingEn: The sword of life, the bow and the speaking lute
sections.headingZh: 生太刀、生弓矢与天诏琴

sections.bodyEn: As Yachihoko, the Deity of Eight Thousand Spears, he went to distant Koshi to woo Princess Nunakawa. Standing at her door he sang how he had heard of a wise and beautiful woman in Koshi, how he had come from afar and stood pulling at her door until dawn while the birds of the forest began to cry. She sang back through the door: be not impatient; when night comes I will be yours. The next night they were married. His chief wife Suseri-bime was deeply jealous. As he was about to go up from Izumo to Yamato, one hand on the saddle and one foot in the stirrup, he sang to her: of three robes he had tried, the black was not right and the kingfisher-blue was not right, but the robe dyed with the juice of the dye-plant sown in the mountain fields suited him; and she would weep like a single clump of grass on the mountain. Suseri-bime came to him lifting a great wine-cup and sang: you are a man and have wives wherever you go, but I am a woman and have no husband but you. They pledged each other with the cup, their hands on each other's necks, and the text says they are at peace together to this day.
sections.bodyZh: 以八千矛神为名的大国主，又到遥远的越国去向沼河比卖求婚。他站在她家门前唱歌，唱自己怎样听说越国有一位聪明美丽的女子，怎样远道而来，拉着门板等到天明，林中的鸟已经开始啼叫。沼河比卖隔着门回唱：请你不要着急，等到夜里，我就会是你的。第二天夜里，两人结为夫妻。正妻须势理毘卖为此十分嫉妒。大国主准备从出云上大和去，一只手搭在马鞍上，一只脚踏在马镫里，唱歌给她听：他换了三套衣服，黑色的不合适，翠鸟一样青色的也不合适，最后换上山田里的染料染成的衣服，才觉得合适；又说，你将来会像山上孤零零的芒草一样哭泣。须势理毘卖举起大酒杯走到他身边，唱道：你是男子，到处都有妻子，而我是女子，除了你没有别的丈夫。两人用酒杯立下誓约，手搭着彼此的脖子，从此和睦相处，书中说他们直到今天仍安然相守。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十四至二十五节。
sections.headingEn: The songs of the Deity of Eight Thousand Spears

sections.bodyEn: Once, at Cape Miho in Izumo, Ōkuninushi saw a deity riding the crests of the waves in a little boat made from a seed-pod of the kagami plant, clothed in the whole stripped skin of some small creature — the character is read by some as a goose and by others as a moth. Asked his name, he did not answer, and none of the attendant deities knew it. Then a toad said: 'Kuyebiko will surely know.' Kuyebiko, called for, said: 'This is Sukuna-bikona, the son of Kami-musubi.' When Ōkuninushi asked Kami-musubi, she said: 'He is truly my child, the one of my children who slipped through between my fingers. Be brothers, and make and consolidate the land together.' So the two made the land together, until Sukuna-bikona crossed over the sea to the Eternal Land. Kuyebiko, the text says, is the scarecrow in the fields today, who cannot walk but knows everything under heaven.
sections.bodyZh: 有一天，大国主在出云的美保岬，看见一位神乘着用萝藦豆荚做成的小船，踏着浪花漂过来，身上穿着用整张剥下来的小动物的皮做的衣服——原文的字一说是鹅，一说指飞蛾。大国主问他的名字，他不回答；问随从的众神，谁也不知道。这时，一只蛤蟆说：久延毘古一定知道。大国主召来久延毘古，久延毘古说：这是神产巢日神的儿子少名毘古那神。大国主去问神产巢日神，神产巢日神说：他确实是我的孩子，是我那些孩子中从我的指缝间漏下去的那一个。你们两个结为兄弟，一起把国土造好、巩固起来吧。从此，大国主和少名毘古那一起造国。后来，少名毘古那渡海去了常世国。书中说，那位知道他名字的久延毘古，就是今天田里的稻草人，虽然不能走路，却知道天下所有的事情。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十七节。

sections.bodyEn: With Sukuna-bikona gone, Ōkuninushi said in sorrow: 'How can I make this land alone? With what deity should I make it?' Then a light shone over the sea, and a deity came illuminating it and said: 'If you will worship me well, I will make the land together with you. Otherwise it cannot be made.' Ōkuninushi asked how he should worship him, and the deity said: 'Worship me on the eastern mountain of the green fence of Yamato.' This, says the text, is the deity who dwells on Mount Mimoro, the mountain now called Miwa in Nara. The Kojiki gives the deity no name here; a variant in the Nihon shoki says that the deity from the sea was Ōkuninushi's own spirit of good fortune and wondrous spirit. Here the making of the land rests. The text goes on to list the children of the Great-Harvest Deity, and then the deities of the Plain of High Heaven turn their attention to the land below. The mountain remains, throughout the later stories, a mountain where a deity dwells.
sections.bodyZh: 少名毘古那走了，大国主忧愁地说：我一个人怎么能把这片国土造好呢？要和哪一位神一起造才好？这时，海面上亮起光来，一位神照着海面过来，说：你要是好好地供奉我，我就和你一起把国土造成。不然的话，国土是造不成的。大国主问：那么，要怎样供奉你呢？那位神说：你把我供奉在大和那青翠如垣墙的群山东边的山上。书中说，这就是住在御诸山上的神。御诸山也就是今天奈良的三轮山。《古事记》在这里没有写出这位神的名字；《日本书纪》的一段异文则说，这位从海上来的神是大国主自己的“幸魂奇魂”。至此，大国主造国的故事告一段落。书中接着列出了大年神的子孙，然后，高天原上的众神开始关心下界的这片国土了。这座山在后来的故事里一直被视为神所居住的山。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十八节。

sections.bodyEn: Amaterasu declared that the Luxuriant Reed-Plains Land of Fresh Rice-Ears should be ruled by her son Ame-no-oshi-ho-mimi. He looked down from the Floating Bridge of Heaven, said that the land below was in a great uproar, and went back to report. Takami-musubi and Amaterasu assembled the deities by the Tranquil River of Heaven, and on Omoikane's counsel they sent Ame-no-hohi, who curried favour with Ōkuninushi and sent no report for three years. Next they sent Ame-no-Wakahiko with the heavenly deer-bow and feathered arrows. He married Ōkuninushi's daughter Shitateru-hime, schemed to take the land for himself, and sent no report for eight years. The deities sent a pheasant, Naki-me, to question him. She perched on the cassia tree at his gate and spoke the heavenly deities' words. Urged by Ama-no-sagu-me, he shot the pheasant with the heavenly bow; the arrow passed through her and flew up to Takagi-no-kami by the Tranquil River. Seeing blood on its feathers, Takagi said: 'If Ame-no-Wakahiko has not disobeyed and shot at evil deities, let this arrow not strike him; if he has an evil heart, let him die by it,' and threw it back down through the hole it had made. It struck Ame-no-Wakahiko in the chest as he lay on his bed, and he died. Hence, says the text, the saying 'beware a returning arrow'.
sections.bodyZh: 天照大神说：丰苇原的瑞穗国应该由我的儿子天忍穗耳命来统治。天忍穗耳命站在天之浮桥上往下一看，说：下面吵闹得很！就回来报告了。高御产巢日神和天照大神在天安河边召集众神商议，思金神出主意，先派了天菩比神下去，他却去讨好大国主，三年都没有回来复命。于是又派天若日子，赐给他天之麻迦古弓和天之波波矢。天若日子一到下界，就娶了大国主的女儿下照比卖，想把这片国土据为己有，八年都没有复命。众神又派了一只名叫鸣女的雉鸡去问他。雉鸡停在天若日子门前的桂树上，传达了天神的问话。天佐具卖劝他射死这只鸟，天若日子就用天神赐的弓箭射穿了雉鸡，箭一直飞到天安河边高木神的面前。高木神看见箭羽上有血，说：如果天若日子没有违命，射的是恶神，这支箭就不要射中他；如果他有邪心，就让他死于此箭。他把箭从箭孔投回去，正射中躺在床上的天若日子的胸口，天若日子当场死去。书中说，“当心还矢”这句话就由此而来。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十至三十一节。

sections.bodyEn: Last, the deities sent Takemikazuchi, with Ame-no-tori-fune. The two came down to the little shore of Inasa in Izumo. Takemikazuchi drew his ten-grasp sword, stood it upside down on the crest of a wave, sat cross-legged on its point and asked Ōkuninushi: 'Amaterasu and Takagi-no-kami have sent us to ask: the Central Land of Reed-Plains that you rule is the land the heavenly deity's child should rule. What is your mind?' Ōkuninushi said: 'I cannot answer. My son Yae-Kotoshironushi will answer, but he has gone to Cape Miho to hunt birds and fish.' Fetched, Kotoshironushi said: 'I obey; offer this land to the heavenly deity's child.' He trod on his boat to overturn it, clapped his hands in the heavenly backward clap, turned the boat into a green fence and hid within it. Then another son, Takeminakata, came carrying a thousand-draught rock on his fingertips and challenged Takemikazuchi to a trial of strength. When he grasped Takemikazuchi's hand it turned into an icicle and then into a sword-blade; Takemikazuchi grasped his in return like a young reed, crushed it and flung it away. Takeminakata fled to the sea of Suwa in Shinano and begged for his life, vowing never to leave it and not to go against his father or Kotoshironushi. At last Ōkuninushi said: 'Let this land be offered. Only build me a dwelling with pillars set deep in the bedrock and cross-beams raised to the Plain of High Heaven, and I will retire into the winding ways.' A palace was built on the shore of Tagishi in Izumo, and Takemikazuchi went back up to report.
sections.bodyZh: 众神最后派出了建御雷神，由天鸟船神陪同。两位神降落到出云国伊那佐的小滨，建御雷神拔出十拳剑，剑尖朝上倒插在浪头上，盘腿坐在剑尖上，问大国主：天照大神和高木神派我们来问你：你统治的苇原中国，是天神之子应当统治的国土，你意下如何？大国主说：我不能回答，我的儿子八重事代主神会回答，可他到美保岬打鸟钓鱼去了。天鸟船神把事代主找来，事代主说：遵命，把这国土献给天神之子吧。说完踏翻了自己的船，拍出“天之逆手”，把船变成青柴垣，藏身其中。另一个儿子建御名方神用指尖托着千引石走来，要和建御雷比力气。他一抓建御雷的手，那只手就变成了冰柱，又变成了剑刃；建御雷反过来抓住他的手，像抓一根嫩芦苇一样捏碎扔开。建御名方逃到信浓的州羽海，求饶说：我决不离开这里，也不违背父亲和事代主的话。大国主终于说：这片国土就献出去吧。只请为我建一座宫殿，宫柱深深立在地底岩石上，屋梁高高架到高天原，我就隐退在弯弯曲曲的道路深处。于是人们在出云的多艺志小滨建起了宫殿，建御雷神回到天上复命。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十二节。
sections.headingEn: Takemikazuchi and the yielding of the land

stories.summaryEn: With the land yielded, Amaterasu's grandson Ninigi is sent down. At the heavenly crossroads a shining deity, Sarutahiko, is questioned by Ame-no-Uzume and offers to guide the descent. Ninigi comes down on the peak of Takachiho in Himuka with five attendant deities, the jewels, the mirror and the Kusanagi sword. He marries Konohana-sakuya-hime, daughter of the mountain deity, but sends back her ugly elder sister Iwanaga-hime, so the lives of his descendants are as brief as blossoms. Doubted by her husband after conceiving in a single night, Konohana-sakuya-hime gives birth inside a burning hall to three sons. The youngest, Hoori, the Luck of the Mountains, loses his brother's fish-hook in the sea; he sails in a bamboo boat to the sea deity's palace, marries Toyotama-bime, recovers the hook from a sea-bream's throat and returns with the tide jewels to subdue his brother. Toyotama-bime gives birth on the shore in a hut thatched with cormorant feathers, is seen in her true form as a great wani, and closes the sea-road behind her.
stories.summaryZh: 国土让出以后，天照大神的孙子迩迩艺命奉命降临。天之八衢上站着放光的猿田毘古神，天宇受卖命上前问话，他自愿为天孙引路。迩迩艺命带着五位随从神、勾玉、镜子和草薙剑，降落在日向的高千穗峰。他娶了大山津见神的女儿木花之佐久夜毘卖，却把丑陋的姐姐石长比卖送了回去，于是天孙子孙的寿命像花一样短暂。木花之佐久夜毘卖一夜受孕，被丈夫怀疑，就在火中生下三个儿子。小儿子山幸彦火远理命借来哥哥海幸彦的鱼钩，弄丢在海里；他乘竹笼小船来到海神之宫，娶了丰玉毘卖，从鲷鱼喉中找回鱼钩，带着潮盈珠与潮干珠回来降服了哥哥。丰玉毘卖在海边鸬鹚羽毛盖的产屋里生下孩子，被丈夫看见了大鳄的真身，从此关闭海路回到海中。
stories.titleZh: 古事记 · 第四部 天孙降临与海神之宫

claims.statement: Kojiki Section XXXIII says that when the land was reported pacified, Ame-no-oshi-ho-mimi proposed his newborn son Ninigi in his place, and Amaterasu and Takagi-no-kami commanded Ninigi to descend and rule the Land of Fresh Rice-Ears.

Kojiki Section XXXIII says that a deity shining up to High Heaven and down to the Central Land stood at the heavenly crossroads, and when Ame-no-Uzume questioned him he named himself the earthly deity Sarutahiko, come to guide the August Grandchild.

Kojiki Section XXXIII says Amaterasu sent five chiefs of companies with Ninigi and gave him the curved jewels, the mirror and the Kusanagi sword, charging him to reverence the mirror as her own spirit.

Kojiki Sections XXXIII–XXXIV say Ninigi pushed through the eight-fold clouds and descended on the peak of Kuji-furu-take of Takachiho in Himuka, called the place exceedingly good, and built his palace there.

Kojiki Sections XXXV–XXXVI say Ame-no-Uzume escorted Sarutahiko home and took his name for the Duchesses of Saru, that Sarutahiko drowned when a shell caught his hand at Azaka, and that she slit the mouth of the sea-slug that would not answer.

Kojiki Section XXXVII says Ōyamatsumi sent both his daughters to Ninigi, and when Ninigi returned the ugly Iwanaga-hime and kept Konohana-sakuya-hime, he declared that the lives of the heavenly deity's descendants would be as brief as blossoms.
Kojiki Section XXXVIII says that when Ninigi doubted the child conceived in one night, Konohana-sakuya-hime gave birth inside a sealed, burning doorless hall to Hoderi, Hosuseri and Hoori.

Kojiki Section XXXIX says Hoori persuaded his brother Hoderi to exchange their gear, lost the fish-hook at sea, and could not make his brother accept five hundred or a thousand hooks forged from his sword in its place.

Kojiki Section XL says the salt deity Shio-tsuchi set Hoori in a tightly woven bamboo boat and told him to follow the current to the sea deity's palace built like fish-scales and sit in the cassia tree by its well.

Kojiki Section XL says Hoori spat a jewel into the vessel of Toyotama-bime's maid at the well, Toyotama-bime fell in love with him at sight, and the sea deity welcomed him on layered rugs and gave her to him in marriage.

Kojiki Sections XL–XLI say the sea deity found the hook in a sea-bream's throat, gave Hoori the tide-flowing and tide-ebbing jewels with counsel, and that Hoori used them to subdue Hoderi, who vowed to be his guard.

Kojiki Sections XLII–XLIII say Toyotama-bime gave birth in an unfinished hut thatched with cormorant feathers, was seen by Hoori in her true form as an eight-fathom wani, and in shame closed the sea-boundary and returned to the sea, leaving her son Ugaya-fuki-aezu.

events.summaryEn: Takemikazuchi went back up and reported that the Central Land of Reed-Plains had been pacified.
events.summaryZh: 建御雷神回到天上，报告苇原中国已经平定。

events.summaryEn: As Ninigi was about to descend, at the heavenly eight-forked crossroads stood a deity whose light shone up to the Plain of High Heaven and down to the Central Land of Reed-Plains.
events.summaryZh: 迩迩艺命正要降临的时候，在天之八衢——天上八条道路交会的地方——站着一位神，他身上发出的光，向上照亮了高天原，向下照亮了苇原中国。

events.summaryEn: Amaterasu assigned to Ninigi five attendant deities, the five chiefs of companies: Ame-no-koyane, Futo-tama, Ame-no-Uzume, Ishi-kori-dome and Tama-no-oya, all of whom had played their part before the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling.
events.summaryZh: 天照大神为迩迩艺命安排了五位随从的神，称为“五伴绪”：天儿屋命、布刀玉命、天宇受卖命、伊斯许理度卖命和玉祖命，他们都是当年在天之岩户前出过力的神。
events.titleEn: The regalia and the five chiefs

events.summaryEn: Ninigi left the heavenly rock-seat, pushed apart the eight-fold heavenly clouds, and with mighty way-dividing made his way down by the Floating Bridge of Heaven to the peak of Kuji-furu-take of Takachiho in Himuka in Tsukushi.
events.summaryZh: 迩迩艺命离开了天上的岩座，分开天上层层叠叠的八重云，威风凛凛地开出一条道路，经过天之浮桥，降落在筑紫日向的高千穗的久士布流多气峰上。

events.summaryEn: Ninigi said to Ame-no-Uzume: 'Escort Sarutahiko, who served as our guide, back home.
events.summaryZh: 迩迩艺命对天宇受卖命说：你送那位为我们引路的猿田毘古神回去吧。
events.titleEn: The Duchesses of Saru and the sea-slug

events.summaryEn: At the cape of Kasasa, Ninigi met a beautiful maiden and asked whose daughter she was.
events.summaryZh: 迩迩艺命在笠沙的岬角遇见一位美丽的少女，问她是谁的女儿。
events.titleZh: 木花之佐久夜毘卖与石长比卖

events.summaryEn: After some time Konohana-sakuya-hime came to Ninigi and said: 'I am with child and my time is near.
events.summaryZh: 过了些日子，木花之佐久夜毘卖来对迩迩艺命说：我怀孕了，就要生产了。

events.summaryEn: Hoderi became the Luck of the Sea, catching fish broad of fin and narrow of fin with his hook; Hoori became the Luck of the Mountains, taking beasts rough of hair and soft of hair with his bow.
events.summaryZh: 火照命成了海幸彦，用鱼钩捕捞海里大大小小的鱼；火远理命成了山幸彦，用弓箭猎取山里大大小小的野兽。
events.titleEn: The luck of the sea and the luck of the mountains

events.summaryEn: As Hoori wept on the seashore, the salt deity Shio-tsuchi came and asked: 'Why do you weep, Sky's Sun-Height?' He told the story of the hook.
events.summaryZh: 火远理命在海边哭泣，这时盐椎神来了，问他：天津日高日子，你为什么哭？
events.titleEn: The salt deity and the road to the sea palace

events.summaryEn: A maid of the sea deity's daughter Toyotama-bime came to the well with a jewelled vessel to draw water.
events.summaryZh: 海神的女儿丰玉毘卖的侍女，拿着玉做的水器来井边打水，看见井水里映出了光，抬头一看，树上坐着一位英俊的男子，觉得十分奇怪。
events.titleEn: The jewel in the vessel and the sea deity's daughter

events.summaryEn: After three years Hoori remembered the past and heaved a great sigh.
events.summaryZh: 三年过去，火远理命想起往事，长长地叹了一口气。

events.summaryEn: Later Toyotama-bime herself came out of the sea and said to Hoori: 'I am with child and my time has come.
events.summaryZh: 后来，丰玉毘卖亲自从海里出来，对火远理命说：我怀孕了，现在就要生了。
events.titleEn: The birth-hut thatched with cormorant feathers

versions.labelEn: Kojiki, Chamberlain translation, Sections XXXIII–XLIII (long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十三至四十三节（长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 天孙降临的诏命、天之八衢的猿田毘古、神器与五伴绪、降临高千穗、猿女君与海参、木花之佐久夜毘卖与石长比卖、火中生子、海幸山幸、海神之宫、井边的玉、潮盈珠与潮干珠、鸬鹚羽的产屋
versions.rightsNote: 张伯伦 1882 年译本属公共领域；本站发布按节顺序的独立讲述，神名采用现代通行读法。

sections.bodyEn: Takemikazuchi went back up and reported that the Central Land of Reed-Plains had been pacified. Amaterasu and Takagi-no-kami — Takami-musubi — then commanded Amaterasu's son Ame-no-oshi-ho-mimi: 'The land is now pacified; go down and rule it as we entrusted it to you.' He answered: 'While I was making ready to descend, a son was born to me, named Ame-nigishi-kuni-nigishi-ama-tsu-hi-daka-hiko-ho-no-ninigi. This child should be sent down.' The child was born of Ame-no-oshi-ho-mimi and Takagi-no-kami's daughter Yorozu-hata-toyo-aki-tsu-shi-hime, so that he was grandson both of Amaterasu and of Takagi. The two great deities commanded Ninigi: 'This Luxuriant Reed-Plains Land of Fresh Rice-Ears is the land you are to rule. Descend as commanded.' Chamberlain translates the long name word by word, roughly Heaven's-Plenty-Earth's-Plenty-Heaven's-Sun-Height-Prince-Rice-ear-Ruddy-Plenty. This August Grandchild is one of the heroes of this part.
sections.bodyZh: 建御雷神回到天上，报告苇原中国已经平定。天照大神和高木神——也就是高御产巢日神——就命令天照大神的儿子天忍穗耳命：现在国土已经平定了，你就照原先的委托，降下去统治那片国土吧。天忍穗耳命回答说：我正在准备降临的时候，生了一个儿子，名叫天迩岐志国迩岐志天津日高日子番能迩迩艺命。应该派这个孩子降下去。这个孩子是天忍穗耳命和高木神的女儿万幡丰秋津师比卖命所生，也就是说，他同时是天照大神和高木神的孙子。于是两位大神对迩迩艺命下令：这丰苇原的瑞穗国，是交给你统治的国土。你就照着命令降下去吧。张伯伦把迩迩艺命的长名字逐字译出，大意是“天地丰饶、天日高照的稻穗丰熟之王子”。这位“天孙”，就是这一部故事的主人公之一。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十三节。

sections.bodyEn: As Ninigi was about to descend, at the heavenly eight-forked crossroads stood a deity whose light shone up to the Plain of High Heaven and down to the Central Land of Reed-Plains. Amaterasu and Takagi-no-kami commanded Ame-no-Uzume: 'Though you are a delicate woman, you are a deity who can face down any deity. Go and ask him who stands in the way where our child is to descend.' She was the goddess who had once danced before the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling and set the gods roaring with laughter. When she asked, the deity answered: 'I am an earthly deity named Sarutahiko. I heard that the child of the heavenly deities was to descend, and I have come to meet him and to serve as his guide.' The shining deity at the crossroads had come not to bar the way but to lead it. Chamberlain renders his name the Deity Prince of Saruta. The text says Ame-no-Uzume was a deity who could outface any deity, which is why she was sent. The Kojiki does not describe Sarutahiko; a variant in the Nihon shoki says his nose was seven hands long, his back more than seven feet tall, and his eyes shone like an eight-hand mirror.
sections.bodyZh: 迩迩艺命正要降临的时候，在天之八衢——天上八条道路交会的地方——站着一位神，他身上发出的光，向上照亮了高天原，向下照亮了苇原中国。天照大神和高木神命令天宇受卖神说：你虽然是个柔弱的女子，却是一位能与任何神面对面而不退缩的神。你去问问他：天神的儿子要降临，是谁在这里挡路？天宇受卖神就是当年在天之岩户前狂舞、逗得众神大笑的那位女神。她上前去问，那位神回答说：我是国津神，名叫猿田毘古神。我听说天神的儿子要降临，所以前来迎接，愿意做天孙的向导。原来这位在路口放光的神，并不是来阻拦，而是来引路的。张伯伦把他的名字译作“猿田之王子神”。原文说天宇受卖命是“与神相对而能胜过对方”的神，所以众神派她去问话。《古事记》没有细写猿田毘古的样子；《日本书纪》的一段异文则说他鼻长七咫，背长七尺多，眼睛像八咫镜一样闪闪发亮。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十三节。

sections.bodyEn: Amaterasu assigned to Ninigi five attendant deities, the five chiefs of companies: Ame-no-koyane, Futo-tama, Ame-no-Uzume, Ishi-kori-dome and Tama-no-oya, all of whom had played their part before the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling. She gave him the curved jewels and the mirror that had drawn her out of the rock-dwelling, and the Kusanagi sword that Susanoo had taken from the serpent's tail, and sent with him Omoikane, Ame-no-tajikarao and Ame-no-iwato-wake. She said: 'Regard this mirror as my august spirit, and reverence it as you would reverence me,' and: 'Omoikane, take charge of the rites and carry on the government.' The text adds that these two are worshipped at the shrine of Isuzu, the shrine at Ise. Mirror, jewels and sword are here placed together in the hands of the August Grandchild for the first time in the story. The text also records the descendants of the five chiefs: Ame-no-koyane is ancestor of the Nakatomi, Futo-tama of the Imbe, Ame-no-Uzume of the Saru-me, Ishi-kori-dome of the mirror-makers and Tama-no-oya of the jewel-makers; Ame-no-iwato-wake, also called Kushi-iwa-mado and Toyo-iwa-mado, is the deity who guards the palace gates.
sections.bodyZh: 天照大神为迩迩艺命安排了五位随从的神，称为“五伴绪”：天儿屋命、布刀玉命、天宇受卖命、伊斯许理度卖命和玉祖命，他们都是当年在天之岩户前出过力的神。天照大神又把当年把她从岩户里引出来的八尺勾玉和镜子，以及须佐之男从大蛇尾中得到的草薙剑交给他，还派了思金神、天手力男神和天石门别神同行。天照大神说：这面镜子，你要把它当作我的御魂，像祭拜我一样祭拜它。又说：思金神，你要承担起祭祀的事务，掌管政事。书中接着说，这两位神如今在五十铃宫受到祭祀，也就是伊势的神宫。故事里的镜、玉、剑，在这里第一次被一起交到天孙手中。书中还一一记下了五位随从神的后人：天儿屋命是中臣连的祖先，布刀玉命是忌部首的祖先，天宇受卖命是猿女君的祖先，伊斯许理度卖命是作镜连的祖先，玉祖命是玉祖连的祖先；天石门别神又名栉石窗神、丰石窗神，是守护宫门的神。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十三节。
sections.headingEn: The regalia and the five chiefs

sections.bodyEn: Ninigi left the heavenly rock-seat, pushed apart the eight-fold heavenly clouds, and with mighty way-dividing made his way down by the Floating Bridge of Heaven to the peak of Kuji-furu-take of Takachiho in Himuka in Tsukushi. Ame-no-oshi-hi and Ama-tsu-kume went before him carrying heavenly rock-quivers, girded with mallet-headed swords, holding heavenly bows and true-deer arrows; the text names them as ancestors of the Ōtomo and Kume clans. Ninigi said: 'This place faces Kara; a straight road runs through to the cape of Kasasa; it is a land where the morning sun shines straight and the evening sun shines bright. This is an exceedingly good place.' There he set his palace pillars deep in the bedrock, raised its cross-beams to the Plain of High Heaven, and dwelt. So the road from High Heaven to the human world was travelled. Where the peak of Takachiho in Himuka lies is disputed — later traditions point to Takachiho in Miyazaki or to the Takachiho peak of the Kirishima mountains — and the Kojiki itself gives no further clue.
sections.bodyZh: 迩迩艺命离开了天上的岩座，分开天上层层叠叠的八重云，威风凛凛地开出一条道路，经过天之浮桥，降落在筑紫日向的高千穗的久士布流多气峰上。天忍日命和天津久米命背着天上的石箭袋，佩着头椎大刀，拿着天上的波士弓和真鹿儿矢，走在天孙的前面开路；书中说，他们是大伴连和久米直两族的祖先。迩迩艺命站在那里说：这里正对着韩国，有一条笔直的路通到笠沙的岬角，早晨的太阳直直照来，傍晚的太阳也照得明亮。所以这里是非常好的地方。他在那里把宫柱深深地立在地底的岩石上，把屋梁高高地架到高天原，住了下来。从高天原到人间的这一段路，就这样走完了。日向的高千穗峰究竟在哪里，后世有宫崎县的高千穗和雾岛山的高千穗峰等不同说法，《古事记》本身没有给出更多线索。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十三至三十四节。

sections.bodyEn: Ninigi said to Ame-no-Uzume: 'Escort Sarutahiko, who served as our guide, back home. Since it was you who learned his name, take his name and serve him.' Therefore, says the text, the women of the Saru-me clan bear the name of the male deity Sarutahiko and are called the Duchesses of Saru. Later, while fishing at Azaka, Sarutahiko had his hand caught by a hirabu shell and sank and drowned in the sea; as he sank to the bottom, as the water bubbled, and as the bubbles burst, three deities were born. Ame-no-Uzume, coming back from escorting him, gathered all the fishes broad of fin and narrow of fin and asked: 'Will you serve the child of the heavenly deities?' All said they would — except the sea-slug, which said nothing. 'This is a mouth that gives no answer!' said Ame-no-Uzume, and slit its mouth with her small knife. That, says the text, is why the sea-slug's mouth is slit to this day. The text adds that in every reign a share of the first fruits of the sea sent from Shima is granted to the Saru-me.
sections.bodyZh: 迩迩艺命对天宇受卖命说：你送那位为我们引路的猿田毘古神回去吧。是你把他的名字问出来的，你就承受他的名字，侍奉他吧。所以，书中说，猿女君一族的女子都带着猿田毘古这位男神的名字，被称为“猿女”。后来，猿田毘古神在阿邪诃打鱼，手被比良夫贝夹住，沉进海里淹死了：他沉到海底时，生出了底度久御魂；海水冒泡时，生出了都夫多都御魂；水泡破开时，生出了阿和佐久御魂。天宇受卖命送猿田毘古回去以后返回，把大大小小的鱼都召集起来，问它们：你们愿意侍奉天神的儿子吗？鱼们都说：愿意侍奉。只有海参一声不吭。天宇受卖命说：这张嘴就是不肯回答的嘴！就用小刀把海参的嘴割开了。所以，书中说，海参的嘴至今仍是裂开的。书中还说，此后每一代天皇在位的时候，志摩国进献的海产初物都要分一份给猿女君。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十五至三十六节。
sections.headingEn: The Duchesses of Saru and the sea-slug

sections.bodyEn: At the cape of Kasasa, Ninigi met a beautiful maiden and asked whose daughter she was. She said: 'I am the daughter of the great mountain deity Ōyamatsumi; my name is Kamu-ata-tsu-hime, also Konohana-sakuya-hime' — the Princess Blossoming like the Flowers of the Trees. He said: 'I wish to marry you. What do you say?' She answered: 'I cannot say; my father Ōyamatsumi will answer.' When Ninigi sent to ask, Ōyamatsumi was delighted, and sent her elder sister Iwanaga-hime with her, together with a hundred tables of gifts. But Iwanaga-hime was very ugly; Ninigi took fright at the sight of her and sent her back, keeping only the younger sister, with whom he spent one night. Ōyamatsumi, ashamed at Iwanaga-hime's return, said: 'I sent both daughters for a purpose: with Iwanaga-hime, the lives of the heavenly deity's descendants would endure like the rocks through snow and wind; with Konohana-sakuya-hime, they would flourish like the blossoms of the trees. Since you have kept only Konohana-sakuya-hime, their lives will be as brief as the blossoms of the trees.' That, says the text, is why the lives of the Heavenly Sovereigns down to this day are not long.
sections.bodyZh: 迩迩艺命在笠沙的岬角遇见一位美丽的少女，问她是谁的女儿。少女说：我是大山津见神的女儿，名叫神阿多都比卖，又叫木花之佐久夜毘卖——意思是“像树上的花一样灿烂盛开的公主”。迩迩艺命说：我想娶你，你看怎样？她说：我不能回答，我的父亲大山津见神会回答。迩迩艺命派人去求婚，大山津见神非常高兴，让她的姐姐石长比卖和她一同出嫁，还带上了满满一百桌的礼物。可是石长比卖长得非常丑陋，迩迩艺命一见就害怕，把她送了回去，只留下了妹妹木花之佐久夜毘卖，与她共度一夜。大山津见神因为石长比卖被送回而深感羞耻，说：我把两个女儿一起献上，是有用意的：有石长比卖在，天神子孙的寿命就会像岩石一样长久，不论风雪；有木花之佐久夜毘卖在，他们就会像树上的花一样繁荣。如今你只留下了木花之佐久夜毘卖，天神子孙的寿命就会像树上的花一样短暂。书中说，所以直到今天，历代天皇的寿命都不长久。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十七节。
sections.headingZh: 木花之佐久夜毘卖与石长比卖

sections.bodyEn: After some time Konohana-sakuya-hime came to Ninigi and said: 'I am with child and my time is near. The child of a heavenly deity must not be born in secret, so I have come to tell you.' But Ninigi said: 'With child after a single night? It cannot be mine. It must be the child of some earthly deity.' She answered: 'If the child I carry is an earthly deity's, the birth will not go well; if it is the heavenly deity's, it will surely go well.' She built a doorless hall eight fathoms wide, went inside, sealed it all round with clay, and when her time came set fire to the hall. In the midst of the flames she bore three sons: the first, born when the fire blazed brightest, Hoderi, whom the text names ancestor of the Hayato of Ata; next Hosuseri; and last Hoori, also called Ama-tsu-hi-daka-hiko-ho-ho-de-mi. Chamberlain renders Hoderi and Hoori as Fire-Shine and Fire-Subside. All three were born safely, and the mother proved her truth by fire.
sections.bodyZh: 过了些日子，木花之佐久夜毘卖来对迩迩艺命说：我怀孕了，就要生产了。天神的孩子不能私下里生，所以来告诉你。迩迩艺命却说：只过了一夜就怀孕了？这一定不是我的孩子，一定是哪个国津神的孩子。木花之佐久夜毘卖说：如果我怀的是国津神的孩子，生产时就不会平安；如果是天神的孩子，就一定平安。她建起一座八寻宽、没有门的大殿，走进去以后用泥土把四面封死，到生产的时候，就在殿里放起火来。在熊熊大火之中，她生下了三个儿子：火势正旺时生的叫火照命，书中说他是阿多隼人的祖先；接着生的叫火须势理命；最后生的叫火远理命，又名天津日高日子穗穗手见命。张伯伦把火照命和火远理命分别译作“火之照耀”和“火之消退”。三个孩子都平安降生，母亲用这场大火证明了自己的清白。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十八节。

sections.bodyEn: Hoderi became the Luck of the Sea, catching fish broad of fin and narrow of fin with his hook; Hoori became the Luck of the Mountains, taking beasts rough of hair and soft of hair with his bow. The word sachi here means both the hunting gear and its yield, and Chamberlain says English has no satisfactory equivalent, so he renders it luck. One day Hoori asked his brother to exchange their gear. Three times he asked and was refused, and at last the elder reluctantly agreed. Hoori took the fish-hook to sea, caught not a single fish, and lost the hook in the water. Hoderi came to ask for it back: 'Mountain luck to the mountain, sea luck to the sea — let us each have our own again.' The younger said he had lost it fishing, but the elder insisted. So Hoori broke up his ten-grasp sword and made five hundred hooks in recompense, but his brother would not take them; he made a thousand, and still his brother refused: 'I want my own hook.' All three brothers' names speak of fire — Fire-Shine, Fire-Climax, Fire-Subside — as if recording the rise and fall of the flames in which they were born.
sections.bodyZh: 火照命成了海幸彦，用鱼钩捕捞海里大大小小的鱼；火远理命成了山幸彦，用弓箭猎取山里大大小小的野兽。“幸”在这里指的是猎具和收获，张伯伦说英语里没有合适的词，只好译作“运气”。有一天，火远理命对哥哥说：我们交换一下猎具用吧。他请求了三次，哥哥都不答应，最后才勉强换了。火远理命拿着哥哥的鱼钩去钓鱼，一条鱼也没有钓到，还把鱼钩弄丢在海里了。哥哥火照命来要回自己的鱼钩，说：山的猎具是山的，海的猎具是海的，我们还是各自换回来吧。弟弟说：你的鱼钩我钓鱼时丢了。哥哥一定要他还。弟弟就把自己佩带的十拳剑打碎，做成五百个鱼钩来赔，哥哥不要；又做了一千个鱼钩来赔，哥哥还是不要，说：我只要我原来的那个鱼钩。三兄弟的名字都与火有关：火照、火须势理、火远理，像是记下了他们在火中出生时火势的起落。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十九节。
sections.headingEn: The luck of the sea and the luck of the mountains

sections.bodyEn: As Hoori wept on the seashore, the salt deity Shio-tsuchi came and asked: 'Why do you weep, Sky's Sun-Height?' He told the story of the hook. Shio-tsuchi said: 'I will make a good plan for you.' He wove a little boat of bamboo so tightly that no water could enter, set Hoori in it and said: 'When I push the boat off, drift for a while and you will meet a pleasant current; follow it. You will come to a palace built like the scales of fishes: the palace of Watatsumi, the sea deity. By its gate there is a well, and by the well a many-branched cassia tree. Sit in that tree, and the sea deity's daughter will see you and counsel you.' Hoori did as he was told, drifted with the current, came to the palace built like fish-scales, and climbed the cassia tree by the well and sat there. Chamberlain renders Shio-tsuchi as the Deity Salt-Possessor; the boat is called in the original a small boat of closely woven bamboo without interstices. Alone in it, Hoori left the land behind and drifted with the current into the depths of the sea.
sections.bodyZh: 火远理命在海边哭泣，这时盐椎神来了，问他：天津日高日子，你为什么哭？他说出了鱼钩的事。盐椎神说：我来为你想个好办法。他编了一艘缝隙紧密、不透水的竹笼小船，让火远理命坐进去，对他说：我把船推出去以后，你就顺着漂一会儿，会遇到一股好的潮流，你就跟着潮流走。前面会有一座宫殿，像鱼鳞一样一层层盖起来的，那就是绵津见神——海神——的宫殿。到了海神宫门口，旁边有一口井，井边有一棵枝叶繁茂的桂树。你就坐在那棵树上，海神的女儿看见你，会替你出主意的。火远理命照着他的话，乘着小船顺着潮流漂去，果然来到了那座鱼鳞般的宫殿前，爬上井边的桂树坐了下来。张伯伦把盐椎神译作“盐之主神”；那艘小船，原文叫“无间胜间之小船”，意思是编得严密、没有一点缝隙的竹笼船。火远理命独自坐在这样的小船里，离开陆地，顺着潮流漂向大海深处。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第四十节。
sections.headingEn: The salt deity and the road to the sea palace

sections.bodyEn: A maid of the sea deity's daughter Toyotama-bime came to the well with a jewelled vessel to draw water. She saw a light in the water, looked up, and saw a handsome man in the tree, and wondered at it. Hoori asked her for water; she drew it and offered it in the jewelled vessel. He did not drink, but loosened a jewel from his neck, took it in his mouth and spat it into the vessel. The jewel stuck fast and could not be removed, so the maid took the vessel, jewel and all, to Toyotama-bime. Wondering, the princess went out to look, was charmed at the sight of him, and they exchanged glances. She told her father: 'There is a beautiful person at our gate.' The sea deity went out himself and said: 'This is Sora-tsu-hi-daka, the son of Ama-tsu-hi-daka.' He brought Hoori in, spread eight layers of rugs of sea-asses' skins and eight layers of silk rugs over them, seated him, feasted him with a hundred tables of gifts, and gave him his daughter Toyotama-bime in marriage. Hoori lived in the sea palace for three years.
sections.bodyZh: 海神的女儿丰玉毘卖的侍女，拿着玉做的水器来井边打水，看见井水里映出了光，抬头一看，树上坐着一位英俊的男子，觉得十分奇怪。火远理命向她要水喝，侍女就打了水，盛在玉器里献给他。他却没有喝，而是解下颈上的玉，含在嘴里，吐进玉器中。那颗玉粘在器皿上，怎么也取不下来。侍女只好把粘着玉的器皿拿去交给丰玉毘卖。丰玉毘卖觉得奇怪，亲自出门去看，一见到他就被他迷住了，两人四目相对。她回去告诉父亲：我们家门口有一位很美的人。海神亲自出来一看，说：这是天津日高的儿子虚空津日高啊。他把火远理命请进宫里，铺上八层海驴皮的垫子，上面再铺八层绸缎的垫子，请他坐下，摆上一百桌礼物宴请他，把女儿丰玉毘卖嫁给了他。火远理命就在海神之宫住了三年。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第四十节。
sections.headingEn: The jewel in the vessel and the sea deity's daughter

sections.bodyEn: After three years Hoori remembered the past and heaved a great sigh. Toyotama-bime told her father: 'In three years he never sighed, but last night he heaved a great sigh.' The sea deity asked him why, and he told of the hook. The sea deity summoned all the fishes great and small and asked whether any had taken it. They said: 'The sea-bream has lately complained of something stuck in its throat and cannot eat; surely it is that.' The hook was found in the bream's throat, washed and given to Hoori, with this counsel: 'When you give it back to your brother, say: this hook is a gloomy hook, a fretful hook, a poor hook, a silly hook — and hand it to him behind your back. If he makes high fields, make yours low; if low, make yours high. I rule the waters, and in three years he will grow poor. If he attacks you in resentment, use the tide-flowing jewel to drown him; if he begs for mercy, use the tide-ebbing jewel to save him.' Then he summoned the wani, and a one-fathom wani said it could carry Hoori home in a day; Hoori rode it home and tied his small sword to its neck in thanks. All fell out as the sea deity said: the elder grew poor, attacked fiercely, was drowned by the tide-flowing jewel until he begged, was saved by the tide-ebbing jewel, and bowed down: 'Henceforth I will be your guard day and night.' That, says the text, is why the Hayato still perform the motions of drowning.
sections.bodyZh: 三年过去，火远理命想起往事，长长地叹了一口气。丰玉毘卖告诉父亲：他住了三年从不叹气，昨夜却长叹了一声。海神问他缘故，他就讲了鱼钩的事。海神把大大小小的鱼都召集起来，问：有没有哪条鱼拿了这个鱼钩？鱼们说：最近鲷鱼说喉咙里卡了东西，吃不下饭，一定是它。一查鲷鱼的喉咙，果然找到了鱼钩。海神把鱼钩洗干净交给火远理命，教他说：你把鱼钩还给哥哥时，要说“这是个忧郁的钩、焦躁的钩、贫穷的钩、愚蠢的钩”，背过手去交给他。哥哥如果在高处种田，你就在低处种；他在低处种，你就在高处种。我掌管着水，三年之内你哥哥一定会穷下去。他要是因此怨恨来攻打你，你就拿出潮盈珠让潮水淹没他；他要是求饶，就拿出潮干珠让潮水退去救他。海神又召来众鳄，一只长一寻的鳄鱼说一天就能送他回去。火远理命骑着它回到人间，把佩带的小刀系在它的脖子上作为谢礼。回去以后，一切都如海神所说：哥哥越来越穷，凶狠地来攻打他，被潮盈珠淹得求饶，又被潮干珠救起，最后叩头说：从今以后，我日夜做你的守卫。书中说，隼人一族至今还表演溺水的动作，就是由此而来。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第四十至四十一节。

sections.bodyEn: Later Toyotama-bime herself came out of the sea and said to Hoori: 'I am with child and my time has come. The child of a heavenly deity must not be born in the sea, so I have come out.' On the shore she built a birth-hut thatched with cormorant feathers, but before the roof was finished her pains came and she went inside. She said to her husband: 'All people of other lands, when they give birth, return to their native form. I too shall take my native form to bear the child. I beg you not to look at me.' Wondering, he peeped in, and saw that his wife had become a wani eight fathoms long, crawling and writhing. He fled in fear. Knowing he had looked, she was overcome with shame, left the child and said: 'I meant always to come and go by the road of the sea, but you have seen my form, and I am ashamed.' She closed the boundary between sea and land and went back down into the sea. The child was named Ugaya-fuki-aezu, Cormorant-Thatch-Meeting-Incompletely. Though she resented his peeping, she could not stop longing for him, and sent her younger sister Tamayori-bime to nurse the child, with a song: red jewels — even their string shines; but you, like white jewels, are nobler still. He answered: my wife, with whom I slept on the island where the wild ducks come, I shall not forget you all my life. Hoori dwelt in the palace of Takachiho five hundred and eighty years. Ugaya-fuki-aezu later married his aunt Tamayori-bime and had four sons, the youngest of whom, Kamu-yamato-ihare-biko, is the future Emperor Jimmu. Here the first volume of the Kojiki ends.
sections.bodyZh: 后来，丰玉毘卖亲自从海里出来，对火远理命说：我怀孕了，现在就要生了。天神的孩子不能生在海里，所以我出来了。她在海边建起一座产屋，用鸬鹚的羽毛做屋顶，可是屋顶还没有盖完，她就要生了，只好走进屋里。临产前她对丈夫说：凡是别国的人生孩子的时候，都会变回自己本来的样子。我现在也要变回本来的样子生产，请你千万不要看我。火远理命觉得奇怪，偷偷往里一看，只见妻子变成了一条八寻长的大鳄，在地上爬动扭曲。他吓得转身逃走。丰玉毘卖知道他偷看了，羞愧难当，留下孩子，说：我本想永远通过海路来往，可是你偷看了我的样子，我实在羞耻。她关闭了海与陆地之间的通路，回到了海里。孩子取名为鹈葺草葺不合命，意思是“鸬鹚羽毛还没有盖完的屋顶”。丰玉毘卖虽然怨恨丈夫偷看，却忍不住思念，便让妹妹玉依毘卖来抚养孩子，托她带去一首歌：红色的玉啊，连穿玉的线都在发光；可是像白玉一样的你的模样，更加高贵。火远理命答歌说：在野鸭飞来的海岛上，与我共寝的妻子啊，我一生都不会忘记你。火远理命住在高千穗宫五百八十年。后来，鹈葺草葺不合命娶了姨母玉依毘卖，生下四个儿子，最小的儿子神倭伊波礼毘古命，就是后来的神武天皇。《古事记》的上卷到这里结束。
sections.evidenceNote: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第四十二至四十三节。
