stories.canonicalTitle: Kalevala, Part 3: Kullervo
stories.editorialNote: 依据克劳福德 1888 年英译《卡勒瓦拉》第三十一至三十六章，按诗章顺序讲述。库勒沃的故事涉及屠杀、虐待、兄妹乱伦与自杀，本篇照原诗交代结果，不渲染细节；温塔莫与卡勒沃结仇的具体缘由与卖身的作价只概括讲述。

series.gapNote: 与上一部之间跳过第十六至三十章：万奈莫宁造船、访问冥界与巨人维普宁，伊尔马里宁赢得波赫约拉的少女与婚礼，勒明凯宁闯宴与逃亡海岛等。

stories.summaryEn: The brothers Untamo and Kalervo fall into a deep feud over a run of petty quarrels; Untamo slays Kalervo's people, sparing only a pregnant woman as a slave. Her son Kullervo vows vengeance in the cradle. Untamo tries three times to kill him — in a barrel thrown into the lake, on a pyre, hanged from an oak — and each time he lives. Every task Kullervo is given he ruins, and at last he is sold as a slave to the smith Ilmarinen. Ilmarinen's wife sends him to herd the cattle and bakes a stone into his bread, on which his father's knife, the only keepsake of his kin, breaks. Kullervo drives home wolves and bears in the shape of cattle, and the mistress is killed as she milks. Fleeing, he finds his parents alive, but on his way home from paying his father's tax he seduces a maiden who proves to be his long-lost sister; she throws herself into the rapids. Kullervo goes to war, destroys Untamo's clan, and comes home to find his family dead. At the place where he wronged his sister he asks his sword whether it will drink his blood, and falls upon it.
stories.summaryZh: 温塔莫与卡勒沃两兄弟因为一连串小事结下深仇，温塔莫杀光了卡勒沃的族人，只留下一个怀孕的女子做奴隶。她生下的库勒沃在摇篮里就发誓复仇。温塔莫三次想杀死他：把他装进桶里扔进湖中，扔进火堆，吊在橡树上，他都活了下来。温塔莫让他干活，他什么都干坏，最后被卖给铁匠伊尔马里宁做奴隶。伊尔马里宁的妻子让他去放牛，在他的面包里烤进一块石头，他父亲留下的唯一遗物——一把刀——在石头上折断了。库勒沃把狼和熊变成牛群赶回家，主妇在挤奶时被它们咬死。他逃进森林，找到了还活着的父母，却在替父亲交税回来的路上诱骗了一个少女，后来才知道她是自己失散多年的妹妹，妹妹投入急流而死。库勒沃出征，灭了温塔莫一族，回到家时亲人都已死去。他来到妹妹遇害的地方，问自己的剑是否愿意饮他的血，然后伏剑而死。
stories.titleZh: 卡勒瓦拉 · 第三部 库勒沃

claims.statement: Kalevala Rune XXXI says the brothers Untamo and Kalervo quarrelled over a run of petty matters until Untamo slew Kalervo's people, sparing only a pregnant woman whom he took as a slave.

Kalevala Rune XXXI says Kullervo, born to the captive woman in Untamo's house, broke his swaddling and cradle in his third month and was heard vowing to avenge his father, so that Untamo resolved to kill him.

Kalevala Rune XXXI says Untamo tried to kill the young Kullervo in a barrel thrown into the lake, on a burning pyre and hanged from an oak, and each time found him alive — fishing, stirring the embers, carving warriors on the tree.

Kalevala Rune XXXI says Kullervo ruined every task Untamo set him — minding a child, clearing the forest, building a fence, threshing the rye — and that Untamo sold him to the smith Ilmarinen in Karelia for worn-out kettles and old tools.
Kalevala Rune XXXII says Ilmarinen's wife sent Kullervo to herd the cattle with a loaf in which she had baked a stone, after praying to Ukko and the forest spirits to protect her herd.

Kalevala Rune XXXIII says Kullervo's father's knife, his only keepsake, broke on the stone in the loaf, and that on a crow's advice he let wolves and bears devour the herd and drove them home in the shape of cattle.

Kalevala Rune XXXIII says Ilmarinen's wife was mauled by the beasts when she went to milk them, that Kullervo refused to save her, reproaching her for the stone in his bread, and that he then fled into the forest.

Kalevala Rune XXXIV says an old woman in a blue robe told the fleeing Kullervo that his parents lived at the edge of Lapland, where he found them, and learned that his elder sister had vanished long ago while picking berries.

Kalevala Rune XXXV says Kullervo, useless at his father's work, was sent to pay the taxes, and on his way home lured a maiden into his sledge who next morning learned that she was Kalervo's lost daughter, his own sister.

Kalevala Rune XXXV says Kullervo's sister threw herself into the rapids when she learned the truth, and that Kullervo, though his mother begged him to live, resolved first to take vengeance on Untamo.

Kalevala Rune XXXVI says only Kullervo's mother promised to weep for him, that he wept only when told of her death, and that with a sword from Ukko he destroyed Untamo's clan and burned their dwellings.

Kalevala Rune XXXVI says Kullervo, finding his family dead, went with his dog to the place where he had wronged his sister, and after his sword answered that it would drink his guilty blood, fell upon it; Väinämöinen then warns against raising a child wrongly.

events.summaryEn: Once, the poem begins, a mother raised a brood of chicks: one was carried to Russia, one to Karelia, and one stayed at home — with such an image the singer opens the tale of two brothers.
events.summaryZh: 从前，有一位母亲养大了一窝小鸡，一只被带到了俄罗斯，一只被带到了卡累利阿，还有一只留在家里——诗人用这样的比喻开始讲述两兄弟的故事。

events.summaryEn: In Untamo's house the woman bore a son.
events.summaryZh: 那个女子在温塔莫家里生下了一个男孩，母亲给他取名叫库勒沃，温塔莫的人则叫他“战争之子”。

events.summaryEn: First Untamo had a barrel made, shut Kullervo inside and threw him into the lake.
events.summaryZh: 温塔莫先叫人做了一只木桶，把库勒沃装进去，扔进了湖里。
events.titleEn: The child who could not be killed

events.summaryEn: Untamo set Kullervo to work.
events.summaryZh: 温塔莫给库勒沃派活。

events.summaryEn: Ilmarinen's wife — the maiden of Pohjola of old, now mistress of the smith's house — looked at the new slave and thought: let him herd the cattle.
events.summaryZh: 伊尔马里宁的妻子，就是当年那位波赫约拉的少女，如今是铁匠家的女主人。
events.titleEn: The bread with a stone in it

events.summaryEn: At noon Kullervo sat down on a hillside, took out the mistress's loaf and cut into it; the blade struck the stone in the middle and snapped.
events.summaryZh: 到了中午，库勒沃坐在山坡上，拿出主妇给的面包，用刀一切，刀刃碰到了中间的石头，啪的一声折断了。

events.summaryEn: At evening Kullervo drove his 'cattle' into the byre, the horn sounding far and wide.
events.summaryZh: 傍晚，库勒沃把那群“牛”赶进了牛栏，号角声响彻四方。

events.summaryEn: Kullervo wandered in the forest, full of grief and anger.
events.summaryZh: 库勒沃在森林里游荡，心中充满了悲伤和愤怒。

events.summaryEn: Back home, Kullervo tried to help his parents but could do nothing right.
events.summaryZh: 回到家里，库勒沃想帮父母干活，却什么也干不好：父亲让他划船，他把船桨划断了，把船底都划穿了；让他撒网捕鱼，他把水搅成了泥浆，把渔网撕成了碎片。

events.summaryEn: The maiden understood everything and was overcome with grief.
events.summaryZh: 少女明白了一切，悲痛欲绝。

events.summaryEn: As he made ready for war, Kullervo asked each of his family: 'When I die, will you weep for me?' His father said: 'No; I will beget a better son.' His brother said: 'No; I will find a better brother.' His sister said: 'No; I will find a better brother.' Only his mother said: 'I will weep for you, in the house and in the fields and everywhere, until my tears run dry.' Kullervo set out.
events.summaryZh: 库勒沃准备出征，他一个个地问家人：我死了，你们会为我哭泣吗？

events.summaryEn: Kullervo came home to find the house empty and the hearth cold; father, mother, brother and sister were all dead.
events.summaryZh: 库勒沃回到家里，家中空无一人，炉灶冰冷，父亲、母亲、兄弟和姐妹都已经死去。

versions.labelEn: Kalevala, Runes XXXI–XXXVI (Crawford translation, long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 《卡勒瓦拉》第三十一至三十六章（克劳福德译本，长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 两兄弟的仇恨、摇篮里的复仇者、杀不死的孩子、无用的仆人与出卖、藏着石头的面包、断刀、主妇之死、找到父母、路上的少女、急流、出征与复仇、卡勒沃之子的结局
versions.rightsNote: 克劳福德 1888 年英译本属公共领域；本站发布按诗章顺序的独立讲述，人名采用现代芬兰语通行拼法。

sections.bodyEn: Once, the poem begins, a mother raised a brood of chicks: one was carried to Russia, one to Karelia, and one stayed at home — with such an image the singer opens the tale of two brothers. The elder, Untamo, and the younger, Kalervo, lived near each other but could never agree. They quarrelled over fishing-grounds, over fields and flocks, over a run of petty matters, and their grudge grew deeper and deeper. At last Untamo gathered a band of warriors and attacked Kalervo with swords. Kalervo's people were all slain and his houses burned to ashes; only one woman, who was with child, survived, and Untamo took her home as a slave to sweep the house, split wood and carry water. To Untamo, Kalervo's line had vanished from the earth. But the child in that woman's womb would one day destroy Untamo's own clan. In Lönnrot's Kalevala these runes are the darkest; they draw chiefly on songs from Karelia and Ingria. In the twentieth century J. R. R. Tolkien was moved by the tale to write his own Story of Kullervo.
sections.bodyZh: 从前，有一位母亲养大了一窝小鸡，一只被带到了俄罗斯，一只被带到了卡累利阿，还有一只留在家里——诗人用这样的比喻开始讲述两兄弟的故事。哥哥温塔莫和弟弟卡勒沃住得很近，却总是合不来。他们为了渔场、为了田地和羊群，为了一连串鸡毛蒜皮的小事争吵不休，怨恨越积越深。终于，温塔莫召集了一群武士，带着刀剑去攻打卡勒沃。卡勒沃的族人全被杀光，房屋被烧成灰烬，只剩下一个怀了孕的女子活了下来，被温塔莫带回家去，做了打扫屋子、劈柴担水的奴隶。在温塔莫看来，卡勒沃一族已经从世上消失了。可是那个女子腹中的孩子，正是后来让温塔莫一族灭亡的人。在隆洛特编排的《卡勒瓦拉》里，库勒沃的这几章最为阴暗，它们主要取材于卡累利阿和英格里亚一带的民间唱本。二十世纪的作家托尔金也深受这个故事的触动，写下了《库勒沃的故事》。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十一章。

sections.bodyEn: In Untamo's house the woman bore a son. His mother named him Kullervo, and Untamo's people called him the son of war. While still in the cradle he showed astonishing strength: in his third month he kicked off his swaddling clothes and broke the bottom of the cradle, and everyone said he would grow to be a mighty man. But as Kullervo grew, one thought filled his heart. Once Untamo heard the child in the cradle say: 'When I am grown and strong, I will avenge my father and the tears my mother has shed.' Untamo was startled and said to his household: 'If this child lives, he will be the ruin of our clan.' He resolved to be rid of him while he was still small. Born in his enemy's house, the child was surrounded by hatred from the start. In the Finnish poem he is often called by his full name, Kullervo son of Kalervo, as though his very name carried the fate of his father's people. Such words from a child still at the breast chilled Untamo's whole household.
sections.bodyZh: 那个女子在温塔莫家里生下了一个男孩，母亲给他取名叫库勒沃，温塔莫的人则叫他“战争之子”。孩子还在摇篮里的时候，就显出了惊人的力气。到了第三个月，他一脚踢开了包着自己的襁褓，把摇篮的底都蹬破了，大家都说：这孩子将来一定会成为一个强壮的人。可是库勒沃一天天长大，心里只有一个念头。有一次，温塔莫听见这个摇篮里的孩子说：等我长大了，有了力气，我要为父亲报仇，为母亲流过的眼泪报仇。温塔莫听了，心里一惊，对家人说：这孩子留着，将来就是我们一族的祸害。他决定趁孩子还小，把他除掉。这个出生在仇人家里的孩子，从一开始就被仇恨包围着。在芬兰语的原诗里，他常被连名带姓地称为“卡勒沃之子库勒沃”，仿佛他的名字本身就背负着父亲一族的命运。这样的话出自一个还在吃奶的孩子之口，温塔莫一家都不寒而栗。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十一章。

sections.bodyEn: First Untamo had a barrel made, shut Kullervo inside and threw him into the lake. After three nights his men went to look: the barrel was floating on the water, and Kullervo sat on top of it with a copper rod in his hand, fishing. Next Untamo had a great pile of birch and pine logs heaped up and threw Kullervo into the fire. After three days they went to look: the pile had burned to ashes, and Kullervo sat in the ashes with a poker, stirring the embers, not a hair singed. Then Untamo had the child hanged from an oak. After three days and nights they went to look: Kullervo was not dead but sat on a branch carving pictures on the trunk with a little knife — all of warriors with swords in their hands. Helpless, Untamo said: 'If this child cannot be killed, let him be a slave and work for us.' Water, fire and rope could not kill him, as if the child held a strength nothing could destroy; yet that strength would bring only disaster to him and to those around him.
sections.bodyZh: 温塔莫先叫人做了一只木桶，把库勒沃装进去，扔进了湖里。过了三个晚上，人们去看，只见木桶浮在水面上，库勒沃坐在桶上，手里拿着一根铜钓竿，正在钓鱼。温塔莫又叫人砍来一大堆桦木和松木，堆成一座高高的柴堆，把库勒沃扔进火里烧。过了三天，人们去看，只见柴堆已经烧成了灰，库勒沃坐在灰烬里，拿着一根拨火棍，正在拨弄余火，头发一根也没有烧焦。温塔莫又叫人把孩子吊在一棵橡树上。过了三天三夜，人们去看，库勒沃没有死，他坐在树枝上，正在用小刀在树干上刻画，刻的全是手拿刀剑的武士。温塔莫无可奈何，只好说：这孩子杀不死，那就让他做奴隶，替我们干活吧。水、火和绳索都没能杀死他，像是在说这个孩子身上有一种无法消灭的力量；可这股力量后来带给他和身边的人的，却只有灾难。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十一章。
sections.headingEn: The child who could not be killed

sections.bodyEn: Untamo set Kullervo to work. First he was told to mind a baby; he hurt it and it died, and he burned the cradle — the poem tells it bluntly, and this retelling gives only the outcome. Next he was sent to clear the forest; he felled the whole forest and cursed the land so that neither grain nor tree would ever grow there. Told to build a fence, he set up whole pines and firs into a wall reaching the sky, with no gap and no gate, so that no one could get in or out. Told to thresh the rye, he beat it to dust and chaff. Untamo said: 'This boy can do nothing right; keeping him will only bring misfortune.' So he sold Kullervo into Karelia, to the smith Ilmarinen, for no more than a few worn-out kettles and some battered farm tools. So Kullervo passed from slave in his enemy's house to slave in a stranger's. Kullervo was not idle; he was enormously strong, but so full of resentment that every task in his hands turned to destruction. Ilmarinen did not know what kind of man he had brought home.
sections.bodyZh: 温塔莫给库勒沃派活。先让他照看一个婴儿，他却把婴儿弄伤、弄死了，还把摇篮烧掉；诗中这一段说得很直接，本篇只交代结果。温塔莫又让他去砍林开荒，他把整片森林都砍倒了，然后诅咒那块地永远不长庄稼、不长树木。温塔莫让他筑篱笆，他把整棵整棵的松树和冷杉竖起来，筑起一道高到天上、没有缝隙也没有门的围墙，谁也进不去出不来。温塔莫让他打黑麦，他把黑麦打成了粉末和糠皮。温塔莫说：这个孩子什么活都干不好，留着他只会带来灾祸。他就把库勒沃卖到了卡累利阿，卖给了铁匠伊尔马里宁，作价不过是几口旧锅和一些破旧的农具。库勒沃就这样从仇人的奴隶，变成了陌生人家的奴隶。库勒沃并不是懒惰，他力大无穷，只是心里装满了怨恨，每一件活计到了他手里，都变成了破坏。伊尔马里宁并不知道，自己买回家的是怎样一个人。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十一章。

sections.bodyEn: Ilmarinen's wife — the maiden of Pohjola of old, now mistress of the smith's house — looked at the new slave and thought: let him herd the cattle. To provide for him she baked a loaf: oats on top, wheat below, and in the middle a stone. She gave it to Kullervo and told him not to eat it until the herd had gone into the woods. Then she spoke long prayers to Ukko and to the master and mother of the forest, asking them to keep the herd safe from wolf and bear, and chanted the charms to the bear, begging it to spare her cattle. Kullervo drove the herd out and pastured them through swamp and wood, lamenting his lot as he went: others ate white bread and drank ale, while he, a slave, had only hard bread and the cattle in the wilderness. In the poem her prayers fill most of the rune, preserving the charms with which old Finnish herders asked safety for their cattle and kept off wild beasts — which makes plain why her herd later comes to grief by wolf and bear.
sections.bodyZh: 伊尔马里宁的妻子，就是当年那位波赫约拉的少女，如今是铁匠家的女主人。她看着这个新来的奴隶，心里想：让他去放牛吧。她要给库勒沃准备路上吃的干粮，就烤了一块面包：上面是燕麦，下面是小麦，中间却藏了一块石头。她把面包交给库勒沃，叮嘱他：等牛群进了树林，你再吃这块面包。然后，她向乌戈、森林的主人和森林之母念了很长的祈祷，请他们保佑牛群平安，不受狼和熊的伤害，又念起对熊的咒语，请熊不要伤害她的牛。库勒沃赶着牛群出了门，在沼泽和林间放牧，一路上抱怨自己的命运：别人吃的是白面包，喝的是麦酒，而他这个奴隶，只能吃干硬的面包，在荒野里放牛。原诗里，她的祈祷占了这一章的大半篇幅，保存了古代芬兰牧人祈求牲畜平安、驱赶猛兽的咒语。读者也就更明白，后面她的牛群为什么会在狼和熊的手里遭殃。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十二章。
sections.headingEn: The bread with a stone in it

sections.bodyEn: At noon Kullervo sat down on a hillside, took out the mistress's loaf and cut into it; the blade struck the stone in the middle and snapped. The knife was the only keepsake left by his father, his last link with the slaughtered people of Kalervo. Kullervo looked at the broken knife and wept: 'This was my only treasure, my father's knife, and it has broken on a mistress's stone.' A crow called to him from a tree: 'Child of Kalervo, why so sad? Drive the herd into the swamp and let the wolves and bears devour them; then call the wolves and bears, give them the shape of cattle, and drive them home at evening.' Kullervo did as the crow said: he drove the herd into the swamp to be devoured, then by his charms turned the wolves into oxen and the bears into cows, and drove the beasts towards his master's house, blowing his horn. With the blade broke the last of Kullervo's patience. He put the broken knife away, thinking only of how to repay the mistress.
sections.bodyZh: 到了中午，库勒沃坐在山坡上，拿出主妇给的面包，用刀一切，刀刃碰到了中间的石头，啪的一声折断了。这把刀是他父亲留下的唯一遗物，是他与被杀光的卡勒沃一族之间仅剩的联系。库勒沃看着断刀，哭了起来，说：这是我唯一的珍宝，是我父亲的刀，如今竟断在一个女主人的石头上。一只乌鸦从树上对他说：你这卡勒沃的孩子，为什么这样悲伤？把牛群赶进沼泽吧，让狼和熊把它们都吃掉，再把狼和熊召来，让它们变成牛的样子，傍晚赶回家去。库勒沃照着乌鸦的话做了：他把牛群赶进沼泽，让狼和熊吃掉了它们，又用咒语把狼变成了牛，把熊变成了母牛，赶着这群野兽，一路吹着号角，向主人家走去。这一刀断下去，断的不只是一把刀，也是库勒沃心中最后的一点忍耐。他把断刀收好，心里只想着怎样报复那个女主人。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十三章。

sections.bodyEn: At evening Kullervo drove his 'cattle' into the byre, the horn sounding far and wide. Ilmarinen's wife said joyfully: 'Thanks be to Ukko, the herd has come home safe.' She took her milking pail and bent to milk, but the 'cow' was a bear, which sprang on her and tore her. She shrieked to Kullervo for help: 'Good herdsman, save me, drive off these beasts, and I will give you the best clothes and the best bread.' Kullervo answered: 'You fed me bread made of stone; now taste your own bitterness.' She prayed to Ukko to shoot Kullervo with his arrows. But no one came to save her, and Ilmarinen's wife died in the byre. The maiden who once wove on the rainbow, for whom Väinämöinen and Ilmarinen had both longed, lost her life over a stone hidden in a loaf. Kullervo blew his horn, left the smith's house and fled into the forest. Ilmarinen was left to grieve for his wife. He wept for her many nights; a later rune tells how he even tried to forge himself a new wife of gold and silver.
sections.bodyZh: 傍晚，库勒沃把那群“牛”赶进了牛栏，号角声响彻四方。伊尔马里宁的妻子高兴地说：感谢乌戈，牛群平安回来了。她提着奶桶去挤奶，俯下身去，那头“母牛”却原来是一只熊，扑上来把她撕咬。她惊叫着向库勒沃求救：好心的牧人啊，救救我，拿开这些野兽吧，我会给你最好的衣服，最好的面包。库勒沃说：你给我吃石头做的面包，现在你自己尝尝苦头吧。她又向乌戈祈求，请他用箭射死库勒沃。可是没有人来救她，伊尔马里宁的妻子就这样死在了牛栏里。这位曾经在彩虹上织布、让万奈莫宁和伊尔马里宁都为之倾倒的少女，就因为一块藏在面包里的石头，丢掉了性命。库勒沃吹起号角，离开了铁匠的家，逃进了森林。伊尔马里宁后来失去了妻子，悲伤不已。他为她哭了许多日夜；后面的诗章会讲到，他甚至想用金子和银子为自己打造一个新的妻子。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十三章。

sections.bodyEn: Kullervo wandered in the forest, full of grief and anger. 'Where shall I go? Whose child am I? I have never had a home.' He resolved to go and take vengeance on Untamo. In the woods he met an old woman in a blue robe, who said: 'Child of Kalervo, your father is not dead. He lives, and your mother lives too; they dwell on the borders of Lapland, near a lake.' Half believing, Kullervo set out, and after long wandering found a house by a lake and saw his father and mother. His mother wept: 'My son, I thought you long dead and shed many tears for you; I thought you had been sold far away.' They told him that he had an elder sister, but that years ago she had gone into the woods to pick berries and never come back, and no one knew where she had gone. It is one of the few warm moments of Kullervo's life: at last he had a home, a father and a mother. But the lost sister lingers in the story like a shadow.
sections.bodyZh: 库勒沃在森林里游荡，心中充满了悲伤和愤怒。他想：我该到哪里去？我是谁的孩子？我从来没有一个家。他决定去找温塔莫报仇。在林中，他遇见一个穿着蓝衣的老妇人，她对他说：卡勒沃的孩子，你的父亲并没有死，他还活着，你的母亲也活着，他们就住在拉普兰的边上，靠近一片湖。库勒沃半信半疑地出发了，走了很久，终于在湖边找到了一座房子，见到了自己的父亲和母亲。母亲哭着说：我的儿子，我以为你早就死了，还为你流了许多眼泪。我还以为你是被卖到远方去了。他们告诉他，他还有一个姐姐，可是很多年前，她到林子里去采浆果，就再也没有回来，谁也不知道她去了哪里。这是库勒沃一生中少有的温暖时刻：他终于有了一个家，有了父亲和母亲。可那个失踪的姐姐，却像一道阴影，留在了故事里。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十四章。

sections.bodyEn: Back home, Kullervo tried to help his parents but could do nothing right. Set to row, he broke the oars and drove the boat's bottom through; set to fish, he churned the water to mud and tore the net to shreds. So his father sent him to pay the taxes. Driving home in his sledge after paying them, he met a maiden on the road and asked her into his sledge; she refused. He met another, who also refused. The third time he met a maiden travelling across the wilds, and with silver and fine cloth he lured her and drew her into the sledge. They spent the night together. In the morning the maiden asked him what family he came from. Kullervo said: 'I am the son of Kalervo.' At this her face changed, and she said: 'I too am Kalervo's daughter — the daughter who lost her way picking berries in the woods long ago.' Neither knew who the other was; two children lost for years met in this terrible ignorance. That night became the greatest misfortune of both their lives.
sections.bodyZh: 回到家里，库勒沃想帮父母干活，却什么也干不好：父亲让他划船，他把船桨划断了，把船底都划穿了；让他撒网捕鱼，他把水搅成了泥浆，把渔网撕成了碎片。父亲只好派他去交税。库勒沃交完了税，赶着雪橇回家，在路上遇见一个少女，请她坐上自己的雪橇，她不肯；又遇见一个少女，也不肯。第三次，他遇见一个在荒野里赶路的少女，就用银子和漂亮的布料引诱她，把她拉上了雪橇。两人在雪橇上过了一夜。第二天早晨，少女问他是哪一家的人。库勒沃说：我是卡勒沃的儿子。少女听了，脸色大变，说：我也是卡勒沃的女儿，就是多年前在林子里采浆果时迷了路的那个女儿。他们谁也不知道对方是谁，两个失散多年的孩子，就在这样的误会里相遇了。这一夜，成了两个人一生中最大的不幸。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十五章。

sections.bodyEn: The maiden understood everything and was overcome with grief. She leapt from the sledge and ran to the roaring rapids of the river, crying that she would rather be swept away by the torrent than live on in the world. She threw herself into the rapids and was swallowed by the raging waters. Kullervo stood by the river, torn with remorse: 'What have I done! I have ruined my sister and ruined myself; all my life I have brought only misfortune on others.' For a while he thought of ending his own life. He went home and told his mother. She pleaded: 'Do not die, my son. Go far away, to a place where no one knows you, and let time ease your grief.' But Kullervo said: 'Before I die there is one thing left to do. I will go to Untamo and avenge my father's people.' The poem gives her sorrowful words before she leaps, lamenting that she was born to misfortune. Kullervo's life, begun in an enemy's cradle, now held nothing but vengeance and remorse.
sections.bodyZh: 少女明白了一切，悲痛欲绝。她从雪橇上跳下来，奔向河边那奔腾的急流，说：我宁愿让急流把我卷走，也不愿再活在这世上。她投身于激流之中，被汹涌的河水吞没了。库勒沃站在河边，悔恨交加，他说：我做了什么样的事啊！我毁了我的妹妹，我毁了我自己，我这一生只给别人带来不幸。他一度想就此结束自己的生命。他回到家里，把这件事告诉了母亲。母亲劝他说：不要死，我的儿子，你可以远远地走开，到一个没有人认识你的地方去，等时间慢慢平息你的悲伤。可是库勒沃说：在我死之前，还有一件事要做。我要去找温塔莫，为我父亲的族人报仇。诗中说她在投水之前留下了悲伤的话，哀叹自己生来就不幸。库勒沃的一生，从仇人家的摇篮开始，到这里，已经只剩下了复仇和悔恨。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十五章。

sections.bodyEn: As he made ready for war, Kullervo asked each of his family: 'When I die, will you weep for me?' His father said: 'No; I will beget a better son.' His brother said: 'No; I will find a better brother.' His sister said: 'No; I will find a better brother.' Only his mother said: 'I will weep for you, in the house and in the fields and everywhere, until my tears run dry.' Kullervo set out. On the way messengers came one after another: your father is dead, your brother is dead, your sister is dead. He would not turn back, saying only: let them be buried. At last a messenger said: your mother is dead. Then he wept. He prayed to Ukko for a good sword, and Ukko gave it. Coming to Untamo's house, Kullervo slew all of Untamo's people and burned their dwellings, leaving only ashes and stones. His father's death was avenged at last. Of all his family, only his mother's love had never changed. Yet vengeance brought Kullervo no comfort; only emptiness awaited him at home.
sections.bodyZh: 库勒沃准备出征，他一个个地问家人：我死了，你们会为我哭泣吗？父亲说：不会，我会再生一个比你更好的儿子。哥哥说：不会，我会找一个比你更好的兄弟。姐妹说：不会，我会找一个比你更好的兄弟。只有母亲说：我会为你哭泣，我会在屋里哭，在田里哭，在每一个地方哭，哭到我的眼泪流干。库勒沃上了路。打仗的途中，一个个使者跑来告诉他：你的父亲死了，你的哥哥死了，你的姐妹死了。他都不肯回去，只说：让他们安葬吧。最后使者说：你的母亲死了。他才流下了眼泪。他向乌戈祈求一把好剑，乌戈给了他。库勒沃来到温塔莫的家，把温塔莫的族人全部杀死，烧毁了他们的房屋，只留下一片灰烬和石头。父亲的仇，终于报了。全家人里，只有母亲的爱从未改变。可是对库勒沃来说，复仇并没有带来安慰，回家时迎接他的只有冷清。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十六章。

sections.bodyEn: Kullervo came home to find the house empty and the hearth cold; father, mother, brother and sister were all dead. He wept at his mother's grave, and from the grave his mother said: 'Take our black dog Musti and go into the forest, and ask the spirits of the forest for a place to rest.' Kullervo went into the forest with the dog and came, without knowing it, to the very wilds where he had wronged his sister. The grass there no longer grew and the leaves had withered, as if the earth itself mourned what had happened. Kullervo drew his sword and asked it: 'My sword, will you drink the blood of a guilty man?' The sword answered: 'I have drunk the blood of the innocent; why should I not drink yours, who are guilty?' Kullervo set the hilt in the ground, point upward, and fell upon it and died. At the end of the rune old Väinämöinen hears of it all and says: people of the future, never raise a child wrongly, never let him grow up in a stranger's cradle, or he will never learn to be upright. So ended the story of Kullervo, son of Kalervo.
sections.bodyZh: 库勒沃回到家里，家中空无一人，炉灶冰冷，父亲、母亲、兄弟和姐妹都已经死去。他在母亲的坟前哭泣，母亲在坟墓里对他说：带上我们的黑狗穆斯蒂，到森林里去吧，向森林的神灵求一个安身的地方。库勒沃带着狗走进森林，不知不觉来到了当年他诱骗妹妹的那片荒野。那里的草不再生长，树叶凋零，仿佛大地也在为那件事哀悼。库勒沃拔出剑来，问它：我的剑啊，你愿意饮一个有罪之人的血吗？剑回答说：我连无辜者的血都饮过，为什么不能饮你这有罪之人的血？库勒沃把剑柄插在地上，剑尖朝上，扑倒在剑上死去了。诗的最后，老万奈莫宁听说了这一切，说：以后的人们啊，不要用错误的方式抚养孩子，不要让孩子在陌生人的摇篮里长大，否则他永远学不会正直。卡勒沃之子库勒沃的故事，就这样结束了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十六章。

stories.canonicalTitle: Kalevala, Part 4: the theft of the Sampo
stories.editorialNote: 依据克劳福德 1888 年英译《卡勒瓦拉》第三十九至四十三章，按诗章顺序讲述。康特勒琴是芬兰的传统弹拨乐器，至今仍被视为民族象征；本篇讲述的是隆洛特编排的史诗文本。

series.gapNote: 与上一部之间跳过第三十七至三十八章：伊尔马里宁打造金女，又到波赫约拉求亲未成。
series.labelEn: Part 4: the theft of the Sampo

stories.summaryEn: Väinämöinen, Ilmarinen and Lemminkäinen sail north in a war-boat that longs for battle, to win back the Sampo forged for Pohjola. In the rapids the boat sticks on the back of a giant pike; Väinämöinen kills it and from its jawbone makes the first kantele, whose music draws every creature of earth and sky to listen; he weeps himself, and his tears fall into the sea as blue pearls. In Pohjola Louhi will not share the Sampo, so Väinämöinen plays all the north to sleep; the heroes open the copper mountain, plough out the Sampo's roots with an ox, and carry it off in their boat. Lemminkäinen cannot help singing, a crane wakes and rouses Pohjola, and Louhi sends fog, a sea monster and a storm that sweeps the kantele overboard; at last she becomes a giant eagle carrying a hundred warriors. Väinämöinen smashes her talons with the rudder; the Sampo falls into the sea and shatters: the large pieces become the riches of the sea, the small ones drift to the shores of Kalevala and bring plenty, and Louhi takes home only the lid, so that Pohjola grows poor.
stories.summaryZh: 万奈莫宁、伊尔马里宁和勒明凯宁乘着一艘渴望出征的战船前往北方，去夺回为波赫约拉锻造的三宝。船在急流中卡在一条巨大的梭鱼背上，万奈莫宁杀死梭鱼，用它的颚骨做成了第一把康特勒琴。他的琴声让天上地下所有的生灵都来倾听，连他自己也流下了眼泪，泪水落进海里，变成了蓝色的珍珠。到了波赫约拉，洛希不肯分享三宝，万奈莫宁就用琴声把整个北方唱入梦乡。英雄们打开铜山的门锁，用牛犁断三宝的根，把它搬上船逃走。勒明凯宁忍不住在船上唱歌，一只鹤被惊醒，叫醒了波赫约拉。洛希派来浓雾、海怪和风暴，康特勒琴落进了大海；最后她化作一只巨鹰，带着上百名武士扑向战船。万奈莫宁用船舵打断了她的爪子，三宝跌进海里摔得粉碎：大块沉入海底，成了大海的财富，小块漂到卡勒瓦拉的岸边，带来了丰收；洛希只抢回了三宝的盖子，波赫约拉从此贫穷下去。
stories.titleZh: 卡勒瓦拉 · 第四部 夺取三宝

claims.statement: Kalevala Rune XXXIX says Väinämöinen persuaded Ilmarinen to go and win back the Sampo, that Ilmarinen forged him a sword adorned with the moon, the sun and the stars, and that they launched by song a war-boat that wept to go to war.
Kalevala Rune XXXIX says that Lemminkäinen, idle on a headland for want of war, hailed the boat and asked to come as the third hero, and that Väinämöinen took him aboard to go for the Sampo.
Kalevala Rune XL says the heroes' boat stuck on the back of a giant pike in the rapids, that Lemminkäinen and Ilmarinen failed to harm it, and that Väinämöinen pierced and lifted it with his sword.

Kalevala Rune XL says Väinämöinen made the first kantele from the giant pike's jawbone, with its teeth for pegs and hair from Hiisi's gelding for strings, and that no one else could draw a fair tune from it.

Kalevala Rune XLI says that when Väinämöinen played the kantele every creature came to listen — the beasts and Tapio of the forest, the birds, the fishes, Ahto king of the sea, and the daughters of the moon and sun, who dropped their spindles.
Kalevala Rune XLI says that all who heard the kantele wept, and that Väinämöinen's own tears rolled into the sea, from which a blue duck brought them up changed into blue pearls.
Kalevala Rune XLII says Louhi refused to share the Sampo and called her warriors, and that Väinämöinen played the kantele until all the people of Pohjola fell asleep.

Kalevala Rune XLII says the heroes opened the copper mountain's doors by song, Ilmarinen buttering the hinges, and when Lemminkäinen could not lift the Sampo they ploughed through its roots with the great ox of Pohjola and carried it to their boat.

Kalevala Rune XLII says that on the third day Lemminkäinen, against Väinämöinen's warning, burst into harsh song, and a startled crane flew screaming to Pohjola and woke its people, so that Louhi found the Sampo gone.

Kalevala Rune XLII says Louhi sent fog, which Väinämöinen cut with his sword, raised the sea monster Iku-Turso, which he banished by the ears, and called up a storm that swept his kantele into the sea.
Kalevala Rune XLIII says Louhi pursued the heroes as a giant eagle carrying her warriors, and that Väinämöinen smashed her talons with the rudder so that her warriors fell into the sea.

Kalevala Rune XLIII says the Sampo fell from the boat as Louhi clutched it and shattered in the sea, its large pieces becoming the sea's riches and its small pieces drifting to Kalevala, where Väinämöinen planted them, while Louhi took home only the lid.

events.summaryEn: Ilmarinen grieved long for his lost wife.
events.summaryZh: 伊尔马里宁失去了妻子，悲伤了很久。
events.titleEn: The sword and the weeping boat

events.summaryEn: As the boat passed a headland, someone on the shore called out: 'Who is sailing on the sea?' It was Lemminkäinen.
events.summaryZh: 船经过一座岬角时，岸上有人在喊：是谁在海上航行？

events.summaryEn: The boat ran into a stretch of wild river, threading between rapids and falls.
events.summaryZh: 船驶进一段湍急的河道，在急流和瀑布之间穿行。

events.summaryEn: Looking at the heap of bones, Väinämöinen wondered what they might become.
events.summaryZh: 万奈莫宁看着那堆鱼骨，心想：这些骨头要是做成一件东西，会是什么样子？

events.summaryEn: Väinämöinen washed his hands, sat down on a stone of singing, set the kantele on his knee and plucked the strings with his fingers.
events.summaryZh: 万奈莫宁洗净双手，坐在一块歌唱的石头上，把康特勒琴放在膝上，用手指拨动琴弦。

events.summaryEn: Everyone who heard the music wept: the young and the old, men and women, even the little children.
events.summaryZh: 所有听见琴声的人都哭了：年轻的人哭了，老人哭了，男人和女人都哭了，连小孩子也哭了。

events.summaryEn: At last the boat reached Pohjola.
events.summaryZh: 船终于到了波赫约拉。

events.summaryEn: The heroes came to the copper mountain of Pohjola, where the Sampo was locked behind nine doors.
events.summaryZh: 英雄们来到波赫约拉的铜山前，三宝就锁在山里的九道门后。

events.summaryEn: The boat sailed smoothly over the sea with the Sampo hidden in the hold, and the three heroes were glad.
events.summaryZh: 船在海上平稳地航行，三宝藏在船舱里，三位英雄心里都很高兴。

events.summaryEn: Louhi in her fury worked magic to pursue the heroes.
events.summaryZh: 洛希大怒，施展魔法追赶英雄们。
events.titleEn: Fog, the sea monster and the storm

events.summaryEn: Louhi built a great war-ship, put a hundred warriors aboard with swords, bows and arrows, and led the pursuit herself.
events.summaryZh: 洛希造了一艘巨大的战船，让上百名武士带着刀剑和弓箭上船，亲自率领他们追赶。

events.summaryEn: Though she had lost her talons, Louhi would not give up.
events.summaryZh: 洛希虽然失去了爪子，却不肯罢休。

versions.labelZh: 《卡勒瓦拉》第三十九至四十三章（克劳福德译本，长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 宝剑与哭泣的船、勒明凯宁加入、大梭鱼、第一把康特勒琴、万物倾听、泪珠、唱睡波赫约拉、挖出三宝、鹤的叫声、雾与海怪与风暴、鹰形的洛希、三宝的碎片
versions.rightsNote: 克劳福德 1888 年英译本属公共领域；本站发布按诗章顺序的独立讲述，人名采用现代芬兰语通行拼法。

sections.bodyEn: Ilmarinen grieved long for his lost wife. Väinämöinen said to him: 'Let us go north to Pohjola and win back the Sampo. You forged it for them, yet they bring us only misfortune; there it grinds grain and wealth and makes the north rich, while we have nothing.' Ilmarinen said: 'The Sampo is locked in the stone mountain of Pohjola behind nine locks, its roots nine fathoms deep; it will be hard to take.' But he agreed, and forged Väinämöinen a sword: on its blade the moon and the sun, on its hilt the stars, on its side a horse neighing, on the knob of the hilt a cat mewing, on the scabbard a dog barking. The two heroes rode to the sea and heard a boat weeping on the shore. It was a war-boat, and it wept: 'The other boats go to war and bring home gold and silver; only I am left here, rotting year after year among the wood-chips.' 'Do not weep,' said Väinämöinen, 'I will take you to war.' He sang, the boat slid into the water of itself, and the heroes boarded it and sailed north.
sections.bodyZh: 伊尔马里宁失去了妻子，悲伤了很久。万奈莫宁对他说：我们到北方的波赫约拉去吧，去把三宝夺回来。你为他们锻造了三宝，他们却只给我们带来不幸；三宝在那里磨出粮食、磨出财富，让北方富足，我们却一无所有。伊尔马里宁说：三宝锁在波赫约拉的石山里，有九道锁，根扎进地下九寻深，很难拿到。可他还是答应了，并且为万奈莫宁打造了一把宝剑：剑刃上有月亮和太阳，剑柄上有星星，剑身上有一匹马在嘶鸣，剑柄的圆头上有一只猫在叫，剑鞘上有一只狗在吠。两位英雄骑马出发，走到海边，听见岸边有一艘船在哭泣。那是一艘战船，它哭着说：别的船都去打仗，带回金银财宝，只有我被丢在这里，在木屑堆里一年年地腐烂。万奈莫宁说：不要哭，我会带你去打仗的。他唱起歌来，船自己滑进了水里，两位英雄登上船，向北方驶去。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十九章。
sections.headingEn: The sword and the weeping boat

sections.bodyEn: As the boat passed a headland, someone on the shore called out: 'Who is sailing on the sea?' It was Lemminkäinen. Living alone by the sea and sullen for lack of a war to fight, he saw the heroes' boat go by and shouted to ask where they were going. Väinämöinen said: 'We are going north to Pohjola, to win back the Sampo.' Lemminkäinen said: 'Let me come too. I will be the third hero; my sword is sharp too, and I can help you in the fighting.' Väinämöinen agreed. Lemminkäinen leapt aboard with a board under his arm; the boat dipped and then sailed steadily on. Väinämöinen sat at the stern steering, Ilmarinen and Lemminkäinen rowed, and the boat sped over the waves like a bird. The three most famous heroes of Kalevala — the singer, the smith and the warrior — set out together for the first time, to do what no one had ever done. In earlier runes this warrior had brought disaster on himself in Pohjola and had to hide on an island for three years; now he stood once more aboard a boat bound for adventure.
sections.bodyZh: 船经过一座岬角时，岸上有人在喊：是谁在海上航行？原来是勒明凯宁。他一个人住在海边，正因为没有了打仗的机会而闷闷不乐，看见两位英雄的船驶过，就大声问他们要到哪里去。万奈莫宁说：我们要到北方的波赫约拉去，去夺回三宝。勒明凯宁说：让我也一起去吧，我会是第三个英雄，我的剑也很锋利，我能在打仗的时候帮上你们的忙。万奈莫宁答应了。勒明凯宁拿着一块木板跳上了船，船身沉了一沉，又平稳地向前驶去。万奈莫宁坐在船尾掌舵，伊尔马里宁和勒明凯宁划桨，船儿像飞鸟一样在海浪上前进。三位卡勒瓦拉最有名的英雄——歌者、铁匠和战士——第一次一同出发，去完成一件谁也没有做到过的事。这位战士在前面的诗章里曾在波赫约拉闯下大祸，不得不逃到海岛上躲了三年，如今他又一次站到了冒险的船上。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第三十九章。

sections.bodyEn: The boat ran into a stretch of wild river, threading between rapids and falls. Väinämöinen chanted charms to the goddess of the rapids and the spirits of the water to let them pass safely. But in the middle of the rapids the boat suddenly stopped, and however they rowed it would not move, as if something held it fast. Lemminkäinen leaned over and looked: 'It is no rock and no tree-trunk beneath us, but a giant pike; our boat is stuck on its back.' He drew his sword and struck into the water, but struck so hard that he nearly fell in, and did the pike no harm; Ilmarinen caught him by the hair and pulled him back. Ilmarinen struck too, and his sword broke, and the pike did not stir. At last Väinämöinen drew his own sword, thrust it into the water and up under the fish, pierced the great pike, lifted it out and cut it in pieces. They hauled it aboard, cooked it on the shore, and the three heroes ate their fill, leaving only a heap of bones.
sections.bodyZh: 船驶进一段湍急的河道，在急流和瀑布之间穿行。万奈莫宁念着咒语，请急流的女神和水中的精灵让船平安通过。可就在急流中央，船忽然停住了，任凭怎么划桨也纹丝不动，好像被什么东西紧紧托住。勒明凯宁探身往水里一看，说：船下面不是礁石，也不是树干，而是一条巨大的梭鱼，我们的船正卡在它的背上。他拔剑向水里砍去，可是用力太猛，自己差点掉进河里，剑也没能伤到梭鱼。伊尔马里宁抓住他的头发，把他拉了回来。伊尔马里宁也拔剑去砍，剑却折断了，梭鱼仍然一动不动。最后，万奈莫宁拔出自己的宝剑，猛地刺进水里，从梭鱼的身下一挑，把这条巨大的鱼刺穿，挑出水面，劈成了几段。他们把梭鱼拖上船，在岸边煮熟，三位英雄美美地吃了一顿，只剩下一堆鱼骨。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十章。

sections.bodyEn: Looking at the heap of bones, Väinämöinen wondered what they might become. He took up the pike's jawbone and said: 'A skilled craftsman could make an instrument of this.' No one knew how, so he set to it himself. From the jawbone he made the body of the harp, from the pike's teeth the pegs, and for strings he took hair from the gelding of the evil spirit Hiisi. So the first kantele in the world was made. Ilmarinen and Lemminkäinen both tried it, but when they plucked the strings the sound was harsh and ugly. In Pohjola people crowded to play it — young men and old, maidens too — but no one could draw a fair tune from it; the sound was rough, people covered their ears, and said the harp was useless and had better be thrown into the water. But the kantele wept, saying it would not be thrown away; it was waiting for one who truly understood it.
sections.bodyZh: 万奈莫宁看着那堆鱼骨，心想：这些骨头要是做成一件东西，会是什么样子？他拿起梭鱼的颚骨，说：如果有一位巧手的工匠，就能用它做成一件乐器。可是谁也不会做，万奈莫宁就自己动手。他用梭鱼的颚骨做成琴身，用梭鱼的牙齿做成调弦的琴钉，又从恶灵希西那匹骟马的身上取来马鬃，做成了琴弦。这样，世界上第一把康特勒琴就造成了。伊尔马里宁和勒明凯宁都想试一试，他们拨动琴弦，发出的却是刺耳难听的声音。他们把琴带到波赫约拉，那里的人们也争着去弹，有年轻人，有老人，有少女，可没有一个人能弹出好听的曲子，琴声粗哑，人们捂着耳朵，说这琴毫无用处，还是扔进水里算了。可是琴自己哭了起来，说它不愿被扔进水里，它只等着一位真正懂得它的人来弹奏。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十章。

sections.bodyEn: Väinämöinen washed his hands, sat down on a stone of singing, set the kantele on his knee and plucked the strings with his fingers. At the first note all around fell silent; the music grew ever lovelier and spread through hills, woods, lakes and seas. The squirrels of the forest leapt from branch to branch to listen; ermine, elk and lynx came, the wolf came out of the swamp and the bear climbed onto the fence. Tapio, king of the forest, came with his household in festive dress to the hilltop. The birds of the sky came too: the eagle left its nest, the hawk dropped from the heights, the swans flew in from the lakes, and even the little finches gathered on his shoulders. The fishes swam to the shore, pike, salmon and whitefish lifting their heads from the water. Ahto, king of the sea, rose from the depths and sat on a water-lily to listen. The maidens of the sky — the daughters of the moon and of the sun, spinning golden thread and weaving silver cloth — let their spindles fall at the sound. Väinämöinen played for many days, and every creature was enchanted.
sections.bodyZh: 万奈莫宁洗净双手，坐在一块歌唱的石头上，把康特勒琴放在膝上，用手指拨动琴弦。第一声响起，四周就安静了下来；琴声越来越美，传遍了山林和湖海。森林里的松鼠从这根树枝跳到那根树枝，跑来倾听；白鼬、麋鹿、山猫都来了，狼从沼泽里走出来，熊爬上了篱笆。森林之王塔皮奥和他的家人穿着盛装来到山岗上。天上的鸟儿也飞来了：鹰离开了巢，鹞子从高空落下，天鹅从湖上飞来，就连小小的燕雀也聚在他的肩头。水里的鱼儿都游到岸边，梭鱼、鲑鱼和白鲑把头伸出水面。海王阿赫托也从海底升起，坐在一朵睡莲上倾听。天上的少女们——月亮的女儿和太阳的女儿——正在纺金线、织银布，听见琴声，手里的纺锤都掉了下来。万奈莫宁一连弹了许多天，所有的生灵都被琴声迷住了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十一章。

sections.bodyEn: Everyone who heard the music wept: the young and the old, men and women, even the little children. At last Väinämöinen himself was moved by his playing and began to weep. His tears were larger than cranberries, rounder than peas, brighter than eggs; they fell from his eyes onto his cheeks, from his cheeks onto his breast, from his breast to his knees, from his knees to his feet, and from his feet rolled into the sea and sank into the dark mud of the bottom. 'Who will bring my tears up from the sea?' said Väinämöinen. The raven tried and failed. A blue duck came, dived into the sea and brought the tears up one by one. They had changed: they had become blue pearls, beautiful enough to crown a king, an ornament for heroes for ever. It is one of the quietest moments in the Kalevala: on the long road to the Sampo the singer pauses, and lets music and tears speak. In the poem the duck is a blue duck.
sections.bodyZh: 所有听见琴声的人都哭了：年轻的人哭了，老人哭了，男人和女人都哭了，连小孩子也哭了。最后，万奈莫宁自己也被琴声打动，流下了眼泪。他的泪珠比越橘还大，比豌豆还圆，比鸡蛋还要光亮，一颗颗从他的眼里落下，落到脸颊上，从脸颊落到胸前，从胸前落到膝上，从膝上落到脚下，又从脚下滚进了大海，沉到了海底的黑泥里。万奈莫宁说：谁能把我的眼泪从海底捞上来？乌鸦来试，没有成功。一只蓝色的野鸭飞来，潜进海里，把那些泪珠一颗颗衔了上来。泪珠已经变了样：它们变成了蓝色的珍珠，美丽得可以戴在国王的头上，成为英雄们永远的装饰。这是《卡勒瓦拉》里最安静的时刻之一：在夺取三宝的长途中，歌者停下来，让音乐和眼泪说话。那只野鸭，在原诗里是一只蓝色的鸭子。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十一章。

sections.bodyEn: At last the boat reached Pohjola. The heroes went into Louhi's hall, and she asked their business. Väinämöinen said: 'We have come to speak of the Sampo. Here it grinds grain and wealth for you; we want a share. If you will not share it, we will take the whole.' Louhi said: 'A squirrel cannot be shared among three, and one Sampo cannot be shared between two households. The Sampo stays in Pohjola, to turn here and grind here.' 'Then we will take it all to Kalevala,' said Väinämöinen. Furious, Louhi summoned all the warriors of Pohjola, who closed in with swords. Unhurried, Väinämöinen took up his kantele and played. At the first notes the people of Pohjola stood still, closed their eyes one by one, and fell to the ground in deep sleep. Then he took his needles of sleep from his pouch and stitched their eyelashes together so that they would not wake for a long time. All the north lay asleep. In this epic the harp and the song are mightier than the sword.
sections.bodyZh: 船终于到了波赫约拉。英雄们走进洛希的大厅，洛希问他们来做什么。万奈莫宁说：我们来商量三宝的事。三宝在你们这里磨出了粮食和财富，我们也想分享一份。如果你不肯分给我们，我们就把它整个拿走。洛希说：一只松鼠不能分给三个人，一个三宝也不能分给两家。三宝留在波赫约拉，在这里转动，在这里磨面。万奈莫宁说：既然如此，我们就把它全部带回卡勒瓦拉。洛希大怒，召集了波赫约拉的全部武士，手持刀剑围了上来。万奈莫宁不慌不忙，拿起康特勒琴弹奏起来。琴声一响，波赫约拉的人们都停下了脚步，一个个闭上眼睛，倒在地上沉沉睡去。万奈莫宁又从口袋里掏出“睡眠之针”，把他们的睫毛缝在一起，让他们久久不能醒来。整个北方都陷入了沉睡。在这部史诗里，琴声和歌声比刀剑更有力量。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十二章。

sections.bodyEn: The heroes came to the copper mountain of Pohjola, where the Sampo was locked behind nine doors. Väinämöinen softly sang the song that opens locks, and the locks loosened one by one; Ilmarinen smeared butter on the hinges so that the heavy copper doors would open without creaking and wake the sleepers. The doors opened, and there was the Sampo, its roots sunk deep in the rock and the earth. 'Let me,' said Lemminkäinen, 'I am strongest.' He braced his feet, clasped the Sampo in his arms and heaved with all his strength, but it did not move; its roots went too deep. So they brought the greatest ox of Pohjola, yoked it to a plough, and ploughed through the Sampo's roots one by one. At last the Sampo came loose; the heroes carried it out of the mountain, loaded it into the boat and hid it in the hold. They cast off and slipped quietly away from the shores of Pohjola, rowing south towards home. Rune X had told of the Sampo's three roots, one in the earth, one at the water's edge, one in the hill by the house; now all three were ploughed through, and the Sampo left the place where it had been rooted so long.
sections.bodyZh: 英雄们来到波赫约拉的铜山前，三宝就锁在山里的九道门后。万奈莫宁轻声唱起开锁的歌，门锁一道道松开了；伊尔马里宁在门轴上抹了黄油，让沉重的铜门打开时不会发出吱呀的响声，免得惊醒睡着的人们。门开了，三宝就在里面，它的根深深地扎进了山岩和地下。勒明凯宁说：让我来，我力气最大。他用脚抵着地，双手抱住三宝，用尽全力往上拔，三宝却纹丝不动，它的根扎得太深了。于是他们牵来波赫约拉最大的一头公牛，套上犁，用犁把三宝的根一根根犁断。三宝终于松动了，英雄们把它从山里抬出来，搬上了船，藏在船舱里。他们解开缆绳，悄悄地离开了波赫约拉的海岸，划着船，向南方的家乡驶去。原诗在第十章里说过，三宝的根有三条：一条扎进大地，一条扎进水边，一条扎进家门前的山丘；如今这三条根都被犁断了，三宝离开了它扎根多年的地方。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十二章。

sections.bodyEn: The boat sailed smoothly over the sea with the Sampo hidden in the hold, and the three heroes were glad. Lemminkäinen could not contain himself: 'We have won the Sampo — how can we not sing at such joy?' Väinämöinen warned him: 'This is no time for singing. Song will be heard and will wake the people of Pohjola. Wait until we are home.' Lemminkäinen held back one day, two days, but on the third he could hold back no longer and began to sing. His voice was harsh and ugly, and the song carried far over the water. A crane standing in the reeds by a swamp was startled by the dreadful singing, flapped up, and flew screaming north. Its cry crossed hills and bays and reached Pohjola, waking all the people who had slept so long with their eyelashes sewn. Louhi woke, ran to the copper mountain, and found the Sampo gone. One song at the wrong moment undid all Väinämöinen's careful plans, and the pursuit would soon be upon them.
sections.bodyZh: 船在海上平稳地航行，三宝藏在船舱里，三位英雄心里都很高兴。勒明凯宁按捺不住，说：我们夺得了三宝，这样的喜事，怎么能不唱歌呢？万奈莫宁劝他说：现在还不是唱歌的时候。唱歌会被人听见，会把波赫约拉的人吵醒，等我们回到家乡再唱吧。勒明凯宁忍了一天、两天，到了第三天，他再也忍不住了，张开嘴就唱了起来。可他的嗓子粗哑难听，歌声在海面上远远传开。一只鹤正站在沼泽边的草丛里，被这难听的歌声吓了一跳，扑腾着翅膀飞了起来，一路尖叫着飞向北方。它的叫声越过了山岭和海湾，飞进了波赫约拉，把那些被缝住睫毛、沉睡已久的人们全都吵醒了。洛希醒来，跑到铜山一看，三宝不见了。一次不合时宜的歌唱，就这样毁掉了万奈莫宁小心翼翼的计划，追兵很快就要来了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十二章。

sections.bodyEn: Louhi in her fury worked magic to pursue the heroes. First she sent the maiden of the mist, and a thick fog covered the sea; the heroes' boat lost its way and lay still for three days and nights. Väinämöinen drew his sword and struck at the fog, cleaving a path through it; the mist scattered and the boat went on. Next Louhi called up the sea monster Iku-Turso, which rose from the deep and raised great waves to overturn the boat. Väinämöinen seized the monster by the ears, lifted it out of the water and asked: 'Iku-Turso, why have you risen from the sea to bar our way?' He commanded it to sink back to the bottom and never again show itself to men, and it sank. Last, Louhi begged Ukko for a raging storm; the waves rose sky-high, the boat pitched and rolled, and a great wave swept Väinämöinen's beloved kantele overboard into the depths. Gazing at the sea he said sorrowfully: 'My joy has sunk into the sea, and I shall never find it again.' That harp was never found again; in a later rune Väinämöinen has to make another.
sections.bodyZh: 洛希大怒，施展魔法追赶英雄们。她先派来浓雾的少女，让大雾笼罩了海面，英雄们的船在雾中迷失了方向，一连三天三夜停在原地。万奈莫宁拔出宝剑，向大雾劈去，劈开了一条路，雾气四散，船又能前进了。接着，洛希唤起了海怪伊库-图尔索。海怪从海底升起，掀起巨浪，要把船掀翻。万奈莫宁伸手抓住海怪的耳朵，把它提出水面，问它：伊库-图尔索，你为什么从海里升起来，挡在我们的路上？他命令海怪沉回海底，永远不许再在人们面前出现。海怪沉了下去。最后，洛希向乌戈求来一场狂风暴雨，海浪滔天，船身摇晃，万奈莫宁心爱的康特勒琴被一阵大浪卷下船去，沉进了海底。万奈莫宁看着大海，伤心地说：我的快乐已经沉进了海里，再也找不回来了。这把琴后来再也没有找回来，万奈莫宁不得不在后面的诗章里重新做了一把。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十二章。
sections.headingEn: Fog, the sea monster and the storm

sections.bodyEn: Louhi built a great war-ship, put a hundred warriors aboard with swords, bows and arrows, and led the pursuit herself. When she was nearly upon them she took a terrible shape: she fixed scythes to her feet for talons, turned the ship into wings and became a giant eagle, carrying a hundred warriors on one wing and a thousand bowmen on her tail, and swooped down on the heroes' boat. Väinämöinen prayed to Ukko for protection. The giant eagle settled on the mast and nearly overturned the boat. Ilmarinen and Lemminkäinen struck at it with their swords; Lemminkäinen cut away a few of its feathers. Väinämöinen pulled the rudder from the water and struck the eagle hard with it, smashing its talons, which fell into the sea until only one small claw was left. Louhi's warriors fell from the eagle's wings into the sea like autumn leaves falling from a tree. It is the grandest battle in the Kalevala: on one side the mistress of the north turned giant eagle with her host, on the other three heroes in one small boat.
sections.bodyZh: 洛希造了一艘巨大的战船，让上百名武士带着刀剑和弓箭上船，亲自率领他们追赶。眼看就要追上了，她又变出了一个可怕的样子：她把镰刀装在脚上做爪子，把船身变成翅膀，变成一只巨大的鹰，一边翅膀上载着一百个武士，尾巴上载着一千个弓箭手，向英雄们的船扑来。万奈莫宁向乌戈祈祷，求乌戈保护他们。巨鹰落在船的桅杆上，船几乎被压翻。伊尔马里宁和勒明凯宁拔剑去砍，勒明凯宁砍下了鹰的几根羽毛。万奈莫宁从水里拔起船舵，用船舵狠狠地向巨鹰打去，打断了它的爪子，鹰爪纷纷掉进海里，只剩下一个小小的爪尖。洛希的武士们也纷纷从鹰的翅膀上跌落，掉进海里，就像秋天的树叶从树上落下来一样。这是《卡勒瓦拉》里最壮观的一场战斗：一边是变成巨鹰的北方女主人和她的大军，一边是一艘小船上的三位英雄。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十三章。

sections.bodyEn: Though she had lost her talons, Louhi would not give up. With the one small claw she had left — her little finger, the poem says — she hooked the Sampo and tried to drag it from the boat. The Sampo slipped from the boat, fell into the sea, and was shattered. The large pieces sank to the bottom, and from them the sea has its endless riches, its fish and its treasures. The small pieces drifted on the waves to the shores of Kalevala. Väinämöinen gathered them one by one on the beach, planted them in the earth, and prayed that they would bring forth rye and barley, plenty and prosperity. Louhi took home to Pohjola only the Sampo's many-coloured lid, and from then on the north grew poorer. From the air Louhi swore fiercely: 'I will send you plague and frost and wild beasts; I will steal the sun and the moon!' Väinämöinen answered that he did not fear her curses, and prayed to Ukko to protect the people of Kalevala, their fields and their crops, and to let the fragments of the Sampo bless the land for ever.
sections.bodyZh: 洛希虽然失去了爪子，却不肯罢休。她用仅剩的那根小小的爪尖——诗中说是她的小指——勾住了三宝，想把它从船上拖走。三宝从船上滑落，跌进了大海，在海中摔成了碎片。大块的碎片沉到了海底，从此大海有了取之不尽的财富，海里的鱼和宝藏都由此而来。小块的碎片随着波浪漂流，漂到了卡勒瓦拉的海岸上。万奈莫宁在岸边一块块地拾起这些碎片，把它们种进土里，祈求它们长出黑麦和大麦，带来丰收和富足。洛希只抢回了三宝那五彩的盖子，带回了波赫约拉，从此北方日渐贫穷。洛希在空中恶狠狠地发誓：我要给你们送去瘟疫，送去冰霜，送去猛兽，我还要把太阳和月亮偷走！万奈莫宁回答说：我不怕你的诅咒。他向乌戈祈祷，请乌戈保护卡勒瓦拉的人们，保护他们的田地和庄稼，让三宝的碎片永远给这片土地带来福祉。
sections.evidenceNote: 《卡勒瓦拉》克劳福德译本第四十三章。

stories.canonicalTitle: Mahābhārata, Part 1: Nala and Damayantī
stories.editorialNote: 依据甘古利英译《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事（第五十二至七十九节），按章节顺序讲述；甘古利的章节编号与浦那精校本不同。《摩诃婆罗多》是在世宗教传统的经典，本篇只讲述这一个文本见证，故事中关于命运与正法的议论照原书交代，不作评判。

series.labelZh: 第一部 · 那罗与达摩衍蒂

stories.summaryEn: When the Pāṇḍavas have lost their kingdom at dice and gone into exile, Yudhiṣṭhira laments that no king was ever so unfortunate, and the sage Bṛhadaśva tells him the story of Nala. Nala, king of the Nishadhas, and Damayantī, princess of Vidarbha, fall in love through a swan's messages. At her svayaṃvara the gods Indra, Agni, Varuṇa and Yama all take Nala's form, but Damayantī knows the real Nala because the gods do not sweat or blink and their feet do not touch the ground. Kali resents it, waits twelve years for a lapse and enters Nala, who loses his kingdom at dice to his brother Pushkara. Exiled in the forest, Nala cuts away half of his sleeping wife's garment at midnight and leaves her. Damayantī survives a python, a hunter, a stampede of elephants and reaches the Chedi kingdom; Nala rescues the nāga Karkoṭaka from a forest fire, is bitten and changed, and becomes Bāhuka, charioteer to King Ṛtuparṇa of Ayodhyā. Damayantī announces a second svayaṃvara; Ṛtuparṇa races there with Bāhuka, teaching him the science of dice on the way, and Kali leaves Nala. Husband and wife know each other again, and Nala wins back his kingdom and forgives his brother.
stories.summaryZh: 般度五子在掷骰中失去王国、流放森林，坚战悲叹世上没有比他更不幸的国王，仙人巨马就给他讲了那罗的故事。尼沙陀国王那罗与毗陀婆公主达摩衍蒂经天鹅传情而相爱。选婿大会上，因陀罗、阿耆尼、伐楼那和阎摩四位天神都化作那罗的模样，达摩衍蒂凭着天神不流汗、不眨眼、脚不沾地的特征认出了真正的那罗。迦利因此怀恨，等了十二年，趁那罗一次疏忽进入他的身体，让他在骰子上把王国输给了弟弟补湿迦罗。那罗与妻子流落森林，在半夜割下她的一半衣裳，丢下她独自离去。达摩衍蒂历经蟒蛇、猎人、商队和象群的灾难，到了车底国；那罗则从林火中救出蛇王迦尔郭吒迦，被它咬后变了模样，化名巴胡迦，做了阿逾陀王利图帕尔纳的车夫。达摩衍蒂宣布第二次选婿，利图帕尔纳乘巴胡迦驾的车一日飞驰百由旬，途中把骰子的学问教给了他，迦利从那罗身上离去。夫妻终于相认，那罗赢回了王国，宽恕了弟弟。
stories.titleZh: 摩诃婆罗多 · 第一部 那罗与达摩衍蒂

claims.statement: Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Section LII says that when the exiled Yudhiṣṭhira lamented that no king was more unfortunate, the sage Bṛhadaśva offered to tell him of Nala, who also lost his kingdom at dice and regained it.
Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Section LIII says Nala and Damayantī came to love each other through report, and that a golden-winged swan released by Nala carried praise of each to the other.
Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Section LIV says Indra, Agni, Varuṇa and Yama, going to Damayantī's svayaṃvara, met Nala and bound him by his promise to be their messenger to her.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Sections LV–LVI say Nala, made invisible by the gods, delivered their suit to Damayantī, who answered that her heart was his and that she would choose him before the gods so that he would not break his word.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Section LVII says that at the svayaṃvara the four gods took Nala's form, and that when Damayantī prayed they showed the marks of gods — no sweat, unblinking eyes, unfaded garlands, feet not touching the ground — so that she chose the real Nala.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Sections LVII–LVIII say the gods gave Nala boons and he lived happily with Damayantī, but Kali, angered that she had chosen a mortal, resolved to enter Nala and ruin him with Dvāpara's help in the dice.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Sections LIX–LXI say Kali entered Nala after twelve years when he prayed without washing his feet, that Nala then lost everything at dice to Pushkara despite all pleading, and that Damayantī sent their children to Vidarbha before following him out of the city.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Sections LXI–LXII say the dice, in the shape of golden birds, carried off Nala's last garment, and that at midnight in a rest-house he cut away half of the sleeping Damayantī's garment and, driven by Kali, abandoned her.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Sections LXIII–LXV say the abandoned Damayantī was saved from a python by a hunter whom she cursed to death when he threatened her, survived a stampede that destroyed a caravan, and was taken in at the Chedi court.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Section LXVI says Nala carried the nāga Karkoṭaka out of a forest fire, that Karkoṭaka bit him at the tenth step and changed his form so that he would not be known, and sent him to King Ṛtuparṇa of Ayodhyā as the charioteer Bāhuka.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Sections LXVII–LXX say the brahmin Sudeva found Damayantī at the Chedi court by her mole, and that the words she sent out after Nala drew a sighing answer from Ṛtuparṇa's charioteer Bāhuka, reported by the brahmin Parṇāda.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Sections LXXI–LXXII say Ṛtuparṇa raced to Damayantī's announced second svayaṃvara with Bāhuka driving, and at a Vibhītaka tree taught him the science of dice in exchange for horse-lore, whereupon Kali left Nala, vomiting Karkoṭaka's venom.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Sections LXXIII–LXXVI say Damayantī tested Bāhuka through her maid Keśinī, knew him by his cooking and his tears for their children, and that when the wind god attested her faithfulness Nala resumed his true form.

Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Sections LXXVII–LXXIX say Nala returned to Nishadha, won back his kingdom from Pushkara in a single throw with the science of dice, forgave his brother, and that Bṛhadaśva then taught the science of dice to Yudhiṣṭhira.

events.summaryEn: Yudhiṣṭhira, eldest of the Pāṇḍava brothers, had lost his kingdom at dice and gone into exile in the forest with his four brothers and their wife Draupadī, to spend twelve years there and a thirteenth in hiding.
events.summaryZh: 般度族的长兄坚战在掷骰中输掉了王国，带着四个弟弟和妻子黑公主流放到森林里，要在那里度过十二年，再隐姓埋名过一年。

events.summaryEn: Long ago there was a king of the Nishadhas named Nala, son of Vīrasena.
events.summaryZh: 从前，尼沙陀国有一位国王，名叫那罗，是英雄维罗森那的儿子。

events.summaryEn: Damayantī grew restless and pale.
events.summaryZh: 达摩衍蒂从此心神不宁，日渐消瘦。

events.summaryEn: The gods made Nala invisible, and he passed unhindered into the inner palace of Vidarbha.
events.summaryZh: 天神让那罗隐去身形，他一路畅通无阻地走进了毗陀婆王宫的后宫。

events.summaryEn: The day of the svayaṃvara came.
events.summaryZh: 选婿大会的日子到了。

events.summaryEn: The four gods were not angry but pleased, and each gave Nala two boons: Indra, that he would see the gods with his own eyes at sacrifices and reach the heavenly worlds; Agni, that fire would appear whenever he wished and that he would have worlds bright as fire; Yama, skill in fine cooking and steadfastness in dharma; Varuṇa, that water would appear whenever he wished, and garlands that never faded.
events.summaryZh: 四位天神没有生气，他们都很高兴，各自赐给那罗两个恩惠：因陀罗让他在祭祀时能亲眼看见天神，并能到达天界；阿耆尼让他想要火的时候火就会出现，并让他拥有像火一样光明的世界；阎摩赐给他烹调的美味和对正法的坚定；伐楼那让他想要水的时候水就会出现，并赐给他永不凋谢的花环。

events.summaryEn: Kali came to Nishadha and waited for Nala to commit some fault.
events.summaryZh: 迦利来到尼沙陀，等着那罗犯下一个过失。

events.summaryEn: Pushkara proclaimed that anyone who sheltered Nala would die.
events.summaryZh: 补湿迦罗下令：谁要是收留那罗，就处死谁。

events.summaryEn: Damayantī woke to find her husband gone and searched the forest weeping and calling.
events.summaryZh: 达摩衍蒂醒来，不见了丈夫，哭喊着在森林里四处寻找。

events.summaryEn: After leaving his wife, Nala saw a great fire in the forest, and from it a voice cried: 'Nala, come and save me!' He went into the fire and found a huge serpent coiled there, the nāga king Karkoṭaka, who said: 'Cursed by the sage Nārada, I cannot move; only you can save me.
events.summaryZh: 那罗离开妻子以后，在森林里看见一场大火，火中有声音喊道：那罗，快来救我！

events.summaryEn: As Bāhuka, Nala served Ṛtuparṇa at Ayodhyā as his charioteer and master of the stables.
events.summaryZh: 那罗以巴胡迦的名字在阿逾陀做了利图帕尔纳的车夫，掌管马厩。

events.summaryEn: Hearing Parṇāda's report, Damayantī understood and devised a plan.
events.summaryZh: 达摩衍蒂听了帕尔纳达的报告，心里明白了，就想出一个办法。
events.titleEn: The hundred-yojana drive and the science of dice
events.titleZh: 百由旬的车程与骰子的学问

events.summaryEn: Ṛtuparṇa's chariot thundered into the capital of Vidarbha, the noise shaking the palace, and Damayantī knew at once that only Nala drove like that.
events.summaryZh: 利图帕尔纳的车隆隆地驶进毗陀婆的都城，车声震动了宫殿，达摩衍蒂一听就知道，只有那罗能把车驾得这样快。

events.summaryEn: Learning the truth, Ṛtuparṇa asked Nala's pardon; Nala taught him the science of horses, and they parted friends.
events.summaryZh: 利图帕尔纳知道了真相，向那罗道歉，那罗也把驾驭马匹的学问教给了他，两人友好地分别。

versions.labelEn: Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana Parva (Ganguli translation, long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事（甘古利译本，长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 坚战的悲叹、天鹅传情、四位天神、使者那罗、五个那罗、迦利的怨恨、掷骰失国、森林中的分离、达摩衍蒂的漂泊、迦尔郭吒迦、寻找那罗、百由旬的车程与骰子的学问、相认、赢回王国
versions.rightsNote: 甘古利 1883–1896 年英译本属公共领域；本站发布按章节顺序的独立讲述。

sections.bodyEn: Yudhiṣṭhira, eldest of the Pāṇḍava brothers, had lost his kingdom at dice and gone into exile in the forest with his four brothers and their wife Draupadī, to spend twelve years there and a thirteenth in hiding. One day, while his brother Arjuna was away in heaven seeking divine weapons, Yudhiṣṭhira sat in the forest full of sorrow. Then the great sage Bṛhadaśva came to their dwelling. Yudhiṣṭhira poured out his grief: 'Is there any king in the world more unfortunate than I? Cheated of my kingdom by crafty gamblers, I suffer in the forest with my brothers and my wife.' Bṛhadaśva said: 'King, I will tell you of a king more unfortunate than you. He too lost his kingdom at dice and went into the forest with his wife; he was even parted from her and suffered alone. Yet he came through it all and won back his wife and his kingdom.' 'Tell me,' said Yudhiṣṭhira. So Bṛhadaśva began the story of Nala, king of the Nishadhas: a tale told by one sage to an unfortunate king about another.
sections.bodyZh: 般度族的长兄坚战在掷骰中输掉了王国，带着四个弟弟和妻子黑公主流放到森林里，要在那里度过十二年，再隐姓埋名过一年。有一天，他的弟弟阿周那去天上求取神兵，还没有回来，坚战坐在林中，心中充满了忧愁。这时，大仙巨马来到他们的住处。坚战向他诉苦说：世上还有比我更不幸的国王吗？我被狡诈的赌徒骗走了王国，带着弟弟和妻子在森林里受苦。巨马说：大王，我给你讲一个比你更不幸的国王的故事。他也是因为掷骰子失去了王国，带着妻子流落森林，后来甚至与妻子分离，独自一人受尽了苦难。可是他终于熬过了一切，重新得到了妻子和王国。坚战说：请你讲给我听。于是巨马开始讲述尼沙陀国王那罗的故事。这个故事，就是一个国王在不幸中讲给另一个不幸的国王听的。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十二节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: Long ago there was a king of the Nishadhas named Nala, son of Vīrasena. He was handsome as the god of love, mighty, learned in the Vedas and skilled with horses; his one weakness was a love of dice. In Vidarbha, King Bhīma had a daughter named Damayantī, more beautiful than the nymphs of heaven. People praised Damayantī before Nala and Nala before Damayantī, so that the two loved each other before they had met. One day Nala caught a swan with golden wings in his palace garden. The swan said: 'King, do not kill me. I will go to Damayantī and praise you before her, so that she will want no one but you.' Nala let it go. The swan flew to Vidarbha and alighted near Damayantī and her maidens; when she ran to catch it, it spoke to her in human speech: 'In Nishadha there is a king named Nala, like a god among men; you and he are made for each other.' Damayantī said: 'Go and say the same to him.'
sections.bodyZh: 从前，尼沙陀国有一位国王，名叫那罗，是英雄维罗森那的儿子。他英俊得像爱神一样，力量强大，精通吠陀，善于驾驭马匹，只有一个弱点：喜欢掷骰子。在毗陀婆国，国王毗摩有一个女儿，名叫达摩衍蒂，美丽得连天上的仙女都比不上。人们在那罗面前常常赞美达摩衍蒂，在达摩衍蒂面前也常常赞美那罗，两人还没有见过面，就已经彼此倾心。有一天，那罗在宫中的花园里抓住了一只金翅膀的天鹅。天鹅对他说：国王，不要杀我，我会到达摩衍蒂那里去，在她面前赞美你，让她除了你谁也不想嫁。那罗放了天鹅。天鹅飞到毗陀婆，落在达摩衍蒂和侍女们的身边，达摩衍蒂追着去抓它，天鹅就用人的语言对她说：尼沙陀国有一位国王，名叫那罗，在男子中他就像天神一样，你和他正好相配。达摩衍蒂说：你也去对他说同样的话吧。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十三节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: Damayantī grew restless and pale. Seeing that his daughter was of an age to marry, King Bhīma proclaimed a svayaṃvara, a gathering where she herself would choose her husband from the kings of the earth. The news reached heaven. Indra king of the gods, Agni god of fire, Varuṇa god of the waters and Yama god of death, hearing from the sage Nārada of Damayantī's beauty, all wished to go. On the way they met Nala hurrying to Vidarbha, and seeing how handsome he was they stopped and said: 'King of the Nishadhas, you are a man true to his word; promise to do us a service and be our messenger.' Nala joined his palms and promised. 'Who are you, and what would you have me do?' Indra said: 'We are gods, come for Damayantī. Go and tell her that the four gods wish to wed her, and that she should choose one of us as her husband.' Nala said: 'I have come for her myself; how can I woo her for others?' The gods said: 'You have promised; keep your word.'
sections.bodyZh: 达摩衍蒂从此心神不宁，日渐消瘦。父亲毗摩王看出女儿到了出嫁的年纪，就宣布为她举行选婿大会，让天下的国王都来，由她亲自挑选夫婿。消息传到了天上。天神之王因陀罗、火神阿耆尼、水神伐楼那和死神阎摩，听仙人那罗陀说起达摩衍蒂的美貌，也都想去参加选婿。四位天神在路上遇见了正赶往毗陀婆的那罗，见他英俊非凡，就停下来对他说：尼沙陀王，你是一个守信的人，请你答应为我们做一件事，做我们的使者。那罗双手合十，答应了。他问：你们是谁？要我做什么？因陀罗说：我们是天神，为了达摩衍蒂而来。你去对她说，四位天神都要娶她，请她在我们之中挑选一位做丈夫。那罗说：我也是为了她而来的，怎么能去替别人求婚呢？天神说：你已经答应了，就要信守诺言。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十四节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: The gods made Nala invisible, and he passed unhindered into the inner palace of Vidarbha. Damayantī and her maidens were startled, shy and delighted to see a handsome man suddenly before them. 'Who are you, and how did you come in? The palace is closely guarded.' 'I am Nala,' he said, 'messenger of the gods. Indra, Agni, Varuṇa and Yama wish to marry you; choose one of them as your husband. It was the gods' power that brought me in unseen.' Damayantī bowed to the gods, then smiled and said to Nala: 'King, my heart has long been yours; I give myself and all I have to you. The swan's words burn in my heart; it was for you that I called these kings together. If you reject me I will take poison, or fire, or water, or the rope.' Nala said: 'With the gods there, how can you choose a mortal? They are the lords of the world; I am not worth the dust of their feet.' Damayantī wept, then found a way: 'I will choose you in the presence of the gods, so that you will not have broken your promise.'
sections.bodyZh: 天神让那罗隐去身形，他一路畅通无阻地走进了毗陀婆王宫的后宫。达摩衍蒂和侍女们看见一个英俊的男子忽然出现在面前，都吃了一惊，又羞又喜。达摩衍蒂问他：你是谁？怎么进来的？宫中守卫森严啊。那罗说：我叫那罗，是天神的使者。因陀罗、阿耆尼、伐楼那和阎摩四位天神都想娶你，请你在他们之中选一位做丈夫。是天神的力量让我进来，没有被人看见。达摩衍蒂向天神行了礼，然后笑着对那罗说：国王，我的心早已属于你。我愿意把自己和一切都交给你。天鹅的话一直在我心里燃烧，正是为了你，我才召集了这许多国王。如果你拒绝我，我就服毒、投火、投水，或者自缢而死。那罗说：天神们都在那里，你怎么能选一个凡人？天神是世界的主宰，我连他们脚下的尘土都比不上。达摩衍蒂哭了，然后想出了一个办法：我会当着天神的面选你，这样你就不算违背承诺。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十五至五十六节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: The day of the svayaṃvara came. Kings garlanded and wearing earrings filled the hall on its golden pillars. Damayantī entered, drawing every eye. Her attendants named the kings one by one, and when she came to Nala's seat she stopped short: five Nalas sat side by side, all alike. The four gods had taken Nala's form and sat beside him. Unable to tell them apart, she prayed in her heart: 'Ever since I heard the swan I have chosen Nala as my husband; my heart and my words have never left him. Gods, if this is true, show your own forms and let me know Nala.' Moved by her truth, the gods showed the marks of gods: they did not sweat, their eyes did not blink, their garlands were fresh and unfaded, their clothes free of dust, their feet did not touch the ground, and they cast no shadow. Only one cast a shadow, his garland beginning to fade, sweat and dust on his brow, his feet on the ground, his eyes blinking — the real Nala. Shyly Damayantī took the hem of his garment and placed her garland round his neck.
sections.bodyZh: 选婿大会的日子到了。国王们佩着香花、戴着耳环，坐满了金柱撑起的大厅。达摩衍蒂走进来，她的美貌吸引了所有人的目光。侍从们一一念出国王们的名字，她走到那罗的座位前，却愣住了：那里并排坐着五个一模一样的那罗。原来四位天神都变成了那罗的模样，坐在他的身边。达摩衍蒂无法分辨，心中焦急，就在心里向天神祈祷：自从听了天鹅的话，我就选定了那罗做丈夫，我的心、我的言语从未离开过他；天神们啊，如果这是真的，请显出你们本来的样子，让我认出那罗。天神被她的诚心感动，显出了天神的特征：他们身上不流汗，眼睛不眨，花环鲜艳不凋，衣上没有灰尘，双脚不沾地面，也没有影子。只有一个人身上有影子，花环已经开始凋萎，额上沾着汗珠和尘土，双脚踏在地上，眼睛会眨——那就是真正的那罗。达摩衍蒂羞涩地拉住他的衣角，把花环戴在了他的颈上。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十七节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: The four gods were not angry but pleased, and each gave Nala two boons: Indra, that he would see the gods with his own eyes at sacrifices and reach the heavenly worlds; Agni, that fire would appear whenever he wished and that he would have worlds bright as fire; Yama, skill in fine cooking and steadfastness in dharma; Varuṇa, that water would appear whenever he wished, and garlands that never faded. Nala and Damayantī married, went home to Nishadha, and lived happily; they had a son and a daughter, and Nala performed many great sacrifices. But on their way back to heaven the gods met Kali and Dvāpara, personifications of the ages of strife and confusion, who were on their way to the svayaṃvara. The gods told them Damayantī had chosen Nala. Kali flew into a rage: 'She chose a mortal in the presence of the gods; I will punish her.' The gods said Nala was perfect in virtue and the choice was just. Kali would not listen and said to Dvāpara: 'I will enter Nala's body, take his kingdom and part him from Damayantī. You enter the dice and help me.'
sections.bodyZh: 四位天神没有生气，他们都很高兴，各自赐给那罗两个恩惠：因陀罗让他在祭祀时能亲眼看见天神，并能到达天界；阿耆尼让他想要火的时候火就会出现，并让他拥有像火一样光明的世界；阎摩赐给他烹调的美味和对正法的坚定；伐楼那让他想要水的时候水就会出现，并赐给他永不凋谢的花环。那罗和达摩衍蒂结了婚，回到尼沙陀，生下了一儿一女，过着幸福的生活，那罗举行了许多盛大的祭祀。可是，天神们在回天上的路上，遇见了迦利和达婆波罗——争斗与混乱时代的化身——正要去参加选婿。天神告诉他们，达摩衍蒂已经选了那罗。迦利大怒，说：她竟然在天神面前选了一个凡人，我要惩罚她。天神劝他说，那罗德行完美，选他是正当的。迦利不听，对达婆波罗说：我要住进那罗的身体里，夺走他的王国，让他和达摩衍蒂分离。你要钻进骰子里帮助我。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十七至五十八节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: Kali came to Nishadha and waited for Nala to commit some fault. He waited twelve full years. At last one day Nala, after answering a call of nature, said his evening prayers without washing his feet, and Kali entered his body. Then Kali went to Nala's brother Pushkara: 'Play dice with Nala; with my help you will win his kingdom.' Pushkara challenged Nala, and Nala, his mind clouded by Kali, could not refuse. They played, and Nala lost his gold, his silver, his chariots, his horses, his clothes, staking more as he lost more, for months on end. His ministers and people came to beg him to stop, and Damayantī pleaded again and again, but he was as one possessed and would hear nothing. Knowing all was lost, Damayantī called the charioteer Vārṣṇeya and had him drive their two children to her father's house in Vidarbha. At last Nala lost the whole kingdom and had nothing but the cloth he wore. Pushkara laughed: 'What have you left to stake? Only Damayantī — stake her.' Heartbroken, Nala said nothing, took off all his ornaments, and left the city in a single garment, Damayantī following in a single garment behind him.
sections.bodyZh: 迦利来到尼沙陀，等着那罗犯下一个过失。他足足等了十二年。终于有一天，那罗小解之后，没有洗脚就去做黄昏的祈祷。迦利趁机钻进了他的身体。接着，迦利去找那罗的弟弟补湿迦罗，对他说：去和那罗掷骰子吧，有我的帮助，你一定能赢得他的王国。补湿迦罗就来向那罗挑战，那罗被迦利迷住了心窍，无法拒绝。两人掷起了骰子，那罗把金子、银子、车辆、马匹、衣服一样样地输了出去，越输越赌，赌了好几个月。大臣和百姓都来劝他，达摩衍蒂也一次次请他停下，可他像着了魔一样，一句话也听不进去。达摩衍蒂知道大势已去，就叫来车夫瓦尔施奈耶，让他驾车把两个孩子送回毗陀婆的娘家。最后，那罗输掉了全部王国，只剩身上的一件衣服。补湿迦罗笑着问他：你还有什么可以赌的？只剩下达摩衍蒂了，把她押上吧。那罗心如刀绞，一言不发，脱下身上所有的饰物，只穿着一件衣服走出了城，达摩衍蒂也穿着一件衣服跟在他身后。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十九至六十一节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: Pushkara proclaimed that anyone who sheltered Nala would die. So Nala and Damayantī left the capital, lived three days outside the city on water alone, and went into the forest. Faint with hunger, Nala saw some golden birds and took off his only garment to throw over them, but the birds carried it off into the sky, crying: 'We are the dice! We came to take even your last garment.' Naked and ashamed, Nala said to Damayantī: 'Here many roads part; this goes to Avanti, that to Vidarbha, your father's land,' and pointed out the road to Vidarbha again and again. Weeping, she said: 'Do you mean to leave me? I will not leave you.' Sharing her single garment, they came to a ruined rest-house and lay down on the ground to sleep. At midnight Nala woke, his mind tossed by Kali. 'If I leave her, perhaps she will go to her father and live in peace.' Finding a knife, he cut away half of Damayantī's garment to cover himself, looked again and again at his sleeping wife, went away and came back and went away again, and at last, driven by Kali, left her and went alone into the forest.
sections.bodyZh: 补湿迦罗下令：谁要是收留那罗，就处死谁。那罗和达摩衍蒂只好离开都城，在城外住了三天，只靠喝水度日，然后走进了森林。那罗饥饿难忍，看见几只金色的鸟，就脱下身上唯一的衣服去罩它们，鸟儿却叼起衣服飞上天空，说：我们就是骰子，我们来是为了夺走你最后的一件衣服。那罗赤着身子，羞愧万分，对达摩衍蒂说：这里有许多条路，这条通往阿般提，那条通往毗陀婆，你父亲的国家。他一再指给她看去毗陀婆的路。达摩衍蒂哭着说：你是要丢下我吗？我不会离开你。两人共披着达摩衍蒂的一件衣服，来到一间破旧的歇脚处，躺在地上睡着了。半夜，那罗醒来，心中被迦利搅得翻腾不止。他想：如果我离开她，她也许会回到父亲那里，过上安稳的日子。他找到一把刀，割下了达摩衍蒂衣裳的一半披在自己身上，看了熟睡的妻子一眼又一眼，走开又回来，回来又走开，最后还是被迦利驱使着，丢下她独自走进了森林。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第六十一至六十二节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: Damayantī woke to find her husband gone and searched the forest weeping and calling. As she went, a huge python coiled around her; she cried for help, and a hunter came and killed the snake. But the hunter, seeing her beauty, meant to assault her. In her anger Damayantī cursed him, and he fell dead. She wandered on, asking the mountain, the trees and some ascetics where her husband was; the ascetics comforted her that she would meet Nala again, and then vanished with their hermitage. Later she joined a caravan of merchants, but as they camped by a lake at night a herd of wild elephants stampeded through the camp and trampled many of them. The survivors called her a woman of ill omen, and she went on alone, ragged and dishevelled, until she came to the capital of the Chedis, with children trailing after her. The queen mother saw her from the palace terrace, sensed nobility beneath the rags, and took her in as a companion to the princess. Damayantī made conditions: she would not eat leavings, would not wash anyone's feet, and would speak with no other men. The queen mother agreed.
sections.bodyZh: 达摩衍蒂醒来，不见了丈夫，哭喊着在森林里四处寻找。她走着走着，被一条巨大的蟒蛇缠住了身子，正在呼救，一个猎人赶来，砍死了蟒蛇救了她。可这个猎人见她美丽，起了邪念，想要侵犯她。达摩衍蒂愤怒地诅咒他，猎人当即倒地而死。她继续在森林中游荡，向山、向树、向苦行者打听丈夫的下落，苦行者们安慰她说，她终会与那罗重逢，说完就连同净修林一起消失了。后来她遇见一支商队，跟着他们赶路，夜里在湖边宿营，一群野象冲进营地，把商人们踩死了许多。幸存的人说她是个不祥的女人，达摩衍蒂只好又独自上路，衣衫褴褛，蓬头垢面，来到了车底国的都城。城里的孩子们跟在她身后看热闹。王太后从宫楼上看见了她，觉得她虽然落魄却气质不凡，就把她接进宫里，让她做公主的侍女。达摩衍蒂提出条件：不吃剩饭，不替人洗脚，不和别的男人说话。王太后答应了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第六十三至六十五节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: After leaving his wife, Nala saw a great fire in the forest, and from it a voice cried: 'Nala, come and save me!' He went into the fire and found a huge serpent coiled there, the nāga king Karkoṭaka, who said: 'Cursed by the sage Nārada, I cannot move; only you can save me. I will be your friend and counsel you.' He made himself as small as a thumb, and Nala picked him up and carried him out of the flames. 'Walk on, counting your steps,' said the nāga, 'and I will repay you.' At the tenth step — the Sanskrit word for ten also sounds like 'bite' — Karkoṭaka bit him, and at once Nala's form changed, short and misshapen. Karkoṭaka said: 'I have changed your form so that no one will know you. Kali, who dwells in you, will be tormented by my venom. From now on no poison and no enemy will harm you. Go to Ayodhyā, to King Ṛtuparṇa, and call yourself Bāhuka, a charioteer. He is a master of dice and will teach you that science in return for your knowledge of horses. When you wish to resume your form, think of me and put on this garment.' He gave Nala two divine garments and vanished.
sections.bodyZh: 那罗离开妻子以后，在森林里看见一场大火，火中有声音喊道：那罗，快来救我！他走进火里，看见一条巨大的蛇盘成一团，那是蛇王迦尔郭吒迦。迦尔郭吒迦说：我被仙人那罗陀诅咒，动弹不得，只有你能救我。我会做你的朋友，给你忠告。它把身子缩小到像拇指那么大，那罗把它拿起来，走出了火焰。蛇王说：你一边走一边数步子，我要报答你。那罗数到第十步——“十”这个词在梵语里听起来也像“咬”——蛇王就咬了他一口。那罗的模样立刻变了，变得矮小丑陋。迦尔郭吒迦说：我改变你的模样，是为了让人们认不出你。附在你身上的迦利会被我的毒液折磨。从此你不会受任何毒物和敌人的伤害。你到阿逾陀去，投奔国王利图帕尔纳，自称车夫巴胡迦，他精通骰子，会把骰子的学问教给你，你教他驾驭马匹的学问。等你想恢复原形时，就想起我，穿上这件衣服。它给了那罗两件神衣，就消失了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第六十六节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: As Bāhuka, Nala served Ṛtuparṇa at Ayodhyā as his charioteer and master of the stables. Every evening he would recite a single verse alone: 'Where does she lie now, tormented by hunger and thirst, weary — does she still think of that fool?' Meanwhile King Bhīma of Vidarbha sent many brahmins out in all directions to search for his daughter and son-in-law. The brahmin Sudeva came to the Chedi court, saw a woman in worn clothes with a wasted face, recognised the lotus-like red mole between her brows, and knew her for Damayantī. Only then did the queen mother learn she was her own niece, and she sent her home to Vidarbha. Back with her parents, Damayantī sent the brahmins out again to seek Nala, telling them to recite these words at every gathering: 'Gambler, where have you gone, having cut away half your wife's garment and left her asleep in the forest? She still wears that half garment and weeps for you day and night.' At last the brahmin Parṇāda came back and reported that at Ayodhyā a charioteer of Ṛtuparṇa named Bāhuka, hearing the words, had sighed and answered: 'A good woman, even when abandoned, guards her own virtue.'
sections.bodyZh: 那罗以巴胡迦的名字在阿逾陀做了利图帕尔纳的车夫，掌管马厩。每天傍晚，他都独自吟诵一句诗：那个受饥渴折磨、疲惫不堪的女人，如今躺在哪里，还在想着那个蠢人吗？另一边，毗陀婆的毗摩王派出许多婆罗门，到四方寻找女儿和女婿。婆罗门须提婆来到车底国，在宫中看见一个穿着破衣、面容憔悴的女子，认出她眉间那颗像莲花一样的红痣，知道她就是达摩衍蒂。王太后这才知道，她原来是自己的外甥女，就派人把她送回了毗陀婆。达摩衍蒂回到父母身边，又请婆罗门们出去寻找那罗，让他们在各地的集会上念出这样几句话：赌徒啊，你割下你妻子的一半衣服，把熟睡的她丢在森林里，你去了哪里？她仍然穿着那半件衣服，日夜为你哭泣。后来，婆罗门帕尔纳达回来报告：在阿逾陀，利图帕尔纳的一个车夫，名叫巴胡迦，听了这几句话，叹着气回答说：好女子即使遭到抛弃，也会守护自己的贞节。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第六十七至七十节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: Hearing Parṇāda's report, Damayantī understood and devised a plan. She sent the brahmin Sudeva to Ayodhyā to tell Ṛtuparṇa that Damayantī of Vidarbha would hold a second svayaṃvara at sunrise the next day, and that if he wished to go he must hurry. From Ayodhyā to Vidarbha was a hundred yojanas, with only a day to cover them. Ṛtuparṇa summoned Bāhuka, who was cut to the heart, thinking his wife meant to remarry, yet chose some lean horses of good breed and drove so fast that the chariot flew like a bird through the sky. On the way Ṛtuparṇa's upper garment blew off, and he wanted to stop for it; 'We are already a yojana past it,' said Bāhuka. Passing a Vibhītaka tree, Ṛtuparṇa, to show off his skill with numbers, told the number of its leaves and fruits. Bāhuka stopped, felled the tree and counted, and the number was exact. 'Teach me this science,' he said, 'and I will teach you the science of horses.' Ṛtuparṇa taught him the science of dice. At that moment Kali came out of Nala's body, vomiting Karkoṭaka's venom, and entered the Vibhītaka tree.
sections.bodyZh: 达摩衍蒂听了帕尔纳达的报告，心里明白了，就想出一个办法。她请婆罗门须提婆到阿逾陀去，对利图帕尔纳说：毗陀婆的达摩衍蒂要举行第二次选婿，就在明天日出的时候，你若想去，就要赶快。从阿逾陀到毗陀婆有一百由旬远，只有一天的时间。利图帕尔纳召来巴胡迦，巴胡迦听了，心如刀割，以为妻子真要改嫁，可还是挑选了几匹瘦弱却有好血统的马，驾着车飞驰起来，快得像鸟儿在天上飞。途中，利图帕尔纳的上衣被风吹落，他想停车去拾，巴胡迦说：已经跑出一由旬远了。路过一棵毗毗陀迦树，利图帕尔纳为了炫耀自己的计数本领，说出了树上的叶子和果实的数目。巴胡迦停下车，把树砍倒一数，果然分毫不差。他说：请把这门学问教给我，我把驾驭马匹的学问教给你。利图帕尔纳把骰子的学问传给了他。就在那一刻，迦利从那罗的身体里出来，吐出了迦尔郭吒迦的毒液，钻进了那棵毗毗陀迦树。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第七十一至七十二节（甘古利译本）。
sections.headingEn: The hundred-yojana drive and the science of dice
sections.headingZh: 百由旬的车程与骰子的学问

sections.bodyEn: Ṛtuparṇa's chariot thundered into the capital of Vidarbha, the noise shaking the palace, and Damayantī knew at once that only Nala drove like that. But the charioteer who stepped down was short and misshapen. Unsure, she sent her maid Keśinī to test him. Keśinī came back and said: 'This charioteer is strange. When he comes to a low doorway it rises for him; water-jars fill themselves; grass in his hand bursts into flame; flowers he touches bloom brighter.' Damayantī had food that Bāhuka had cooked brought and tasted it: it was Nala's cooking. She sent her maid with their two children to him, and Bāhuka, seeing them, clasped them and wept. At last she called him in. Wearing the half garment, she asked him weeping: 'Why did you leave your sleeping wife in the forest?' Nala said: 'That was Kali's doing, and now he has left me. But why are you holding a second svayaṃvara?' 'Only to bring you back,' said Damayantī. A voice from the sky — the wind god — bore witness that she had been faithful throughout. Nala thought of Karkoṭaka, put on the divine garment and resumed his true form, and husband and wife held each other close.
sections.bodyZh: 利图帕尔纳的车隆隆地驶进毗陀婆的都城，车声震动了宫殿，达摩衍蒂一听就知道，只有那罗能把车驾得这样快。可是走出来的车夫却矮小丑陋。达摩衍蒂不敢确定，就派侍女盖希妮去试探他。盖希妮回来说：这个车夫很奇怪：他走到低矮的门前，门会自己升高；水罐会自己装满水；他把草拿在手里，草会燃起火来；他碰过的花朵，反而开得更加鲜艳。达摩衍蒂又让人把巴胡迦做的饭菜拿来尝了一口，正是那罗做菜的味道。她又让侍女带着两个孩子去见他，巴胡迦一见孩子，就抱着他们痛哭起来。达摩衍蒂终于把他请进屋里。她穿着那半件衣服，哭着问他：你为什么在森林里丢下熟睡的妻子？那罗说：那是迦利做的，如今他已经离开了我。可你为什么又要举行第二次选婿？达摩衍蒂说：那只是为了把你找回来。天上传来风神的声音，证明她一直忠贞不二。那罗想起迦尔郭吒迦，穿上那件神衣，恢复了本来的模样。夫妻二人紧紧相拥。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第七十三至七十六节（甘古利译本）。

sections.bodyEn: Learning the truth, Ṛtuparṇa asked Nala's pardon; Nala taught him the science of horses, and they parted friends. After a month in Vidarbha, Nala went back to Nishadha with a chariot, sixteen elephants, fifty horses and six hundred foot-soldiers, and stood before his brother Pushkara: 'Let us play again. I stake all my wealth and Damayantī; you stake your kingdom. If you will not play, let us decide it with the bow.' Sure of winning, Pushkara laughed: 'Gladly — I have long wished to win Damayantī.' But Nala now had the science of dice, and with a single throw he won back the whole kingdom and its wealth. Pushkara went pale, expecting death. But Nala said: 'None of this was your fault; it was Kali's doing. You are still my brother. I forgive you; go back safely to your city.' He brought his wife and children home to Nishadha and ruled his kingdom again. Bṛhadaśva said to Yudhiṣṭhira: 'Nala suffered more deeply than you, and at last his good days came; so will yours.' And he taught Yudhiṣṭhira the science of dice.
sections.bodyZh: 利图帕尔纳知道了真相，向那罗道歉，那罗也把驾驭马匹的学问教给了他，两人友好地分别。那罗在毗陀婆住了一个月，然后带着一辆车、十六头大象、五十匹马和六百名步兵，回到尼沙陀，来到弟弟补湿迦罗的面前，说：我们再来掷骰子吧。我用我的一切财富和达摩衍蒂作赌注，你用你的王国作赌注；如果你不愿意掷骰子，我们就用弓箭决一胜负。补湿迦罗以为自己一定会赢，笑着说：好啊，我早就想赢得达摩衍蒂了。可这一次，那罗已经掌握了骰子的学问，只掷了一把，就赢回了全部的王国和财富。补湿迦罗吓得面无人色，以为必死无疑。那罗却对他说：这一切不是你的过错，而是迦利做的。你仍然是我的弟弟，我宽恕你，你可以平安地回到你的城里去。他把妻子儿女接回尼沙陀，重新统治了王国。巨马对坚战说：那罗遭受的苦难比你更深，而他终于等到了好日子。你也会这样。他还把骰子的学问传授给了坚战。
sections.evidenceNote: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第七十七至七十九节（甘古利译本）。
