stories.summaryEn: Kay Kāvus, shah of Iran, hears a demon disguised as a minstrel sing the praises of Māzandarān and, ignoring Zāl's warnings, marches to conquer that land of demons — only to be blinded with his whole army by the White Demon's dark cloud and hail and taken captive. Riding Rakhsh, Rostam takes the short and perilous road to rescue him and passes seven stages: Rakhsh kills a lion; a ram leads him, fainting with thirst, to a spring; Rakhsh wakes him three times and helps him kill a dragon; he unmasks a witch disguised as a fair woman; he captures Olād as his guide; he tears off the head of the demon Arzhang; and at last, at noon when the demons sleep, he enters the White Demon's cave, kills him and with the blood of his liver restores the sight of the shah and his warriors. The king of Māzandarān turns himself into a rock in battle and is carried back to camp by Rostam until he comes out. But Kay Kāvus learns nothing: tempted again by a demon, he tries to fly to heaven on a throne drawn by four hungry eagles, crashes into a forest, and once more must be found by Rostam.
stories.summaryZh: 伊朗国王凯·卡乌斯听了一个魔鬼扮成的歌手赞美马赞德兰的歌，不顾扎尔的劝告，率军去征服这片魔鬼之地，结果被白魔用黑云和冰雹弄瞎了双眼，连同大军一起被俘。鲁斯塔姆骑着拉赫什，选择了一条近而险的路去营救国王，一路闯过七关：拉赫什杀死了扑来的狮子；一只公羊把渴得昏倒的他引到泉边；拉赫什三次唤醒他，与他一起杀死了恶龙；他识破了化作美女的女巫；他擒住乌拉德做向导；他斩下了阿尔章魔的头；最后他趁正午魔鬼们沉睡，闯进白魔的洞穴，杀死白魔，取出它的肝，用它的血让国王和勇士们重见光明。随后，马赞德兰国王在战斗中把自己变成一块岩石，被鲁斯塔姆扛回营中逼了出来。可是凯·卡乌斯并没有吸取教训：他又听了魔鬼的话，用四只饥饿的鹰拉着宝座想飞上天空，最后从空中跌进了森林，又一次需要鲁斯塔姆去把他找回来。
stories.titleZh: 列王纪 · 第二部 鲁斯塔姆的七关

claims.statement: The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says Kay Kāvus, enchanted by a demon disguised as a minstrel singing of Māzandarān, resolved to conquer it, and his alarmed champions sent for Zāl.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says that when Kay Kāvus, scorning Zāl's warning, ravaged Māzandarān, the White Demon brought darkness and a storm of stones and hail that blinded the shah and his army, who were taken captive.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says Rostam chose the short, perilous road to Māzandarān, and that on the first night, as he slept, Rakhsh killed a lion that attacked them, for which Rostam scolded him.
The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says that in the second stage Rostam, fainting with thirst in the desert, prayed to God and was led by a ram to a spring.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says that in the third stage Rakhsh three times woke Rostam to a dragon that hid itself by magic, and that when Rostam finally saw it Rakhsh bit the dragon and Rostam cut off its head.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says that in the fourth stage a witch disguised as a beautiful girl joined Rostam at a feast, and that when he named God she turned back into a hag and he killed her.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says that in the fifth stage Rostam, after tearing off the ears of a field-keeper who struck him, defeated and lassoed the local lord Olād and made him his guide with the promise of Māzandarān's throne.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says that in the sixth stage Rostam rode alone into the camp of the demon Arzhang, tore off his head and flung it among the demons, who fled in terror.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says that in the seventh stage Rostam entered the White Demon's cave at noon when the demons slept, woke the demon rather than strike him sleeping, and after a desperate fight killed him and tore out his liver.
The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says the blood of the White Demon's liver, dropped by Rostam into the eyes of Kay Kāvus and his champions, restored their sight.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('The March into Mazinderan'), says that when the king of Māzandarān turned himself into a rock in battle, Rostam carried the rock to the Iranian camp and threatened it until the king came out, and that Olād was then made ruler of Māzandarān.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Kai Kaous Committeth More Follies'), says that, tempted by a demon to rule the sky, Kay Kāvus tried to fly on a throne drawn by hungry eagles straining after meat on spears, fell into a forest, and was found and rebuked by Rostam and the champions.

events.summaryEn: Kay Kāvus inherited the throne of Iran and, seated in state with his champions around him and treasure heaped high, thought no one in the world more mighty than he.
events.summaryZh: 凯·卡乌斯继承了伊朗的王位，坐在宝座上，看着满朝的勇士和堆积如山的财宝，以为天下再也没有人比他更强大。

events.summaryEn: Zāl hastened to court and earnestly urged the king: 'Māzandarān is the land of demons; they bewitch men with magic.
events.summaryZh: 扎尔赶到宫中，恳切地劝国王：马赞德兰是魔鬼的国度，他们会用魔法迷惑人，以前的国王都不敢去，你不要拿伊朗的勇士和自己的性命去冒险。

events.summaryEn: When Zāl received the letter he said to his son Rostam: 'The king is in peril, and only you can save him.
events.summaryZh: 扎尔收到信，对儿子鲁斯塔姆说：国王落难了，只有你能救他。

events.summaryEn: The next day Rostam entered a scorching desert; the sun burned the earth like fire, and there was not a drop of water nor a patch of shade.
events.summaryZh: 第二天，鲁斯塔姆走进了一片炎热的沙漠，烈日像火一样烤着大地，四周没有一滴水，也没有一片树荫。

events.summaryEn: That night Rostam slept by the spring, telling Rakhsh not to fight beasts alone again but to wake him at any danger.
events.summaryZh: 那天夜里，鲁斯塔姆睡在泉水边，叮嘱拉赫什：不要再自己去和野兽打斗，有危险就叫醒我。

events.summaryEn: On the fourth day Rostam crossed a lovely valley to a spring, where beneath the trees rich carpets were spread with roast lamb, bread, fruit and a flask of wine, and a lute lay beside them.
events.summaryZh: 第四天，鲁斯塔姆穿过一片美丽的山谷，来到一眼泉水边，只见树荫下铺着华丽的毯子，摆满了烤好的羊肉、面包、水果和一瓶美酒，旁边还放着一把琴。

events.summaryEn: On the fifth day Rostam entered a land of darkness without sun or moon, where he could not see his hand before him; he let Rakhsh find the way, and after a long time came out into the light, to green fields.
events.summaryZh: 第五天，鲁斯塔姆走进了一片没有日月、伸手不见五指的黑暗之地，他让拉赫什自己找路，走了很久，终于重见光明，来到一片绿油油的田野。

events.summaryEn: Olād led Rostam on and told him: 'Ahead is the camp of the demon Arzhang, one of the chiefs of the demon host of Māzandarān, who guards the road to the king's prison; beyond it lie seven great mountains, and in a cave among them lives the White Demon with thousands of demons on guard.' Rostam tied Olād to a tree, waited for dawn, then rode alone on Rakhsh into Arzhang's camp with a roar like thunder that shook the demons' hearts.
events.summaryZh: 乌拉德带着鲁斯塔姆向前走，告诉他：前面是魔鬼阿尔章的营地，他是马赞德兰魔鬼军队的首领之一，守着通往国王监牢的道路；过了那里，再往前是七座大山，白魔就住在山中的一个洞穴里，他身边有成千上万的魔鬼守卫。

events.summaryEn: Rostam found Kay Kāvus and the champions of Iran in their prison, all blind and suffering in darkness.
events.summaryZh: 鲁斯塔姆找到了被关押的凯·卡乌斯和伊朗的勇士们，他们都瞎了眼睛，在黑暗中受苦。

events.summaryEn: Rostam came out of the cave with the White Demon's liver, the sunlight on his blood-soaked body; Olād, seeing him, took him for a demon and was terrified until he spoke.
events.summaryZh: 鲁斯塔姆带着白魔的肝走出洞穴，阳光照在他满是鲜血的身上，乌拉德看见他，吓得以为是魔鬼出来了，直到他开口说话才放下心来。

events.summaryEn: Restored to strength, Kay Kāvus wrote to the king of Māzandarān commanding him to come and submit, surrender his treasure and become a vassal of Iran.
events.summaryZh: 凯·卡乌斯恢复了力量，写信给马赞德兰的国王，命令他前来投降，交出财宝，做伊朗的属国。
events.titleEn: The king who became a rock

events.summaryEn: But Kay Kāvus did not grow cautious from this lesson.
events.summaryZh: 可是凯·卡乌斯并没有因为这次教训变得谨慎。

versions.labelZh: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本：进军马赞德兰、凯·卡乌斯的更多愚行（长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 魔鬼歌手、白魔的冰雹、两条路与狮子、沙漠中的公羊、恶龙、女巫、乌拉德、阿尔章魔、白魔的洞穴、重见光明、化为岩石的国王、飞天的宝座
versions.rightsNote: 齐默恩 1883 年的英文散文转述本属公共领域；本站据此发布独立讲述，人名采用现代通行的波斯语转写。

sections.bodyEn: Kay Kāvus inherited the throne of Iran and, seated in state with his champions around him and treasure heaped high, thought no one in the world more mighty than he. One day a strange minstrel came to the palace gate asking to sing before the king. He was in truth a demon. He struck his lute and sang of Māzandarān: flowers bloom there in every season, nightingales sing in the gardens, tulips cover the hills, the air is warm and fragrant, the cities are heaped with gold and jewels, and its fair maidens are past counting. Kay Kāvus was enchanted and declared at once: 'I will march and conquer Māzandarān and add its wealth and beauty to Iran.' The champions were aghast, for they knew Māzandarān was the home of demons, which even the wise kings Jamshīd and Fereydūn had not dared to attack. Not daring to oppose the king, they secretly sent a messenger riding through the night to Zābulistān to fetch Zāl.
sections.bodyZh: 凯·卡乌斯继承了伊朗的王位，坐在宝座上，看着满朝的勇士和堆积如山的财宝，以为天下再也没有人比他更强大。有一天，宫门口来了一个陌生的歌手，请求在国王面前献唱。他其实是一个魔鬼变的。他弹起琴，唱起了马赞德兰：那里四季鲜花盛开，夜莺在花园里歌唱，山上长满了郁金香，空气温暖而芬芳，城里堆满了金子和宝石，美丽的少女多得数不清。凯·卡乌斯听得入了迷，当即宣布：我要率军去征服马赞德兰，把那里的财富和美景都收归伊朗。满朝的勇士都惊呆了，他们知道马赞德兰是魔鬼居住的地方，以前的贤明君王贾姆希德和法里东都不敢去冒犯。他们不敢劝阻国王，就悄悄派人连夜赶到扎布尔斯坦，去请扎尔。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

sections.bodyEn: Zāl hastened to court and earnestly urged the king: 'Māzandarān is the land of demons; they bewitch men with magic. No king before you has dared to go; do not risk the champions of Iran and your own life.' But Kay Kāvus said: 'I am mightier than Jamshīd and Fereydūn, with more champions and more treasure; what can demons do to me? If you are afraid, stay at home.' Zāl could do nothing but take his leave. Kay Kāvus led his army into Māzandarān, burning and plundering, carrying off treasure and captives. In terror the king of Māzandarān sent for the White Demon, chief of the demons. In the night the White Demon summoned a black cloud that plunged the world into darkness, then rained down stones and hail, and the Iranian army fell into confusion in the dark. When day came Kay Kāvus and all his champions were blind, and the demons seized them and cast them into a dungeon. In the darkness Kay Kāvus repented bitterly and secretly sent a message to Zāl: 'I did not listen to you, and this is my fate; come quickly and save me.'
sections.bodyZh: 扎尔赶到宫中，恳切地劝国王：马赞德兰是魔鬼的国度，他们会用魔法迷惑人，以前的国王都不敢去，你不要拿伊朗的勇士和自己的性命去冒险。凯·卡乌斯却说：我比贾姆希德和法里东更强大，我有更多的勇士和财宝，魔鬼又能把我怎样？你若是怕，就留在家里吧。扎尔无可奈何，只好告辞。凯·卡乌斯率领大军进入马赞德兰，烧杀抢掠，掳走了许多财宝和人口。马赞德兰的国王大为惊恐，派人去请魔鬼的首领白魔。白魔连夜召来一片乌云，天地间一片漆黑，接着降下了石头和冰雹，伊朗的军队在黑暗中乱成一团。等到天亮，凯·卡乌斯和他的勇士们全都瞎了眼睛，被魔鬼们抓住，关进了地牢。凯·卡乌斯在黑暗中后悔不已，偷偷派人给扎尔送信：我没有听你的话，如今落得这样的下场，快来救我吧。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

sections.bodyEn: When Zāl received the letter he said to his son Rostam: 'The king is in peril, and only you can save him. Two roads lead to Māzandarān: one long and safe, six months' journey; the other short and perilous, only two weeks, but beset by lions, dragons, witches and demons.' 'I choose the short road,' said Rostam; 'may God protect me.' He put on his war-coat of tiger-skin, took his grandfather's mace, mounted Rakhsh and set out, covering two days' journey in each day. On the first evening he killed a wild ass by a reed-bed, roasted it and ate, then took off Rakhsh's bridle to let him graze and lay down to sleep among the reeds. At midnight a fierce lion came back to its lair, saw the sleeping man and horse, and sprang at Rakhsh. Rakhsh leapt up like fire, struck the lion's head with his forefeet, seized its back in his teeth, threw it down and trampled it to death. Waking to find the dead lion, Rostam scolded Rakhsh: 'Who told you to fight a lion? If it had killed you, how would I have walked to Māzandarān with my mace and war-coat? Next time danger comes, wake me first.'
sections.bodyZh: 扎尔收到信，对儿子鲁斯塔姆说：国王落难了，只有你能救他。从这里到马赞德兰有两条路：一条长而安全，要走六个月；另一条短而凶险，只要两个星期，可路上有狮子、恶龙、女巫和魔鬼。鲁斯塔姆说：我选那条近路，愿神保佑我。他穿上虎皮做的战袍，带上祖父的铁杵，骑上拉赫什出发了，一天走两天的路程。第一天傍晚，他在一片芦苇荡边打了一头野驴，烤来吃了，然后摘下拉赫什的辔头，让它去吃草，自己躺在芦苇丛里睡着了。半夜，一头凶猛的狮子回到它的巢穴，看见熟睡的人和马，就向拉赫什扑过来。拉赫什像火一样跳起来，用前蹄猛击狮子的头，用牙齿咬住狮子的背，把它摔在地上踩死了。鲁斯塔姆醒来，看见死狮，却责备拉赫什说：谁让你去和狮子打？要是你被它咬死了，我怎么背着铁杵、穿着战袍走到马赞德兰去？下次遇到危险，先把我叫醒。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

sections.bodyEn: The next day Rostam entered a scorching desert; the sun burned the earth like fire, and there was not a drop of water nor a patch of shade. After a long march man and horse were spent with thirst; Rakhsh slowed, and Rostam fell from his back and lay on the burning sand, his tongue cracked, close to dying of thirst. He raised his head and prayed: 'O God, you know I took this road to save the king. I fear no enemy, but I would not die of thirst in this wilderness; save me.' At that moment a fat ram passed close by him. 'This ram must be going to drink,' thought Rostam. He struggled to his feet and followed it, sword in hand, and not far off he found a clear spring. He and Rakhsh drank their fill and washed off the dust. Rostam did not harm the ram, but blessed it towards heaven and thanked the Creator for sending it to save his life.
sections.bodyZh: 第二天，鲁斯塔姆走进了一片炎热的沙漠，烈日像火一样烤着大地，四周没有一滴水，也没有一片树荫。走了很久，人和马都渴得精疲力竭，拉赫什的脚步越来越慢，鲁斯塔姆也从马上摔了下来，躺在滚烫的沙子上，舌头干裂，眼看就要渴死了。他抬起头，向造物主祈祷：神啊，你知道我是为了去救国王才走上这条路的，我不怕任何敌人，可是我不愿意渴死在这荒野里，求你救救我吧。就在这时，一只肥壮的公羊从他身边走过。鲁斯塔姆想：这只羊一定是去喝水的。他挣扎着站起来，拿着剑跟在公羊后面，走了不远，果然看见了一眼清澈的泉水。他和拉赫什痛痛快快地喝足了水，洗净了身上的尘土。鲁斯塔姆没有伤害那只公羊，而是向天空祝福它，感谢造物主派它来救了自己的性命。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

sections.bodyEn: That night Rostam slept by the spring, telling Rakhsh not to fight beasts alone again but to wake him at any danger. At midnight a huge dragon crawled from its den, eighty cubits long, its breath like fire, so fearsome that not even elephants dared enter that meadow. Seeing it, Rakhsh ran to Rostam, pawing the ground and neighing to wake him. Rostam woke and looked around, but the dragon had hidden itself by magic, and he saw nothing; he cursed Rakhsh for disturbing his sleep and lay down again. The dragon came again, Rakhsh woke him again, and again it vanished. Rostam in fury said: 'Wake me again for nothing and I will cut off your head and walk to Māzandarān myself.' The dragon came a third time, and Rakhsh, heedless of the threat, ran again to wake him. This time the Creator let Rostam see the dragon. He drew his sword and fought it, but the dragon was so strong it nearly crushed him. Rakhsh rushed in, bit the dragon's shoulder and tore its flesh, and Rostam struck off its head. He begged Rakhsh's pardon and thanked the faithful horse for saving his life.
sections.bodyZh: 那天夜里，鲁斯塔姆睡在泉水边，叮嘱拉赫什：不要再自己去和野兽打斗，有危险就叫醒我。半夜，一条巨大的恶龙从洞里爬了出来，它长八十腕尺，吐出的气像火一样，连大象都不敢靠近这片草地。拉赫什看见恶龙，连忙跑到鲁斯塔姆身边，用蹄子刨地、嘶叫，把他叫醒。鲁斯塔姆醒来四处张望，恶龙却用魔法隐去了身形，他什么也没看见，就骂拉赫什打扰他睡觉，又躺下了。恶龙又出现了，拉赫什又把他叫醒，恶龙又不见了，鲁斯塔姆大怒，说：你再这样无缘无故地吵我，我就砍下你的头，自己走到马赞德兰去。恶龙第三次出现，拉赫什不顾一切地又跑来叫醒他。这一次，造物主让鲁斯塔姆看见了恶龙。他拔出剑，和恶龙搏斗起来，恶龙太强大了，几乎要把他压倒。拉赫什冲上去，一口咬住恶龙的肩膀，把它的皮肉撕开，鲁斯塔姆趁机一剑砍下了恶龙的头。他向拉赫什道歉，感谢这匹忠诚的马救了他的命。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

sections.bodyEn: On the fourth day Rostam crossed a lovely valley to a spring, where beneath the trees rich carpets were spread with roast lamb, bread, fruit and a flask of wine, and a lute lay beside them. It was a feast laid by witches. Hungry, Rostam sat down, ate and drank, took up the lute and sang: 'I, Rostam, am a wanderer who never knows a day of rest; every day I fight lions or dragons, and seldom do I find such a feast and so fair a garden.' A witch heard the song, changed herself into a beautiful girl with cheeks like spring flowers, and came and sat beside him. Pleased, Rostam poured a cup of wine and gave it to her, naming the Creator and thanking God for the wine and the fair companion. But at the name of God the witch's face changed; her beauty vanished and she became again a black-faced, wrinkled old hag. Seeing through her, Rostam cast his lasso around her neck and cut her in two with his sword.
sections.bodyZh: 第四天，鲁斯塔姆穿过一片美丽的山谷，来到一眼泉水边，只见树荫下铺着华丽的毯子，摆满了烤好的羊肉、面包、水果和一瓶美酒，旁边还放着一把琴。原来这是女巫们设下的筵席。鲁斯塔姆饿了，坐下来大吃大喝，拿起琴弹了起来，唱道：我鲁斯塔姆是个漂泊的人，一生没有安宁的日子，每天不是和狮子打，就是和恶龙斗，很少能见到这样的筵席和美丽的花园。歌声传开，一个女巫听见了，把自己变成一个美丽的少女，脸颊像春天的花朵，走到他的身边坐下。鲁斯塔姆很高兴，倒了一杯酒递给她，并说出了造物主的名字，感谢神赐给他美酒和佳人。可是女巫一听见神的名字，脸色就变了，她的美貌消失了，变回了一个又老又丑的黑脸巫婆。鲁斯塔姆看穿了她，抛出套索套住她的脖子，拔剑把她砍成了两半。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

sections.bodyEn: On the fifth day Rostam entered a land of darkness without sun or moon, where he could not see his hand before him; he let Rakhsh find the way, and after a long time came out into the light, to green fields. Weary and sleepy, he took off his sweat-soaked war-coat, let Rakhsh graze in the crops and lay down to sleep. The keeper of the fields came running, struck his feet with a stick and cursed him for letting his horse spoil the crops. Rostam woke, said nothing, seized the man and wrenched off both his ears. Holding his head, the keeper ran to complain to the local lord, Olād. Olād came with a band of warriors to punish the stranger. Rostam rode out on Rakhsh, scattered Olād's men, and caught Olād alive with his lasso. 'If you guide me to the White Demon's cave and to where the king is held,' said Rostam, 'when I have conquered Māzandarān I will make you king of this land; if you deceive me, your life is forfeit.' Olād agreed, and became Rostam's guide.
sections.bodyZh: 第五天，鲁斯塔姆走进了一片没有日月、伸手不见五指的黑暗之地，他让拉赫什自己找路，走了很久，终于重见光明，来到一片绿油油的田野。他又累又困，就脱下被汗浸透的战袍，让拉赫什在田里吃庄稼，自己躺下睡着了。看守田地的人跑来，用棍子打他的脚，骂他放马糟蹋庄稼。鲁斯塔姆醒来，一言不发，抓住那人，一把拧下了他的两只耳朵。看田人捂着头跑去向当地的领主乌拉德哭诉。乌拉德带着一群武士赶来，要惩罚这个陌生人。鲁斯塔姆骑上拉赫什迎战，把乌拉德的武士杀得四散奔逃，又抛出套索，活捉了乌拉德。鲁斯塔姆对他说：如果你给我带路，带我找到白魔的洞穴和国王被关押的地方，等我打败了马赞德兰，我就让你做这片土地的国王；如果你骗我，我就要你的命。乌拉德答应了，从此做了鲁斯塔姆的向导。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

sections.bodyEn: Olād led Rostam on and told him: 'Ahead is the camp of the demon Arzhang, one of the chiefs of the demon host of Māzandarān, who guards the road to the king's prison; beyond it lie seven great mountains, and in a cave among them lives the White Demon with thousands of demons on guard.' Rostam tied Olād to a tree, waited for dawn, then rode alone on Rakhsh into Arzhang's camp with a roar like thunder that shook the demons' hearts. Hearing it, Arzhang rushed out of his tent to fight. Rostam spurred forward, seized Arzhang by the head and ears, wrenched his head from his body and flung it among the demons. Seeing their chief's head roll on the ground, the demons fled in terror, many trampling one another to death as they ran. Having scattered Arzhang's host, Rostam went back to Olād, untied him, and bade him lead on to the imprisoned king.
sections.bodyZh: 乌拉德带着鲁斯塔姆向前走，告诉他：前面是魔鬼阿尔章的营地，他是马赞德兰魔鬼军队的首领之一，守着通往国王监牢的道路；过了那里，再往前是七座大山，白魔就住在山中的一个洞穴里，他身边有成千上万的魔鬼守卫。鲁斯塔姆把乌拉德绑在一棵树上，等到天亮，独自骑着拉赫什冲进了阿尔章的营地，发出一声雷鸣般的怒吼，震得魔鬼们心惊胆战。阿尔章听见吼声，从帐篷里冲出来迎战。鲁斯塔姆策马上前，伸手抓住阿尔章的头和耳朵，把他的头从身子上拧了下来，扔到魔鬼们中间。魔鬼们看见首领的头滚落在地，吓得魂飞魄散，四散逃命，许多魔鬼在逃跑中自相践踏而死。鲁斯塔姆杀散了阿尔章的军队，回到乌拉德身边，给他松了绑，让他继续带路，去找被关押的国王。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

sections.bodyEn: Rostam found Kay Kāvus and the champions of Iran in their prison, all blind and suffering in darkness. Hearing Rostam's voice, the king wept with joy and said: 'Only blood from the White Demon's heart dropped in our eyes can restore our sight.' So Rostam had Olād guide him to the White Demon's lair. They crossed the seven mountains to the mouth of a bottomless cave guarded by many demons. Olād said: 'Wait until the sun is highest and the heat greatest; then the demons sleep.' At noon Rostam rushed the entrance, killed the guards and went into the black cave. It was dark as hell; he rubbed his eyes and at last saw a huge form lying there like a mountain, its face black and its hair white: the White Demon. Rostam would not strike him sleeping, but woke him with a great shout. The White Demon sprang up, seized a stone like a millstone and charged. They fought for their lives in the cave; Rostam cut off one of the demon's legs, yet still it grappled him on one leg, and blood and sweat ran through the cave. At last Rostam lifted the White Demon, dashed him to the ground, plunged his dagger into his breast, and tore out his liver.
sections.bodyZh: 鲁斯塔姆找到了被关押的凯·卡乌斯和伊朗的勇士们，他们都瞎了眼睛，在黑暗中受苦。国王听见鲁斯塔姆的声音，悲喜交加，对他说：只有白魔心脏里的血滴进我们的眼睛，我们才能重见光明。鲁斯塔姆就让乌拉德带他去白魔的住处。他们越过七座大山，来到一个深不见底的洞穴前，洞口有许多魔鬼守卫。乌拉德说：等太阳升到最高、天气最热的时候再进去，那时魔鬼们都会睡觉。鲁斯塔姆等到正午，冲向洞口，杀死了守卫的魔鬼，走进了漆黑的洞中。洞里黑得像地狱一样，他擦了擦眼睛，才看见一个巨大的身影躺在那里，像一座山，脸是黑的，头发是白的，那就是白魔。鲁斯塔姆没有趁他睡着下手，大吼一声把他叫醒。白魔跳起来，拿起一块磨盘大的石头冲了过来。两人在洞中殊死搏斗，鲁斯塔姆一剑砍断了白魔的一条腿，白魔仍用一条腿扑上来和他扭打，鲜血和汗水流满了洞穴。最后，鲁斯塔姆把白魔举起来摔在地上，用匕首刺进他的胸膛，挖出了他的肝。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

sections.bodyEn: Rostam came out of the cave with the White Demon's liver, the sunlight on his blood-soaked body; Olād, seeing him, took him for a demon and was terrified until he spoke. 'I have killed the White Demon and opened the gates of Māzandarān,' said Rostam; 'I will not forget your service.' Together they went back to where the king was held. Rostam dropped blood from the White Demon's liver into Kay Kāvus's eyes, and at once the king's eyes were bright again; he saw the sunlight and Rostam before him. Then Rostam dropped the blood into the eyes of the champions of Iran, and all of them saw again. The captive Iranian host cheered, embraced Rostam and praised him as the saviour of Iran, the champion of champions. Kay Kāvus took his throne and ordered a great feast to celebrate the victory for seven days, with prayers of thanks to the Creator. He said to Rostam: 'But for you, Iran would have no king.'
sections.bodyZh: 鲁斯塔姆带着白魔的肝走出洞穴，阳光照在他满是鲜血的身上，乌拉德看见他，吓得以为是魔鬼出来了，直到他开口说话才放下心来。鲁斯塔姆说：我已经杀死了白魔，打开了马赞德兰的大门，你的功劳我不会忘记。两人一起回到关押国王的地方。鲁斯塔姆把白魔肝中的血滴进凯·卡乌斯的眼睛里，国王的眼睛立刻亮了起来，又看见了阳光，看见了眼前的鲁斯塔姆。接着，鲁斯塔姆又把血滴进伊朗勇士们的眼睛里，所有的人都重见了光明。被囚禁的伊朗军队欢呼起来，他们拥抱鲁斯塔姆，赞美他是伊朗的救星，是勇士中的勇士。凯·卡乌斯坐在宝座上，命令摆设盛大的宴席，一连七天庆祝胜利，向造物主献上感恩的祷告。他对鲁斯塔姆说：没有你，就没有伊朗的国王。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

sections.bodyEn: Restored to strength, Kay Kāvus wrote to the king of Māzandarān commanding him to come and submit, surrender his treasure and become a vassal of Iran. The king of Māzandarān haughtily refused, gathered a host of demons and men with war-elephants, and came out to battle. For seven days the armies fought on the plain without either winning. On the eighth day Rostam reached the king of Māzandarān and thrust his spear at him, but just as it was about to strike, the sorcerer king turned himself into a huge rock; the spear struck stone and could not harm him. The Iranian champions were astonished, and none could move the rock. Rostam leapt down, lifted the rock alone, carried it all the way back to the Iranian camp, threw it down before the king's tent and said to it: 'Come out, or I will smash you to pieces with my hammer and throw you into the fire!' The king inside the rock was afraid, came out of the stone and took human shape again. Kay Kāvus had the wicked sorcerer put to death. Keeping his promise, Rostam asked the king to make Olād ruler of Māzandarān, and the army of Iran returned home laden with spoils.
sections.bodyZh: 凯·卡乌斯恢复了力量，写信给马赞德兰的国王，命令他前来投降，交出财宝，做伊朗的属国。马赞德兰国王收到信，傲慢地拒绝了，召集了魔鬼和人组成的大军，带着战象前来迎战。两军在平原上激战了七天，不分胜负。第八天，鲁斯塔姆冲到马赞德兰国王面前，举起长矛刺去，眼看就要刺中，那位会魔法的国王忽然把自己变成了一块巨大的岩石，长矛刺在石头上，再也伤不了他。伊朗的勇士们都惊呆了，谁也搬不动这块岩石。鲁斯塔姆跳下马，一个人把岩石扛了起来，一直扛回伊朗的营地，扔在国王的帐篷前，对着岩石说：快出来，否则我就用铁锤把你砸成碎块，扔到火里烧掉！岩石里的国王害怕了，从石头里走了出来，变回了人形。凯·卡乌斯下令处死了这个作恶多端的魔法师。鲁斯塔姆履行了诺言，请国王封乌拉德为马赞德兰的统治者。伊朗的大军满载着战利品，凯旋回国。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。
sections.headingEn: The king who became a rock

sections.bodyEn: But Kay Kāvus did not grow cautious from this lesson. Later a demon came again to tempt him: 'You rule the whole earth; why not rule the sky? Should not the sun, moon and stars be yours as well?' Again Kay Kāvus was tempted. He asked his wise men how to fly to the sky, and at last hit on a plan: he had four young eagles taken from their nests and reared on the choicest meat; then he had a throne made, set a long spear upright at each of its corners with a piece of mutton hanging from each spear-point, and bound four eagles that had been starved for days to its four corners. Straining for the meat above them, the eagles flew upward and carried the throne into the sky. Kay Kāvus rose higher and higher, above the clouds. But the eagles tired and could fly no more, and the throne fell from the sky into a desolate forest. Kay Kāvus escaped death but lay trapped in the forest, hungry and afraid. Rostam and the champions searched far and wide and at last found him. The champions rebuked him sharply: 'Again and again you listen to demons; you act like a madman.' Ashamed, Kay Kāvus shut himself away in penitence for many days.
sections.bodyZh: 可是凯·卡乌斯并没有因为这次教训变得谨慎。后来，一个魔鬼又来迷惑他，对他说：你已经统治了整个大地，为什么不去统治天空呢？天上的日月星辰，难道不该属于你吗？凯·卡乌斯又动了心。他问智者们怎样才能飞上天空，最后想出一个办法：他让人从鹰巢里捉来四只小鹰，用最好的肉喂养长大，然后造了一个宝座，在宝座的四角各竖一根长矛，矛尖上挂着一块羊肉，再把四只饿了好几天的鹰绑在宝座的四角。鹰想吃矛尖上的肉，拼命往上飞，就把宝座带上了天空。凯·卡乌斯坐在宝座上，越飞越高，越过了云层。可是鹰飞累了，再也飞不动了，宝座从空中坠落下来，跌进了一片荒凉的森林。凯·卡乌斯侥幸没有摔死，却困在林中又饿又怕。鲁斯塔姆和勇士们四处寻找，终于找到了他。勇士们严厉地责备他：你一次又一次地听信魔鬼，像个疯子一样。凯·卡乌斯羞愧难当，从此闭门忏悔了许多日子。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“凯·卡乌斯的更多愚行”一节。

stories.canonicalTitle: Shahnameh, Part 3: Rostam and Sohrāb
stories.editorialNote: 依据齐默恩 1883 年英文散文转述本《列王纪》中“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节，按顺序讲述。齐默恩的本子是节选与改写，不是完整译本，细节可能与菲尔多西原诗不同；父子相残的结局照原书交代，不渲染细节。

series.labelZh: 第三部 · 鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布

stories.summaryEn: Hunting on the border, Rostam loses Rakhsh to thieves and tracks him to Samangān. At night the princess Tahmineh comes to his chamber, saying she has long admired him and wishes to marry him and bear his son. They marry, and when he leaves he gives her an armlet: if a son is born, let him wear it on his arm. The boy, Sohrāb, grows wondrously fast and at ten has no equal. Learning from his mother that his father is Rostam, he resolves to invade Iran, overthrow Kay Kāvus and make his father king. Afrāsiyāb of Tūrān secretly orders his generals to keep father and son apart, hoping one will kill the other. Sohrāb takes the White Castle, from which the warrior maiden Gordāfarid escapes him by a ruse; Kay Kāvus summons Rostam and rages at his delay. When the armies meet, Sohrāb asks again and again for Rostam, but an Iranian captive tells him Rostam is not there, and Rostam himself hides his name. Father and son fight for three days: the first undecided; on the second Sohrāb throws his father but is tricked into sparing him; on the third Rostam, his strength restored by prayer, throws Sohrāb and drives a dagger into his breast. Dying, Sohrāb names his father; Rostam sees the armlet and is broken with grief. He sends to Kay Kāvus for the elixir of life, but the king delays, and Sohrāb dies in his father's arms.
stories.summaryZh: 鲁斯塔姆在边境打猎时，拉赫什被人偷走，他一路追到萨曼甘国。夜里，公主塔米娜来到他的房中，说她仰慕他已久，愿嫁给他，为他生一个儿子。两人成婚，鲁斯塔姆临别时留下一枚臂环，说生了儿子就戴在他的手臂上。孩子苏赫拉布长得飞快，十岁就无人能敌。他从母亲那里得知父亲是鲁斯塔姆，就决心率军攻入伊朗，推翻凯·卡乌斯，让父亲做国王。图兰王阿夫拉西亚布暗中命令将领们不让父子相认，盼着两人自相残杀。苏赫拉布攻下白堡，被女战士戈尔达法丽德用计脱身；凯·卡乌斯急召鲁斯塔姆，又因他迟到而发怒。两军对阵，苏赫拉布一再问起鲁斯塔姆，伊朗的俘虏却骗他说鲁斯塔姆不在军中，鲁斯塔姆自己也隐瞒了名字。父子二人斗了三天：第一天不分胜负，第二天苏赫拉布摔倒了父亲却被骗放过了他，第三天鲁斯塔姆向神求回力气，把苏赫拉布摔倒，一剑刺进了他的胸膛。苏赫拉布临死说出父亲的名字，鲁斯塔姆看见了臂环，悲痛欲绝。他派人向凯·卡乌斯求取长生药，国王却迟迟不给，苏赫拉布死在了父亲的怀里。
stories.titleZh: 列王纪 · 第三部 鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布

claims.statement: The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says Rakhsh was stolen by Turanian riders while Rostam slept after hunting on the border, and that Rostam tracked him to Samangān, whose king welcomed him as a guest.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says Tahmineh, princess of Samangān, came to Rostam's chamber by night, told him she had long loved him and wished to bear his son, and that Rostam then asked the king for her hand and married her.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says Rostam, leaving Samangān, gave Tahmineh an armlet to bind on their son's arm if a son were born, and that she bore Sohrāb and bound it on him.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says Sohrāb grew wondrously fast, learned from Tahmineh that Rostam was his father, and resolved to invade Iran, overthrow Kay Kāvus and set Rostam on the throne.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says Afrāsiyāb sent the generals Hūmān and Bārmān with an army to support Sohrāb, secretly charging them to keep father and son from knowing each other so that one might kill the other.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says the warrior maiden Gordāfarid rode out against Sohrāb from the White Castle, was revealed when he knocked off her helmet, and escaped him with a false promise before the castle's people fled by a secret way.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says Kay Kāvus summoned Rostam against the young invader, raged at his delay and ordered him hanged, and that Rostam rode off in anger until Gūdarz persuaded him that he would be thought afraid.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says Rostam, spying in the Turanian camp, unknowingly killed Tahmineh's brother Zende-razm, who was to point him out to Sohrāb, and that the captive Hajīr lied to Sohrāb that Rostam was not with the army.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says that on the first day Sohrāb asked his opponent whether he was Rostam, son of Zāl, that Rostam denied it, and that they fought with spears, swords and maces till evening without a victor.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says that on the second day Sohrāb threw Rostam and was about to kill him, but Rostam claimed an Iranian custom that a foe may be slain only at the second fall, and Sohrāb let him go.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says Rostam prayed for the return of the strength he had once asked God to lessen, and on the third day threw Sohrāb and stabbed him, whereupon the dying Sohrāb said his father Rostam would avenge him.

The Shahnameh, as retold by Zimmern ('Rustem and Sohrab'), says Rostam recognised his dying son by the armlet he had left with Tahmineh, that Kay Kāvus withheld the healing elixir, and that Sohrāb died, Rostam carried him home, and Tahmineh died of grief within a year.

events.titleEn: The warrior maiden of the White Castle

events.summaryEn: Sohrāb rode up before the Iranian host and shouted his challenge, then charged into the camp and cut down the banner before Kay Kāvus's tent, and not one Iranian champion dared come out.
events.summaryZh: 苏赫拉布骑马冲到伊朗军前，大声挑战，又冲进营中，砍倒了凯·卡乌斯帐前的旗帜，伊朗的勇士们没有一个敢出来应战。

events.summaryEn: On the second day, as soon as Sohrāb saw Rostam he came to meet him smiling: 'Did you sleep well?
events.summaryZh: 第二天，苏赫拉布一见到鲁斯塔姆，就笑着迎上去说：昨夜你睡得好吗？
events.titleEn: The ruse of the second day

events.summaryEn: Having escaped, Rostam went to a stream, washed himself, knelt and prayed to the Creator.
events.summaryZh: 鲁斯塔姆脱身以后，来到一条溪边，洗净了身体，跪在地上向造物主祈祷。

events.summaryEn: At these words the world went dark before Rostam's eyes and he fell senseless.
events.summaryZh: 鲁斯塔姆听见这句话，眼前一黑，昏倒在地。

versions.labelEn: Zimmern, The Epic of Kings: Rustem and Sohrab (long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本：鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布（长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 丢失的拉赫什、塔米娜的夜访、留下的信物、苏赫拉布的成长、阿夫拉西亚布的阴谋、白堡的女战士、国王的召唤、营帐边的夜探、错认、第一天与第二天、第三天、长生药与哀悼
versions.rightsNote: 齐默恩 1883 年的英文散文转述本属公共领域；本站据此发布独立讲述，人名采用现代通行的波斯语转写。

sections.bodyEn: One day, restless in heart, Rostam took his bow and lasso and rode Rakhsh to hunt on the border between Iran and Tūrān. On a plain he shot a wild ass, kindled a fire of branches, roasted it and ate his fill, then took off Rakhsh's bridle to let him graze and lay down on the grass to sleep. A band of Turanian riders passed, saw the splendid horse grazing alone, cast their lassos over him and led him off to their city. Rostam woke and searched everywhere, but there was no trace of Rakhsh. He was anxious and vexed: without Rakhsh he must walk in his heavy armour carrying his mace — how the Turanians would mock him! He followed the hoofprints all the way to the gate of the city of Samangān. When the king and nobles of Samangān heard that Rostam had come they rode out to meet him, and the king said: 'Hero, no one in my land would dare to harm you; your horse will surely be found. Be my guest in the palace tonight.'
sections.bodyZh: 有一天，鲁斯塔姆心中烦闷，就带上弓箭和套索，骑着拉赫什到伊朗与图兰交界的地方去打猎。他在一片原野上射死了一头野驴，用树枝生起火来，烤了野驴，吃饱以后，摘下拉赫什的辔头让它去吃草，自己躺在草地上睡着了。这时，一群图兰的骑手路过，看见这匹骏马在原野上独自吃草，就抛出套索把它套住，牵回城里去了。鲁斯塔姆醒来，四处寻找，不见拉赫什的踪影，心中又急又恼：没有了拉赫什，他穿着沉重的铠甲，带着铁杵，只能徒步行走，图兰人会怎样嘲笑他？他顺着马蹄印一路追去，一直追到了萨曼甘国的城门口。萨曼甘的国王和贵族们听说鲁斯塔姆来了，都出城迎接，国王对他说：英雄啊，在我的国土上，没有人敢伤害你，你的马一定能找回来，今晚请到我的宫中做客吧。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

sections.bodyEn: The king of Samangān held a great feast for Rostam, and when he had drunk he was led to a chamber hung with brocade to rest. Deep in the night the door opened softly; a slave-girl came in carrying a lighted candle, and behind her a beautiful maiden, her face like the moon, her figure like a cypress, her brows like bows and her hair like a dark lasso. Astonished, Rostam asked who she was and why she came at night. 'I am the daughter of the king of Samangān,' she said; 'my name is Tahmineh, and no one in this land has seen my face. I have heard many tales of you — how you fear neither lion nor dragon nor demon, how the earth trembles at your mace. I have long given you my heart and secretly vowed to marry no one but you. Now God has brought you to our city, and I have come to tell you: if you will, I wish to be your wife and bear you a son as brave as you. And I will have your Rakhsh found.' Seeing her as wise as she was beautiful, Rostam was glad, and the next day he sent a wise priest to ask the king for her hand. The king rejoiced and gave him his daughter by the proper rites.
sections.bodyZh: 萨曼甘的国王为鲁斯塔姆举行了盛大的宴会，鲁斯塔姆喝了酒，被领到一间铺着锦缎的卧室里休息。夜深了，房门忽然悄悄打开，一个侍女提着一支点燃的蜡烛走进来，身后跟着一位美丽的少女，她的脸像月亮，身段像柏树，眉毛像弯弓，头发像黑色的套索。鲁斯塔姆惊奇地问她是谁，深夜来做什么。少女说：我是萨曼甘国王的女儿，名叫塔米娜，在这片土地上没有人见过我的面容。我听过许多关于你的故事：你怎样不怕狮子、恶龙和魔鬼，你的铁杵怎样让大地颤抖。我早就倾心于你，暗暗发誓除了你谁也不嫁。如今神把你送到了我们的城里，我来是要告诉你：如果你愿意，我想做你的妻子，为你生一个像你一样勇敢的儿子。而且，我会让人把你的拉赫什找回来。鲁斯塔姆见她既美丽又聪慧，心中欢喜，第二天就请一位智慧的祭司向国王求婚。国王非常高兴，当即按照礼仪把女儿嫁给了他。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

sections.bodyEn: Soon after the marriage Rakhsh was found, and Rostam had to return to Iran. At parting he took from his arm an armlet set with a jewel, a treasure known to all, and gave it to Tahmineh: 'Keep this well. If God gives you a daughter, braid it into her hair and may it keep her safe; if you bear a son, bind it on his arm, that he may become brave as I am, and by this token let him come to find me.' He embraced Tahmineh, mounted Rakhsh and rode off towards Iran, and never came back to Samangān. Nine months later Tahmineh bore a son with a face bright as the moon and a smile like a flower, and people said he was the very image of Rostam and of his grandfather Sām. Tahmineh named him Sohrāb and bound the armlet on his arm.
sections.bodyZh: 婚后不久，人们找回了拉赫什，鲁斯塔姆必须回到伊朗去了。临别时，他从自己的手臂上解下一枚臂环——上面镶着一颗宝石，是一件人人都认得的珍宝——交给塔米娜，说：好好保管它。如果神赐给你一个女儿，就把它编进她的头发里，愿它保佑她平安；如果你生了一个儿子，就把它系在他的手臂上，让他像我一样成为勇敢的人，让他凭着这件信物来找我。说完，他拥抱了塔米娜，跨上拉赫什，向伊朗的方向驰去，从此再也没有回到萨曼甘。九个月以后，塔米娜生下了一个儿子，他的脸像月亮一样明亮，笑起来像花一样灿烂，人们说他长得和鲁斯塔姆、和祖父萨姆一模一样。塔米娜给他取名为苏赫拉布，把那枚臂环系在了他的手臂上。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

sections.bodyEn: Sohrāb grew astonishingly fast: at one month he was like a child of a year, at three he rode and shot, at five he had a lion's courage, and at ten no one in Samangān could match him in arms. Broad-chested and strong-armed, he ran swift as the wind. One day he came to his mother and asked: 'Why am I taller and stronger than other children? Who is my father? What shall I say when people ask about my birth?' Tahmineh said: 'Do not be angry, child. Your father is the great Rostam, son of Zāl, grandson of Sām; there is no braver hero in the world.' She showed him a letter Rostam had sent and three jewels, and warned him: 'Never let Afrāsiyāb, king of Tūrān, know this; he is Rostam's enemy and would seek to harm you. Nor let your father know you have grown into a warrior, or he will call you away from me.' Sohrāb's blood was fired: 'I will lead an army against Iran, overthrow Kay Kāvus and set my father Rostam on the throne; then I will defeat Afrāsiyāb, so that the world has no longer two kings.'
sections.bodyZh: 苏赫拉布长得出奇地快：一个月大时就像一岁的孩子，三岁时就学会了骑马射箭，五岁时有了狮子般的勇气，到了十岁，萨曼甘没有一个人能和他比武。他胸膛宽阔，手臂粗壮，跑起来像风一样快。有一天，他来到母亲面前，问她：我为什么比别的孩子都高大强壮？我的父亲是谁？别人问起我的家世，我该怎样回答？塔米娜说：孩子，不要生气，你的父亲就是伟大的鲁斯塔姆，扎尔的儿子，萨姆的孙子，世上没有比他更勇敢的英雄。她拿出鲁斯塔姆寄来的信和三颗宝石给他看，又叮嘱他：千万不要让图兰王阿夫拉西亚布知道这件事，他是鲁斯塔姆的仇敌，会想办法害你；也不要让你父亲知道你已经长成了一个勇士，否则他会把你从我身边叫走。苏赫拉布听了，热血沸腾，说：我要率领大军进攻伊朗，推翻凯·卡乌斯，让我的父亲鲁斯塔姆坐上王位；然后再去打败阿夫拉西亚布，让天下不再有两个国王。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

sections.bodyEn: Sohrāb chose himself a horse worthy of him and gathered an army. When the news reached Afrāsiyāb, king of Tūrān, he secretly rejoiced and devised a wicked plan. He sent two generals, Hūmān and Bārmān, with twelve thousand picked men and many gifts to join Sohrāb, as though to support his attack on Iran. In private he told the two: 'Keep this secret: father and son must never know each other. If Sohrāb meets Rostam in battle, contrive that neither knows who the other is. Perhaps the young warrior will kill Rostam, and Iran will lose its strongest pillar; perhaps Rostam will kill the boy, and grief will break Rostam's heart. Either way Tūrān gains.' Hūmān and Bārmān took their orders and came to Samangān with gifts and a letter from Afrāsiyāb, and Sohrāb welcomed them gladly, knowing nothing of the plot behind them.
sections.bodyZh: 苏赫拉布为自己挑选了一匹配得上他的骏马，召集了一支军队。消息传到图兰王阿夫拉西亚布那里，他心中暗喜，想出了一个阴险的计策。他派出两位将领胡曼和巴尔曼，带着一万二千名精兵和许多礼物去投奔苏赫拉布，表面上是支持他攻打伊朗。他在私下里对两位将领说：这件事一定要保守秘密，千万不能让父子二人相认。如果苏赫拉布在战场上遇见鲁斯塔姆，就要想办法让他们彼此不知道对方是谁。也许这个年轻的勇士会杀死鲁斯塔姆，那样伊朗就失去了最强的支柱；也许鲁斯塔姆会杀死这个孩子，那样鲁斯塔姆的心也会被悲伤压垮。不论哪一种，对我们图兰都有好处。胡曼和巴尔曼领了命令，带着礼物和阿夫拉西亚布的书信来到萨曼甘，苏赫拉布高兴地接待了他们，一点也不知道这背后的阴谋。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

sections.bodyEn: Sohrāb led his army into Iran and came to the White Castle on the border. Its champion Hajīr rode out against him and was unhorsed and taken prisoner within a few passes. The people in the castle were in dismay. Among them was a maiden named Gordāfarid, daughter of the commander, brave and skilled in arms. She hid her hair in a helmet, put on armour, rode out and challenged Sohrāb. They fought; her arrows fell thick as rain, but Sohrāb took them on his shield, charged, and with his spear knocked off her helmet, and her long hair tumbled down. Only then did he see his foe was a maiden, and he was astonished and drawn to her. Seeing her peril, Gordāfarid said: 'You will be mocked if you fight a woman before both armies. Let us make peace: the castle and all in it are yours, and I will wait for you within.' Sohrāb believed her and followed her to the gate, but she slipped inside, shut the gate, and laughed at him from the walls: 'Warrior of Tūrān, go home; when Rostam comes, your good days are over.' That night the people of the castle escaped by a secret passage, and when Sohrāb stormed it the next day it was empty.
sections.bodyZh: 苏赫拉布率领大军进入伊朗，来到边境上的白堡。守城的勇士哈吉尔出城迎战，几个回合就被苏赫拉布打下马来，成了俘虏。城中的人们惊慌失措。这时，城里有一位名叫戈尔达法丽德的少女，她是守将的女儿，勇敢而精通武艺。她把头发藏进头盔里，穿上铠甲，骑马出城，向苏赫拉布挑战。两人交战，她射出的箭像雨点一样密集，苏赫拉布用盾牌挡住，冲上前去，用长矛挑落了她的头盔，她的长发一下子披散下来，苏赫拉布这才发现对手是一个少女，心中又惊又爱。戈尔达法丽德见势不妙，就对他说：你若在两军面前和一个女子交战，会被人笑话的。不如我们讲和，城堡和城里的一切都归你，我在城中等你。苏赫拉布相信了她，跟到城门前，她却一闪身进了城，关上城门，在城墙上笑着对他说：图兰的勇士啊，你还是回去吧，等鲁斯塔姆来了，你就没有好日子过了。当天夜里，城里的人们从一条秘密的地道逃走了，第二天苏赫拉布攻进城时，城中已经空无一人。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。
sections.headingEn: The warrior maiden of the White Castle

sections.bodyEn: When news of the White Castle's fall reached Kay Kāvus, the king was terrified and at once wrote to Rostam, sending the champion Gīv riding day and night to Zābulistān to beg him to come with all speed against the young enemy. Reading the letter and hearing of a young champion from Tūrān, Rostam wondered: 'How could Tūrān have such a hero? I had only one child, in Samangān, and he is still small; it cannot be he.' He was in no hurry, kept Gīv feasting at his house for several days, and only then set out. When they reached the court, Kay Kāvus flew into a rage, accused Rostam of scorning the royal command, and ordered him and Gīv hanged. Rostam was furious: 'I am the guardian of Iran, not your slave! Deal with the young man yourself this time.' He mounted Rakhsh and rode off. The champions were dismayed; old Gūdarz rode after him and said: 'People will say Rostam left because he feared the young man.' Unwilling to bear the name of coward, Rostam returned to court, and Kay Kāvus begged his pardon.
sections.bodyZh: 白堡失守的消息传到凯·卡乌斯那里，国王惊恐万分，立刻写信给鲁斯塔姆，派勇士吉夫日夜兼程送到扎布尔斯坦，请他火速前来抵挡这个年轻的敌人。鲁斯塔姆读了信，听说图兰来了一个年轻的勇士，心中奇怪：图兰怎么会有这样的英雄？我只在萨曼甘有过一个孩子，可他还小，不可能是他。他并不着急，留吉夫在家中饮酒作乐，一连几天才出发。等他们来到凯·卡乌斯的宫廷，国王勃然大怒，骂鲁斯塔姆藐视王命，下令把他和吉夫一起吊死。鲁斯塔姆怒不可遏，说：我是伊朗的守护者，不是你的奴隶！你这次自己去对付那个年轻人吧。他骑上拉赫什扬长而去。众位勇士都慌了，年老的古达尔兹赶去追他，劝他说：人们会说鲁斯塔姆是怕了那个年轻人才走的。鲁斯塔姆听了，不愿背上胆怯的名声，就回到了宫中，凯·卡乌斯也向他道了歉。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

sections.bodyEn: The Iranian army came before the White Castle and faced the Turanians across the plain. At night Rostam put on Turanian clothes and stole into the enemy camp to see the young champion for himself. He saw Sohrāb seated at the head of the feast, tall and straight as a cypress, noble of face, and marvelled in his heart. Beside Sohrāb sat Zende-razm, Tahmineh's brother, whom she had sent with the army to point out Rostam to Sohrāb on the field. As Zende-razm left the tent he met the stranger in the dark and challenged him; Rostam struck him on the head with his fist and killed him. So the one man who knew Rostam by sight was dead. In the morning Sohrāb climbed a height and had the captive Hajīr point out the tent of each Iranian champion; he asked especially about a great green tent with a banner painted with a dragon before it and a tall horse tethered beside it. Hajīr thought: if I say this is Rostam's, the young man will seek him out and may kill him. So he lied: 'That is an ally from China; Rostam is not with the army; he is in Zābulistān for a festival.'
sections.bodyZh: 伊朗大军来到白堡前，与图兰军队隔着平原对阵。夜里，鲁斯塔姆换上图兰人的衣服，悄悄潜入敌营，想亲眼看看这个年轻的勇士。他看见苏赫拉布坐在宴席的主位上，身材高大，像一棵挺拔的柏树，相貌英武，鲁斯塔姆心中暗暗称奇。坐在苏赫拉布身边的，是塔米娜的兄弟赞德·拉兹姆，塔米娜派他随军，就是为了在战场上把鲁斯塔姆指认给苏赫拉布。赞德·拉兹姆出帐时，在暗处撞见了陌生的鲁斯塔姆，喝问他是谁，鲁斯塔姆一拳打在他的头上，把他打死了。唯一认得鲁斯塔姆的人，就这样死去了。第二天早晨，苏赫拉布登上高处，让俘虏哈吉尔把伊朗军中每一位勇士的帐篷指给他看，他特别问到一座绿色的大帐篷，帐前竖着一面绘着龙的旗帜，旁边拴着一匹高大的骏马。哈吉尔心想：如果说出这是鲁斯塔姆，这个年轻人一定会去找他决斗，也许会把他杀死。于是他撒谎说：那是一位从中国来的盟友，鲁斯塔姆不在军中，他在扎布尔斯坦过节。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

sections.bodyEn: Sohrāb rode up before the Iranian host and shouted his challenge, then charged into the camp and cut down the banner before Kay Kāvus's tent, and not one Iranian champion dared come out. Kay Kāvus had to ask Rostam to fight. Rostam put on his tiger-skin coat and rode Rakhsh out between the armies. Looking at the young man, he felt a stirring he could not name, and said: 'Young man, you are still so young; why come to your death? I have seen many battlefields and overcome countless demons and champions; I pity you and would not kill you.' Gazing at the old hero, Sohrāb too felt a strange kinship and asked: 'Tell me truly, are you Rostam, son of Zāl?' To keep his name hidden, Rostam answered: 'I am not Rostam, only one of his men; he is a great hero, and I have not even a stable of my own.' Sohrāb's hope fell. They fought with spears, swords and maces until the spears broke, the swords were notched and the maces bent; both ran with sweat and were spent, and when evening came neither had won, and they agreed to fight again the next day.
sections.bodyZh: 苏赫拉布骑马冲到伊朗军前，大声挑战，又冲进营中，砍倒了凯·卡乌斯帐前的旗帜，伊朗的勇士们没有一个敢出来应战。凯·卡乌斯只好请鲁斯塔姆出战。鲁斯塔姆穿上虎皮战袍，骑着拉赫什来到两军之间。他看着眼前这个年轻人，心中涌起一种说不出的感情，对他说：年轻人，你还这样年轻，何必来送死？我见过许多战场，打败过无数魔鬼和勇士，我可怜你，不忍心杀你。苏赫拉布望着这位老英雄，心中也忽然生出一种奇怪的亲切感，问道：请你告诉我实话，你是不是鲁斯塔姆，扎尔的儿子？鲁斯塔姆为了不让对方知道自己的身份，回答说：我不是鲁斯塔姆，我只是他的一个手下，他是一位大英雄，而我连马厩都没有。苏赫拉布失望极了。两人用长矛、刀剑和铁杵交战，长矛断了，刀剑卷了刃，铁杵弯了，两人都汗流浃背，筋疲力尽，直到黄昏也分不出胜负，只好约定第二天再战。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

sections.bodyEn: On the second day, as soon as Sohrāb saw Rostam he came to meet him smiling: 'Did you sleep well? Why should we fight? My heart feels a kinship with you I cannot explain; let us lay down our arms and sit and drink together. Tell me — are you truly not Rostam?' Rostam said: 'We agreed yesterday to wrestle; say no more of this.' They dismounted and wrestled from morning till noon, and Sohrāb, like a lion falling on its prey, threw Rostam to the ground, sat on his chest and drew his dagger to cut off his head. Quick-witted in his peril, Rostam said: 'Young man, among us in Iran there is a custom: when two champions wrestle, the one who first throws his foe may not kill him; only when he throws him a second time may he take his life.' Young and proud, Sohrāb believed it and let him go. Back in camp Hūmān heard of it and rebuked him: 'You have let go a lion already in the net; you will regret it.' But Sohrāb thought little of it.
sections.bodyZh: 第二天，苏赫拉布一见到鲁斯塔姆，就笑着迎上去说：昨夜你睡得好吗？我们为什么要打仗呢？我心里对你有说不出的亲近，我们放下武器，坐下来一起喝酒吧。告诉我，你真的不是鲁斯塔姆吗？鲁斯塔姆说：我们昨天约好了要摔跤，不要再说这些话了。两人下马摔跤，从早晨一直扭打到中午，苏赫拉布像一头狮子扑向猎物一样，把鲁斯塔姆摔倒在地，骑在他的胸口上，拔出匕首就要砍下他的头。鲁斯塔姆急中生智，说：年轻人，在我们伊朗有一个规矩：两个勇士摔跤，第一次把对手摔倒的人不能杀他，要第二次摔倒对手才能取他的性命。苏赫拉布年轻而骄傲，相信了这番话，就放开了他。回到营中，胡曼听说了这件事，责备苏赫拉布说：你放走了一头已经落进网里的狮子，你会为此后悔的。苏赫拉布却不以为意。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。
sections.headingEn: The ruse of the second day

sections.bodyEn: Having escaped, Rostam went to a stream, washed himself, knelt and prayed to the Creator. It is told that in his youth his strength had been so great that when he walked on rock his feet sank into the stone, and he had asked God to take back part of it so that he could walk like other men. Now he prayed God to give that strength back, and God granted his prayer. On the third day they met again and wrestled once more. This time, with all his strength restored, Rostam seized Sohrāb by the head and waist, lifted him like an uprooted tree and dashed him to the ground. Knowing the young man would not stay down long, he drew his dagger and drove it into Sohrāb's breast. Sohrāb turned over in his blood and sighed: 'I have brought this on myself; fate gave the key of my life into your hand. But know this: wherever you flee, though you become a fish in the sea or a star in the sky, my father will find you and avenge me. My father is Rostam. I came here only to find him.'
sections.bodyZh: 鲁斯塔姆脱身以后，来到一条溪边，洗净了身体，跪在地上向造物主祈祷。据说他年轻的时候力气大得惊人，走在岩石上，双脚都会陷进石头里，他曾经请求神收回一部分力量，好让他能像常人一样行走。现在，他祈求神把那份力量还给他。神应允了他的祈祷。第三天，两人又在战场上相遇，又一次摔起跤来。这一次，鲁斯塔姆恢复了全部的力量，他抓住苏赫拉布的头和腰，像拔起一棵树一样把他举起来，重重地摔在地上。他知道这个年轻人不会被压在地上太久，就迅速拔出匕首，刺进了苏赫拉布的胸膛。苏赫拉布在血泊中翻过身来，叹息着说：这是我自作自受，命运把我的钥匙交到了你的手里。可是你要知道，无论你逃到哪里，就算你变成水里的鱼、天上的星，我的父亲也会找到你，为我报仇。我的父亲就是鲁斯塔姆。我来这里，只是为了找他。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

sections.bodyEn: At these words the world went dark before Rostam's eyes and he fell senseless. When he came to, he asked trembling: 'What token have you that you are Rostam's son? I am Rostam!' Sohrāb said: 'Undo my armour and look at my arm.' Rostam undid the armour and saw the armlet he had once left with Tahmineh. He tore his clothes and his hair and cried aloud: 'I have killed my own son with my own hand.' Sohrāb said: 'Weeping is useless now; this was fated.' Rostam sent Gūdarz to Kay Kāvus to beg the elixir kept in the king's treasury that heals every wound. But Kay Kāvus thought: if this young man lives and father and son join together, will my throne be safe? and he delayed. Rostam resolved to go and beg it himself, but before he reached the king a messenger overtook him: Sohrāb was dead. In his grief Rostam would have killed himself with his dagger, but the others held him back. He burned his tent and his throne, wrapped his son's body in golden brocade and carried it home to Zābulistān for burial. When the news reached Samangān, Tahmineh tore her clothes and wept day and night, clasping her son's armour and his horse, and within a year she followed her son out of the world.
sections.bodyZh: 鲁斯塔姆听见这句话，眼前一黑，昏倒在地。醒来后，他颤抖着问：你有什么能证明你是鲁斯塔姆的儿子？我就是鲁斯塔姆！苏赫拉布说：解开我的铠甲，看看我的手臂。鲁斯塔姆解开铠甲，看见了那枚自己当年留给塔米娜的臂环。他撕扯着自己的衣服和头发，痛哭失声，说：我亲手杀死了我的儿子。苏赫拉布说：哭也没有用了，这是命中注定的。鲁斯塔姆派古达尔兹去见凯·卡乌斯，请求国王赐给他宫中珍藏的长生药，能治好一切创伤。凯·卡乌斯却心想：如果这个年轻人活下来，父子二人联手，我的王位还能保得住吗？他迟迟不肯给药。鲁斯塔姆决定亲自去求，还没有走到国王那里，就有人追上来报告：苏赫拉布已经死了。鲁斯塔姆悲痛欲绝，想用匕首自尽，被众人拦住。他烧掉了自己的帐篷和宝座，用金色的锦缎包裹儿子的遗体，带回扎布尔斯坦安葬。消息传到萨曼甘，塔米娜撕碎了衣裳，日夜痛哭，抱着儿子的战袍和骏马，不到一年，就随着儿子离开了人世。
sections.evidenceNote: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。
