stories.canonicalTitle: Soushen ji: thirteen tales of the strange
stories.editorialNote: 依据古腾堡计划所收《搜神记》二十卷本，按卷次选读十三则，用白话独立讲述。今本《搜神记》是后人从类书中辑录重编的，卷次与条目未必是干宝原书的面貌；东海孝妇一则中关于周青血溅竹竿的部分，原书标为“长老传云”的传说。
stories.summaryEn: Gan Bao, a historian of the Eastern Jin, gathered accounts of immortals, ghosts and strange events into the Soushen ji, In Search of the Supernatural. This reading follows the juan in order through thirteen of its tales: the filial Dong Yong sells himself to bury his father, and the Weaving Maiden of heaven comes down to weave his debt away; the swordsmith Gan Jiang is killed by the king of Chu, and his son Chi Bi gives his own head and sword to a stranger, who beheads the king in a boiling cauldron so that the three heads are buried together as the Tomb of the Three Kings; Fan Juqing keeps a promise across a thousand li and learns in a dream of his dead friend's burial; a filial widow of Donghai dies unjustly, her blood flows up the pole and the commandery suffers three years of drought; from the graves of Han Ping and his wife grow catalpas whose roots and branches intertwine, the trees of longing; Chang'e steals the elixir and flees to the moon; a girl's jesting promise to a horse ends with the horse's hide carrying her off and both turning into silkworms; a woman in a feather robe, her robe hidden, marries and bears daughters, then finds it and flies away; Ziyu, princess of Wu, dies of longing and meets her beloved as a ghost; Song Dingbo outwits a ghost and sells it as a sheep; the girl Li Ji, with a sword and a dog, kills the serpent that devoured maidens; and the dog Black Dragon soaks itself to put out a fire around its drunken master.
stories.summaryZh: 东晋史官干宝收集了许多关于神仙、鬼怪和奇异之事的记载，编成《搜神记》。本篇按卷次选读其中十三则：孝子董永卖身葬父，天上的织女下凡为他织绢还债；铸剑师干将被楚王杀害，儿子赤比把自己的头和剑交给一位侠客，侠客在汤镬中斩下楚王的头，三颗头煮在一起，葬为三王墓；范巨卿千里赴约，又在梦中得知亡友的葬期；东海孝妇蒙冤而死，鲜血逆流而上，郡中三年大旱；韩凭夫妇死后，两座坟上长出的梓树枝根相交，被称为相思树；嫦娥偷了不死药奔向月亮；少女戏言许嫁的马被杀，马皮卷走少女，化成了蚕；披着羽衣的女子被藏起衣服，嫁人生女，最后找回羽衣飞去；吴王之女紫玉相思而死，化为鬼魂与韩重相会；宋定伯骗过了一个鬼，把它当羊卖了；少女李寄带着剑和狗，斩杀了吞食少女的大蛇；义犬黑龙用湿透的身体扑灭野火，救了醉卧的主人。
stories.titleZh: 搜神记选读：十三个志怪故事

claims.statement: Soushen ji juan 1 says Dong Yong sold himself to bury his father, and that the woman who became his wife wove a hundred bolts of silk in ten days to repay his master, revealed herself as the Weaving Maiden sent by the Lord of Heaven for his filial piety, and rose into the sky.

Soushen ji juan 11 says the swordsmith Gan Jiang, foreseeing that the king of Chu would kill him for taking three years, brought only the female sword and left word that the male sword lay behind a pine on a stone, which his son Chi Bi found behind the pine pillar of the hall.

Soushen ji juan 11 says Chi Bi gave his own head and sword to a stranger, who boiled the head before the king of Chu, cut off the king's head into the cauldron and then his own, so that the three heads were buried together as the Tomb of the Three Kings.

Soushen ji juan 11 says Fan Juqing kept his two-year promise to visit Zhang Yuanbo, and that after Zhang's death a dream summoned him to the burial, where the coffin would not move until he came and bade his friend farewell.

Soushen ji juan 11 says a filial widow of Donghai was falsely condemned for her mother-in-law's suicide, that three years of drought followed until a new governor sacrificed at her grave, and adds the elders' tale that her blood flowed up the bamboo pole as she had sworn.

Soushen ji juan 11 says that after King Kang of Song took Han Ping's wife, both husband and wife took their own lives, and that from their separate graves grew catalpas whose roots and branches intertwined, with a pair of mandarin ducks in them, called the Trees of Longing.

Soushen ji juan 14 says Heng'e stole the drug of deathlessness that Yi had obtained from the Queen Mother of the West, consulted the diviner Youhuang, who called the journey auspicious, and entrusted herself to the moon, becoming the toad.

Soushen ji juan 14 tells that a girl promised in jest to marry the horse if it brought her father home, that her father shot the horse, and that its hide carried her off and both turned into silkworms in a tree thereafter called sang, the mulberry.

Soushen ji juan 14 tells of a man of Xinyu who hid the feather robe of one of several bird-women, married her and had three daughters, until she found the robe under the grain stack, flew away, and later came back for her daughters.

Soushen ji juan 16 says Ziyu, daughter of King Fuchai of Wu, died of grief when her father refused Han Zhong, met him as a ghost at her tomb and gave him a pearl, and appeared to her father to clear him, vanishing like smoke when her mother embraced her.

Soushen ji juan 16 says Song Dingbo, meeting a ghost at night, pretended to be a new ghost, learned that ghosts fear human spittle, carried the ghost into the market of Wan where it turned into a sheep, and sold it for fifteen hundred cash after spitting on it.

Soushen ji juan 19 says Li Ji, youngest of six daughters, volunteered as the sacrifice to the great serpent of Yongling that had devoured nine girls, and killed it with a sword, a snake-biting dog and honeyed rice cakes, after which the king of Yue made her his queen.

Soushen ji juan 20 says the dog Black Dragon saved its drunken master Li Xinchun from a grass fire by soaking itself in a stream and wetting the grass around him until it died of exhaustion, and that the governor had it buried in the Tomb of the Faithful Dog.

events.summaryEn: In the Han dynasty there was a man of Qiancheng named Dong Yong.
events.summaryZh: 汉朝的时候，千乘县有一个人叫董永。
events.titleEn: Dong Yong and the Weaving Maiden

events.summaryEn: Gan Jiang and Mo Ye of Chu forged swords for the king of Chu, and it took them three years.
events.summaryZh: 楚国的干将和莫邪为楚王铸剑，用了三年才铸成。

events.summaryEn: The king of Chu dreamed of a boy with a foot's breadth between his brows who said he would take vengeance, and the king offered a thousand pieces of gold for him.
events.summaryZh: 楚王梦见一个少年，两眉之间宽一尺，说要来报仇。
events.titleEn: The Tomb of the Three Kings

events.summaryEn: In the Han dynasty Fan Shi, styled Juqing, of Jinxiang in Shanyang, was a close friend of Zhang Shao of Runan, styled Yuanbo.
events.summaryZh: 汉朝的范式，字巨卿，是山阳金乡人，和汝南的张劭是好朋友，张劭字元伯。

events.summaryEn: In the Han dynasty there was in Donghai commandery a filial daughter-in-law who served her mother-in-law with great devotion.
events.summaryZh: 汉朝的时候，东海郡有一位孝顺的媳妇，奉养婆婆非常尽心。

events.summaryEn: Han Ping, a retainer of King Kang of Song, married a woman of the He family who was very beautiful, and King Kang took her from him.
events.summaryZh: 宋康王的舍人韩凭，娶了何氏为妻，何氏非常美丽，宋康王就把她夺了去。

events.summaryEn: Yi obtained from the Queen Mother of the West the drug of deathlessness, and his wife Heng'e — later more often written Chang'e — stole it and fled to the moon.
events.summaryZh: 后羿向西王母求得了长生不死的药，他的妻子姮娥——后来人们多写作嫦娥——偷了这药，奔向月亮。

events.summaryEn: An old tale says: in high antiquity a man went far away to war, leaving at home only his daughter and a stallion, which she tended herself.
events.summaryZh: 古老的传说讲：远古的时候，有一个人出远门去征战，家里没有别人，只剩下一个女儿和一匹公马，女儿亲自喂养这匹马。
events.titleEn: The girl who became a silkworm

events.summaryEn: A man of Xinyu county in Yuzhang saw six or seven women in a field, all in robes of feathers, not knowing that they were birds.
events.summaryZh: 豫章郡新喻县有一个男子，看见田里有六七个女子，都穿着羽毛做的衣服，他不知道她们其实是鸟。

events.summaryEn: Ziyu, youngest daughter of King Fuchai of Wu, was eighteen, outstanding in talent and beauty.
events.summaryZh: 吴王夫差的小女儿名叫紫玉，十八岁，才华和容貌都很出众。

events.summaryEn: Song Dingbo of Nanyang, when he was young, was walking at night and met a ghost.
events.summaryZh: 南阳有个叫宋定伯的人，年轻的时候，有一次夜里赶路，遇到了一个鬼。

events.summaryEn: In Minzhong of Eastern Yue there is a ridge called Yongling, tens of li high, and in a valley to its northwest lived a great serpent seven or eight zhang long and more than ten spans round, which the local people dreaded.
events.summaryZh: 东越闽中有一座庸岭，高几十里，岭的西北山谷里住着一条大蛇，长七八丈，粗十几围，当地人都很害怕。

events.summaryEn: In the time of Sun Quan there lived in Jinan in Xiangyang a man named Li Xinchun who kept a dog called Black Dragon.
events.summaryZh: 三国孙权的时候，襄阳纪南有一个人叫李信纯，家里养了一条狗，名叫黑龙，他非常喜爱这条狗，走到哪里都带着它，吃饭喝酒的时候也总分给它一份。
events.titleEn: The tomb of the faithful dog

versions.labelEn: Gan Bao, Soushen ji: thirteen selected tales (long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 干宝《搜神记》选读十三则（长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 董永与织女、干将莫邪、三王墓、范巨卿与张元伯、东海孝妇、韩凭夫妇、嫦娥奔月、女化蚕、毛衣女、紫玉与韩重、宋定伯卖鬼、李寄斩蛇、义犬冢
versions.rightsNote: 《搜神记》原文属公共领域；本站发布白话的独立讲述，不照录原文。

sections.bodyEn: In the Han dynasty there was a man of Qiancheng named Dong Yong. He lost his mother young and lived with his father, labouring hard in the fields with his father riding beside him in a little deer-cart. When his father died, Dong Yong was too poor to bury him, so he sold himself as a bondservant and used the price for the funeral. His master, knowing him to be worthy and filial, gave him ten thousand cash and sent him home. When Dong Yong had finished three years of mourning, he set out for his master's house to fulfil his bond. On the road he met a woman who said: 'I wish to be your wife,' and they went on together. The master said: 'I gave you the money; you need not come.' Dong Yong said: 'By your kindness my father was buried. Humble as I am, I must work with all my strength to repay you.' 'What can your wife do?' 'She can weave.' 'If so, let her weave me a hundred bolts of fine silk.' His wife wove in the master's house and finished in ten days. Coming out of the gate she said to Dong Yong: 'I am the Weaving Maiden of heaven. Because of your great filial piety, the Lord of Heaven sent me to help you repay your debt.' With that she rose into the sky, and no one knew where she had gone.
sections.bodyZh: 汉朝的时候，千乘县有一个人叫董永。他从小失去了母亲，和父亲相依为命，在田里拼命干活，干活时用一辆小鹿车拉着父亲跟在身边。父亲去世了，董永穷得连下葬的钱都没有，就把自己卖给别人做奴仆，用卖身的钱为父亲办了丧事。买他的主人知道他是个贤孝的人，给了他一万钱，让他回家去。董永为父亲守完三年的孝，就动身去主人家，准备履行做奴仆的义务。路上遇到一个女子，对他说：我愿意做你的妻子。两人就一起去了。主人说：钱已经送给你了，你不必来了。董永说：承蒙您的恩惠，我父亲才得以安葬。我虽然是个小人物，也一定要尽力干活，报答您的厚恩。主人问：你的妻子会做什么？董永说：会织布。主人说：既然这样，就让你妻子为我织一百匹细绢吧。董永的妻子就在主人家织绢，十天就织完了。她走出门，对董永说：我是天上的织女。因为你极其孝顺，天帝派我来帮你还债。说完，凌空而去，再也不知道她去了哪里。
sections.headingEn: Dong Yong and the Weaving Maiden

sections.bodyEn: Gan Jiang and Mo Ye of Chu forged swords for the king of Chu, and it took them three years. The king, angry at the delay, meant to kill them. The swords were a pair, male and female. Mo Ye was then with child and near her time. Gan Jiang said to his wife: 'I took three years to forge the king's swords; he is angry, and if I go he will surely kill me. If you bear a son, when he is grown tell him: go out of the door and look at the southern mountain; a pine grows on a stone; the sword is at its back.' Then he took the female sword to the king. The king, furious, had the sword examined, and the examiner said: 'There should be two swords, a male and a female; the female has come, but the male has not.' Angrier still, the king had Gan Jiang killed at once. Mo Ye bore a son named Chi Bi. When he was grown he asked his mother: 'Where is my father?' She said: 'Your father forged swords for the king of Chu; it took three years, the king was angry and killed him. When he left he told me to tell you: go out of the door and look at the southern mountain; a pine grows on a stone; the sword is at its back.' Chi Bi went out and looked south, but saw no mountain — only the stone base beneath the pine pillar in front of the hall. He split the back of the pillar with an axe and found the male sword. From then on he thought day and night of vengeance on the king of Chu.
sections.bodyZh: 楚国的干将和莫邪为楚王铸剑，用了三年才铸成。楚王嫌他们太慢，十分恼怒，想要杀掉他们。剑铸成了一对，一雄一雌。那时莫邪怀着身孕，快要生产了。干将对妻子说：我为楚王铸剑，三年才成，楚王已经发怒，我去了他一定会杀我。你若生的是男孩，等他长大了，告诉他：出了家门望南山，松树长在石头上，剑就在它的背后。说完，干将就带着雌剑去见楚王。楚王大怒，叫人察看那把剑，相剑的人说：剑本来有两把，一雄一雌，现在雌剑来了，雄剑却没有来。楚王更加愤怒，立刻杀了干将。莫邪后来生下一个儿子，取名赤比。赤比长大以后，问母亲：我的父亲在哪里？母亲说：你父亲为楚王铸剑，三年才成，楚王发怒，把他杀了。他走的时候嘱咐我告诉你：出了家门望南山，松树长在石头上，剑就在它的背后。赤比走出门向南望去，并没有看见山，只看见堂屋前松木柱子下面的石墩。他用斧头劈开柱子的背面，果然得到了那把雄剑。从此，他日夜想着要向楚王报仇。

sections.bodyEn: The king of Chu dreamed of a boy with a foot's breadth between his brows who said he would take vengeance, and the king offered a thousand pieces of gold for him. Hearing of it, Chi Bi fled into the mountains, singing sorrowfully as he went. A stranger met him and asked: 'You are so young; why do you weep so bitterly?' 'I am the son of Gan Jiang and Mo Ye. The king of Chu killed my father, and I would avenge him.' The stranger said: 'I hear the king has offered a thousand gold for your head. Give me your head and your sword, and I will avenge you.' 'Gladly!' said Chi Bi; he cut his own throat and, holding up his head and sword in both hands, offered them, his body standing rigid. 'I will not fail you,' said the stranger, and only then did the body fall. The stranger took the head to the king, who was delighted. 'This is the head of a hero,' said the stranger; 'it should be boiled in a cauldron.' The king did so. For three days and nights it boiled without softening, and it leapt out of the water, glaring in fury. 'The boy's head will not soften,' said the stranger; 'let Your Majesty come and look at it, and it surely will.' The king went to the cauldron; the stranger swung the sword and the king's head fell into the soup; then he cut off his own head, and it too fell in. The three heads boiled away together until none could be told apart, so the soup and flesh were divided and buried in three graves, called together the Tomb of the Three Kings. It lies, the text says, in the bounds of Northern Yichun county in Runan.
sections.bodyZh: 楚王梦见一个少年，两眉之间宽一尺，说要来报仇。楚王就悬赏千金捉拿他。赤比听说了，逃进山里，一边走一边悲歌。有一位陌生的侠客遇见他，问：你年纪这么小，为什么哭得这样悲伤？赤比说：我是干将莫邪的儿子，楚王杀了我父亲，我要报仇。侠客说：听说楚王悬赏千金要你的头，你把头和剑交给我，我替你报仇。赤比说：太好了！就自刎而死，两手捧着自己的头和剑交给侠客，身体直挺挺地站着不倒。侠客说：我不会辜负你的。尸体这才倒下。侠客提着头去见楚王，楚王大喜。侠客说：这是勇士的头，应当放在汤镬里煮烂。楚王照办了。头煮了三天三夜，也没有煮烂，还从沸水中跳出来，瞪着眼睛，满脸怒气。侠客说：这孩子的头煮不烂，请大王亲自到锅边看一看，就一定会烂了。楚王走到锅边，侠客挥剑一砍，楚王的头掉进了汤里；侠客又挥剑砍下自己的头，头也掉进了汤里。三颗头一起煮烂，再也分辨不出是谁的。人们只好把汤和肉分成三份埋葬，统称为“三王墓”。书中说，墓在汝南北宜春县境内。
sections.headingEn: The Tomb of the Three Kings

sections.bodyEn: In the Han dynasty Fan Shi, styled Juqing, of Jinxiang in Shanyang, was a close friend of Zhang Shao of Runan, styled Yuanbo. They studied together at the Imperial Academy. When they took leave to go home, Fan said to Zhang: 'In two years I will come back and visit your parents and see your children,' and they fixed the day. As the day drew near Zhang told his mother and asked her to prepare food for the guest. She said: 'A parting two years ago, a word spoken a thousand li away — how can you trust it so?' 'Juqing is a man of his word; he will not fail.' 'Then I will brew wine for you.' On the day, Fan came, paid his respects in the hall, drank happily and left. Later Zhang fell gravely ill and died. Fan suddenly dreamed of Zhang in a black ceremonial cap with hanging tassels, slippers on his feet, calling: 'Juqing, I died on such a day and shall be buried at such a time, returning for ever to the Yellow Springs. If you have not forgotten me, can you still come in time?' Fan woke weeping, put on the mourning dress for a friend and galloped off to reach the burial. Before he arrived the cortège had set out; at the grave, as the coffin was to be lowered, it would not move. Zhang's mother stroked it and said: 'Yuanbo, are you waiting for someone?' and they halted. After a while a white carriage drawn by a white horse came wailing. Seeing it, the mother said: 'That must be Fan Juqing.' Fan knelt before the coffin: 'Go now, Yuanbo! Life and death take different roads; farewell for ever.' The thousand mourners all wept. Fan took the rope and drew the coffin, and only then did it move forward.
sections.bodyZh: 汉朝的范式，字巨卿，是山阳金乡人，和汝南的张劭是好朋友，张劭字元伯。两人一同在太学读书。后来各自告假回乡，范式对张劭说：两年以后我会回来，到你家拜见你的父母，看看你的孩子。两人约定了日期。约期快到的时候，张劭把这件事告诉母亲，请母亲准备饭菜等候客人。母亲说：两年前的分别，千里之外的一句话，你怎么就这样当真呢？张劭说：巨卿是守信的人，一定不会失约。母亲说：既然这样，我就为你酿酒吧。到了那一天，范式果然来了，登堂拜见，畅饮尽欢而别。后来张劭得了重病去世。范式忽然梦见张劭戴着黑色的礼帽，帽缨垂下，趿着鞋子来叫他：巨卿，我某日死了，将在某时下葬，永远回到黄泉。你若没有忘记我，还能赶得上吗？范式惊醒，悲伤地流下眼泪，穿上为朋友服丧的衣服，赶在下葬的日子飞奔而去。他还没有赶到，送葬的队伍已经出发。到了墓穴边，正要下葬，灵柩却怎么也推不动。张劭的母亲抚着棺木说：元伯，难道你还在盼着谁吗？就把灵柩停了下来。过了一会儿，只见一辆白车、一匹白马号哭着奔来。母亲远远望见，说：这一定是范巨卿。范式来到灵前，叩头说：走吧，元伯！死生不同路，从此永别了。送葬的上千人都流下了眼泪。范式亲手执绋牵引，灵柩这才向前移动。

sections.bodyEn: In the Han dynasty there was in Donghai commandery a filial daughter-in-law who served her mother-in-law with great devotion. The mother-in-law said: 'She works so hard to care for me; I am old — why cling to my remaining years and burden the young?' and hanged herself. The old woman's daughter went to the authorities: 'This daughter-in-law killed my mother.' The officials seized her and tortured her cruelly, and unable to bear it she falsely confessed. Lord Yu, then a prison clerk of the commandery, said: 'This woman served her mother-in-law for ten years and is known everywhere for her filial piety; she would never kill her.' The governor would not listen. Unable to prevail, Lord Yu wept at the office clasping the record of her case and resigned. Thereafter the commandery suffered drought, with no rain for three years. When a new governor came, Lord Yu told him: 'The filial widow should not have died; the former governor killed her unjustly, and that is the cause of the calamity.' The governor at once went himself to sacrifice at her grave and set up a memorial to her. Rain fell immediately, and that year brought a great harvest. The text adds what the elders told: her name was Zhou Qing; before her execution she had a carriage bear a bamboo pole ten zhang long hung with five banners, and swore before the crowd: 'If I am guilty, let me be killed and my blood flow down; if I die unjustly, let my blood flow upward.' After the execution her blood, blue-yellow, ran up the pole to its top and then down along the banners.
sections.bodyZh: 汉朝的时候，东海郡有一位孝顺的媳妇，奉养婆婆非常尽心。婆婆说：媳妇奉养我这样辛苦，我已经老了，何必吝惜剩下的岁月，长久拖累年轻人呢？就上吊自尽了。婆婆的女儿到官府告状，说：是这个媳妇杀了我母亲。官府把她抓起来，严刑拷打，孝妇受不了酷刑，只好屈打成招。当时，于公在郡里做狱吏，说：这个媳妇奉养婆婆十年，孝顺的名声远近皆知，一定不会杀人。太守不听。于公据理力争也没有用，抱着她的案卷在官府痛哭了一场，辞职而去。此后，郡中大旱，三年不下雨。后来新的太守到任，于公对他说：孝妇不该死，前任太守冤杀了她，灾祸的原因就在这里。太守立刻亲自去祭拜孝妇的坟墓，并为她立碑表彰。天上立刻下起雨来，那一年获得了大丰收。书中又记下了老人们的传说：孝妇名叫周青，临刑前，用车载着一根十丈长的竹竿，上面挂着五面旗幡，她当众发誓：我周青如果有罪，甘愿被杀，血会顺着往下流；如果我是冤死的，血就会逆流而上。行刑以后，她的血呈青黄色，顺着旗杆一直流到了竿顶，又顺着旗幡流了下来。

sections.bodyEn: Han Ping, a retainer of King Kang of Song, married a woman of the He family who was very beautiful, and King Kang took her from him. When Han Ping showed his resentment, the king imprisoned him and sentenced him to hard labour on the city walls. His wife secretly sent him a letter, its words deliberately obscure: 'The rain falls long; the river is wide and the water deep; the sun rising strikes the heart.' The king obtained the letter and showed it to his courtiers, but none could understand it. The minister Su He explained: 'The rain falls long — she grieves and longs; the river is wide and the water deep — they cannot reach each other; the sun strikes the heart — in her heart she resolves to die.' Soon after, Han Ping killed himself. His wife secretly rotted her clothes. When the king took her up a high terrace, she threw herself off; the attendants grabbed at her, but the cloth tore in their hands, and she died. In her sash she left a letter: 'The king wanted me to live; I wanted to die. I beg that my bones be given to Han Ping to be buried with him.' The king, furious, refused, and had the villagers bury them apart, the two graves facing each other. 'If you two love each other so,' said the king, 'make your graves join, and I will not stop you.' Overnight a great catalpa grew from the head of each grave; in ten days each was a full armspan thick, and they bent towards each other, roots entwined below and branches interlaced above. A pair of mandarin ducks, male and female, roosted always in the trees, never leaving morning or evening, necks entwined, crying mournfully. The people of Song pitied them and called the trees the Trees of Longing.
sections.bodyZh: 宋康王的舍人韩凭，娶了何氏为妻，何氏非常美丽，宋康王就把她夺了去。韩凭心怀怨恨，康王把他关进牢里，罚他去做筑城的苦役。何氏偷偷给韩凭送去一封信，故意写得很隐晦：雨水绵绵，河大水深，太阳照着心。康王得到了这封信，给左右的人看，谁也看不懂。大臣苏贺解释说：雨水绵绵，是说她又愁又想；河大水深，是说彼此不能来往；太阳照着心，是说她心里已经有了寻死的念头。不久，韩凭就自杀了。何氏暗中把自己的衣服弄得腐烂。康王和她一起登上高台，她纵身跳下，左右的人去拉她，衣服一扯就碎，没有拉住，她就摔死了。她在衣带上留下遗书：大王想让我活着，我却愿意死去。希望把我的尸骨赐给韩凭，与他合葬。康王大怒，偏不答应，让同乡人把他们分开埋葬，两座坟遥遥相望。康王说：你们夫妻相爱不止，如果能让两座坟合在一起，我就不再阻拦。一夜之间，两座坟头各长出一棵大梓树，十天就粗得要两人合抱，树干弯曲着彼此靠近，树根在地下交缠，树枝在上面交错。又有一对鸳鸯，一雌一雄，常常栖息在树上，早晚都不离开，交颈悲鸣，声音令人感动。宋国人为他们哀伤，就把这两棵树叫作“相思树”。

sections.bodyEn: Yi obtained from the Queen Mother of the West the drug of deathlessness, and his wife Heng'e — later more often written Chang'e — stole it and fled to the moon. Before she went she found a diviner named Youhuang and asked him to cast the yarrow stalks for her. Having divined, Youhuang said: 'Auspicious. The light-winged bride goes west alone. She will meet darkness in the sky; let her not fear, let her not be startled; afterwards she shall greatly prosper.' So Heng'e entrusted herself to the moon and became the toad in the moon. The entry in the Soushen ji is only a few lines, yet it is among the earliest written witnesses to the story of Chang'e's flight to the moon. Here, having stolen the drug, she becomes a toad — unlike the lovely moon-fairy of later times; and the diviner's words seem to say that the westward journey, though dark, will end well. Why Yi sought the drug and why Chang'e stole it, the text does not say; all the later explanations have grown in the silence around these few lines.
sections.bodyZh: 后羿向西王母求得了长生不死的药，他的妻子姮娥——后来人们多写作嫦娥——偷了这药，奔向月亮。临走之前，她找到一位名叫有黄的占卜者，请他用蓍草为自己占一卦。有黄占卜以后说：吉利。轻盈飘逸的嫁出的女子，独自将要向西远行。路上会遇到天色昏暗，不要害怕，不要惊慌，以后将会大大昌盛。于是姮娥就把自己托身于月亮之中，成了月亮里的蟾蜍。这则记载在《搜神记》里只有寥寥数语，却是后来嫦娥奔月故事最早的几种文字见证之一。书中说她偷药之后化为蟾蜍，与后世“月宫仙子”的美丽形象并不一样；那位占卜者的卦辞，似乎在说这次西行虽然艰险，却会有好的结果。至于后羿为什么去求药、嫦娥为什么偷药，书中都没有说，后来的种种解释，都是在这几句话的空白处生长出来的。

sections.bodyEn: An old tale says: in high antiquity a man went far away to war, leaving at home only his daughter and a stallion, which she tended herself. Living alone in a remote place and missing her father, she said to the horse in jest: 'If you can bring my father home, I will marry you.' At these words the horse broke its halter and ran off straight to her father. Surprised and glad, the father mounted it. The horse gazed back the way it had come, neighing mournfully without end. 'This horse would not act so for nothing,' said the father; 'has something happened at home?' and he rode home in haste. Thinking the horse had uncommon feeling, he fed it the best fodder, but it would not eat; whenever it saw the girl come or go it leapt and kicked in joy and rage, again and again. Wondering, the father asked his daughter privately, and she told him everything. 'Say nothing,' he said, 'lest the family be shamed; and do not go in and out.' He set a crossbow and shot the horse, and spread its hide to dry in the courtyard. While he was away, the girl played with a neighbour's daughter beside the hide, kicking it: 'You beast, wanting a human wife! You got yourself flayed for it — why bring such misery on yourself?' Before she had finished, the hide sprang up, wrapped her round and carried her away. Days later she and the hide were found among the branches of a great tree, both turned into silkworms spinning cocoons on the tree. A neighbour woman took the cocoons and raised them, and her yield was many times that of ordinary silkworms. So the tree was named sang, the mulberry — sang, that is, sorrow.
sections.bodyZh: 古老的传说讲：远古的时候，有一个人出远门去征战，家里没有别人，只剩下一个女儿和一匹公马，女儿亲自喂养这匹马。她独自住在偏僻的地方，思念父亲，就跟马开玩笑说：你要是能把我父亲接回来，我就嫁给你。马听了这句话，挣断缰绳跑走了，一直跑到父亲那里。父亲看见马，又惊又喜，就骑上了它。马望着来的方向，不停地悲鸣。父亲说：这匹马无缘无故这样，家里莫非出了什么事？急忙骑马赶回了家。父亲觉得这匹马有非同寻常的情义，就用好草好料喂它，马却不肯吃，每次看见女儿进出，就又喜又怒地跳跃踢打，不止一次。父亲觉得奇怪，悄悄问女儿，女儿把实情告诉了他。父亲说：不要声张，免得辱没家门。你也不要再进出了。于是他埋下弓弩射死了马，把马皮晒在院子里。父亲出门后，女儿和邻家的女孩在马皮旁边玩耍，用脚踢着马皮说：你是畜生，还想娶人做妻子？落得被剥皮的下场，何苦呢！话还没说完，马皮忽然跳了起来，卷起女孩就跑。几天以后，人们在一棵大树的枝间找到了女孩和马皮，都已经变成了蚕，在树上吐丝结茧。邻家的妇人把茧取回去养，收成比普通的蚕多好几倍。人们就把那种树叫作“桑”，“桑”就是“丧”的意思。
sections.headingEn: The girl who became a silkworm

sections.bodyEn: A man of Xinyu county in Yuzhang saw six or seven women in a field, all in robes of feathers, not knowing that they were birds. He crept up, took the feather robe one of them had taken off, hid it, and then went towards the birds. The birds all flew away, but one could not fly without her robe. The man took her as his wife, and she bore him three daughters. Later the mother had her daughters ask their father, learned that the robe was hidden beneath the stacked grain, found it, put it on and flew away. Afterwards she came back for her three daughters, and they too flew away. The tale is only a few lines in the Soushen ji, yet it is among the earliest Chinese records of the feather-robed maiden: the hidden garment, the forced marriage, the flight once the robe is found — motifs that recur in later legends across China and are often compared with swan-maiden tales the world over. The text does not say what she said as she left, nor what became of the man; it leaves only the ending in which the mother comes back and takes her daughters away one by one.
sections.bodyZh: 豫章郡新喻县有一个男子，看见田里有六七个女子，都穿着羽毛做的衣服，他不知道她们其实是鸟。他悄悄爬过去，拿到其中一个女子脱下的羽衣，把它藏了起来，然后走向那些鸟。鸟儿们各自飞走了，只有一只没有了羽衣，飞不起来。男子就娶了她做妻子，生了三个女儿。后来，母亲让女儿去问父亲，得知羽衣藏在稻谷堆的下面，就找到了它，穿上羽衣飞走了。后来她又回来迎接三个女儿，女儿们也都飞走了。这则故事在《搜神记》里只有短短几行，却是中国关于“羽衣仙女”最早的记载之一：被藏起的衣服、被迫的婚姻、找回羽衣以后的离去，这些情节后来在许多地方的传说里一再出现，人们常把它与世界各地的“天鹅处女”故事相比。书中没有说她临走时说了什么，也没有说那个男子后来怎样，只留下母亲回来把女儿们一个个接走的结局。

sections.bodyEn: Ziyu, youngest daughter of King Fuchai of Wu, was eighteen, outstanding in talent and beauty. A youth named Han Zhong, nineteen, was versed in the arts of the Way. Ziyu loved him; they exchanged letters in secret, and she promised to be his wife. Han Zhong went to study in Qi and Lu, and before leaving asked his parents to seek her hand from the king. The king was furious and refused. Ziyu, her grief pent up within her, died and was buried outside the Chang Gate. Three years later Han Zhong came back and asked his parents about the match. They said: 'The king was furious; Ziyu died of grief and is already buried.' Weeping bitterly, Han Zhong took offerings to mourn at her tomb. Ziyu's spirit came out of the grave and said in tears: 'After you left, I thought your parents' suit to my father would surely succeed; who could have known what fate awaited me after we parted!' Turning her head and bending her neck she sang: 'A crow on the southern hill, a net spread on the northern hill; the crow has flown high — what can the net do now?' She asked him into the tomb. 'Life and death take different roads,' he said; 'I fear to offend; I dare not.' 'I know that life and death take different roads,' she said, 'but once we part today we shall never meet again. Do you fear that as a ghost I will harm you?' Moved, he followed her into the tomb and stayed three days and nights. At parting she gave him a bright pearl an inch across. When Han Zhong went to the king and told what had happened, the king raged, thinking he had robbed the grave, and ordered his arrest. Ziyu's spirit appeared before the king as he dressed his hair and knelt to clear Han Zhong. The queen, hearing her, came out to embrace her, but Ziyu vanished like smoke.
sections.bodyZh: 吴王夫差的小女儿名叫紫玉，十八岁，才华和容貌都很出众。有一个少年叫韩重，十九岁，懂得道术。紫玉爱慕他，两人私下书信往来，紫玉答应嫁给他。韩重要到齐鲁一带去求学，临走前托父母去向吴王求婚。吴王大怒，不肯把女儿嫁给他。紫玉郁结而死，葬在阊门之外。三年后韩重回来，问父母求婚的事，父母说：吴王大怒，紫玉郁结而死，已经下葬了。韩重痛哭，带着祭品到墓前吊唁。紫玉的魂魄从墓中出来，流着泪对他说：你走以后，你让父母向父王求婚，我以为一定能如愿，没想到分别以后遭此命运，又能怎样呢！她扭过头，弯着颈子唱道：南山有乌鸦，北山张罗网；乌鸦已经高飞去，罗网又能怎么样！她邀韩重进入坟墓，韩重说：死生不同路，我怕有罪过，不敢从命。紫玉说：死生不同路，我也知道；可是今天一别，就永远不会再见了。你是怕我是鬼会害你吗？韩重被她的话感动，跟她进了坟墓，住了三天三夜。临别时，紫玉拿出一颗一寸大的明珠送给他。韩重去见吴王，说出了这件事，吴王大怒，以为他盗墓，要抓他。紫玉的魂魄出现在正在梳妆的吴王面前，跪着替韩重辩白。吴王的夫人闻声出来抱她，紫玉却像烟一样消散了。

sections.bodyEn: Song Dingbo of Nanyang, when he was young, was walking at night and met a ghost. He asked who it was, and it said: 'I am a ghost. And who are you?' Dingbo lied: 'I am a ghost too.' 'Where are you going?' 'To the market at Wan.' 'So am I.' So they went on together for some li. The ghost said: 'Walking is too slow; let us take turns carrying each other.' 'Excellent,' said Dingbo. The ghost carried him first for some li and said: 'You are very heavy — are you not a ghost?' 'I am newly dead,' said Dingbo, 'so my body is heavy.' When Dingbo carried the ghost it weighed almost nothing. So they took turns several times. Dingbo said: 'Being a new ghost, I do not know what ghosts fear or avoid.' 'Only human spittle,' said the ghost. They went on and came to a river. Dingbo had the ghost cross first and heard no sound at all; when he crossed himself the water splashed noisily. 'Why do you make a sound?' asked the ghost. 'I died only lately and am not used to crossing water; do not think it strange.' As they neared the market of Wan, Dingbo hoisted the ghost onto his shoulder and held it fast. The ghost shrieked and begged to be put down, but Dingbo paid no heed and went straight into the market, where he set it down and it turned into a sheep. He sold the sheep, spitting on it lest it change again, and went off with fifteen hundred cash. As Shi Chong said at the time: 'Dingbo sold a ghost and got fifteen hundred.'
sections.bodyZh: 南阳有个叫宋定伯的人，年轻的时候，有一次夜里赶路，遇到了一个鬼。他问对方是谁，鬼说：我是鬼。鬼反问：你又是谁？宋定伯骗它说：我也是鬼。鬼问：你要到哪里去？宋定伯说：要到宛城的集市去。鬼说：我也要去宛城的集市。两个就一起走了几里路。鬼说：走路太慢了，我们轮流背着走，怎么样？宋定伯说：好极了。鬼就先背宋定伯走了几里，说：你太重了，莫非不是鬼吧？宋定伯说：我是新死的鬼，所以身子重。轮到宋定伯背鬼，鬼几乎没有一点重量。这样轮换了好几次。宋定伯又说：我是新鬼，不知道鬼有什么害怕和忌讳的？鬼说：只是不喜欢人的唾沫。两个继续往前走，路上遇到一条河，宋定伯让鬼先过，听上去一点声音也没有；宋定伯自己过河，水声哗哗作响。鬼又问：你过河怎么有声音？宋定伯说：我新死不久，还不习惯过水，你别见怪。快到宛城集市时，宋定伯把鬼扛在肩上，紧紧抓住它。鬼大叫起来，声音咋咋地响，要他放自己下来，宋定伯不理它，一直走到集市中间，才把它放在地上，鬼变成了一只羊。宋定伯就把羊卖了，怕它再变化，还朝它吐了唾沫，得了一千五百钱才离开。当时石崇有一句话：定伯卖鬼，得钱千五。

sections.bodyEn: In Minzhong of Eastern Yue there is a ridge called Yongling, tens of li high, and in a valley to its northwest lived a great serpent seven or eight zhang long and more than ten spans round, which the local people dreaded. Many of the commandants of Dongye and the officials of its counties died because of it. Sacrifices of oxen and sheep brought no peace. The serpent made known, now in dreams and now through shamans, that it wished to eat a girl of twelve or thirteen. The officials were troubled, but the evil did not cease, so they sought out daughters of bondmaids and of criminals, reared them, and on the first day of the eighth month sent one to the mouth of the serpent's cave, and it came out and devoured her. So it went year after year, until nine girls had been given. That year they sought again and had found no one. Li Dan of Jiangle county had six daughters and no son; the youngest, named Li Ji, volunteered. Her parents refused. Li Ji said: 'My parents are unlucky: six daughters and no son — it is as if you had none. I cannot save my parents as Tiying did; I cannot support you and only waste food and clothing; my life is no use, and I had better die early. Selling my body will bring a little money to support you — is that not good?' Out of love her parents still would not let her go, so she slipped away in secret. She asked the officials for a good sword and a dog that could bite snakes. On the first of the eighth month she sat in the shrine with the sword in her bosom and the dog beside her. First she set at the cave mouth several piculs of rice cakes soaked in honey and parched flour. The serpent came out, its head as big as a granary and its eyes like two-foot mirrors, and smelling the cakes it fell to eating them. Li Ji loosed the dog, which seized and bit it, and she struck it from behind several times with the sword. In agony the serpent burst out into the shrine courtyard and died. Li Ji went into the cave and found the skulls of the nine girls; she brought them all out and sighed: 'You were timid and weak, and the serpent devoured you — how pitiful.' Then she walked slowly home. The king of Yue, hearing of it, took Li Ji as his queen, made her father magistrate of Jiangle, and gave gifts to her mother and sisters. From then on there were no more evil creatures in Dongye, and songs about her are sung to this day.
sections.bodyZh: 东越闽中有一座庸岭，高几十里，岭的西北山谷里住着一条大蛇，长七八丈，粗十几围，当地人都很害怕。东冶的都尉和属县的官员，有很多被它害死。人们用牛羊祭祀，也得不到平安。大蛇有时托梦给人，有时让巫祝传话，说要吃十二三岁的童女。官员们都很忧虑，可是灾祸一直不止，只好四处寻找婢女所生的女孩和犯罪人家的女儿，养起来，到八月初一祭祀时，送到蛇洞口，大蛇出来把她们吞吃。这样年复一年，已经用了九个女孩。那一年又要征募，还没有找到人。将乐县的李诞家有六个女儿，没有儿子，最小的女儿名叫李寄，自愿应征。父母不答应。李寄说：父母命苦，只生了六个女儿，没有一个儿子，有我们和没有一样。女儿不能像缇萦那样救父母，既不能供养你们，又白白耗费衣食，活着没有益处，不如早点死。卖了我的身子，可以得到一点钱来供养父母，岂不是好事？父母疼爱她，始终不肯让她去，李寄就偷偷地走了。她向官府要了一把好剑和一条会咬蛇的狗。到了八月初一，她坐在庙里，怀里揣着剑，牵着狗。她先把几石米做成的糍粑浇上蜂蜜和炒面，放在洞口。大蛇出来了，头大得像谷仓，眼睛像二尺宽的铜镜，闻到糍粑的香味，就先去吃糍粑。李寄放出狗，狗扑上去撕咬，李寄从后面挥剑砍了好几下。大蛇痛得冲出洞来，到了庙前的空地上就死了。李寄走进洞里察看，找到了那九个女孩的骷髅，全部拿了出来，叹息道：你们胆怯软弱，被蛇吃掉，真是可怜。说完，她慢慢地走回家去。越王听说了，聘李寄为王后，任命她的父亲为将乐县令，母亲和姐姐们也都得到了赏赐。从此，东冶再也没有妖邪之物，歌颂她的歌谣至今还在流传。

sections.bodyEn: In the time of Sun Quan there lived in Jinan in Xiangyang a man named Li Xinchun who kept a dog called Black Dragon. He loved it dearly; it went everywhere with him, and at every meal and every cup of wine he shared with it. One day Li Xinchun drank outside the city, grew very drunk, could not get home, and fell asleep in the grass. As it happened, the governor Zheng Xia came out to hunt, and seeing the grass in the fields grown deep, had men set fire to it. Li Xinchun lay just downwind. Seeing the fire coming, the dog tugged at its master's clothes with its teeth, but he lay too drunk to stir. Thirty or fifty paces away there was a stream; the dog ran to it, plunged in, soaked itself, ran back and rolled round and round its master, wetting the grass about him, back and forth again and again, until its master was spared the fire. But exhausted by carrying water, the dog fell dead at his side. When Li Xinchun woke and saw the dog dead with its coat soaked through, he was amazed; then he saw the traces of the fire, understood, and wept aloud. When the governor heard of it he said with feeling: 'This dog repaid kindness more deeply than a man. A man who does not know gratitude — how can he compare with a dog?' He ordered a coffin, clothes and coverlets, and had Black Dragon buried. Today, the text says, there is a Tomb of the Faithful Dog at Jinan, more than ten zhang high.
sections.bodyZh: 三国孙权的时候，襄阳纪南有一个人叫李信纯，家里养了一条狗，名叫黑龙，他非常喜爱这条狗，走到哪里都带着它，吃饭喝酒的时候也总分给它一份。有一天，李信纯在城外喝酒，喝得大醉，来不及回家，就躺在草丛里睡着了。正好太守郑瑕出城打猎，看见田野里的草很深，就派人放火烧草。李信纯躺的地方正好在下风口，黑龙看见大火烧过来，就用嘴拉扯主人的衣服，可李信纯醉得一动不动。他躺的地方附近有一条小溪，相距三五十步，黑龙就奔到溪边，跳进水里，把全身打湿，跑回主人身边，绕着主人打滚，把身上的水洒在主人周围的草上，这样来回跑了不知多少趟，终于让主人躲过了大火。可是黑龙运水累得筋疲力尽，倒在主人身边死去了。不久，李信纯醒了过来，看见狗已经死了，全身的毛都是湿的，非常惊讶，再看看大火烧过的痕迹，明白了一切，放声痛哭。这件事传到太守那里，太守感慨地说：狗报恩，比人还要深。人若不知道报恩，怎么比得上狗呢！他就命人准备棺椁和衣被，把黑龙安葬了。书中说，今天纪南还有一座义犬冢，高十几丈。

storySeries.descriptionEn: Butler's prose Odyssey read in two parts across all twenty-four books: the wanderings (Books I–XII) and the homecoming (Books XIII–XXIV) — thirty-two chapters in all.

storySeries.descriptionEn: Four parts read in the order of Book II of Apollodorus's Library: Perseus, and his descendant Heracles from birth through the twelve labours to the pyre on Oeta — forty-nine chapters in all.
storySeries.descriptionZh: 按阿波罗多洛斯《书库》第二卷的顺序连读四部：珀尔修斯，以及他的后代赫拉克勒斯从出生、十二项任务到火葬堆上升天，共四十九章。

storySeries.descriptionEn: Seaton's translation of Apollonius's Argonautica read in two parts across all four books: the outward voyage (Books I–II) and the fleece and the return (Books III–IV) — twenty-six chapters in all.
storySeries.descriptionZh: 按西顿英译阿波罗尼俄斯《阿尔戈英雄纪》的四卷连读上下两部：上部远航（第一至二卷），下部金羊毛与归航（第三至四卷），共二十六章。

storySeries.descriptionEn: The last chapters of Snorri's Gylfaginning read in two parts: the death of Baldr and the binding of Loki (chapters 49–50), and Ragnarök, the new world and the vanishing of the hall around Gylfi (chapters 51–54) — twenty-five chapters in all.
storySeries.descriptionZh: 按斯诺里《欺骗古鲁菲》最后几章的顺序连读两部：巴德尔之死与洛基受罚（第49–50章），诸神黄昏、新世界与古鲁菲的幻境消失（第51–54章），共二十五章。

storySeries.descriptionEn: The Morris and Magnússon translation of the Völsunga saga read in three parts: Sigmundr (chapters 1–13), Sigurðr the dragon-slayer (13–24) and Sigurðr and Brynhildr (25–32) — thirty-six chapters in all.
